summary: Repository initialized with docs/skills, agent pointers, Woven Dusk webfront, and utils layout.

why: Completes initialization plan with verified npm run build and uv run read-skills.

summary: Merged original DESIGN.md and woven-dusk SKILL.md into a single all-in-one design reference at docs/skills/woven-dusk-design/SKILL.md.
why: Consolidates Vercel/Geist structural guidance and Woven Dusk palette into one canonical document for agents and developers.

summary: Removed redundant docs/ and root markdown files. Consolidated workflow and project context into global-project-rules skill. docs/ now holds skills, changelog, and plans only.
why: Reduces duplicate documentation the user did not need.

summary: Added README.md, docs/purpose.md, and docs/goals.md with ReliaQuest grant context, architecture, five-phase timeline, and evaluation criteria. Updated global-project-rules and pyproject.toml.
why: Documents what Ariadne is and what the prototype must deliver by October 2026.

summary: Replaced high-level five-phase timeline with week-by-week roadmap (Wk 1-16) including ITS check-in, midpoint review, pitch workshop, and October ReliaQuest pitch milestones.
why: README and docs/goals.md now reflect the actual project schedule and task breakdown.

summary: Implemented a class-based DatasetDownloader in utils/download/ and wired it into main.py under a --download flag. Configured sequential job-specific logging (e.g. logs/1-download.log), updated pyproject dependencies with requests, and updated README.md Quick Start.
why: Integrates external MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC data acquisition into the repository CLI with persistent audit logs under logs/ of each execution.

summary: Pinned MITRE ATT&CK dataset version to v19.0 and CAPEC to v3.9 for reproducible evaluations. Restructured the download folders to be versioned (e.g. data/raw/attack/v19.0/) and added data/versions.json to track pinned versions in Git.
why: Ensures research and evaluation metrics remain completely reproducible across updates to the public data sources.

summary: Converted the roadmap tables in goals.md to checklists and marked the first two setup/download tasks as completed after verification.
why: Allows tracking project milestone progress in a clear checklist format.

summary: Added the Status column with checkboxes to the Roadmap tables in README.md, marking the first two setup tasks as completed.
why: Keeps the README roadmap synchronized with goals.md for consistent project status tracking.

summary: Fixed DatasetDownloader to decompress gzip-encoded HTTP responses when streaming to disk. GitHub raw serves ATT&CK JSON with Content-Encoding: gzip; writing response.raw without decode_content saved binary .json.gz data instead of plain JSON. Updated global-project-rules to require committing and pushing to GitHub after testing completes.
why: Downstream consumers expect valid enterprise-attack.json STIX, not gzip-compressed bytes with a .json extension. Agents should land verified work on GitHub promptly.

summary: Added an implementation plan for the ATT&CK Neo4j knowledge graph builder. The plan covers the build CLI contract, ATT&CK preprocessing into processed pairs, Neo4j graph artifacts, optional live loading, and validation phases.
why: Defines the next data-layer goal before implementation so the raw ATT&CK dataset can be converted reproducibly into a Neo4j fixture.

summary: Revised the ATT&CK graph builder plan to prioritize portable graph artifact generation before any database loading. The updated plan now centers on a normalized graph model, JSONL nodes and relationships, schema and constraint Cypher, Neo4j CSV files, and manifests.
why: Keeps the data-layer build reproducible and database-neutral so future experiments can swap graph backends after stable artifacts exist.

summary: Added the portable graph build CLI contract to main.py with --build attack|capec|all and --dry-run. Introduced utils/kg_builder as the artifact builder entry point and updated goals.md and README.md to describe the database-neutral ATT&CK artifact workflow.
why: Establishes the public build surface before implementing STIX normalization and artifact exporters.

summary: Added the artifact-focused KG builder package layout under utils/kg_builder with config, models, io, preprocess, schema, exporters, and validate modules plus KGBuildRunner orchestration stubs.
why: Organizes the build pipeline around raw input, normalized graph modeling, and portable artifact exporters before implementing ATT&CK loading.

summary: Implemented reproducible ATT&CK raw dataset discovery via data/versions.json and gzip-aware STIX bundle loading with source path, bundle id, object count, and version reporting. Added fixture and real-dataset loader tests.
why: Ensures the builder can locate and parse the pinned enterprise-attack.json before normalization.

summary: Implemented ATT&CK STIX preprocessing into a normalized graph model with node label mapping, relationship conversion, derived HAS_TECHNIQUE and HAS_SUBTECHNIQUE edges, and deprecated/revoked filtering. Added fixture and real-dataset preprocessing tests.
why: Establishes the database-neutral boundary and processed pairs checkpoint format for downstream artifact export.

summary: Wired the ATT&CK build pipeline to export nodes.jsonl, relationships.jsonl, schema.json, and manifest.json with endpoint validation and manifest counts tied to the processed pairs checkpoint.
why: Delivers the primary portable interchange format for later loaders and experiments.

summary: Added schema.cypher, constraints.cypher, and Neo4j CSV exporters generated from the normalized graph model with deterministic output and row-count checks against JSONL artifacts.
why: Prepares Neo4j-compatible import files without requiring a live database during the build phase.

summary: Added artifact validation for node uniqueness, relationship endpoints, label/type allowlists, deterministic ordering, manifest hash verification, and reproducibility across repeated builds.
why: Proves graph artifacts are internally consistent and reproducible before any database load phase.

summary: Added KG builder pytest suite, CLI regression tests, README artifact documentation, and deferred Neo4j loader notes. Documented the portable graph artifact workflow as the active Wk 3-4 data-layer deliverable.
why: Completes the reproducible ATT&CK artifact builder with tests and user-facing documentation.

summary: Added a plan to promote ATT&CK JSONL/schema/manifest files into a canonical graph interchange layer and treat Neo4j/Cypher and Gremlin as generated export targets.
why: Defines the next robust data-layer migration before changing the existing graph builder implementation.

summary: Refined the canonical ATT&CK graph export plan to require a full canonical-path migration, multi-label node records, Gremlin node/edge JSONL exports, and source registry metadata for future specialist agents.
why: Clarifies that canonical artifacts are the only truth source and backend databases are reproducible projections for federated graph experiments.

summary: Verified the ATT&CK canonical artifact contract for runtime graph loading. Confirmed build output paths, manifest hashes, cross-backend export validation, and source card metadata after a full --build attack run and kg_builder pytest suite pass.
why: Step 1 of the runtime graph loader plan establishes the built-artifact boundary loaders must consume before any Neo4j or Gremlin adapter work begins.

summary: Added utils/graph_loader config and registry modules that resolve attack datasets to source cards, canonical manifests, and backend export files. Missing manifests, exports, unsupported backends, and not-yet-built CAPEC datasets fail with clear errors.
why: Step 2 of the runtime graph loader plan introduces a reusable dataset resolution layer before CLI wiring or database adapters.

summary: Extended main.py with --dataset and --graph for load, verify, and health commands while keeping --build artifact generation unchanged. Added graph_loader CLI dispatch, health TCP checks, and CLI regression tests plus README load examples.
why: Step 3 exposes the public runtime loading command surface before GraphStore adapters and orchestration are implemented.

summary: Defined the GraphStore abstract contract and an in-memory adapter for loader tests. The interface covers connect/close, schema setup, idempotent upserts, count queries, sampling, health checks, and post-load verification against canonical manifest counts.
why: Step 4 isolates backend-specific loading behind one contract before Neo4j and Gremlin adapters are added.

summary: Added semantic graph validation for ATT&CK node labels, relationship types, allowed source-target patterns, required properties, dangling references, and derived tactic/subtechnique links. Validation runs against canonical JSONL before any database write.
why: Step 5 gates runtime loading on domain meaning, not just artifact file integrity.

summary: Added graph loader preflight checks for canonical artifact integrity, manifest SHA-256 verification, semantic validation, and optional Neo4j/Gremlin TCP reachability before writes.
why: Step 6 fails fast when built artifacts, hashes, semantics, or backend endpoints are not ready for loading.

summary: Added the Neo4jGraphStore Bolt adapter with constraint application, parameterized MERGE upserts for canonical nodes and relationships, and post-load count verification. Added neo4j driver dependency and Cypher generation unit tests.
why: Step 7 enables programmatic ATT&CK loading into the Docker Neo4j fixture with idempotent merges keyed on canonical ids.

summary: Added the GremlinGraphStore WebSocket adapter with idempotent vertex and edge upsert traversals against TinkerPop Gremlin Server, plus gremlinpython dependency and traversal unit tests.
why: Step 8 loads the same ATT&CK projection into the Docker Gremlin fixture using the generated Gremlin JSONL export contract.

summary: Implemented the dataset load orchestrator with backend factory, batched upserts, independent multi-backend results, semantic validation gating, and wired CLI load dispatch.
why: Step 9 coordinates preflight, semantic validation, Neo4j/Gremlin adapters, and post-load verification through one loader path.

summary: Added runtime load manifest writing after successful semantic validation and post-load verification. Manifests record canonical manifest hash, adapter version, endpoint, counts, and verification results per backend.
why: Step 10 distinguishes built canonical artifacts from verified live database state for operators and future agents.

summary: Added no-load dataset verification and graph health command implementations. Verify checks manifest hashes, semantic rules, runtime manifests, backend reachability, and live counts; health checks endpoint TCP reachability only.
why: Step 11 gives operators cheap readiness checks without triggering another load.

summary: Completed the ATT&CK runtime graph loader with documentation, structure updates, Docker integration tests, and a full operator workflow from download through build, docker start, load, health, and verify. Verified Neo4j live load of 1914 nodes and 21042 relationships against the canonical manifest.
why: Step 12 documents and validates the runtime loading phase so federated specialist agents can rely on reproducible live graph projections.

summary: Migrated the ATT&CK graph builder to a canonical interchange pipeline. Canonical JSONL, schema, and manifest now live under data/graphs/attack/canonical/ with multi-label NodeRecord and EdgeRecord types. Neo4j CSV/Cypher and Gremlin JSONL exports are generated under data/graphs/attack/exports/, validated for cross-backend equivalence, and registered in data/source_cards/attack.json.
why: Separates ground-truth graph data from backend-specific projections so federated specialist agents can query the same ATT&CK graph through Neo4j or Gremlin experiments.

summary: Added Docker-managed graph infrastructure under docker/ with pinned Neo4j 5.26 and Gremlin 3.8.0 images. Introduced utils/infrastructure/docker_manager.py and main.py --docker start|stop|status with optional version overrides and readiness waits before the CLI exits.
why: Gives developers a reproducible local Neo4j and Gremlin stack without manually running docker compose.

summary: Clarified Docker status output with container names and fixed Gremlin readiness checks to use TCP instead of HTTP. Compose service names remain neo4j and gremlin while containers run as ariadne-neo4j and ariadne-gremlin.
why: Docker Desktop shows the folder-based project name docker, which was easy to confuse with the compose file path; clearer logging and a working Gremlin probe prevent false startup failures.

summary: Switched Neo4j startup readiness from HTTP browser probes to TCP checks on the Bolt port. Neo4j can accept port 5455 before HTTP is ready, which raised RemoteDisconnected and failed docker-start even though containers were running.
why: Startup should wait for query ports to accept connections without crashing on transient HTTP handshake failures.

summary: Added docs/structure.md as a short repository navigation guide covering top-level layout, data paths, utilities, Docker stack, web demo, and where to find key components.
why: Gives developers and agents a single quick-reference map without reading the full README or skills.

summary: Added a detailed runtime graph loader plan for loading built ATT&CK canonical artifacts into Neo4j, Gremlin, or both through a common GraphStore abstraction.
why: Defines the next implementation phase for the requested --dataset attack --graph neo4j|gremlin|all command surface without changing code yet.

summary: Refined the ATT&CK runtime graph loader plan with a semantic validation layer and no-load graph health/verify commands. The plan now gates database writes on domain-level node and edge validation before loading Neo4j or Gremlin.
why: Strengthens the planned loader so it validates graph meaning, not just artifact existence, counts, hashes, and backend connectivity.

summary: Added a general graph artifact structure reference under docs/references that documents canonical, exports, and runtime folders for graph builder agents. The reference defines required files, record shapes, build flow, validation logic, and why canonical truth is separated from backend projections and live runtime state.
why: Provides a reusable contract for agentic graph builders that need to reproduce the ATT&CK artifact layout across many knowledge graph types.

summary: Added a CAPEC XML canonical graph builder plan under docs/plans. The plan validates the proposed discovery-first XML approach, aligns it with the existing canonical graph artifact pipeline, and stages CAPEC parsing, validation, exports, source cards, and Gremlin runtime loading.
why: Defines the ordered execution path for implementing CAPEC XML parsing before any code changes are made.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (1/12): Added namespace-aware source contract inspection for the pinned v3.9 catalog. Verified Attack_Pattern_Catalog root, Version, Date, required collections, versioned download paths, and full-catalog build scope with fixture and real-data tests.
why: Establishes the reproducible CAPEC XML source boundary before parser and graph builder implementation begins.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (2/12): Extended BuildPaths with first-class CAPEC raw, discovery, processed-pairs, canonical, export, and dataset helper paths while preserving unchanged ATT&CK path resolution. Added path-resolution tests and capec_discovery_report_path naming for discovery artifacts.
why: Gives the CAPEC builder the same reproducible directory contract as ATT&CK before XML parsing work begins.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (3/12): Added namespace-aware CAPEC XML discovery with path inventory, attribute capture, repeated-structure detection, text-bearing and XHTML path reporting, and processed discovery artifacts under data/processed/discovery/.
why: Provides a schema-drift-tolerant inventory layer before semantic CAPEC normalization and graph mapping begin.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (4/12): Normalized CAPEC XML attack patterns, categories, views, external references, nested execution data, and unmapped fields into deterministic processed-pairs checkpoint records at data/processed/pairs/capec.json.
why: Creates a stable intermediate boundary for entity resolution and canonical graph materialization without coupling to a specific graph backend.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (5/12): Defined the CAPEC canonical schema module with node labels, relationship natures, derived edge vocabulary, required properties, and allowed source-target patterns for graph validation and export.
why: Separates CAPEC graph semantics from ATT&CK schema rules so future validation and Gremlin specialist agents can use a CAPEC-specific vocabulary.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (6/12): Added deterministic CAPEC entity ID helpers for attack patterns, weaknesses, taxonomy entries, external references, execution steps, and relationships with collision-safe prefixes separate from ATT&CK STIX ids.
why: Ensures reproducible canonical graph identifiers and cross-reference resolution before node and edge materialization.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (7/12): Materialized CAPEC processed-pairs checkpoints into canonical NodeRecord and EdgeRecord graphs with reference stubs, execution-step ordering, source-declared relationship direction, and CapecGraphMetadata.
why: Produces the backend-neutral CAPEC graph boundary needed for canonical artifact export and Gremlin runtime loading.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (8/12): Made canonical JSONL, schema, Neo4j Cypher/CSV, and Gremlin exporters dataset-aware for ATT&CK and CAPEC graphs with matching export counts and CAPEC-specific schema generation.
why: Lets one exporter pipeline emit backend projections from either dataset without hardcoded ATT&CK vocabulary.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (9/12): Added dataset-aware graph validation with CAPEC-specific label, relationship, required-property, and edge-pattern checks plus graph_loader CAPEC semantic rules.
why: Fails CAPEC builds before export or load when canonical records are inconsistent or use illegal semantic patterns.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (10/12): Wired --build capec and --build all through KGBuildRunner, added CAPEC manifest metadata, source-card registration, PeerOf/CanAlsoBe relationship natures, and external-reference stub resolution for real-catalog builds.
why: Makes CAPEC a first-class build target with reproducible canonical artifacts and planner-facing source-card metadata.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (11/12): Enabled CAPEC dataset resolution, semantic validation, Gremlin memory-store loading, and verify dispatch in the graph loader after canonical artifacts are built. Deduplicated CAPEC relationship materialization for repeated weakness and step links.
why: Lets operators load and verify the CAPEC Gremlin projection through the same runtime path as ATT&CK once artifacts exist.

summary: CAPEC XML Canonical Graph Builder (12/12): Documented the CAPEC download, build, export, Gremlin load, health, and verify workflow in README, goals, and structure. Full kg_builder and graph_loader regression suites pass after end-to-end CAPEC artifact generation.
why: Completes the CAPEC canonical graph builder plan with operator-facing docs and verified regression coverage for federated agent development.

summary: Added authored connection, safety, provenance, and entity_descriptions sections to ATT&CK and CAPEC source cards via a rebuild-safe overlay mechanism. Authored overlays live in data/source_cards/overlays/ and are committed; CAPEC safety section auto-merges allowed_edge_patterns and relationship_natures from schema.json. Added 10 new contract tests and docs/source_cards.md documenting the generated-vs-authored split.
why: Source cards now carry the full metadata specialist agents need for safe, cited queries — completing the Wk 5 source-cards milestone.

summary: .env Config (1/5): Added the python-dotenv dependency and a central configuration loader (utils/config.py) exposing load_env() plus typed env_str/env_int/env_bool/data_dir helpers, with 16 unit tests. load_env() reads the root .env into os.environ only at explicit entry points so the test suite stays deterministic.
why: First step toward a single, centrally-labeled .env file for all project configuration, replacing tunable values scattered across modules.

summary: .env Config (2/5): Added a fully-commented .env.example template at the repo root grouping all tunable settings into seven labeled sections (dataset versions, data dir, Docker image versions, host ports, Neo4j credentials, graph URIs, runtime tuning), each documenting what it controls and where it is read. Generated a git-ignored live .env from it; .env.example is tracked while .env stays ignored.
why: Gives operators one clearly-labeled central place to change project configuration without hunting through modules.

summary: .env Config (3/5): Wired the Python data pipeline to the central .env. DatasetDownloader now resolves ATTACK_VERSION/CAPEC_VERSION/ARIADNE_DATA_DIR from the environment (class constants remain the fallbacks), LoaderConfig.from_data_dir reads ARIADNE_DATA_DIR and routes its env reads through the typed helpers, and main.py calls load_env() before importing config-bearing modules. Full kg_builder + graph_loader suites pass (134 tests).
why: Routes the download/build/load pipeline through one central config while preserving identical default behavior.

summary: .env Config (4/5): Drove the Docker stack from the central .env. docker-compose.yml now parameterizes image versions, host ports, and NEO4J_AUTH with ${VAR:-default} fallbacks; docker_manager.py reads ports and the start timeout from the environment and layers docker/.env (committed base) then the root .env via --env-file so root values win. Infrastructure tests pass and docker compose config resolves with defaults and honors overrides.
why: Lets operators change Docker image versions, ports, and credentials from the one central file without breaking the committed fallback or default behavior.

summary: .env Config (5/5): Documented the central .env workflow. Added a Configuration section to README.md (cp .env.example .env, what flows where, precedence), updated the Docker note, and recorded .env.example plus the docker/.env role in docs/structure.md. Full utils test suite passes (141 passed, 2 integration skips) and the CLI entry point loads cleanly with load_env().
why: Completes the central-config plan with operator-facing docs so the single labeled .env file is discoverable and its precedence is clear.

summary: Fixed verify command treating missing runtime manifests as errors. Backends with no load manifest are now silently skipped rather than failing verification. This allows ATT&CK verify to pass when only Neo4j was loaded, and CAPEC verify to pass when only Gremlin was loaded.
why: The verify command checked all backends for every dataset, but the project design only loads ATT&CK into Neo4j and CAPEC into Gremlin. Missing manifests from never-loaded backends caused false failures.

summary: Authored docs/plans/planning-agent-plan.md: a 7-phase plan for the federated planning agent (card loader+enrichment, content-probe discovery, plan schema + deterministic self-eval gate, hybrid deterministic/OpenAI-compatible drafters, bounded ReAct loop, plan-level evaluation, CLI+docs).
why: Plans the Wk 6-7 planning agent per the edge-case briefing before implementation, so each phase is validated and committed independently.

summary: Planning Agent (1/7): Added utils/planner scaffold — typed SourceCardView reasoning over introspected fields, a committed card-enrichment layer that fills safety limits/provenance/entity glosses on the generated cards (overlays were removed), a declared canonical join-key registry for the ATT&CK technique-id <-> CAPEC MAPS_TO->TaxonomyEntry bridge, PlannerConfig env wiring, and 20 unit tests with fixtures.
why: Gives the planner a stable, fully-populated ground-truth input so later phases (discovery, gate, drafter) route over consistent cards without reintroducing git-ignored overlays.

summary: Planning Agent (2/7): Added utils/planner/discovery.py — a per-request content-probe liveness layer (connect + non-trivial node count + expected-label check, not a bare socket open), each probe bounded by its own short timeout in a daemon thread, with a short-TTL re-probe cache. Reuses the graph_loader Neo4j/Gremlin stores. 9 unit tests plus a verified live read of the running Docker stack (CAPEC live with 4888 nodes in Gremlin; Neo4j correctly marked down on auth failure).
why: Gives the planner a ground-truth view of which graphs are actually loaded right now so it routes only to live sources and marks parts needing a down source unsupported.

summary: Planning Agent (3/7): Added utils/planner/schema.py (machine-readable Plan: sub-questions with required per-sub-question Limits, declared joins, explicit unsupported parts, rationale/assumptions, partial flag, JSON round-trip) and utils/planner/gate.py — a fully deterministic self-evaluation gate validating that every named source is live, every entity exists in that source's card, declared join keys are real and canonical, per-sub-question limits are present and within card bounds, and the plan is non-degenerate. 17 unit tests.
why: This is the planner's core safety mechanism: the LLM drafts and deterministic code grades, so unroutable plans are rejected with specific reasons before they ship.

summary: Planning Agent (4/7): Added the PlanDrafter protocol with a card-grounded DeterministicDrafter (keyword routing over labels/relationships/glosses that builds gate-valid plans by construction, marks down/unsupported parts, records rationale+assumptions) and a configurable OpenAICompatibleDrafter posting to a local /v1/chat/completions endpoint (default localhost:9090 / default-model) with robust JSON extraction and DrafterUnavailable fallback. A HybridDrafter falls back to deterministic when the LLM is unreachable. 29 unit tests incl. a guarded live test; verified the real model emits a gate-valid partial plan against the live CAPEC-up/ATT&CK-down environment.
why: Provides the probabilistic drafting seam behind a protocol so the LLM drafts and deterministic code grades, with an always-available deterministic fallback for testing and offline use.

summary: Planning Agent (5/7): Added utils/planner/agent.py — the bounded self-evaluating ReAct loop (PlanningAgent.plan): re-probe live sources, draft, deterministically gate, feed specific rejection reasons back into the next draft, cap at max_iterations, and on exhaustion degrade to an honest partial plan (keep gate-valid parts via gate.valid_subset, surface the rest as unsupported, never loop forever or fabricate, never emit a degenerate plan as success). Recorded a per-iteration trace, refined the deterministic drafter's gloss matching to curb over-decomposition, and exported PlanningAgent. 7 loop tests; verified end-to-end against the live env with both deterministic and LLM drafters.
why: Ties discovery, drafting, and the gate into one terminating entry point that always emits a routable or honestly-partial plan with an inspectable trace.

summary: Planning Agent (6/7): Added utils/planner/evaluation/ — a plan-level scorer (source-selection precision/recall, unnecessary-source-call count, expected-entity recall, schema adherence via the gate, and honesty/partial correctness, decoupled from downstream answer success), a 7-case expected-plan corpus with dev and holdout splits including out-of-scope and source-down cases, a run_corpus runner, and a run_eval CLI. Added stub_live_view for deterministic scoring. 9 tests; deterministic agent passes the corpus 7/7 (schema/source-recall/honesty all 1.0).
why: Scores the planner on its plan output against fixed reference plans so a good plan is never blamed for a downstream failure, with a frozen holdout split guarding against overfitting.

summary: Planning Agent (7/7): Wired the --plan/--plan-llm CLI (utils/planner/cli.py + main.py) to probe the live graphs and emit the routing plan as JSON; added docs/planner_agent.md (contract, discovery, gate, drafters, plan schema, config), and updated README, docs/structure.md, and docs/goals.md to mark the Wk 6-7 planning agent complete and document utils/planner. Verified --plan end-to-end against the live stack (CAPEC live, ATT&CK down -> partial plan) with both deterministic and LLM drafters. 3 CLI tests; full planner suite (88) green.
why: Makes the planning agent runnable from the CLI over the live graphs and documents its contract, completing the planning-agent deliverable.

summary: Added notebooks/planner_playground.ipynb — an interactive notebook to drive the planning agent: probe live graphs, inspect source cards and the canonical join key, plan questions with a plan_question() helper (deterministic and local-LLM drafters), run a batch incl. out-of-scope/partial cases, dump the full machine-readable plan, and score the expected-plan corpus. Robust repo-root path setup so imports work from notebooks/. Executed end-to-end headlessly against the live stack (exit 0).
why: Gives an easy, runnable way to test and demo the planning agent against the running Docker servers without the CLI.

summary: Planning Agent fix: the deterministic drafter now requires at least one identifier (node-label/relationship-name) match to select a source; a lone gloss/description match no longer pulls a whole source in or fabricates a spurious cross-source join. _match_card returns id_hits/gloss_hits separately and selection gates on id_hits>0. Fixes over-selection where e.g. 'which groups use which techniques' routed to both ATT&CK and CAPEC. Added a regression test; full planner suite (89) and eval corpus (7/7, 0 unnecessary calls) green.
why: The keyword fallback over-selected sources on weak description-level matches, producing confusing cross-source plans for single-source questions.

summary: Added --yolo-all single-command pipeline flag. Running uv run main.py --yolo-all now orchestrates the full stack in one invocation: download datasets, build canonical artifacts, check credentials (non-interactive), start Docker, load ATT\u0026CK into Neo4j and CAPEC into Gremlin, then verify both graphs. Each step prints a live status line; a Unicode box-drawing summary table is printed at the end. Already-done steps are skipped automatically.
why: The user had to run six or more separate commands to go from a fresh checkout to a running stack. A single entry-point reduces friction and makes onboarding trivial.

summary: Error-Handling (0/4): Authored docs/plans/error-handling-recovery-plan.md, a 4-step plan to make the --yolo-all pipeline self-heal. Root cause of 'relationship type not in schema': the builder writes canonical artifacts into an un-cleaned existing directory and _step_build skips rebuilding when a stale manifest is present, so on-disk artifacts can disagree with the freshly written allowlist schema.
why: Plan the requested recovery policy (back up + rebuild on existing-artifact failures; retry transient; flag others for human input) before implementation so each phase is validated and committed independently.

summary: Error-Handling (1/4): Added utils/recovery.py — backup_directory/prepare_clean_dir/restore_directory (move existing artifacts to a timestamped <parent>/_backups copy before a clean rebuild), classify_failure (stale_state | transient | needs_human, with transient taking precedence), and retry_with_backoff (bounded exponential retry of transient failures). 15 unit tests in utils/graph_loader/tests/test_recovery.py.
why: A single dependency-free, tested home for the copy-then-replace, failure-classification, and retry primitives the builder and pipeline runner will consume.

summary: Error-Handling (2/4): KGBuildRunner.build_attack and build_capec now call recovery.prepare_clean_dir on the canonical directory instead of ensure_dir, so any existing on-disk canonical artifacts are moved to data/graphs/<dataset>/_backups/canonical-<ts> and each build writes into a clean directory. 2 new tests in utils/kg_builder/tests/test_build_recovery.py; full kg_builder suite green (62 passed).
why: A re-build that merged into an un-cleaned directory could leave a stale relationships.jsonl disagreeing with the freshly written allowlist schema, causing 'relationship type not in schema'. Clean rebuilds make this impossible while preserving the prior copy.

summary: Error-Handling (3/4): Made YoloRunner resilient. _step_build now validates existing canonical artifacts and, when stale/corrupt, rebuilds clean (the builder backs the old copy up) instead of blindly skipping; a clean rebuild that still fails is escalated as needs_input. Network/IO steps (docker start, load attack, load capec, verify) run through a _guarded retry-with-backoff that classifies failures: transient errors retry then fail, non-recoverable errors become a new needs_input status (symbol '?', halts abort-steps, non-zero exit in main.py). Summary table reports needs-input steps with a remediation hint. retry_with_backoff resolves time.sleep at call time so it is patchable. 15 new yolo tests; full util suite 139 passed.
why: Implements the requested policy: existing-artifact failures self-heal via backup-and-replace, transient errors retry, and genuinely stuck failures ask for human input instead of crashing opaquely.

summary: Error-Handling (4/4): Documented the recovery layer. Added utils/recovery.py and utils/yolo.py to the docs/structure.md utilities table with a 'Pipeline error handling' subsection (backup-and-replace under data/graphs/<dataset>/_backups, transient retry, NEEDS INPUT escalation), and added a 'One-command pipeline' subsection to README.md describing --yolo-all and its self-healing behavior.
why: Keep the repo map and operator docs truthful about the new module and the pipeline's error-handling guarantees.

summary: Authored docs/plans/specialist-agents-plan.md: a 6-phase plan for the two source-specific query specialists (Cypher/ATT&CK-Neo4j, Gremlin/CAPEC-Gremlin) built on one shared scaffold with four language-specific swap points (builder, validator, connector, normalizer), a shared evidence schema with provenance, federation into the planner workflow, a step-by-step notebook, and merge-to-main.
why: Plans the Wk 7-9 specialist agents per the source briefing before implementation so each phase is validated and committed independently.

summary: Specialist Agents (1/6): Added the shared scaffold for the two query specialists under utils/specialists/ — input/output contracts (SpecialistTask, EvidenceRecord+Provenance, SpecialistResult, EvaluatorTrace), env-driven SpecialistConfig, the deterministic evidence emitter + contract check, the shared resolve-to-schema step (entity->card mapping, seed-id/T-number/CAPEC-id extraction, canonical join-endpoint, STIX-type pairing), the BaseValidator pre-run-gate orchestration, and the QuerySpecialist ReAct loop (intake->resolve->draft->gate->execute->assess->normalize->handoff) with capped redraft and full evaluator traces. 24 unit tests; planner suite still green (88).
why: Locks the shared/language-specific boundary and the evidence contract once, before either engine is built, so both specialists emit the schema synthesis joins on identically.

summary: Specialist Agents (2/6): Added the Cypher specialist (utils/specialists/cypher/) for MITRE ATT&CK on Neo4j — deterministic MATCH-template builder (technique->mitigations, group/tactic->techniques, node lookup, label scan), a static pre-run gate (single-statement, MATCH+RETURN, card label/edge membership, STIX-type/label pairing, write-clause rejection, LIMIT inject/clamp, and a new shared cap_reasons hook rejecting unbounded/over-depth variable-length paths), a READ_ACCESS Neo4j connector with per-query timeout, and a row->evidence normalizer. Registered the integration/live pytest marks. Live-verified T1047 -> M1038/M1040/M1018/M1026.
why: Brings the ATT&CK query specialist up green against the live Neo4j graph in isolation, proving the shared scaffold end-to-end before the harder Gremlin side.

summary: Specialist Agents (3/6): Added the Gremlin specialist (utils/specialists/gremlin/) for MITRE CAPEC — deterministic g.V() traversal builder (capec lookup, neighbors, the MAPS_TO ATT&CK join filtered to taxonomy ATTACK, label scan) emitting a single literal .limit bound, the heavier pre-run gate (g.V()/g.E() start, mutating-step rejection, hasLabel/out/in/both label+edge-direction checks against allowed_edge_patterns, and traversal-depth REJECTION via cap_reasons), a TinkerPop connector with per-query timeout, and an elementMap->evidence normalizer that derives CAPEC-N ids and emits T-prefixed ATTACK join values. Live-verified CAPEC-66 -> CWE-89/CWE-1286 and CAPEC-1 -> T1574.010. 89 specialist tests green.
why: Brings the CAPEC query specialist up green against the live Gremlin graph with the strict label/direction/depth validation property graphs require, completing both specialists in isolation.

summary: Specialist Agents (4/6): Wove the specialists into the planner workflow. Added utils/specialists/federation.py (SpecialistRouter/run_plan: dispatch each planner SubQuestion to the specialist serving its source, collect normalized evidence into a FederatedEvidence bundle with a join_index over the shared ATT&CK-technique-id key and cross-source-join detection — evidence, not prose), utils/specialists/cli.py (run_query_command: plan then run specialists, print queries/records/summaries/provenance JSON), and a main.py --query/--query-llm route mirroring --plan. Also made the seedless Cypher scan prefer substantive labels (Technique) over admin nodes (Matrix). Verified end-to-end live: credential-theft question routes to both sources, CAPEC MAPS_TO returns 177 ATTACK-mapped techniques, exit 0. 94 specialist tests green.
why: Individual specialists in isolation do not prove the pipeline; routing a real planner Plan through them with provenance intact is the federated query the project exists to demonstrate.

summary: Specialist Agents (5/6): Added notebooks/planning-schematic-agents.ipynb — a runnable step-by-step demo of the full planner -> specialists workflow (live probe, source-card schematic, plan, Cypher and Gremlin specialists with per-step evaluator traces, full federation, a real cross-source T-number join, and gate-rejection safety cases); executed headlessly end-to-end (exit 0). Hardened the Gremlin connector to confine its client + asyncio event loop to a dedicated worker thread so it runs inside a Jupyter kernel without the 'event loop already running' crash. Added docs/specialist_agents.md and updated README, docs/structure.md, and docs/goals.md (Wk 7-8 Cypher and Wk 8-9 Gremlin checked off).
why: Gives an inspectable, runnable demonstration of the federated query workflow against the live stack and documents the specialists' contract and four swap points.

summary: Specialist Agents (6/6): Full regression and merge. The specialist suite is green (94 passed) and the whole utils/ suite is 335 passed, 2 skipped. Two FAILING tests (graph_loader test_verify_fails_without_runtime_manifest and infrastructure test_cli_help_shows_docker_choices) are PRE-EXISTING on the branch base commit and unrelated to the specialists (stale assertions vs. the shipped verify-skip behavior and the metavar='VERSION' help text); each is flagged for a separate fix. Merged the specialist-agents branch into main with --no-ff (no push).
why: Completes the two source-specific query specialists per the implementation plan with a verified, isolated, reviewed implementation merged onto main.

summary: Reconciled origin/main (Pipeline Error-Handling series) with the specialist-agents work via a merge commit, then fixed two pre-existing stale tests so the suite is fully green: test_cli_help_shows_docker_choices now expects the actual metavar 'VERSION' (main.py uses metavar='VERSION'), and the verify-without-runtime-manifest test now asserts the shipped skip-and-pass behavior (renamed to test_verify_skips_backends_without_runtime_manifest) per the 2026-06-27 verify change. Full utils/ suite: 363 passed, 2 skipped.
why: The remote main had advanced with unrelated error-handling work; merging it in and correcting two stale tests that contradicted shipped behavior makes main a clean, fully-green superset ready to push.

summary: Added docs/plans/nextjs-workbench-ui.md: the staged plan to replace the webfront with the Ariadne analyst workbench from the provided mockup, migrating web/ from React/Vite to Next.js App Router + Tailwind v4 + Motion while keeping Woven Dusk tokens and Geist. Eight phases: scaffold, types/fixtures, shell+header, left+center, inspector, event-based animations, responsive/a11y/states, docs+merge.
why: The user requested a faithful, compartmentalized reproduction of the mockup with event-based animations ready for a future live workflow; a validated step-by-step plan precedes implementation per the planner skill.

summary: Workbench UI (1/8): Migrated web/ from React/Vite to Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/postcss) + Motion 12, with Geist/Geist Mono via the geist next/font package. Ported the Woven Dusk tokens into app/globals.css as a Tailwind @theme plus shadow-as-border utilities and the mockup's pulse/ring/skel keyframes; removed the Vite config, index.html, and src/ entry. Pinned ESLint to 9.x (eslint-config-next 16's bundled eslint-plugin-react still calls the ESLint-10-removed getFilename).
why: The analyst workbench is a full-height streaming SPA dashboard; the chosen Next.js stack and a correctly wired Woven Dusk token/Geist/Tailwind base must exist before any workbench component is built.

summary: Workbench UI (2/8): Added web/lib/types.ts (TypeScript mirrors of the planner/specialist trace objects — Plan, SubQuestion, EvaluatorTrace, EvidenceRecord, Provenance, SpecialistResult, FederatedEvidence — plus UI view-model types and StageStatus/RunStatus enums), web/lib/fixtures.ts (the WMI->CAPEC sample run as a fully-typed WorkbenchRun with a real nested FederatedEvidence for the Raw JSON tab), and web/lib/conversations.ts. Added Vitest with web/lib/__tests__/fixtures.test.ts (7 tests) asserting the fixture's stages, 8 micro-steps, 4 records, and complete provenance.
why: The inspector and answer card must be pure functions of trace data so a live streaming backend can later replace the fixture unchanged; typing against the real to_dict() shapes keeps that swap honest, and the smoke test guards the fixture's contract.

summary: Workbench UI (3/8): Built the full-height three-region AppShell (268px conversations rail / fluid center / 420px inspector, shadow-as-border seams, internal-scroll regions) and the HeaderBar (Ariadne thread-glyph wordmark, Analyst Workbench tag, live InfraStatusPill badges, Run Pipeline ghost button, Neo4j login). Added shared Woven Dusk primitives: Pill, StatusDot, an icon set, and a CodeBlock with a lightweight json/cypher/gremlin syntax highlighter, plus lib/ui.ts style constants. page.tsx now composes the shell with region stubs.
why: The non-scrolling shell, header, and reusable primitives are the frame and vocabulary every later region depends on; building them first prevents layout churn and keeps styling consistent.

summary: Workbench UI (4/8): Built the left Conversations rail (grouped Today/Yesterday/This week list, active teal thread-edge, Plan/Query mode pills, New button) and the center chat thread: ThreadHeader, right-aligned UserMessage, the structured AnswerCard (MiniStepper status strip, grounded prose with inline ProvenanceChips, footer cross-source JoinChips, View-JSON/Copy/Export actions), and the Composer (Plan/Full-answer + deterministic/LLM toggles, Send). Added a WorkbenchProvider client context so provenance chips and stepper segments can focus inspector stages (consumed in phase 5).
why: These are the analyst's primary read/write surfaces; wiring the cross-panel focus context now lets the Answer Card drive the inspector once it is built.

summary: Workbench UI (5/8): Built the right Inspector — the product centerpiece. InspectorPanel (own collapsible aside with reopen rail), InspectorTabs (Trace/Evidence/Join/Raw), ProgressMeter, and the Trace timeline: a vertical thread with planner TraceStages (probe/draft/gate/emit, shield emphasis on the gate) and SpecialistLanes (backend badge, the eight micro-step checkpoints with shield+ring on the never-cut pre-run gate and normalize, the validated Cypher/Gremlin query via the highlighter, and expandable evidence records). Added Evidence/JoinIndex/RawJson tabs. Provenance chips and stepper segments now focus + scroll the right stage via the WorkbenchProvider; collapse reflows the chat to full width.
why: Seeing exactly what the agent did, step by step, is what turns a generic chat UI into a trustable analyst tool; the inspector renders the actual trace objects so the same components light up when a live stream replaces the fixture.

summary: Workbench UI (6/8): Made the UI animate on pipeline EVENTS. Added lib/runMachine.ts (useRunMachine: a timed event sequence flipping node statuses pending->running->pass, the shape a live SSE stream would emit) and lib/motion.ts (shared Motion variants incl. status-driven dot animation). Folded the machine into WorkbenchProvider (wrapped in MotionConfig reducedMotion=user) and wired status-reactive animation across the mini-stepper dots + outcome chip, the trace markers and the thread that grows as stages pass, the specialist micro-step cascade, the progress bar, the answer-card skeleton->reveal, tab cross-fades, and the collapse width. Added a RunController Replay button. Verified end-to-end: progress advances 0->2->4 stages, answer reveals on the answer event, no console errors.
why: The request is explicit that animations be an event-based approach so a future live workflow drives them; centralizing a status machine + Motion variants makes each part animate off a status prop, which is exactly the seam a real stream plugs into.

summary: Workbench UI (7/8): Made the workbench responsive and accessible. Below lg the inspector becomes a right slide-over drawer (shared InspectorContent extracted; InspectorPanel is now desktop-only, InspectorDrawer added with its own drawerOpen state defaulting closed + a floating reopen button); below md the conversations rail becomes a left slide-over via a header hamburger (MobileMenuButton + leftOpen). Decoupled desktop inline-collapse (inspectorOpen) from the mobile drawer (drawerOpen) with an openInspector() helper used by chips and the View-JSON action. Added aria-current/aria-pressed/aria-labels, kept teal focus rings, and honor prefers-reduced-motion via MotionConfig + CSS. The loading skeleton and answered/partial/no_sources states are type-driven.
why: Woven Dusk + ADA require intentionally-designed mobile (not just stacked) and color-plus-label status; the three-region shell needed drawer behavior so the dense inspector and rail work on small screens.

summary: Workbench UI (8/8): Updated docs for the Next.js webfront stack — global-project-rules layer table (React/Vite -> Next.js App Router + Tailwind v4 + Motion) and Commands (added 'cd web && npm test' Vitest line); docs/structure.md web tree label and the Web Demo section (new app/ + components/ + lib/ map, event-based run-state machine note, dev/build/lint/test commands). Final regression green: npm run build, npm run lint, and npm test (7 passed) all pass.
why: Global rules require a changelog entry and that webfront changes compile; the stack change from React/Vite to Next.js must be reflected in the canonical repo docs so future agents use the right commands and structure.

summary: Fix: the root Python .gitignore rule 'lib/' was silently excluding web/lib/ (the Next.js app's TypeScript source: types, fixtures, conversations, ui, motion, runMachine, and the Vitest test), so the merge to main was missing it and the build failed with @/lib module-not-found. Added scoped negations (!web/lib/ and !web/lib/**) and committed the seven web/lib files. Merged main now passes npm run build, npm run lint, and npm test (7 passed).
why: web/lib is application source, not a Python build artifact; without un-ignoring it the merged webfront could not compile. Verified end-to-end on main after the fix.

summary: Added root app.py: a Python launcher for the Ariadne web server that verifies the Node toolchain, installs web/ JavaScript dependencies on first run (skippable with --skip-install, forceable with --install), and starts the Next.js app — dev with hot reload by default, or --prod for a production build+start, with --port/--host flags. Also pinned turbopack.root to web/ in web/next.config.ts so a stray lockfile elsewhere can't misdirect Turbopack root inference. Verified app.py boots the server to HTTP 200 with no lockfile warning.
why: The user asked for a single root entry point that runs everything the web server needs; app.py mirrors main.py's role for the Python side and removes the manual cd web && npm install && npm run dev steps.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (plan): staged plan for wiring the static Next.js workbench to the live Python backend — a new FastAPI service layer (api/) wrapping utils/ for live-source health, the federated query pipeline (real SSE stage events), LLM/connection config, and infra control; Next.js proxies /api and app.py launches both. Written to docs/plans/frontend-backend-integration.md.
why: The workbench is currently static (no fetch/API); the user wants it fully interactable — see Neo4j/Gremlin liveness, run conversational queries with a staged event sequence, and configure the LLM from the app, incorporating everything main.py can do.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (1/8): scaffolded the api/ FastAPI service and added GET /api/health. The health service probes each graph backend over TCP (per-backend live/down/starting verdict, never raising — unlike run_graph_health which raises ConnectionError) and folds in docker compose state so a booting container reads as 'starting'. Added fastapi, uvicorn[standard], httpx deps and the api package to the wheel targets. 5 pytest contract tests pass (shape, no-raise, docker-unavailable, uri parsing).
why: Every other endpoint depends on a running service and a stable JSON contract; live-source health is the simplest real capability and the first user-visible goal (is Neo4j/Gremlin up).

summary: Frontend↔Backend (2/8): added GET/PUT /api/config to view and edit the env-backed LLM and connection settings. GET resolves through PlannerConfig/SpecialistConfig.from_env() and redacts the Neo4j password (returns neo4j_password_set bool only); PUT validates (http base_url, positive timeout/max_tokens, bolt/ws URIs) and persists via utils.config.set_env_values which preserves .env layout and mirrors into os.environ so edits take effect on the next query without a restart. Documented the PLANNER_LLM_*/SPECIALIST_LLM_* keys in .env.example (section 8). 9 new pytest contract tests pass (14 total).
why: The user must configure the LLM (model, endpoint, enable flag, limits) directly within the app; this is the backend half of that settings form.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (3/8): added POST /api/query, a Server-Sent-Events stream of the federated pipeline. The sync generator reuses the planner→specialists→FederatedEvidence composition (mirroring run_query_command) and emits a real event at each boundary — status, probe (live sources with node counts), plan (with trace), per-specialist results as each completes, evidence bundle, and a server-composed grounded answer (from per-source summaries + the cross-source join index; the pipeline emits evidence, not prose). Starlette iterates the sync generator in its threadpool so blocking graph queries never stall the event loop. Exit codes mirror the CLI (2 no-cards, 1 partial, 0 clean). 8 stub-driven contract tests assert event order/shapes (22 total); validated end-to-end against the live stack (attack 2611 + capec 4888 nodes, 399 records, 84 cross-source correlations, exit 0).
why: This is the heart of the request: make the chat show the real sequence of events when a question is asked, driven by the actual federated query against Neo4j and Gremlin.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (4/8): added the web data layer. web/lib/api.ts is a typed client (getHealth/getConfig/putConfig + a streamQuery SSE helper that POSTs and parses event/data frames off the ReadableStream, since EventSource can't POST). web/lib/adapt.ts is the single backend→WorkbenchRun adapter: pure builders map the Plan/FederatedEvidence/probe/answer payloads onto live sources, four planner stages, per-source lanes with the eight micro-steps, evidence rows, join candidates, and the answer (chips + cross-source join pairs) — components stay unchanged. Added API/SSE wire types to types.ts and a Next rewrite proxying /api/* to FastAPI (same-origin, no CORS). 9 Vitest adapter cases reproduce the canonical WMI run from the federated bundle (16 web tests total); npm build, lint, test all green.
why: The front end must consume real backend data without changing every component; a typed client plus one adapter is the clean seam, and the proxy keeps the browser same-origin.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (5/8): rewired the run lifecycle to live events. runMachine.ts now holds the active WorkbenchRun and a submit() that opens the /api/query SSE stream, advancing liveStatus and rebuilding the run via the adapter as each event arrives (probe→plan→per-specialist→evidence→answer→done); the offline timed replay() is kept for the Run/Replay demo controls. A new client Workbench component bridges the context run to the three regions as props (every presentational component unchanged). The Composer is now interactive (controlled textarea, mode/drafter toggles, Enter-to-send, disabled while running) and AnswerCard handles the error state. Validated live in-browser: submitting a question streams to a real answer (399 records, 84 cross-source correlations) with lanes built from live Cypher/Gremlin data, the Running… state shows, and there are no console errors; build/lint/test green.
why: This delivers the conversational flow and the staged, animated reveal driven by the real federated query — the core 'sequence of events when we ask a question'.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (6/8): live infra status + in-app settings. A new InfraStatusBar client component polls GET /api/health every 5s so the header pills reflect real Neo4j/Gremlin reachability (HeaderBar is now a client component); the pill renders 'LIVE' without a count when the TCP probe has no node count. A new SettingsPanel modal (opened from the header gear) loads GET /api/config and edits the planner+specialist LLM knobs (enable, base URL, model, timeout, max tokens) and the graph connection (URIs, user, write-only password) via PUT /api/config, with validation errors surfaced and a 'Saved · applies to the next query' confirmation. Added a GearIcon and settingsOpen state to the workbench context. Validated live: pills present, panel loads all sections (12 inputs), and a planner-model edit round-trips and persists through the proxy. build/lint/test green.
why: Closes the two remaining priority goals — a live is-it-up indicator and an in-app form for the env-backed LLM/connection settings.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (7/8): infra control actions covering the remaining main.py modes. POST /api/admin streams an SSE log feed for docker start/stop/status, graph health/load/verify, and data download/build — each runs in a worker thread while a temporary root-logging handler forwards the modules' real log output as 'log' events, then a 'done' event with ok/message (failures reported, not raised). A new settings 'Infrastructure & data' section (InfraActions) runs these with a dataset/graph selector and a streamed log console; api.ts gained a generic postSseStream reader shared by streamQuery and a new streamAdmin. 8 stub-driven backend tests assert event order/validation/handler cleanup (30 backend total). Validated live end-to-end through the proxy and UI (graph-health streams real logs → ✓ completed).
why: The user asked to incorporate every main.py capability; these host/admin operations complete that surface, exposed as a streamed admin console.

summary: Frontend↔Backend (8/8): made app.py launch both processes and refreshed the docs. app.py now starts the FastAPI service (via `uv run uvicorn`, falling back to the interpreter) and the Next.js app together, passing API_PORT so the web proxy targets the service, with coordinated Ctrl+C shutdown and --api-port/--prod flags. docs/structure.md gained an api/ section + a rewritten web section and updated 'not yet in repo' (synthesis prose agent only); global-project-rules added the api/ layer, the app.py launcher, and the `pytest api/tests/` + `python app.py` commands. Full regression green: 30 api tests, 16 web tests, npm lint + build, and a clean app.py dual-launch boot (proxied health + full query SSE → answered, exit 0).
why: app.py must run everything the web server needs; with a required backend it has to start both, and the canonical docs must describe the two-process architecture so future agents don't assume the static-only UI.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (plan): wrote docs/plans/full-pipeline-visibility.md. Audit found the backend already streams the complete pipeline (plan.to_dict with iteration trace, per-specialist result.to_dict with raw query + full records + 6-step evaluator traces, full FederatedEvidence with join index) but the front end discards most of it and the chat is single-run. The 6-phase plan exposes a multi-turn chat, full trace depth (planner iterations + evaluator reasons/detail + task metadata + skipped/unsupported), uncapped evidence with full properties/provenance, a multi-payload raw-JSON surface incl. the literal SSE event stream, and adds the last missing main.py admin modes (graph-stop, yolo-all).
why: User asked the workbench to do everything main.py can — full chat, full trace, evidence and raw JSON, end to end. The gap is front-end exposure + multi-turn chat, not the backend.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (1/6): multi-turn chat + raw event/payload capture. Replaced the single-run model with a conversation of turns in runMachine.ts (runs[] + activeRunId + streamingRunId + selectRun/newConversation); each turn now also retains the literal ordered SSE event log and the raw probe/plan/answer payloads (new WorkbenchRun fields, threaded through buildRun). ChatThread renders the full thread (clicking a turn selects it; empty state when cleared); the left rail is driven by real turns with a New action; AnswerCard/MiniStepper take a `live` prop so only the streaming turn animates while past turns render their own baked status. Validated live: asked two questions, all turns persisted with independent ANSWERED/PARTIAL chips, rail switching moved the inspector turn label, and New reset to empty. build + lint + 18 web tests green.
why: The user asked for full chat interfaces; the workbench was single-run with a static mock rail. Multi-turn state + per-turn raw capture is the foundation the deeper trace/evidence/raw-JSON views build on.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (2/6): full trace depth in the inspector. Re-grounded the specialist lane micro-steps to the SIX real EvaluatorTrace steps (intake, resolve, pre-run gate, execute, assess, normalize) — the invented draft/handoff steps are gone. Each lane now renders a Task block (entities, seed_ids, join_key, limits, rationale), an Evaluator trace section (one expandable LaneTraceRow per trace entry, including gate/execute retries, revealing reasons + the full detail JSON), and an error line when a specialist fails. The planner stages now expose the full plan.trace iteration history (gate stage) plus full sub-question detail (draft) and joins/unsupported-with-reasons/assumptions/rationale (emit). TraceTab gained a Skipped & unsupported section that renders when present. Validated live: a query showed all six pills, iteration trace with drafter, expandable detail JSON (timing_ms/template/injected), and task metadata. build + lint + 20 web tests green, no console errors.
why: User asked to see the full trace; the UI was discarding the planner loop history, per-step reasons/detail, task metadata, and skipped/unsupported, and showing two micro-steps the pipeline never emits.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (3/6): uncapped, fully-detailed evidence. The adapter no longer truncates (dropped the 200-row evidence cap and the 6-per-lane cap) and now carries each record's complete properties/related/join_values plus full provenance (the exact query, record_id, timestamp) into the view-model. The Evidence tab gained a text filter (by id/name/label) with a 'showing X of Y' counter and incremental reveal (60 + Show more / Show all) so hundreds of records stay responsive without silent loss; each row expands to the full record JSON and the provenance query (cypher/gremlin). Specialist lanes gained the same reveal (initial 8). Added 3 adapter tests incl. a 250-record no-cap assertion. Validated live against a ~399-record query: lanes showed '177/222 total · showing 8', the Evidence tab filtered (2 of 4) and expanded a record to full JSON + Cypher provenance.
why: User asked to see the full evidence; the UI was capping at 200/6 records and collapsing each to a one-line blob, hiding properties, adjacency, and the provenance query.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (4/6): multi-payload raw-JSON surface + literal SSE event stream, and a tab-switch fix. RawJsonTab now takes the whole run and offers a payload selector — Events / Plan / Probe / Evidence / Answer — each a copyable pretty-printed JSON block; Events renders the turn's ordered SSE log (one color-coded entry per event with its data) so the pipeline is visible start to finish. While validating, found and fixed a real defect: InspectorContent used AnimatePresence mode='wait', and the heavier Phase-2 trace tab's nested-motion subtree never completed its exit, which stalled ALL inspector tab switching; replaced it with a remount+fade of the active tab (no exit wait). Validated live: switched across all four tabs, Events showed '11 events · pipeline order', Plan payload showed request/sub_questions/trace/iteration, copy buttons present.
why: User asked for raw JSON and to see the full evidence-backed pipeline start to finish; only the federated bundle was exposed and the event log/plan/probe/answer were not. The tab-switch stall (regression from the richer trace tab) had to be fixed for any of this to be reachable.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (5/6): admin completeness — graph-stop and yolo-all. The two remaining main.py modes are now reachable from the app: api/models.py adds 'graph-stop' and 'yolo-all' to the AdminAction literal; api/services/infra.py dispatches graph-stop → docker_stop_service(target) (reusing the request's graph field) and yolo-all → YoloRunner().run() (summarizing steps/failed/needs_input), both streamed through the existing log-forwarding SSE wrapper. The settings InfraActions panel gains a danger-styled graph 'Stop' button (uses the graph selector) and a 'yolo-all (full pipeline)' button. 5 new stubbed backend tests (35 api total, all green). Validated live: both buttons render in settings and the admin SSE path streams '✓ graph-health completed' end to end (destructive graph-stop/yolo-all intentionally not executed against the live stack).
why: User asked to incorporate every main.py capability; graph-stop and yolo-all were the only CLI modes not yet exposed in the app.

summary: Pipeline Visibility (6/6): docs + full regression + merge. docs/structure.md now describes the multi-turn chat, the full Trace/Evidence/Raw-JSON+event-stream inspector surfaces, and the completed admin coverage (graph-stop, yolo-all) on POST /api/admin. Full regression green in the worktree: 35 api tests, 23 web tests, npm lint + build, and a clean app.py dual-launch (proxied query → answered, exit 0). Merged the full-pipeline-visibility worktree into main (commit only, not pushed per the session override).
why: The workbench now does everything main.py can — full chat, full trace, full evidence, raw JSON end to end — so the canonical docs must reflect it and the feature is merged.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (1/5): independent raw recount oracle. New utils/graph_loader/fixture_qa package with raw_counts.py that recounts ATT&CK node labels straight from the raw STIX bundle and CAPEC AttackPattern/Category/View from the raw XML, deliberately NOT reusing the build preprocessors so a systematic build drop is catchable. Tracks excluded revoked/deprecated (ATT&CK) and retired-status patterns (CAPEC). 5 unit tests over synthetic fixtures, all green; validated against real data (ATT&CK 2611 nodes, 157 revoked + 251 deprecated; CAPEC 615/78/13).
why: Existing --graph verify only compares live DB against the build manifest; there was no independent raw->manifest reconciliation, which is the highest-value fixture-QA check per the BRON/GraphKer findings.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (2/5): live referential-integrity store methods. Added ReferentialIntegrityResult to models and a referential_integrity() method to the GraphStore contract, implemented for Neo4j (Cypher dangling/id-less queries), Gremlin (traversal for id-less vertices and edges with id-less endpoints), and the in-memory test store. 3 new tests plus the store-contract suite green; validated live: both running graphs report 0 dangling edges and 0 id-less nodes.
why: The harness must query the live graph for dangling edges (referential integrity), and backend-specific traversal belongs in the store layer so the harness stays backend-agnostic.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (3/5): fixture-QA harness + CLI. New utils/graph_loader/fixture_qa/harness.py reconciles raw==manifest==live for a dataset (three-way node counts over raw-derivable labels, manifest-vs-live counts, live referential integrity, and revoked/deprecated handling), writes data/graphs/<ds>/runtime/fixture-qa-report.json, and raises on failure. Wired as `uv run main.py --graph fixture-qa --dataset <ds>` (added to GRAPH_ACTIONS + main dispatch + help). While writing the injected-store tests, caught and fixed a real bug: the report's errors list was computed but never assigned to FixtureQAReport, so failures surfaced with no detail. 12 fixture_qa tests green; ran live against both graphs: attack 5/5 checks pass, capec 4/4 pass.
why: Codifies the ad-hoc planning checks into a repeatable, auditable gate that independently reconciles the raw MITRE sources against the build manifest and the live graph — the report's highest-value fixture-QA item.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (4/5): pinned data snapshot via sha256. The downloader now records sha256+size for each raw source into metadata.json and a new checksums block in versions.json, plus a `pin_snapshot()` backfill and `uv run main.py --pin` to pin files already on disk without re-downloading. New utils/kg_builder/snapshot.py verifies a raw file against its pin and is called at the top of build_attack/build_capec (fail-fast on drift); source-card provenance now carries raw_sha256 + snapshot_pinned. Pinned the live snapshot: ATT&CK v19.0 sha256 df520ea0..., CAPEC v3.9 sha256 70279a2d... (both cross-checked against sha256sum). 10 new tests; full kg_builder + download suites green (86).
why: Gold REF answers are computed against a specific data state; a recorded checksum makes every build reproducible and blocks silent MITRE upstream drift (e.g. v19.1) from shifting evaluation scores — the auditability the proposal promises ReliaQuest.

summary: Fixture-QA & Snapshot (5/5): docs, full regression, merge. docs/structure.md gains a 'Fixture QA and snapshot pinning' section plus utility-table and finding-things rows; README roadmap records the fixture-QA harness + pinned snapshot and updates the ITS check-in note. summary: Composite Keys & Orphans (2/6): graph-wide identity constraints + constraint introspection. constraints_cypher_lines now emits attack_stix_id_unique (AttackObject.id IS UNIQUE — the STIX UUID backstop) and attack_id_type_unique ((attack_id, stix_type) IS UNIQUE — the composite join key that allows legitimate cross-type ID reuse while forbidding true duplicates), plus a capec_object_id_unique parity constraint on CapecObject. GraphStore gained list_constraint_names() (Neo4j SHOW CONSTRAINTS, Gremlin default empty, memory parses the artifact for tests). Rebuilt both datasets, reloaded live graphs; verified all 13 constraints live on Neo4j 5.26 Community including the composite. Fixture-qa passes attack 5/5, capec 4/4; 178 tests green. Note: an errant attack-into-gremlin load during validation was reverted by restarting the in-memory Gremlin container and reloading capec.
why: Step 3 identity contract: an ATT&CK ID alone is not unique across STIX types (224 raw collisions), so the database must enforce the (attack_id, stix_type) pair mechanically; introspection lets the harness detect a silently missing constraint.

summary: Step 5 Golden Evalset (1/5): gold-bank materialization. New utils/specialists/evalset/gold_bank.py parses the pinned raw snapshot directly (ATT&CK v19 STIX bundle + CAPEC 3.9 XML, deliberately independent of kg_builder) into utils/specialists/tests/golden/gold_bank.json: technique→mitigations, group→techniques, tactic→techniques (kill-chain derived), object lookups incl. Campaigns, sub-technique maps, CAPEC pattern fields, declared-nature hierarchy + inverse children map, CWE links, ATT&CK taxonomy mappings, deprecated list.
