summary: Composite Keys & Orphans (3/6): composite-key checks in fixture-qa. New utils/graph_loader/fixture_qa/composite_keys.py enumerates the attack_id collision set independently from the raw bundle (all objects, jq-equivalent) and from the canonical artifact, compares both exactly against a checked-in expected fixture (expected/attack_collisions.json: 224 raw collisions, all attack-pattern+course-of-action; 0 canonical), asserts every canonical node carries id/attack_id/stix_type, that no (attack_id, stix_type) pair is duplicated, and that the live Neo4j exposes attack_stix_id_unique + attack_id_type_unique (via the new list_constraint_names). 5 new harness tests (14 fixture_qa total, incl. collision-drift and missing-constraint regressions); live fixture-qa attack now 9/9 checks, capec 4/4; 180 tests green.
why: Step 3 A.3/A.4: the collision set becomes a regression fixture and the harness fails loudly if a new collision creeps in, a constraint silently disappears, or an identity property goes missing.

summary: Step 5 Golden Evalset (2/5): compiled machine-checkable question banks. utils/specialists/evalset/questions.py + compile_banks.py compile 45 single-source questions (24 ATT&CK / 21 CAPEC) into tests/golden/{attack,capec}_questions.json — every entry is a full SpecialistTask payload + ID-set assertions with gold resolved from the bank at compile time, incl. Campaign coverage (C0027/C0001), the v19 TA0112 tactic, and negatives (T9999, G9999, CAPEC-99999, CAPEC-116 no-mapping, deprecated CAPEC-557 status). GremlinQueryBuilder now routes declared-direction ChildOf/CanPrecede neighbour traversals. 64 evalset tests green (routing per entry, param-only seeds, staleness guards); 93 existing specialist tests still green. Findings recorded: Group/Tactic name-lookups unroutable; CAPEC Typical_Severity/Likelihood not ingested into the graph.
why: Bank entries must route to the exact builder template they claim to exercise and carry only snapshot-derived gold, so drift between bank, builder, and gold fails in milliseconds without a database.

summary: Composite Keys & Orphans (4/6): orphan/island resolution for both graphs. Fixed a real CAPEC Cause-B bug: normalize_view read a nonexistent Member_Of element so zero IN_VIEW edges ever materialized (all 13 Views stranded); it now parses Members/Has_Member and the graph pass resolves each member against category vs attack-pattern ID sets (67 IN_VIEW edges; 9 remaining orphan Views are all Type=Implicit filter views, declared not-traversable). New fixture_qa/orphans.py splits orphans dead-vs-live against the recorded policy (attack exclude-at-load: 0 dead; capec load-and-tag: 54 deprecated AttackPatterns + 55 Categories), exact-matches live orphans to checked-in allow-lists (attack: the 8 unreferenced DataComponents; capec: 9 implicit views by id + 52 uncited ExternalReferences by label count), asserts the named regressions (Matrix->15 Tactics, every live DataComponent connected), and checks ChildOf endpoint labels + DAG acyclicity. GraphStore gained orphan_ids() (Neo4j/Gremlin/memory) and the harness compares live orphan sets to the canonical scan exactly. Live: attack 14/14, capec 9/9 checks; 185 tests green.
why: Step 4: every disconnected node must be correctly connected, correctly filtered, or explicitly declared unreachable — and the exact-match allow-list means a fixed orphan that stays listed fails as loudly as a new one.

summary: Step 5 Golden Evalset (3/5): AI-verified gold bank + a real cross-layer bug fixed. A 90-agent verification workflow re-derived all 45 golden claims from the raw snapshot (two independent verifiers per claim: jq/grep vs self-written Python, both barred from reading the code under audit) — 90/90 verdicts agree, zero discrepancies; report at utils/specialists/tests/golden/VERIFICATION.md. The suite also caught a live contract bug: the Gremlin loader stores edge labels SCREAMING_SNAKE (CHILD_OF) while the source card declares CAPEC vocabulary (ChildOf), so hierarchy traversals ran clean and returned zero rows. Fix: public gremlin_edge_label() on the loader; the specialist builder emits and the validator matches through it, and the gate now rejects card-vocabulary edge labels outright (new regression test). Golden capec suite 21/21 live; 179 specialist tests green.
why: The user cannot domain-review security gold answers; two-way independent re-derivation substitutes for that review, and the zero-row hierarchy failure is precisely the silent-wrong-answer class Step 5 exists to catch.

summary: Composite Keys & Orphans (5/6): cross-database join-key resolution. New fixture_qa/cross_db.py resolves every CAPEC ATTACK taxonomy mapping against the ATT&CK canonical under the composite pair (attack_id, stix_type=attack-pattern) — never digits alone — and exact-matches the result to a checked-in baseline (expected/capec_attack_resolution.json: 179/189 unique technique ids resolve, rate 0.9471; the 10 legitimate misses are the revoked-in-v19 T1562 family and the Mobile-only T1513). The named CAPEC-555 regression asserts the mapping resolves to exactly T1021/T1114.002/T1133. Wired into fixture-qa for capec (runs when the attack canonical is present); capec now 11/11 checks live; 2 new test modules (21 fixture_qa tests); full builder/loader suites green.
why: Part C: this is where the composite key earns its keep across databases — a resolution-rate drop between builds is a drift alarm, and the CAPEC-555 assertion catches mapping-direction inversion bugs.

summary: Step 5 Golden Evalset (4/5): golden live suites green. New tests/golden_runner.py (backend-agnostic id normalization, id-pool assertions, trace checks with honest-empty handling) + test_golden_attack.py / test_golden_capec.py parameterize every bank entry through the real specialists against the live stack. Live result: attack 24/24, capec 21/21 — all 45 golden questions answer correctly (ID-set assertions, exact names, Abstraction/Status properties, bounded scans, honest empties). Full regression 549 passed / 1 skipped across utils/ + api/.
why: The golden suites measure answer correctness, not just query success — the layer that catches the confident-but-wrong 97% class before Step 6 builds on it.

summary: Composite Keys & Orphans (6/6): source-card identity contract, docs, full regression. Source cards gain an identity block — auto-generated base (join_key [attack_id, stix_type] / [capec_id], unique backstop id, constraint names, measured canonical collision set) merged with a hand-authored overlay policy (join-on-both-fields rule, exclude-at-load vs load-and-tag statements, declared not-traversable types: 8 ATT&CK DataComponents, 9 implicit CAPEC views, 52 uncited ExternalReferences). docs/structure.md documents the composite-key, orphan, and cross-DB checks and the new verified state (attack 4369/27669, 14 checks; capec 4888/6984, 11 checks). Full regression green: 439 passed / 1 skipped across utils/ + api/; final live fixture-qa passes both datasets.
why: The source card is the contract the planner and synthesis agents read; the identity policy and declared dead-ends must live there, and canonical docs must reflect the new fixture-layer guarantees before merging.

summary: Step 5 Golden Evalset (5/5): docs + merge. docs/structure.md documents the evalset package (snapshot-derived gold bank, compiled question banks, 90-agent verification report), the golden live suites and runner semantics, and the gremlin_edge_label() convention contract. Full regression re-run green (549 passed / 1 skipped incl. 45/45 golden live). Merging worktree-step5-golden-evalset into main (commit-only session: not pushed).
why: Canonical docs must describe the evalset layer before it lands; the golden suite is now the Step 5 acceptance gate and the measurement base for Steps 6-7.

summary: Added docs/plans/step6-synthesis-verification-plan.md — the implementation plan for the Step 6 synthesis agent: a new utils/synthesis/ package with a claims-with-citations composer (deterministic always-on, LLM behind SYNTHESIS_LLM_* flags with hybrid fallback), an always-deterministic claim verifier (citation resolution + id-pool grounding + join-index checks; unsupported claims cut from prose and flagged), principled abstention with the executed query as proof on empty-but-ok results, API answer-seam wiring, and a live synthesis golden suite over the 45 Step 5 bank questions measuring unsupported-claim rate.
why: Session directive: plan before building; Step 6 is the layer that catches queries that ran cleanly but do not support the sentence the agent wrote, and abstention is the demonstrable trustworthiness feature.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (1/6): synthesis contracts + deterministic composer. New utils/synthesis/ package: contracts.py (Citation, Claim with entity_ids/kind, Abstention with executed-query proof, ClaimVerdict, VerificationReport with unsupported-claim-rate metrics, SynthesizedAnswer whose rendered_claims() returns nothing until verified and only supported claims after), config.py (SYNTHESIS_LLM_* env vars, LLM off by default), composer.py (DeterministicComposer: one cited fact claim per non-empty result, correlation claims from the cross-source join index, abstentions for empty-but-ok results, notes for failures/unsupported/skipped). 17 hermetic tests using real EvidenceRecord/FederatedEvidence fixtures.
why: The claims-with-citations structure is what makes Step 6 verification mechanical: every sentence carries the record pointers and entity ids the verifier will check, and an answer cannot render prose before it proves itself.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (2/6): deterministic claim verifier + abstention enforcement. New utils/synthesis/verifier.py: verify_answer() rules every claim supported/unsupported via four checks (must cite; citations must resolve to actually-retrieved records with id normalization; every asserted entity id must be grounded in the cited records id pool; correlation claims must be backed by the cross-source join index) — unsupported claims are cut from rendered prose and kept flagged. Abstention is enforced deterministically: missing abstentions on empty-but-ok results are derived from evidence with the executed query as proof, wrong query proofs are replaced, and false abstentions over real evidence are removed. Shared id normalization extracted to utils/synthesis/grounding.py (golden_runner now imports it). 17 new adversarial tests (fabricated entity cut, unretrieved-record citation cut, empty-source citation cut, false abstention removed); 126 hermetic tests green.
why: This is the Step 6 core: a deterministic guard the model cannot sweet-talk, catching the query-ran-clean-but-answer-is-wrong class and guaranteeing honest evidence-backed abstention.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (3/6): LLM composer + hybrid factory, all output verifier-gated. New utils/synthesis/llm_composer.py (OpenAICompatibleComposer: temperature-0 JSON claims contract, evidence-only prompt with capped record context and an explicit MUST-abstain list of empty sub-questions, ComposerUnavailable on any transport/HTTP/parse failure) and factory.py (HybridComposer falling back to the deterministic composer with the reason recorded on the answer; synthesize() = compose + mandatory verify_answer as the single entry point). 14 stubbed-HTTP tests including the decisive fabrication-then-cut chain: a model that invents M9999 and omits its abstention ships with the fabricated claim flagged-and-cut and the abstention repaired with the executed query. 48 synthesis tests green.
why: Mirrors the proven planner drafter pattern; the LLM never bypasses the deterministic verifier, which is exactly the Step 6 chain — gates catch bad queries, retries catch visible failures, verification catches clean-but-unsupported prose.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (4/6): synthesis wired into the API answer seam and the CLI. api/services/query.py now runs synthesize() over the federated evidence at the marked seam and attaches the verified answer additively under answer.synthesis (claims with per-claim verdicts, rendered_claims, enforced abstentions with executed-query proof, verification metrics, composer/fallback) while keeping the deterministic headline/sections/cross_source the UI renders today; event order unchanged. utils/specialists/cli.py prints a Synthesized answer (verified) section: supported claims with citations, abstentions with query proof, CUT lines for flagged claims, and the verification roll-up. 2 new API contract tests (verified synthesis shape; honest-empty abstention with query proof); 183 hermetic tests green; live CLI smoke on T1047 shows 2/2 claims supported.
why: The seam api/services/query.py reserved for the synthesis agent now carries a verified answer without breaking the existing web contract — additive fields only, LLM off by default reproduces deterministic semantics.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (5/6): synthesis golden suite green live. New utils/synthesis/tests/test_golden_synthesis.py parameterizes all 45 Step 5 bank questions (24 ATT&CK via live Neo4j Cypher specialist, 21 CAPEC via live Gremlin specialist), bundles each result as FederatedEvidence, synthesizes deterministically, and asserts at the answer layer: unsupported-claim rate 0% on every question, every rendered claim cited, and every expect_empty negative yields exactly one abstention whose query proof equals the executed query with the honest doesnt-establish statement and zero claims. Live: 45/45 passed.
why: This is the Step 6 acceptance gate: the same AI-verified questions that gate the specialists now measure the answer layer — faithfulness, groundedness, and unsupported-claim rate from docs/goals.md become executable checks.

summary: Step 6 Synthesis (6/6): docs + full regression + merge. docs/structure.md documents the utils/synthesis/ package (claims-with-citations composers, always-deterministic verifier with cut/flag semantics, enforced abstention with executed-query proof, synthesize() entry point, shared grounding), the synthesis golden suite as the answer-layer metric gate, and the updated Not Yet in Repo (synthesis agent shipped; UI rendering of answer.synthesis + tables/figures remain). docs/goals.md checks off the Wk 10 synthesis-agent row. Full regression green: 644 passed / 1 skipped across utils/ + api/ including 45/45 specialist golden and 45/45 synthesis golden live. Merging worktree-step6-synthesis into main (commit-only session: not pushed).

summary: Step 7 plan committed: docs/plans/step7-evalset-gaps-plan.md. Six phases plugging the evalset holes — campaign gold maps materialized from the pinned STIX bundle (56 live campaigns confirmed in bundle and graph), new campaign_techniques/campaign_attribution Cypher templates, a schema-boundary refusal in the shared specialist so Asset questions get an honest 'not in this source' instead of a substitute node lookup, a boundary abstention variant in synthesis, AI-verified new gold, and extended golden live suites.

summary: Step 7 Evalset Gaps (1/6): campaign gold maps materialized from the pinned snapshot. gold_bank.py parse_attack_bundle now derives campaign_techniques (live uses edges, campaign->attack-pattern) and campaign_attribution (attributed-to, campaign->intrusion-set) under the same exclude-at-load policy; gold_bank.json regenerated (55 campaigns w/ techniques, 25 w/ attribution). New anchor tests pin the v19 census (56 live Campaigns) and web-verified attributions C0027->G1015, C0028->G0034. 67 evalset tests green including the regeneration-matches-committed discipline check.

summary: Step 7 Evalset Gaps (2/6): campaign query templates + schema-boundary refusal. CypherQueryBuilder gains campaign_techniques (Campaign-USES->Technique) and campaign_attribution (Campaign-ATTRIBUTED_TO->Group) routed ahead of the group branch that would otherwise capture them; CypherNormalizer groups attribution rows into one Campaign record with related groups. QuerySpecialist.run now refuses at the schema boundary: entities the card doesn't model (e.g. Asset, ICS-only) return an honest empty — ok, zero records, NO substitute query — with a boundary trace, instead of silently degrading to node_lookup and answering a different question. 8 new hermetic tests; 215 specialist tests green; live smoke: C0027 techniques, C0028->G0034 attribution, T1047 asset ask refused honestly.

summary: Component Evaluation (1/8): shared statistics scaffold. New utils/evaluation/ package with stats.py — pure-Python percentile (type-7 linear interpolation, matching numpy's default; mean deliberately omitted since latency is right-skewed), Wilson binomial score interval (stays in [0,1] and behaves at the x==n ceiling where the deterministic query builder lives), and a seeded percentile-bootstrap CI (byte-reproducible). 14 hermetic tests in utils/evaluation/tests/test_stats.py assert known-input percentiles (1..100 -> p50=50.5/p95=95.05/p99=99.01), Wilson symmetry/ceiling/point-containment, and bootstrap determinism.
why: Every downstream component metric (VA/EX pass rates, latency percentiles) needs the same CI/percentile math; building it once as a pure hermetic module keeps every scorer consistent and testable before any live data is involved.

summary: Component Evaluation (2/8): planner sub-question-quality sub-score + dev/holdout reporting + drafter selector. scorer.py now measures decomposition beyond entity recall — count_correct (right number of sub-questions, defaulting to one per expected source), routing_correct (each sub-question routed to an expected source and every expected source covered), and dependency_correct (join declared iff the question is multi-hop) — combined into decomposition_score and a composite sub_question_quality; aggregate() adds mean_sub_question_quality/decomposition and routing/count/dependency accuracy rates. corpus.py gains an optional expected_sub_question_count override. run_eval.py adds a --drafter deterministic|llm|hybrid selector (LLM best-effort via the config factory, falls back to deterministic and reports which ran) and a dev-vs-holdout breakdown. 7 new tests; planner suite 97/97; corpus still 7/7 pass_rate 1.0.
why: 'Sub-question quality' needs the decomposition check (count/routing/dependency) the proposal names, not just entity recall; adding it before corpus expansion means the new cases are scored on the complete metric set, and scoring both drafters is the honest deterministic-floor + LLM-lift presentation.

why: These 40 are the catalogue entries that measure the join itself — cross-source answer accuracy and CAPEC-to-ATT&CK mapping recall cannot be scored without them.

summary: QA Catalogue Expansion (5/7): two-verifier AI re-derivation of all Step 10 gold. The 67 new entries were expressed as 93 machine-checkable claims (detection chains, software sets, hierarchy, tactic-x-mitigation intersections, DC analytics, retired-id exclusions, CAPEC execution flows/skills/consequences, abstraction chains, CWE bridges, every federated must_correlate intersection with its mitigation/tactic unions and reverse-pattern sets, and the no-mapping negatives). VERIFICATION.md extended with the protocol and census.
why: The established substitute for hand domain-review at scale: no gold answer ships unless two independent derivations from the raw snapshot agree with it exactly.

summary: Component Evaluation (3/8): planner corpus expanded 7 -> 31 (24 generated + 7 curated), snapshot-derived. New build_corpus.py derives single-source expected plans from the specialist golden banks: a candidate is kept only when the deterministic planner selects the gold source (source-recall==1.0) and the plan is schema-adherent, capped at 3 per builder-template, with every excluded question reported (9 unroutable bare lookups, 8 adversarial, 12 template-cap) — no silent drops. Cases carry origin (curated|generated) and tier; a deterministic quarter is frozen into holdout. Corpus-wide hard guarantees hold (source_recall/schema/honesty == 1.0); the honest measurement picture surfaces real findings — precision 0.887 (7 unnecessary source calls from mitigation/mapping over-routing), pass_rate 0.774. Regression tests split: strict pass on the 7 curated anchors, hard-guarantee + reproducibility checks on the generated set (skip when data cards unbuilt). Planner suite 99/99.
why: A 7-case corpus is too small to be statistically defensible for source-selection scoring; deriving from the specialist banks makes the planner and specialists answer the same catalogue and turns the planner's real routing imprecision into reported, diagnosable metrics.

summary: QA Catalogue Expansion (6/7): live federated golden runner. New utils/specialists/tests/test_golden_federated.py assembles each of the 40 federated bank entries into a real planner Plan (sub-questions + a JoinDeclaration when sequenced) and drives the committed federation path — SpecialistRouter dependency sequencing, join harvesting, bundle_evidence — then deterministic synthesis. Asserts per entry: live cross-source join values EQUAL the snapshot-computed must_correlate set (never fabricated: expect_no_correlation entries must yield zero), per-side golden-runner assertion blocks plus the federated-only expect_dependency_skip/expect_skipped vocabulary, exactly-one sequencing audit row with seed counts for sequenced positives, honest double abstention for negatives (producer keeps its executed-query proof, consumer carries none), and partial degradation with the answerable side intact (boundary, attack-down, capec-down staged via specialist injection). Skips cleanly unless BOTH backends are live. All golden layers green live: 46 attack + 34 capec + 40 federated + 7 acceptance + 80 synthesis = 207, first full run.
why: The catalogue is only a ruler if the live system can be held against it; this is the layer that measures the join itself, not just the sides.

summary: Component Evaluation (4/8): hermetic Query Validity (VA) scorer. New utils/specialists/evalset/score_validity.py drives each specialist's own builder+validator through the same resolve->draft->gate retry loop as base.py but stops before any DB call, so VA (the grammar / valid-accuracy metric) is fully hermetic and reproducible. Reports first-pass VA and post-retry VA per specialist per tier with Wilson CIs; schema-boundary questions (no query drafted) are reported separately, never in the denominator. Result confirms the design: attack 30/30 and capec 21/21 first-pass VA (100%, 2 Asset boundaries excluded) — the deterministic builder never free-generates, so VA sits at the ceiling and any later EX miss points at routing/seeds, not malformed queries. 5 hermetic tests.
why: VA is the community-standard syntactic-validity metric; because the gate runs before the database, VA is measurable without live infra, and near-ceiling VA is the evidence that Ariadne sidesteps the generation-hallucination failure mode of free-form text-to-query systems.

summary: Component Evaluation (5/8): snapshot-derived EX gold + Execution Accuracy scorer + error taxonomy. questions.py now attaches an ex_gold block (full expected id set + the id surface to compare: node=the looked-up node, neighbors=id_pool minus the seed inputs, join=T-prefixed ATTACK join values only) derived from the gold bank; technique-fanout gold is the top-level Technique slice (matching the builder's sub-technique roll-up) so a correct answer is not penalised. New score_execution.py runs each bank question live and reports exact-set-match EX and precision/recall/F1 with Wilson CIs, bucketing every miss (missing_hop/over_broad/mismatch/empty_when_nonempty/fabricated_nonempty/boundary_failure/cardinality). Live result: attack 32/32 and capec 21/21 exact-match, precision 1.0, empty taxonomy — the deterministic specialists reproduce the independently-parsed snapshot, which also confirms ingestion faithfulness. score_validity.build_specialists now loads .env so the live path connects. 9 tests (hermetic taxonomy/pool + live EX); evalset+golden 140/140.
why: EX (result-set correctness, phrasing-invariant) is the community-standard text-to-query metric; partial credit + a taxonomy turn the pass/fail banks into diagnosable findings, and comparing the live graph to independently-derived gold doubles as an ingest-faithfulness check.

summary: Component Evaluation (6/8): bounded-execution safety-adherence audit + adversarial gate probes. New score_safety.py independently audits every gate-accepted query for read-only + LIMIT-present-and-<=cap + no unbounded/over-depth traversal (adherence 30/30 attack, 21/21 capec, zero breaches), and fires hand-crafted adversarial drafts (writes, DETACH DELETE, CALL{}, LOAD CSV, unbounded/over-depth var-length paths, addV/addE/drop/property, unknown labels) straight at the validator asserting a 100% block rate. The unknown-label probe surfaced a real gate gap: the Gremlin validator's hasLabel/out/in/both regexes matched only double-quoted labels, so a single-quoted unknown label (g.V().hasLabel('Secret')) bypassed schema conformance; hardened the four regexes to accept both quote styles. Now 10/10 and 7/7 probes blocked, no leaks. New fixtures/adversarial_probes.py; 6 hermetic tests; full specialist suite 290/290.
why: Safety-constraint adherence is named in the proposal but never scored; the gate is the enforcement point, so auditing accepted queries and probing it with malicious drafts is the honest hermetic test — and the probe did its job, finding and fixing a single-quote schema-validation bypass before it could matter.

summary: Component Evaluation (7/8): per-stage timing hooks + segmented latency harness. base.py now additively records timing_ms on the gate/assess/normalize trace steps (execute already had it) — no behavioural change. New latency.py repeat-runs the catalogue to n>=200 per specialist, discards the warm-up repetition, and reports p50/p95/p99 with bootstrap CIs plus the p50/p99 gap, segmented by specialist and tier and cold-vs-warm, and broken down by draft+gate/execute/assess/normalize stage. Live run: attack p50=1.06ms/p99=4.42ms, capec p50=2.38ms/p99=7.51ms (Gremlin ~2x Neo4j, as expected for a different engine), execute-dominated with a negligible deterministic gate, cold-start slightly above warm — the whole 434-sample sweep in ~3s. 4 tests (hermetic clock-injected shaping + live shape); specialists+api 339/339.
why: Latency is right-skewed so the mean misleads; percentiles segmented and staged point at which stage/segment is slow, and the stage timing had to exist on the trace before the harness could attribute a tail. The hooks also feed the coming report without re-instrumenting.

summary: Step 11 (2/7): end-to-end pipeline scorer utils/evaluation/score_e2e.py. Mirrored SynthesisEdge in the payload type (ServerSynthesis.edges) and added SynthesisGraphEdge to the SynthesisView projection; web/lib/adapt.ts maps source_id/target_id/rel -> source/target/rel. deriveEdges gained an explicit-mode branch behind the same seam: when the payload carries edges it uses them verbatim and skips all inference, otherwise it falls back to Option-A inference. AnswerNetworkPlot relabels 'derived' -> 'provenance-exact' and swaps its caption when exact edges are present (isProvenanceExact). Fixture now carries explicit edges. 5 new web tests (explicit vs fallback, rel passthrough, adapter projection); 96 web tests green, lint + build clean.
why: Completes A->B: the only thing that changed from the inferred plot is the edge source, exactly as the seam was designed for — component, nodes, table, and renderer untouched.

summary: Analyst Tables & Network Plot (6/6): docs. structure.md 'Not Yet in Repo' rewritten — Deliverable #4 (analyst-facing table + compact CAPEC-ATT&CK-mitigation network plot) is delivered, with the provenance-exact-vs-derived edge distinction documented and remaining polish (richer figures, exact technique->mitigation edges) noted. goals.md Wk-10 row updated from 'tables/figures/diagrams remain UI work' to delivered. Full backend regression green (1001 passed / 1 skipped, live goldens included); 96 web tests + lint + build green.
why: The docs advertised the deliverable as unbuilt; they must reflect that the table and network plot now ship, and stay honest about what remains.

summary: Answer UX backend: synthesis now emits a natural-language 'narrative' final answer (LLM composer writes final_answer; deterministic composer assembles it from grounded claim sentences), and the LLM drafter toggle now governs synthesis (llm_enabled=use_llm) so the LLM is used throughout when selected. Added /api/health 'llm' field (LlmHealth reachability probe of the synthesis endpoint) for a header LLM Live/Dead pill.
why: The workbench showed only a mechanical headline and never surfaced an actual LLM answer, the synthesis LLM was never engaged from the UI, and analysts had no signal for whether the LLM endpoint was reachable.

summary: Answer-card UX: sections (Retrieved evidence, Verified answer, Claim table, Network plot) are now collapsible disclosures with counts, closed by default, while a new open 'Final answer' shows the synthesis narrative first. New CollapsibleSection component. Rewrote the network-plot caption in plain English and dropped the jargon 'provenance-exact/derived' badge and the '⇢ sequenced' note. Copy now confirms 'Copied ✓' and Export downloads the evidence JSON with 'Exported ✓'. Added an LLM Live/Dead header pill fed by /api/health.llm next to Neo4j/Gremlin.
why: Analysts asked for a cleaner, scannable answer card, a real natural-language final answer, plain-English plot text, working Copy/Export buttons, and an at-a-glance LLM reachability signal.

summary: Real natural-language final answer: added a dedicated LLM 'narrator' (utils/synthesis/narrator.py) that writes a short prose answer to the question from the evidence, wired best-effort into synthesize() when the LLM is enabled. This is reliable where the full claims-JSON LLM call truncates on large evidence (gemma emits hidden reasoning tokens, so max_tokens raised 4096→8192). Rewrote the deterministic fallback narrative to collapse the many 'X is corroborated…' sentences into one readable summary. Made the network plot always-open (non-collapsible) and defaulted the composer drafter to LLM so the natural-language answer shows by default.
why: The 'Final answer' was an unreadable wall of repeated deterministic sentences and the LLM path silently fell back on large queries; analysts need an actual explaining-and-answering natural-language response, the plot visible by default, and the LLM answer surfaced without hunting for a toggle.

summary: synthesize() now composes claims deterministically always (grounded, fast) and uses the LLM solely for the prose narrative via the narrator. This drops the doomed full-claims LLM call that generated ~8k tokens before failing on large evidence, cutting LLM-drafter latency and eliminating the spurious 'LLM composer unavailable' fallback while keeping the great natural-language answer. Fabrication-cut safety is still covered by testing the LLM composer + verifier directly.
why: The hybrid claims LLM call always truncated on large evidence, wasting time and mislabeling the result as a fallback; claims are grounded by construction so deterministic composition is both faster and equally correct, leaving the LLM to do what it's good at — the prose answer.

summary: Reworked the answer card from stacked drop-downs into a tabbed container: Evidence, Verified Answers, Claim Table, Network Plot, Logs. One panel open at a time; clicking the active tab collapses to just the thin tab strip; Network Plot opens by default (first meaningful tab when it's absent). Tabs appear progressively as data is extracted. Replaced the static loading skeleton with a live phase status ('Probing the live graphs', 'Planning the route', 'Extracting evidence…', 'Reasoning over the evidence') with a pulsing indicator and advancing progress bar. Per-stage timings now render in seconds (26.2s, 1.3s, 0.05s) right-justified next to Copy/Export.
why: The analyst asked for a tabbed layout that collapses to a single strip, a network plot open by default, a live 'what is it doing now' status instead of a blank loader, and step timings in seconds by the actions.

summary: Fixed the live answer status appearing stuck on the first phase: the run machine now rebuilds the streaming turn on every 'status' SSE event, so the label advances the instant a phase is announced (Planning during the ~12s planner LLM, Reasoning during the ~20s narrator) instead of lagging behind the slow step. Redesigned the answer-card tabs to look like an obvious tab bar — leading icons per section (Evidence/Verified/Claim/Network/Logs), tinted active tab with a teal underline on a baseline hairline.
why: The status sat on 'Probing the live graphs' for 25-30s because status events never triggered a re-render, and the pill-style tabs didn't read as tabs; the analyst asked for a live phase readout and obvious, iconographic tabs.

summary: Authored docs/plans/langgraph-orchestration-migration-plan.md: an 8-step plan converting the custom iter_pipeline orchestrator into a LangGraph agent-driven workflow (shared PipelineState, planner/specialists/synthesis as subgraphs, custom-event streaming preserving the exact SSE contract, consumer cutover, langgraph.json, and byte-identical e2e baseline regeneration as the equivalence proof). Plan only — no implementation.
why: The user asked for a robust migration plan to replace the hand-rolled probe→plan→specialists→bundle→synthesize generator with a real LangGraph StateGraph while keeping the ~1,035-test regression suite, web SSE contract, and committed evaluation baseline intact.

summary: Expanded the LangGraph migration plan from 8 to 9 steps: new Step 8 overhauls app.py into a preflighted launcher (utils/launcher/ package: dependency/port/source-card/Neo4j/Gremlin/LLM checks plus a LangGraph compile check, readiness-gated startup, prefixed ANSI child-log streaming, a subsystem status board, and a post-ready SSE smoke query), and Step 9 now requires a cold-start first-boot acceptance run in dev and --prod. Deliverables table gains the launcher modules and their hermetic tests.
why: The user flagged that the plan must overhaul app.py and how it displays information — the launcher is the works-the-first-time gate, so every failure mode must be caught, named, and remediated at boot instead of on the analyst's first query.

summary: LangGraph Migration (1/9): added langgraph>=1.0 (resolved 1.2.8) and langchain-core to pyproject and scaffolded utils/orchestration/ (OrchestrationConfig with ORCH_CHECKPOINTER/ORCH_RECURSION_LIMIT env knobs, agents/{planner,specialists,synthesis} subpackages, tests). Documented the ORCH_* block and the previously undocumented PIPELINE_TIMEOUT_S in .env.example. Note: langgraph-sdk pins websockets 15.x (down from 16) — full 1051-test regression green including live gremlin goldens, so gremlinpython is unaffected.
why: Foundation step of the LangGraph migration plan: prove the dependency resolves on Python 3.13 and perturbs nothing before any orchestration code exists.

summary: LangGraph Migration (2/9): shared graph state schemas in utils/orchestration/state.py — PipelineState (super-graph; specialist results/skips/sequencing/timings accumulate via operator.add reducers, timings/by_id merge via merge_dicts), PlanningState (draft-gate loop; trace accumulates, feedback overwrites), SynthesisState (compose-narrate-verify). All wrap the existing frozen contracts (Plan, SpecialistResult, FederatedEvidence, SynthesizedAnswer) untouched. 4 new tests round-trip real contract objects through compiled StateGraphs and prove delta-accumulation; full 1055-test regression green.
why: State is the LangGraph seam everything else builds on; wrapping the existing contracts instead of redefining them keeps the 98 test modules and SSE to_dict() JSON contracts stable.

summary: LangGraph Migration (3/9): the planner draft→gate→revise/degrade loop now runs as a LangGraph subgraph (utils/orchestration/agents/planner/{nodes,graph}.py) — draft and gate nodes wrap the configured PlanDrafter and the deterministic gate, a conditional edge feeds rejection reasons back or degrades at the iteration cap. Degradation logic extracted to utils/planner/degrade.py (shared by the node and the compat _degrade method, avoiding a circular import). PlanningAgent keeps its exact signature, trace format, and max_iterations<=0 defensive path; all 12 planner loop tests green unmodified plus 3 new subgraph tests.
why: The bounded self-evaluating ReAct loop is exactly LangGraph's conditional-loop idiom; converting it first proves the facade-over-subgraph pattern the rest of the migration reuses.

summary: LangGraph Migration (4/9): specialist execution as a LangGraph subgraph (utils/orchestration/agents/specialists/{nodes,graph}.py) — a deliberate sequential conditional-edge cycle over execution_order (not a Send fan-out, preserving deterministic ordering) with producer→consumer seed harvesting, dependency skips (failed/empty/never-run producer), honest deadline skips, per-specialist timings, and specialist-start/specialist/skipped events emitted via get_stream_writer before each blocking call. 6 new hermetic subgraph tests (order, seeding, three skip modes, event order); full 1064-test regression green.
why: The highest-risk stage of the migration: the sequencing/seeding/skip semantics are analyst-facing honesty guarantees pinned by golden tests, so they move into graph nodes verbatim rather than being reinterpreted.

summary: LangGraph Migration (5/9): synthesis as a LangGraph subgraph (utils/orchestration/agents/synthesis/{nodes,graph}.py) — an unconditional compose→verify→narrate chain preserving the real synthesize() order (verification gates claims BEFORE the best-effort LLM narrator rewrites prose). synthesize() delegates to the compiled graph; _apply_llm_narrative made public as apply_llm_narrative for the narrate node. 4 new tests (verifier-always-runs with a stub composer, LLM-off no-op narrator, unreachable-narrator fallback reason, facade≡graph byte equality); all 146 existing synthesis tests green unmodified, full 1068-test regression green.
why: Making verify an unconditional edge encodes the 'verifier is not optional' invariant structurally; note the plan drafted this as compose→narrate→verify but the shipped order is compose→verify→narrate to stay byte-identical with current behavior.

summary: LangGraph Migration (6/9): the cutover. utils/orchestration/main.py wires the super-graph (check_cards → probe → plan → mode-conditional → announce_querying → specialists subgraph → bundle → synthesize) emitting the exact status/probe/plan/skipped/specialist-start/specialist/evidence/answer/done vocabulary via get_stream_writer; iter_pipeline is now a thin adapter draining graph.stream(stream_mode=custom, subgraphs=True) — subgraph events do NOT bubble without subgraphs=True, discovered empirically. PipelineRun/pipeline_timeout_s moved to orchestration.main; utils/specialists/pipeline.py is a re-export shim. The caller-owned PipelineRun rides in graph state and is mutated at the same boundaries (SSE reads run.timings mid-stream). 6 new golden event-parity tests (query/plan/no-cards/dependency-skip/timeout sequences + payload key sets + mid-stream timings); test_pipeline.py and api/tests green UNMODIFIED; full 1074-test regression green; live federated query verified: answered/exit 0, 20 claims, 18 cross-source joins.
why: This is the moment LangGraph becomes the real orchestrator; the event stream is a load-bearing public contract so parity is pinned by dedicated goldens rather than assumed.

summary: LangGraph Migration (7/9): consumers cut over — api/services/query.py and utils/specialists/cli.py import iter_pipeline/PipelineRun from utils.orchestration.main (utils/specialists/pipeline.py stays a documented re-export shim). Added langgraph.json + utils/orchestration/studio.py so langgraph dev can inspect the super-graph; ORCH_CHECKPOINTER=true now compiles with InMemorySaver and a per-run thread_id (smoke-tested). New Orchestration config group (checkpointer/recursion_limit/pipeline_timeout_s) exposed through GET/PUT /api/config (OrchestrationGroup/OrchestrationUpdate models) and an Orchestration (LangGraph) section in the web settings modal. Full 1074-test backend regression, api contract tests, web lint+98 vitest+production build all green; verified live over HTTP: /api/config serves the group through the proxy and one SSE query streams the exact golden event sequence.
why: Makes utils/orchestration the single canonical composition, gives the team the visual graph debugger, and closes the gap where the new orchestration knobs could not be edited from the settings UI.

summary: Graph Search Toolbar (1/3): web/lib/graph.ts gains field-scoped search and N-hop neighborhood expansion. nodeMatchesQuery now honors a SearchField set (name/id/description/label; type gates the edge-type seeding in toForceGraphData), and a new pure expandByHops BFS grows the matched node set outward by up to N undirected hops without crossing hidden edge types or revealing hidden-label nodes. Defaults (all fields, 0 hops) reproduce the previous output exactly. 21 new Vitest cases; 159 web tests green.
why: The analyst wants the Graph Explorer search to be scoped to specific portions of a node (title vs description vs id) and to reveal everything within N jumps of a match (e.g. all nodes two away from 'fishing'), so the matching logic lands first as pure tested functions.

summary: Graph Search Toolbar (2/3): the Graph Explorer search is now one toolbar line — a Jumps selector on the far left (Matches only / Within 1-3 jumps), an 'In' field-scope dropdown with checkboxes (Name/ID/Description/Label/Edge type, at least one always on), the search input + button, and the dataset's node/edge counts right-aligned on the same line. GraphSecondaryNav keeps only the dataset tabs (counts moved), and GraphExplorer persists hops+fields per dataset alongside the existing query/filter state. Tests (159), lint, and the Next production build all green.
why: The analyst asked for the search to share a line with the node/edge counts, a left-side jumps control to reveal everything within N hops of a match (e.g. two away from 'fishing'), and a way to point the search at titles vs descriptions vs ids.

summary: Graph Search Toolbar (3/3): live-verified and merged. Against the running stack (fallback ports 16600/16601; defaults held by a concurrent session) the real 4,369-node ATT&CK payload was pulled through the web proxy and driven through the new logic — 'phishing' neighborhoods grow monotonically at 0/1/2 jumps, name-/description-/id-only scopes narrow correctly, and defaults reproduce the pre-change output id-for-id. Merged worktree-graph-search-toolbar into main; post-merge 159 web tests, lint, and the production build are green.
why: Land the toolbar on main only after proving the jump-expansion and field-scoping behave on real graph data, per the plan's final validation step.

summary: LangGraph Migration (8/9): app.py overhauled into a preflighted, readiness-gated, smoke-verified launcher. New utils/launcher/ package: preflight.py (ordered CheckResults with named remediations — npm, python deps, port conflicts, node_modules, source cards, Neo4j/Gremlin content probes, LLM endpoint, and a LangGraph super-graph compile check), display.py (prefixed [api]/[web] ANSI streaming with error highlighting, TTY/NO_COLOR fallback, and a boxed status board with URLs/orchestrator/data versions/check verdicts), supervise.py (spawn API → poll /api/health → spawn web → poll port → ready; crash reports show the dead child's tail), smoke.py (plan-mode SSE smoke by default, --smoke full for a federated query, --no-smoke to skip). app.py is a thin phase driver that re-execs under uv run when the project env is inactive (guarding against a stray langgraph namespace package that fools bare imports). 23 hermetic launcher tests; manual matrix verified live: occupied ports → named hard fail; dev boot → all-green board + plan smoke OK (then honestly reported the Next 16 single-dev-server conflict with a concurrent session); --prod boot → full federated smoke answered (exit 0), page 200 via proxy, clean port release on SIGINT. Full 1097-test regression green.
why: The launcher is the migration's works-the-first-time gate: every failure mode is caught, named, and remediated at boot — including a LangGraph wiring error — instead of surfacing on the analyst's first browser query.

summary: LangGraph Migration (9/9): final validation + docs. Full 1097-test regression green including the live golden suites against the loaded Docker stack. Regenerated the e2e evaluation (LLM-off): every deterministic section — all four e2e metrics, 120 case verdicts, by-tier tables — byte-identical to the committed baseline (the only diffs were the opt-in LLM judge's own non-reproducible verdict text and the judge-derived diagnosis line, so the committed judge=llm baseline was restored, not clobbered). First-boot acceptance: --prod cold start fully green (preflight → readiness gates → status board → FULL federated smoke answered exit 0 → page 200 via proxy → clean port release on SIGINT); dev mode green through preflight/gates/board/plan-smoke, then correctly detected and reported the Next 16 single-dev-server conflict with a concurrent session (an environment constraint, not a launcher defect). Docs updated: structure.md (utils/orchestration + utils/launcher rows, langgraph.json in the tree, launcher + SSE prose), README (LangGraph in the tech stack, launcher feature bullet, status blurb), global-project-rules repo map.
why: Closes the migration: LangGraph demonstrably orchestrates the same pipeline (byte-identical deterministic evaluation), the launcher proves the stack works the first time from cold, and the docs no longer advertise the old hand-rolled orchestrator.

summary: Launcher display fix: the always-show-errors rule matched the substring 'error' , so Next dev-overlay React tree lines (AppDevOverlayErrorBoundary, NotAllowedRootHTTPFallbackError, RedirectErrorBoundary) leaked through the quiet filter as garbled fragments after startup. Replaced the marker list with a word-boundary regex (\berror\b, TypeError:-style prefixes, exception/traceback/failed/fatal/unhandled tokens, Next's ⨯ glyph) shared by the highlighter and the filter. 2 new regression tests pin the exact leaked lines as non-errors and real error forms as errors; 25 launcher tests green.
why: First real-world dev boot after the launcher overhaul showed component-name false positives spamming the clean output; genuine error headlines still surface while identifier noise is filtered.

summary: Clickable References (1/4): new web/lib/references.ts — tokenizeReferences() splits assistant answer prose into ordered text/reference tokens, detecting CAPEC (CAPEC-###), ATT&CK technique/sub-technique (T####/T####.###), and mitigation (M####) ids with word-boundary guards that reject ST1566/T15660/CAPEC-98x while allowing trailing punctuation. followUpPrompt()/hasReference() helpers included. 12 Vitest cases pin detection, the example sentence's token order, case-insensitivity, boundaries, and an exact round-trip; regex vocabulary mirrors classifyEntity in synthesisGraph.ts.
why: Groundwork for making CAPEC/ATT&CK ids in chat answers clickable follow-ups — isolating the detection as a pure, tested lib function before any React wiring depends on it.

summary: Chat network plot is now inspectable. Clicking a node or an edge opens an in-plot detail panel (reusing the Graph Explorer's themed ElementInspector as an overlay on the plot box) showing the entity's proper name, type, and properties; edges are now selectable (they previously just deselected), and a background click or a close button clears the panel. Subgraph nodes are enriched with real names/descriptions projected from the turn's federated evidence via a new pure buildEntityDetails(federated) lookup threaded through synthesisToGraphPayload, so hover labels and the panel show human titles (e.g. 'Windows Management Instrumentation') instead of bare ids ('T1047'). GraphCanvas gained an optional onBackgroundClick prop (Explorer unaffected). 6 new synthesisGraph unit tests (lookup build, record-over-join precedence, name/property stamping, id fallback, back-compat when details omitted); 118 web tests green, lint clean, npm run build passes.
why: The plot showed only attack-pattern ids with no way to learn what a clicked node actually was; analysts need the real name and details for the thing they select, and edges should be inspectable too.

summary: Clickable References (2/4): composer prefill plumbing. WorkbenchContext exposes setComposerDraft(text) plus an imperative registerComposerFill channel — the Composer registers a fill handler (setQuestion + focus + caret-to-end) on mount and setComposerDraft invokes it, so a click event drives the input without a state-in-effect (satisfies react-hooks/set-state-in-effect). Fills and focuses but never auto-sends; the analyst edits and presses Send. Lint clean, 110 vitest pass.
why: Gives answer-prose reference links a way to seed a follow-up question into the chat box below without lifting composer state or coupling components directly.

summary: Clickable References (3/4): inline ReferenceLink + RefText renderers wired into every assistant-prose surface. ReferenceLink renders an in-text CAPEC/ATT&CK id as a tinted, dotted-underline button that calls setComposerDraft(followUpPrompt(id)); RefText tokenizes a string and swaps ref tokens for links, plain text verbatim. Applied in AnswerCard (final answer, verified-claim sentences, evidence Paragraph text segments) and ClaimTable (claim column); the unused Fragment import dropped. Lint clean, 110 vitest pass, Next 16 production build + TypeScript green.
why: Turns the ids analysts read in answers into one-click follow-up seeds without touching the provenance chips or reading flow — the interactable feature requested.

summary: Clickable References (4/4): validation + merge. Verified against the live stack — a real /api/query answer's narrative and claim prose contained CAPEC-98, T1566, T1598, which tokenizeReferences detects exactly; a headless integration test (throwaway jsdom + testing-library, not committed) mounted WorkbenchProvider+Composer+RefText and confirmed a reference-link click fills the composer with 'Could you provide me more details on CAPEC-98?' and focuses it, re-filling on a second click. Merged main (network-plot inspector) into the feature branch: reconciled the AnswerCard React import (dropped now-unused Fragment, kept useMemo) and interleaved changelog entries. Post-merge: lint clean, 118 vitest, Next 16 build + TypeScript green.
why: Closes the feature: the requested interaction works end-to-end and coexists with the concurrently-landed inspectable network plot on the same AnswerCard surface.

summary: Authored docs/plans/conversational-threads-plan.md: an 11-step plan converting Ariadne's single-shot query tool into a persisted, memory-inclusive, multi-threaded chat. Adds a conversational orchestration layer (Orchestration -> Router -> {memory-grounded Answer | Graph Extraction -> Validation -> Answer}) that wraps the existing planner->specialist->synthesis pipeline as a Graph Extraction subgraph, a stdlib-SQLite thread store under data/, LLM auto-titling, and delete/rename. The existing POST /api/query stays byte-identical; conversational turns ride a new conversation-aware path. Plan only -- no implementation.
why: The analyst asked to turn the one-question/one-answer interface into ChatGPT-style savable threads with full cross-turn memory, and to wrap the current agents in a router/validation/answer layer so follow-ups (e.g. 'tell me more about T1598') resolve from memory and re-query the graphs when needed.

summary: Conversational Threads (1/11): added the stdlib-SQLite ConversationStore (utils/conversation/store.py) — CRUD for threads + turns with per-op short-lived connections, foreign-key ON DELETE CASCADE, WAL journaling, monotonic per-thread turn seq, and JSON turn payloads for full rehydration. utils/conversation/config.py resolves the DB path (ARIADNE_CONVERSATION_DB override, default data/conversations.sqlite3); documented in .env.example. 14 hermetic temp-DB tests green.
why: Every downstream consumer (conversational graph, API, web sidebar) reads/writes savable threads through this store, so it lands first with proven CRUD/ordering/cascade semantics before anything depends on it.

summary: Conversational Threads (2/11): added the LangGraph seam for the conversation graph. utils/conversation/state.py defines ConversationState (question/history/resolved_question/route/extraction+validation loop fields/final answer; trace accumulates via operator.add, scalars overwrite) wrapping the existing FederatedEvidence/SynthesizedAnswer contracts untouched. utils/conversation/config.py gains ConversationLLMConfig + ConversationConfig.from_env (CONVERSATION_LLM_* knobs, ARIADNE_CONVERSATION_MAX_VALIDATION_ITERS, CONVERSATION_QUICK_ANSWER, CONVERSATION_HISTORY_TURNS) — LLM off by default so the layer degrades to deterministic fallbacks. 8 new tests (compiled-StateGraph delta accumulation + contract pass-through + env parsing/DB-path override); documented in .env.example.
why: State + config are the seam every conversational agent node builds on; wrapping the frozen contracts and defaulting the LLM off preserves the repo's reproducible LLM-off ethos before any agent code exists.

summary: Conversational Threads (3/11): the redirect (router) and memory-grounded Answer agents. utils/conversation/llm.py wraps the OpenAI-compatible chat call behind one testable seam (LLMUnavailable on disabled/failed). router.py classifies quick-vs-graph and ALWAYS falls back to graph (LLM off/error/unparseable/unknown, or quick disabled) so no fact-seeking turn is ever answered from ungrounded model knowledge. answer.py composes the final reply: graph path wraps the verified synthesis narrative (deterministic fallback = narrative verbatim, byte-identical to today's grounded answer), quick path answers using ONLY established facts (deterministic fallback = fact summary or an honest clarification). 17 new stub-LLM + fallback tests (39 conversation tests green).
why: These two LLM nodes are the conversational brain; building them in isolation with grounding-safe fallbacks de-risks the graph assembly and keeps the no-hallucination guarantee even when the model is down.

summary: Conversational Threads (4/11): the Graph Extraction wrapper and Validation agent. graph_extraction.py reuses utils.orchestration.iter_pipeline verbatim (default_runner drives it, forwards every pipeline event onto the conversation stream, and returns evidence/answer/plan/status via the caller-owned PipelineRun); augment_question folds validation retry hints (focus + prior-attempt reason) into the question so a re-run searches with new parameters; the runner is injectable so tests need no live backends. validation.py is the bounded sufficiency gate: LLM judges completeness and, when insufficient and under the cap, returns follow-up focuses + a reason to loop back; the retry cap is enforced in the node (forced pass at max_validation_iters) and the deterministic fallback is always pass, so the loop can never spin. 12 new tests (51 conversation tests green).
why: The extraction wrapper must reuse the golden-pinned pipeline without reinterpreting it, and the analyst explicitly asked for a post-extraction 'not enough info -> search again with new parameters' loop, which needs a hard cap and a reproducible LLM-off path.

summary: Conversational Threads (5/11): assembled the conversation super-graph. New orchestration.py entry agent rewrites the user's message into a standalone question by resolving references from memory (deterministic fallback = message as-is, so single-turn behavior is unchanged). graph.py compiles START->orchestration->router->{quick:answer | graph:extraction->validation->(retry extraction | answer)}->finalize->END; every node emits its custom event (status/context/route/forwarded pipeline events/validation/final/conversation/done). The pipeline's inner `done` is suppressed on forward so the conversation emits exactly one terminal done. main.py's iter_conversation drains the custom stream. 6 new tests pin the exact event order for quick/graph/retry/cap/persist-hook paths; 56 conversation + 26 orchestration tests green.
why: This is where the layered conversational architecture becomes real; the emitted stream is a load-bearing UI contract, so ordering and the retry loop are pinned by dedicated goldens rather than assumed, exactly as the LangGraph migration did.
note: All LLM clients default to the shared (off-by-default) client, so the LLM-off path is deterministic: route=graph, validation=pass, answer=synthesis narrative verbatim.

summary: Conversational Threads (6/11): auto-titling + persistence helpers. naming.py title_for names a thread from its first message (LLM short title; deterministic fallback = cleaned/truncated question, so LLM-off stays reproducible). persistence.py adds pure domain helpers the API composes: facts_from_synthesized (only verified/rendered claim texts become a turn's reusable facts) and history_from_turns (rebuilds the memory list fed into the next turn — user->content, assistant->content+facts, with a recency limit). Decided persistence to the store lives in the API layer (owns SSE serialization), so the graph's finalize node dropped its persist hook and just emits conversation{id}+done; the client refreshes the thread list on done for the title. 14 new tests (69 conversation tests green).
why: Naming makes threads savable-with-a-name and the fact/history helpers are the memory mechanism (a turn's verified facts feed future memory-grounded quick answers); keeping persistence in the API keeps utils/conversation storage-agnostic and reuses existing event serialization.

summary: Conversational Threads (7/11): the API surface. Refactored api/services/query.py to expose render_pipeline_event (byte-identical /api/query output — test_query.py green UNMODIFIED). New api/services/conversations.py: thread CRUD over the store plus stream_conversation_events, which rebuilds memory from stored turns via history_from_turns, drives iter_conversation, presents forwarded pipeline events through render_pipeline_event and native events as-is, and on the terminal conversation event persists the user+assistant turns (assistant payload carries final_answer/route/validation/verified-facts/replayable events) and auto-titles a brand-new thread. api/models.py gains Conversation* models; api/main.py registers GET/POST /api/conversations, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/conversations/{id}, and POST /api/conversation-query (SSE). 10 new contract tests (CRUD via TestClient on a temp store; streaming via injected runner+stub clients); full 130-test api+conversation suite green.
why: Exposes savable threads and the memory-inclusive conversational stream to the web app while leaving the existing stateless /api/query contract and its golden tests byte-identical, per the resolved endpoint-coexistence decision.

summary: Conversational Threads (8/11): frontend API client, types, and rehydration adapter. web/lib/conversations.ts is the typed thread client (list/create/get/rename/delete) + streamConversation (POST /api/conversation-query via the existing postSseStream). types.ts extends the QueryEvent union with context/route/validation/final/conversation and adds the thread DTOs, StoredTurn/AssistantPayload, and a ConversationalReply plus optional reply/route/validation on WorkbenchRun. adapt.ts maps the reply/route/validation onto the run (existing buildRun behavior unchanged). New web/lib/rehydrate.ts buildRunFromStoredTurn folds a stored turn's replayable events through the shared reducer, then falls back to the persisted top-level fields. New Vitest specs for the client (fetch-mocked CRUD + 404) and rehydration (graph/quick/defensive).
why: Isolates all backend-shape knowledge in lib/ so the presentation layer stays a pure function of WorkbenchRun, and replay-based rehydration reconstructs a saved thread's turns without re-running the pipeline.

summary: Conversational Threads (9/11): run machine + context wiring. runMachine.ts extracts applyConversationEvent — the shared reducer folding one SSE event into a ConversationAccumulator — used by BOTH live streaming and stored-turn rehydration. submit() now streams /api/conversation-query via streamConversation, lazily creating a thread if none is active, and handles the new context/route/validation/final/conversation events (final -> the reply bubble). Added thread state + actions surfaced through WorkbenchContext: conversations, conversationId, conversationsLoading, refreshConversations, newConversation (POSTs a real thread), selectConversation (GET + rehydrate turns), deleteConversation, renameConversation; the list refreshes on done so the auto-title appears. replay()/EMPTY_RUN preserved. New runMachine Vitest spec covers the quick and graph (with validation-retry) reducer paths.
why: The run machine is the single source of truth for turn state; extending it (not the components) keeps the threading/memory logic in one tested place, and one shared reducer guarantees a rehydrated thread renders identically to a live one.

summary: Conversational Threads (10/11): ChatGPT-style sidebar + conversational rendering. ConversationsPanel/ConversationItem now render persisted threads from the backend, grouped by real date buckets (Today/Yesterday/Previous 7 days/Older via new ui.ts dateBucket/relativeTimeLabel), with loading + empty states, inline rename (Enter/Escape/blur), and delete-with-confirm; Workbench.tsx sources the list from context instead of deriving it from in-memory turns. New ReplyMessage.tsx renders the conversational reply bubble with a route indicator (Answered from memory / Queried the graphs), a validation-retry indicator, copy, and a Show/Hide evidence toggle; ChatThread.tsx renders question -> reply bubble -> collapsible grounded AnswerCard for graph turns (quick turns show only the reply). icons.tsx gains Pencil/Trash. Web gates green: 134 vitest, lint clean, production build succeeds; zero new tsc errors (two pre-existing errors live in untouched test files).
why: Delivers the actual modern threaded chat the analyst asked for — a real conversation sidebar and a memory-grounded reply over the collapsible provenance card — while keeping the grounded AnswerCard as the trust surface.

summary: Conversational Threads (11/11): end-to-end validation + docs. Full regression green — 964 backend (non-live) + 134 web vitest, web lint clean, production build succeeds; the existing /api/query golden suite is byte-identical (untouched). Live end-to-end against the running Neo4j: created a thread, asked 'Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-98 map to?' (grounded T1566/T1598), then a memory follow-up on T1598 (grounded mitigations M1054/M1017 with cross-source corroboration) — 4 turns persisted with verified facts + replayable events, thread auto-titled, rename/delete/404 all verified. Docs updated: structure.md (utils/conversation row, the conversations + conversation-query endpoints, threaded-chat prose, tests line), README (conversational memory tech-stack + key-feature bullets), global-project-rules repo map. Note: a clean browser click-through was not run because a concurrent session occupies the default web ports (16500/16501); the API-level live E2E + full web test/build suite cover the behavior.
why: Closes the feature: the layered conversational architecture demonstrably works end-to-end with real cross-turn memory over live graphs, the pre-existing pipeline stays byte-identical, and the docs describe the new conversation layer, endpoints, and threaded chat.

summary: Fix: the conversation layer now actually uses the operator's LLM. Previously the router/orchestration/answer agents had their own CONVERSATION_LLM_ENABLED that defaulted off, so with the workbench on the 'llm' drafter the reply prose came from the synthesis LLM but references were never resolved and the router always fell back to graph — a follow-up like 'provide more details on it' hit the planner literally and returned no records. Now ConversationConfig.with_llm_enabled ties the whole conversational flow to the per-turn drafter (drafter='llm' -> orchestration resolves references, router decides quick-vs-graph, answer memory-grounds), and ConversationLLMConfig inherits SYNTHESIS_LLM_* (endpoint/model/timeout) so no second setup is needed. Router parsing hardened: handles fenced ```json, distinguishes a network/timeout error from an unparseable reply in the reason, and adds a lenient single-keyword fallback. Verified live over Neo4j: 'what did it map to again?' resolves 'it' from memory, routes quick, and answers WITHOUT re-probing; 'mitigations for T1598' routes graph and probes. 7 new tests; 971 backend green.
why: The analyst reported that follow-ups lost memory and the agent probed the graphs every turn; the root cause was the new conversation LLM group defaulting off and not inheriting the already-configured endpoint, so the agentic router/reference-resolution never ran.

summary: Conversation answers now surface the retrieved node/edge metadata, not just the synthesis one-liner. The graph-path Answer agent gets an evidence_brief() distilled from the extracted records — primary_id/name/label, the node description (e.g. CAPEC-98's 'social engineering technique...' text), a few key attributes (Abstraction/Status/tactic/platforms/detection), related entries, and join targets — and the _GRAPH_SYSTEM prompt now tells it to draw on those details for 'tell me more' follow-ups and, when the primary entity is exhausted, to name the specific mapped entities it could look up next. Everything stays grounded (the brief is only the graph's own returned metadata; the agent is told to use only it). Deterministic fallback unchanged (narrative verbatim). 6 new tests; 975 backend green. Verified live: 'What does CAPEC-98 map to?' now includes the phishing description and offers T1566/T1598; the follow-up honestly reports CAPEC-98 is covered and offers to dive into the mapped techniques.
why: The analyst pointed out the ATT&CK/CAPEC nodes carry rich metadata (descriptions) that was extracted into evidence.properties but never used — the synthesis narrative only stated the mapping, so 'provide more information' hit a dead end despite the description being right there in the record.

summary: Added an 'Export chat' action pinned to the right edge of the thread title strip. New web/lib/export.ts buildChatExport() serializes the whole thread to shareable Markdown (title, then each turn as '## N. You' + the assistant reply tagged 'queried the graphs' / 'answered from memory', turns separated by ---), with a fallback for turns lacking a conversational reply. ThreadHeader is now a client component with a copy-to-clipboard Export button (disabled on an empty thread, shows 'Copied'); ChatThread passes it all runs. 4 new Vitest cases; web test (138)/lint/build green.
why: The analyst asked for a way to export a chat from the title strip so they can share conversations; copying the thread as Markdown makes it easy to paste back into a chat.

summary: Turned the thread-title 'Export chat' action into an 'Export' dropdown with two choices. web/lib/export.ts keeps buildChatExport (Chat Only) byte-identical and adds buildFullHistoryExport (Full History), a pure serializer that, per turn, emits a step-by-step 'Pipeline' trace of what ran in what order — routing decision, planner stages, each specialist query with its record count/latency (ordered by arrival), sequencing notes, validation verdict, and timings — then the assistant reply; quick (memory-answered) turns render 'answered from memory (no graph queried)'. ThreadHeader.tsx became a click-away popover (reusing the graph toolbar's dropdown pattern) offering Chat Only / Full History, both copying Markdown to the clipboard. 4 new export tests (162 web vitest green), lint clean, production build succeeds, no new tsc errors.
why: The analyst wanted more detail from the front page: 'Export chat' split into Export -> Chat Only / Full History, where Full History gives step-by-step information on what was done in what order. All the pipeline data (plannerStages/lanes/route/validation/timings) already lives on the client WorkbenchRun, so Full History is a pure serializer with no backend change.
note: Live-verified against the running stack on fallback ports 16600/16601 (defaults held by a concurrent session): streamed a real graph turn (CAPEC-98 -> T1566/T1598) and a memory follow-up, then ran the actual client rehydration + buildFullHistoryExport over the persisted turns — the graph turn rendered the probe/plan/gate stages plus the real Gremlin and Cypher queries with record counts, and the follow-up rendered the memory line. A browser click-through was not run because the Chrome extension was not connected.

summary: Entity Dossier (1/6): added a gated single-entity 'node_dossier' Cypher template. utils/specialists/cypher/builder.py now routes a seeded, non-join task whose text reads as a deep dive ('details/describe/tell me about/more on…') to _node_dossier, which projects n.attack_id/name/properties_json (the ATT&CK description lives in that JSON blob) plus a capped, typed, directional 1-hop neighborhood (collect over OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]-(m), first 25 neighbors + true size for a '+N more' marker); the anchor label falls back to the seed-id prefix when unnamed. Every other input still hits the lean node_lookup (bare id/name), so existing pipeline goldens are byte-identical. 3 builder tests (routing+validation, label inference, non-trigger fallback); 327 specialist tests green.
why: An analyst asked for full details on M1049 and got 'no further details available' because the single-entity node_lookup only returned id+name — never the description or the 23 MITIGATES edges that exist. The dossier template fetches both; gating + fallback keeps it additive so no golden churn.

summary: Entity Dossier (2/6): the dossier normalizer populates the evidence record. utils/specialists/cypher/normalizer.py detects the node_dossier row shape (a properties_json column) and builds one rich EvidenceRecord per entity: it parses properties_json to lift the description (+ a few key attrs mirroring the answer agent's _BRIEF_ATTRS) into properties, and turns the returned neighbor list into typed/directional related items {id,name,type,direction,label}, recording the true neighbor_total and a neighbors_truncated flag for a '+N more' tail. A node with no neighbors still yields a description record; malformed properties_json degrades to no description rather than raising. 3 normalizer tests; 330 specialist tests green. Live-verified end to end against Neo4j: the M1049 dossier query returns the full Antivirus/Antimalware description + 23 typed MITIGATES edges, and the answer agent's evidence_brief now surfaces them.
why: evidence_brief already consumes properties['description'] and related but received empties because the single-entity path emitted properties={}/related=[]; populating them is what makes the graph answer actually include the description and the mitigated techniques.

summary: Entity Dossier (3/6): the dossier model + memory formatters (pure, in utils/conversation/persistence.py). dossiers_from_records builds an EntityDossier (id, name, truncated description, capped typed DossierEdge tuple, true neighbor_total) from ONLY the dossier-shaped evidence records (gated on the properties['neighbor_total'] marker, so ordinary rows are never mistaken for held entities). dossier_index_line renders the tiny always-on 'Entities held in memory: M1049 (Antivirus/Antimalware).' line; dossier_detail_block renders the analyst's requested compact format — an entity/description line then 'adjacent:' with '* Edge Title (Type) -> Node Title (ID)' per neighbor (arrow flips to '<-' for inbound), capped at 15 lines with a '+N more' tail. entity_ids_in detects ATT&CK/CAPEC/CWE ids in a follow-up so the right dossier can be pulled. 5 tests; 85 conversation tests green.
why: Isolating the model and index/detail split as tested pure functions pins the exact requested memory format and gives the hybrid strategy (Step 4) the two pieces it injects — an always-on index plus an on-demand detail block — without any LangGraph changes.

summary: Entity Dossier (4/6): hybrid memory wiring — keyed dossier cache + on-demand injection. api/services/conversations.py now snapshots the turn's federated evidence (off the answer/evidence event) and, in _persist_turn, stores dossiers_from_records keyed by entity id under payload['entity_dossiers'] (facts stay verified-claim strings only — the adjacency is NOT dumped into always-on memory). Before each turn, memory_injection(question, turns) builds an always-on index line naming every held entity plus the full detail block for the entities THIS turn refers to (ids named in the question ∪ the most-recently-hydrated entity, for pronoun follow-ups), and these are appended as one synthetic assistant history entry (content='' so render_history_messages skips it; facts surface via known_facts) — so no LangGraph agent/state change. New persistence helpers: dossier_payload/_dossier_from_payload, dossiers_from_turns (latest wins), _recent_dossier_ids, memory_injection. Tests: dossiers persist keyed + not in facts, a follow-up naming M1049 injects its block, a pronoun follow-up resolves via recency. 62 api + 85 conversation tests green.
why: Realizes the analyst's chosen strategy — keep the neighborhood handy and pull just the relevant entity into context on a follow-up, with a tiny always-on index so the model knows what memory holds — keeping per-turn context lean while falling back to a fresh graph query if a reference is missed.

summary: Entity Dossier (5/6): Gremlin/CAPEC parity. Hoisted the describe-intent detector into utils/specialists/resolve.py as the shared is_dossier_intent (both builders now agree; cypher builder refactored onto it). gremlin/builder.py gains _capec_dossier — a project('node','out','in') traversal returning the vertex elementMap plus its outgoing/incoming edges as {rel, other:elementMap}; untyped outE()/inE() surface every edge kind and sidestep the schema gate's rel-type/direction checks (the analogue of Cypher's untyped -[r]-), and it routes at the seeded, non-join lookup branch on describe intent. gremlin/normalizer.py gains _normalize_dossier producing the same record shape as Cypher (description + attrs in properties; typed/directional related {id,name,type,direction,label}; capped at 25 with true neighbor_total + truncation flag), keyed on the CAPEC-N display id. 3 tests; 333 specialist tests green. Live-verified end to end via the connector: CAPEC-98 (Phishing) routes capec_dossier, passes the validator, and yields the description + 26 typed neighbors rendered into the compact adjacency memory block (CAPEC-631 etc.), exercising the '+N more' cap.
why: Cross-source parity so 'tell me about CAPEC-98' is as rich as the ATT&CK path, reusing the exact same evidence_brief + memory-formatter path so the compact adjacency representation is backend-agnostic.

summary: Entity Dossier (6/6): full regression + live E2E. Whole non-live backend suite green (1204 passed, 1 skipped) — the gated dossier template churned ZERO goldens/evalset banks. Live E2E against the running Neo4j via the real conversation-query endpoint (drafter=llm): the exact question that used to fail — 'Could you provide me more details on M1049?' — now runs the node_dossier template and answers with the full Antivirus/Antimalware description AND 'related to 23 different techniques, including T1027, T1059, T1566', offering specific mapped techniques to explore. The assistant turn persisted the M1049 dossier keyed by id (23 typed neighbors) WITHOUT leaking the adjacency into always-on facts, and memory_injection over the real stored turns produces the always-on index line plus the on-demand 'adjacent: * Mitigates (MITIGATES) -> Compression (T1027.015)' detail block for named, pronoun (recency), and mixed follow-ups.
why: Closes the feature the analyst asked for: single-entity 'tell me about X' now returns the description + edges instead of 'no further details', and the neighborhood is held handy (keyed cache + hybrid index/on-demand injection) so follow-ups are cheap without bloating context.
note: A clean live follow-up ANSWER that consumes the cached memory could not be captured because the local LLM at :9090 began returning empty router completions mid-session (router fell back to graph and mis-resolved the pronoun); the memory injection reaching the pipeline is proven deterministically on the real persisted turns and by unit tests, independent of that transient LLM degradation.

summary: Created docs/plans/definitional-name-lookup-plan.md — a 6-step plan to answer definitional name-lookup questions (e.g. 'What exactly is User Training and Software Configuration?') by adding deterministic name-term extraction + definitional-intent detection to the shared resolver, name-anchored dossier templates in the Cypher/Gremlin builders that reuse the Entity Dossier normalizer + memory formatters, planner routing that sends definitional questions to a first-class name-lookup sub-question, and a clear deterministic abstention when a name cannot be resolved.
why: Name-only definitional questions currently return 'no information' because retrieval anchors only on canonical ids; the graph holds the descriptions but there is no by-name path, and the miss message shown to the analyst is garbled local-LLM free-text rather than an honest, actionable statement.

summary: Frontend Refresh (1/6): neutralized the base palette. web/app/globals.css @theme tokens shift the canvas from green-charcoal to near-black neutral (bg #0e0f11, surface #17181a, console #101113), border to neutral gray #2a2b2e, and de-green the muted text scale (muted #9a9a97, faint/dim greys); lib/ui.ts neutralizes the sage accent + CONSOLE_BG; four hardcoded rgba(27,33,34,x) old-bg fills (MiniStepper/AppShell/InspectorDrawer/ConversationItem) become rgba(14,15,17,x). Teal #4e9e96 and amber #c9924a remain the only accents. woven-dusk-design skill palette table + CSS-vars synced. Verified: production build + lint green; built CSS bundle carries the new tokens and none of the old green hexes.
why: The analyst asked for a cleaner, less-green interface with blacks/dark grays as the base and green only as an accent; the base surface + sage-text tokens were the source of the overall green cast.

summary: Frontend Refresh (2/6): thread titles are now short + fast. utils/conversation/naming.py _SYSTEM prompt is tightened to a lightweight '2-5 words, Title Case, no punctuation' instruction, title_for drops max_tokens 32->16 so the first-turn title completion returns faster, and a new _clamp_words caps a generated title at 5 words (char bound + deterministic fallback unchanged). 1 new test; 8 naming + 97 conversation/api-conversation tests green.
why: The analyst wanted AI-generated titles that are a short 2-5 words based on the query, with the generation kept lightweight so the response returns as quickly as possible.

summary: Frontend Refresh (3/6): compact pill sidebar.
