ConversationItem is now a single rounded 'pill box' row (rounded-[10px], tight px-2.5 py-[7px]) — active = teal tint + teal ring, idle lightens on hover — and its title wraps to two lines (line-clamp-2) instead of truncating mid-word; the '# turns' Pill and 'X ago' time metadata are removed, so each row is title-only. ConversationsPanel tightens spacing (gap-1 pill list, compact date-group headers) and drops the turnCount/timeLabel props + relativeTimeLabel import. AppShell desktop rail widened 212->236px for readable titles. Web build + lint + 162 vitest green.
why: The analyst asked for a far more compact side menu with each chat styled as a pill box, titles no longer cut off after ~15 chars, and the turn-count / 'hours ago' metadata removed.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (1/6): the shared resolver now lifts deterministic name anchors and recognizes definitional intent. utils/specialists/resolve.py gains a name_terms tuple on ResolvedTask, populated by _extract_name_terms (priority: quoted phrases, then Title-Case runs, then filtered single tokens) with card label/relationship words, scaffolding vocabulary, stopwords and id-shaped tokens excluded and multi-word runs kept whole (so 'Software Configuration' survives even though 'Software' is a label word). New is_definitional_intent predicate is a superset of is_dossier_intent that also matches bare 'what is/are X' phrasings. 5 new resolver tests; 498 specialist tests green.
why: A name-only definitional question ('What exactly is User Training and Software Configuration respectively?') produces no id, so the id-only resolver found nothing to anchor on; name_terms + definitional intent give the builders (steps 2-3) a deterministic, card-grounded anchor to emit a name dossier, and leave the existing by-id dossier gating untouched.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (2/6): the Cypher builder now answers a name-only definitional question. New _node_dossier_by_name template (utils/specialists/cypher/builder.py) matches any description-bearing ATT&CK label (Technique/SubTechnique/Mitigation/Tactic/Group/Software/Campaign/DataComponent/DetectionStrategy) whose lower-cased name CONTAINS an extracted name term, returning the SAME dossier row shape (id/name/properties_json + capped typed 1-hop + true total) as the by-id dossier so the existing normalizer surfaces the description and neighbors unchanged. It routes at the seedless fallback when name_terms + definitional intent are present, replacing the catastrophic label scan. Tightened validator _ATTACK_ID_FILTER_RE to the predicate form (attack_id IN/=/…) so a name-scoped query returning the id is no longer misread as an unscoped id filter, while the STIX-ambiguity guard still rejects a real unscoped id filter. 4 new builder tests + validator round-trip; 502 specialist, 244 planner/synthesis tests green.
why: This is the core retrieval fix: 'What exactly is User Training and Software Configuration?' now emits a validator-safe name dossier that returns the mitigations' descriptions instead of falling through to a bare label scan / empty result.

summary: Frontend Refresh (4/6): the evidence disclosure now reads as an extension of the chat container. ChatThread's TurnBlock wraps the reply bubble and the expanded AnswerCard in ONE rounded bg-surface container that owns the shadow; ReplyMessage and AnswerCard gain a `docked` prop that drops their own bubble chrome (max-width/rounding/surface/shadow) so, when expanded, the evidence card extends seamlessly beneath the reply separated only by a hairline seam (SHADOW.insetTop) instead of floating as a separate standalone card. Standalone (undocked) AnswerCard for reply-less/mid-stream turns is unchanged. Web build + lint + 162 vitest green.
why: The analyst asked that the 'Show evidence and sources' dropdown be visually integrated as an extension of the chat container itself rather than appearing as a separate, standalone container.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (3/6): Gremlin/CAPEC parity for name-only definitional lookups. utils/specialists/gremlin/builder.py gains _capec_dossier_by_name, which anchors an AttackPattern by a case-insensitive name match on the extracted name terms (reusing the concept-scan's TextP.regex, with regex metacharacters/quotes escaped) and returns the identical project('node','out','in') dossier projection. It routes at the seedless branch when name_terms + definitional intent are present (priority: capec ids -> concept terms -> name terms -> unscoped scan). No normalizer change needed: GremlinNormalizer dispatches _normalize_dossier by row shape and keys on the node's own id, so a seedless name dossier normalizes to the same description + typed related record shape as the by-id and Cypher paths. 3 new builder/normalizer tests + GremlinValidator round-trip; 505 specialist tests green.
why: Cross-source parity so a CAPEC-named definitional question ('What is Phishing?') returns the pattern's description + typed neighbors instead of a wall of unscoped rows, keeping the backend-agnostic evidence_brief + memory formatters intact.

summary: Frontend Refresh (5/6): queries run in the background across chat switches, with a per-chat swirl. runMachine is refactored from a single global in-flight stream to a per-conversation registry: `streams` (a ref-map of AbortController + accumulator + timers keyed by conversation id), plus `runsByConversation` / `liveStatusByConversation` / `streamingByConversation` state so each conversation's turns and live status fold independently of which chat is on screen. selectConversation/newConversation NO LONGER cancel a running stream (a streaming target keeps its live in-memory turns; a completed one re-hydrates from the backend); submit opens a keyed stream; the exposed `replaying` now reflects only the ACTIVE conversation so the composer is enabled in a different chat while another streams. New pure `upsertRunInto` helper + exposed `busyConversationIds` set; a new SwirlIcon (animate-spin) renders on busy sidebar rows (ConversationItem gains `busy`, threaded via ConversationsPanel + Workbench; context already forwards it). 3 new invariant tests; web build + lint + 165 vitest green.
why: The analyst reported that switching to another chat stopped a running query; queries must continue in the background regardless of the active chat, and the tab where a query is running should show a swirl to indicate progress.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (4/6): the planner now routes a definitional name question to a specialist. utils/planner/drafter.py DeterministicDrafter gains a definitional bridge: on a keyword-router dead end, if the request reads as 'what is X'/'define X' (is_definitional_intent, lazy-imported to avoid a package-init cycle), it routes a join-free name-lookup sub-question to every live source (entities = the card's probe label, so it is gate-valid; the entity name reaches the specialist via the sub-question text). drafter_factory.HybridDrafter now also consults the deterministic floor when the primary (LLM) drafter routes nothing, so an LLM 'unsupported/incomplete' plan no longer dead-ends. llm_drafter._SYSTEM_PROMPT gains a rule that a definitional name question is answerable by name, not unsupported. Regenerated the planner corpus (build_corpus): previously-unroutable id lookups (A-LKP) and CAPEC abstraction-hierarchy questions (C-ABS) are now routable, and the index-based holdout split reshuffled. 7 new drafter tests; 105 planner + 505 specialist tests green.
why: Name-term extraction and the name-dossier templates only help if a sub-question actually reaches a specialist; the LLM path dead-ended to 'unsupported' and the keyword router mis-/under-routed name-only questions, so the planner needed a deterministic definitional route (and an LLM floor) to make the first pass reach the new name dossier.

summary: Frontend Refresh (6/6): full regression + live E2E + docs. Web gate green (production build, lint clean, 165 vitest); backend regression green (148 conversation + api tests — the naming-prompt change churned nothing else). Live E2E against the running stack (Neo4j 4369 nodes, Gremlin 4769, LLM :9090) on alt ports 16600/16601: two conversation-query streams for two different threads were launched concurrently and genuinely INTERLEAVED (both started 12:14:32.6; thread B's specialists ran at :41 while thread A's ran at :51; B finished :53 while A continued to :58), each returning a real grounded graph answer (A: CAPEC-98 -> T1566/T1598; B: six mitigations for T1566 incl. M1017/M1049) — proving the backend serves independent per-conversation streams in parallel, the server-side foundation of client-side background execution. structure.md updated for the compact pill rail, container-extending evidence, and background streams + swirl.
why: Close the feature set: prove the palette/sidebar/evidence/background-query changes are green across the whole web + conversation test surface and that concurrent per-conversation streaming works live, then land on main.
note: A browser click-through of the client-side switch-chat-and-swirl flow was not run: no Chrome extension was connected (list_connected_browsers empty) and the preview MCP can't attach to a hand-started server (its precheck keys on the concurrent session's port 16500). The client behavior is covered by the per-conversation upsertRunInto invariant tests + full type-checked build; the live concurrency precondition is proven above.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (5/6): synthesis now gives a clear, actionable message when a name cannot be resolved. utils/specialists/resolve.py exposes definitional_name_terms (card-agnostic). utils/synthesis/composer.py: an empty result from a name-dossier query (detected precisely via _is_name_lookup on the query signature, so ordinary honest-empty abstentions are untouched) now abstains with 'No entity named X was found ... give its id (e.g. T1566, M1017, or CAPEC-98)'; a planner-unsupported part with a model-authored (often garbled) reason is no longer echoed verbatim (only clean source-availability reasons are), replaced by a deterministic 'could not be matched ... name it or give its id' note; and when there is no grounded claim the narrative becomes an honest clarification naming what was searched. utils/synthesis/factory.py gates the LLM narrator off when there are no claims, so it cannot hallucinate prose over an empty evidence set. 8 new composer/narrator tests (+1 updated); 657 synthesis+specialist, 105 planner tests green.
why: The analyst asked that when the system truly needs more information it say so clearly; previously an empty/unsupported answer surfaced the local planner model's garbled free-text ('the request What is incomplete') or a bare 'no evidence' line. This makes the abstention deterministic, specific (names the entity, offers the id path), and immune to the weak local model's phrasing.

summary: Definitional Name Lookup (6/6): live E2E verified and two precision/robustness fixes it surfaced. (a) resolve.py Title-Case extraction now keeps a within-name connector ('Phishing for Information', 'Denial of Service') as ONE term but still splits on 'and'/'or', so a common word ('Third' in 'Flibbertigibbet the Third') is no longer left standing alone to spuriously CONTAINS-match 'third-party' nodes. (b) gremlin/builder _capec_dossier_by_name wildcard-sanitizes each name term (non-alphanumerics -> '.') instead of re.escape, because Python 3.13 re.escape emits '\ ' for spaces which the Gremlin server's Groovy parser rejects (a multi-word CAPEC name errored server-side). Also fixed an orchestration synthesis-graph test to exercise the narrator-fallback path with a claim (the narrator is now skipped when there are no claims). Full backend regression green: 1230 passed, 1 skipped (incl. live golden suites). Live E2E (LLM-off) against Neo4j/Gremlin: 'What exactly is User Training and Software Configuration respectively?' returns M1017 + M1054 with descriptions on the first pass; 'What is Phishing?' returns 22 ATT&CK + 4 CAPEC records cross-source; an unknown name returns a clear, actionable abstention. Merged to local main with --no-ff.
why: Closes the reported failure: a name-only definitional question that used to return 'no information' (the graph held the descriptions but there was no by-name path) now answers with the entities' descriptions on the first pass, and a genuine miss states plainly what it couldn't find and how to disambiguate.

summary: Frontend Refresh follow-up: sidebar title polish + auto-scroll to newest turn. ChatThread scrolls its message list to the bottom (smooth) whenever the last turn's id changes, so a just-submitted query scrolls into view. ConversationItem titles are now a SINGLE line filling the full row width, fading out at the right edge via a mask-image linear-gradient (instead of a 2-line clamp or ellipsis); rename/delete are absolutely positioned and slide OVER the faded end of the title on hover (with a gradient backing blending them onto the row) so no horizontal space is reserved for them, and the busy swirl sits at the right edge when idle. Full title still available via the row's title tooltip + DOM text (a11y). Web build + lint + 165 vitest green; new code confirmed present in the built client bundle.
why: The analyst asked that submitting a query scroll down to it, and that sidebar titles be a single full-width line whose text fades at the edge, with the edit/delete actions overlapping the text on hover to save space.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (1/6): scaffolded utils/evaluation/harness/ — a decoupled run→judge→report agent system. contracts.py adds JSON-serialisable AnswerRecord + CorrectnessVerdict dataclasses and write_jsonl/read_jsonl so the three stages share only files, never imports. golden.py normalises the attack/capec/federated banks into GoldenEntry and extracts the gold expected-id set the judge grades against (single = must_include_ids∪must_include_related; federated = must_correlate; expect_empty/expect_boundary/expect_no_correlation = honest-abstention gold). 11 hermetic tests green.
why: The analyst asked for a system that runs the golden set through the local AI, judges how correct each answer is, and reports — with the three concerns handled by separate agents. Fixing the persisted artifact schema and gold-extraction first lets the runner/judge/reporter stay decoupled.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (2/6): the runner agent (run_stage.py) drives each golden entry through the live pipeline and persists AnswerRecords to answers.jsonl, reusing score_e2e's run_single/run_federated drivers and its one-router-per-degradation-mode setup. cli.py orchestrates the stages (--stage run|judge|report|all, --set, --limit, --tier, --no-live, --llm, --llm-pipeline). New ids.py scans id-shaped tokens (ATT&CK/CAPEC/CWE shapes) from the answer PROSE so produced_ids reflect what the deterministic composer states in-text ('e.g. M1038, M1040') rather than only structured entity_ids. Per-entry failures are captured on the record, not fatal; hermetic when the stack is down. 21 hermetic tests green + live smoke: 2/2 attack answers produced with prose-scanned ids matching gold.
why: Stage 1 of the decoupled agent system — turn golden questions into persisted answers once, so judging and reporting never re-run the slow live pipeline. Prose id-scanning is needed because the composer lists related ids in the claim text, which is what the correctness judge and the deterministic backstop must see.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (3/6): correctness_judge.py grades an answer against the golden expected answer (the new capability the analyst asked for — how correct, not just how faithful). DeterministicCorrectness computes id recall/precision/F1 of the golden expected ids vs the ids the answer states (with honest-abstention handling for expect_empty gold, and run-failure = incorrect). LocalLLMCorrectness asks the local LLM at the EVAL_LLM endpoint to rate correctness 0..1 + a {correct,partial,incorrect} label + one-line rationale, reusing EvalConfig + the llm_judge JSON extractor; the id recall/precision are always computed mechanically even on an LLM verdict so they are never model-invented. HybridCorrectness falls back to the deterministic floor on any transport/parse failure. 33 hermetic tests green + live: graded two real smoke answers against :9090 (A-MIT-01 correctness 0.75/partial, A-MIT-02 0.40/partial with grounded rationales).
why: This is the core of the request: the local AI judging how correct each answer is against the known answer key, with a reproducible deterministic backstop so a correctness number always exists and the id math is trustworthy.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (4/6): the judge agent (judge_stage.py) reads answers.jsonl, grades each answer's correctness via the correctness judge, and writes judgments.jsonl — a standalone stage that imports only the shared contracts + judge, so a fixed answers.jsonl can be re-judged (LLM off, then on) without re-running the pipeline. JudgeAgent.from_args wires --llm/--judge-sample into an EvalConfig; run_files handles missing/empty inputs honestly and prints a label breakdown + LLM coverage. 37 hermetic tests green. Live over the smoke answers: deterministic grades 2/2 partial; --llm against :9090 LLM-graded one (0.75) and cleanly fell back to the deterministic floor on the other when the local model returned an unusable completion.
why: Stage 2 of the decoupled agent system: judging is separated from running so the (slow, live) pipeline runs once and grading can be repeated cheaply and in either mode, with graceful degradation when the flaky local LLM misbehaves.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (5/6): the reporter agent (report_stage.py) joins judgments.jsonl with answers.jsonl and aggregates overall + per-set + per-tier + per-source correctness (pass rate with a Wilson 95% CI via stats.py, mean correctness, mean id recall/precision, LLM coverage) plus a lowest-scoring-answers list with missing ids + rationale, writing golden-eval.md and golden-eval.json. No wall-clock timestamp is embedded so an LLM-off report is byte-reproducible. cli.py --stage all now chains run→judge→report. 42 hermetic tests green + live: produced a full report from the smoke judgments (mean correctness 0.68, per-group tables, worst-answers with the local LLM's rationale 'listed three of the four required IDs, missing M1026').
why: Stage 3 of the decoupled agent system — the analyst's final reporting, produced purely from persisted judgments so it is cheap, repeatable, and never re-runs the pipeline or judge.

summary: Golden Eval Harness (6/6): wired the harness into the CLI and verified end-to-end. main.py gains --golden-eval (argparse.REMAINDER) that forwards all flags to utils.evaluation.harness.cli, so `uv run main.py --golden-eval --stage all --set all --llm` runs the whole run→judge→report system. docs/evaluation/golden/ (run artifacts) gitignored; structure.md + global-project-rules commands document the harness. Verified: 1291 backend tests collect with no import breakage; evaluation suite 91 passed; LIVE end-to-end via main.py across all three sets (2 attack + 2 capec + 2 federated) — 6/6 answered through the real pipeline, all 6 correctness-graded by the local LLM at :9090 (4 correct, 2 partial, 0 incorrect), report written at pass rate 66.67% / mean correctness 0.858 with per-set/tier/source tables and a lowest-scoring-answers list.
why: Makes the decoupled correctness harness a first-class CLI entry and proves it works live end-to-end across single-source and federated questions with the local AI judging correctness against the golden expected answers — closing the analyst's request.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (1/6): authored docs/plans/answer-truncation-fix-plan.md. Diagnosed why conversation answers truncate mid-sentence and why raising the LLM max-token budget did nothing: the displayed reply comes from the conversation answer agent, whose max_tokens reads CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS (default 1024) and does NOT inherit SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS; no LLM seam inspects finish_reason (a length stop is shown verbatim, and content=None on a length stop degrades silently); and the answer prompt (12 history turns + a 10-record evidence brief) crowds out the completion within a bounded model context window. Planned a 6-phase fix (config inheritance, finish_reason capture+logging, graceful truncation render, evidence-brief budget, docs/.env, regression+merge).
why: The analyst reported answers cut off mid-word and that increasing max tokens had no effect; the plan records the confirmed multi-cause diagnosis and a staged, individually-validated remedy before any code changes.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (2/6): CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS now inherits SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS when unset (utils/conversation/config.py ConversationLLMConfig.from_env), mirroring the existing base_url/model/timeout inheritance. Previously the conversation answer agent's output budget was hardcoded to CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS or 1024 and ignored the synthesis knob, so raising SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS never reached the agent that writes the visible reply. Added 3 config tests (inherit-24000, conversation-override-wins, 1024 default when nothing set); conversation config suite green (11).
why: The single most direct cause of 'I raised max tokens but nothing changed': the visible answer is written by the conversation answer agent, which read a different, un-inherited max-tokens knob.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (3/6): the shared conversation LLM client now captures the truncation signal (utils/conversation/llm.py). Added a CompletionResult(content, finish_reason, usage) dataclass and a complete_verbose() that returns it without raising on a length stop, normalizes null content to '', and logs a WARNING with prompt/completion token counts when finish_reason=='length' (so the operator can see when the model context window, not max_tokens, is the ceiling). complete() now delegates to complete_verbose() and, on empty content, distinguishes a length-truncation ('raise CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS or the model context window') from a genuinely dead model. New utils/conversation/tests/test_llm.py (9 tests); full conversation suite green (98).
why: A finish_reason=='length' reply is truncated, not complete; the code discarded that signal so chopped answers reached the analyst and null-content length stops degraded silently. Surfacing finish_reason + usage makes truncation observable and lets the answer agent react.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (4/6): the conversation answer agent now renders truncation gracefully (utils/conversation/agents/answer.py). Both the quick and graph paths call the shared client's complete_verbose() via a new _llm_reply() helper: a length-stopped, non-empty reply is tidied (a dangling unbalanced '(...' id fragment like '(T1561.' is stripped) and gets an explicit note ('Response truncated at the model's output limit — increase CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS or the model's context window, or ask for fewer items at a time.'), while a length stop that produced no visible content falls back to the complete deterministic verified narrative instead of an empty reply. Updated the test stubs to complete_verbose and added 2 truncation-render tests; conversation suite green (100).
why: A mid-word chop must never reach the analyst: it reads as a broken app. Making truncation explicit (and never showing a bare cut) turns an alarming failure into a clear, actionable signal while the verified claim table remains the trust surface.

summary: Golden Eval Harness — agentic mode + 16-way concurrency + one-command run. The runner gains an --agentic mode that drives each RAW golden question through the real iter_pipeline(question, use_llm=True) — the local LLM plans/routes (planner, which unlike the deterministic planner extracts entity seeds like T1047 from raw text), drafts specialist queries, and composes synthesis — i.e. the actual agentic process the workbench uses, rather than replaying the bank's pre-authored task. Both stages now run on a thread pool (--concurrency, default 16): the runner fans questions out concurrently (agentic builds per-call specialists so it is thread-safe; the gold path uses thread-local routers), and the judge grades concurrently and by default grades the WHOLE set with the LLM (the 20-cap only applies if --judge-sample is passed). The decoupled barrier is preserved: all answers are collected before any grading. Single command: `uv run main.py --golden-eval --agentic --llm`. 47 harness + 96 evaluation tests green; live 6-question agentic+LLM sample: 6/6 answered through the real pipeline (LLM planner seeded T1047/CAPEC-555/etc.), all 6 LLM-graded 5 correct/1 partial, pass rate 83%, mean correctness 0.979.
why: The analyst clarified they want ONE command that passes every question through the LLM agentic process (not the deterministic/gold-injected path), collects all answers, and only then grades them — at 16 concurrency. The prior run showed 'pipeline LLM: OFF' and injected gold tasks, so it never exercised the agentic LLM flow.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (5/6): the answer agent's evidence brief is now capped in aggregate, not just per record (utils/conversation/agents/answer.py). Added _MAX_BRIEF_CHARS=3000 total budget on top of _MAX_BRIEF_RECORDS; extracted _unique_records()/_record_brief_line() helpers and rewrote evidence_brief() to stop once the running size would exceed the budget, always including at least the first record and appending an explicit 'more records omitted' marker when it drops any. Record-heavy turns (queries returning hundreds of nodes) can no longer inflate the answer prompt past the model's context window and force a truncation. 4 new brief tests; answer suite green (17).
why: Record-heavy turns were the ones truncating: a big evidence brief crowded the completion out of the model's context window. Bounding the brief in aggregate leaves headroom for the answer regardless of how many records a query returned.

summary: Answer Truncation Fix (6/6 docs): documented the answer output budget + context-window ceiling in .env.example. CONVERSATION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS is now shown as inheriting SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS (commented out rather than pinned at 1024), with a note that the real ceiling is the model's context window (server caps completion at n_ctx - prompt_tokens) and that a cut-off reply is logged as finish_reason=length and shown with an explicit truncation note. Also fixed the operator .env (gitignored, not committed): the Synthesis block had PLANNER_LLM_BASE_URL/MODEL where SYNTHESIS_LLM_BASE_URL/MODEL belong, so synthesis+conversation silently defaulted to the dead :9090; repointed to http://localhost:4000/v1 model skynet. Verified end-to-end that the conversation answer agent now resolves :4000/skynet with a 24000-token budget.
why: Prevent recurrence: the knob docs now say which value the visible answer reads and that n_ctx — not max_tokens — is the true limit; the env fix restores a live endpoint after a copy-paste error had pointed synthesis/conversation at a dead server.

summary: Chat composer: clear input on send + allow typing while a turn streams. web/components/center/Composer.tsx now calls setQuestion("") and refocuses the textarea immediately after submit(), so the sent text no longer lingers in the box. Removed disabled={replaying} (and the now-dead disabled:opacity-60 class) from the textarea so the analyst can compose the next question while the current turn is still streaming. Send remains gated by canSend (still requires !replaying) because runMachine.startStream supersedes any in-flight turn per conversation, so enabling send mid-stream would abort the running query. Verified: eslint clean on the file; the two pre-existing tsc errors are in untouched lib/__tests__ files.
why: The analyst reported that after sending a message the input kept the previous text and would not let them type a new one. Clearing on send and un-disabling the textarea lets them write the next question right away without losing the streaming behavior.

summary: Chat composer: drop the focus outline and auto-grow to 6 lines. web/components/center/Composer.tsx textarea gains focus:outline-none focus-visible:outline-none to override the global :focus-visible ring (globals.css:133) for this input only — the global a11y ring is untouched for the rest of the app. Added a useEffect keyed on `question` that autosizes the textarea to its scrollHeight, capped at 6 lines (lineHeight*6 + vertical padding); past the cap it scrolls internally (overflowY auto) instead of pushing the toolbar down. Covers typing, imperative fill, and clear-on-send uniformly. eslint clean.
why: The analyst found the focus outline on the message box annoying and wanted the box to expand as they type, up to 6 lines.

summary: Chat composer: actually remove the focus outline. The prior focus-visible:outline-none Tailwind utility never took effect: Tailwind v4 emits utilities inside @layer utilities, and the global :focus-visible ring (globals.css:133) is UNLAYERED, so it wins regardless of specificity. Fixed by adding an unlayered rule `.composer-input:focus-visible { outline: none }` in globals.css and tagging the textarea with the composer-input class; specificity (0,2,0) > (0,1,0) and both are unlayered, so the composer opts out while the app-wide focus ring stays intact. Dropped the dead focus/focus-visible:outline-none Tailwind classes from the textarea.
why: Screenshot showed the teal (--color-focus) ring still drawn on the composer after the first attempt — the layer interaction, not specificity, was the real cause.

summary: Chat column width: constrain the center conversation to a centered ~60% column on large screens instead of spanning 100% of the pane. web/components/center/ChatThread.tsx wraps the scrolling run list in an mx-auto w-full lg:w-[60%] container; Composer.tsx applies the same width to the docked input bar so it lines up under the messages; ThreadHeader.tsx wraps its title strip in the same centered column (full-width bottom border retained). Below lg the column stays full width so it does not get cramped when the rail/inspector are open. Verified: eslint clean on all three files; the two pre-existing tsc errors are in untouched lib/__tests__ files.
why: The analyst asked that the chat not take up 100% of the chat window width, but only ~60% and be centered properly.

summary: Chat column width: widen the centered conversation column from ~60% to ~75% on large screens across ChatThread.tsx, Composer.tsx, and ThreadHeader.tsx (lg:w-[75%]).
why: The analyst asked to make the chat column 75% wide.

summary: Chat now renders assistant replies as GitHub-flavored markdown. New web/components/center/Markdown.tsx wraps react-markdown + remark-gfm + remark-breaks with Woven Dusk-styled overrides (bold/italic/lists/headings/code/blockquote/tables/links), preserving inline CAPEC/ATT&CK ReferenceLink linkification via a recursive linkifyChildren over text nodes. ReplyMessage.tsx swaps RefText for Markdown; UserMessage.tsx gains whitespace-pre-wrap so typed questions keep newlines. Added vitest.config.ts (@/ alias) and lib/__tests__/markdown.test.tsx render tests.
why: The analyst reported chat did not render markdown: newlines collapsed and bold/italic/bullets showed as literal syntax.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (1/8): added `max_hops` (ORCH_MAX_HOPS, default 1) and `assess_mode` (ORCH_ASSESS_MODE, default deterministic) to OrchestrationConfig with env plumbing and validation (hop floor of 1, unknown assess modes fall back to deterministic). Extended test_config.py.
why: First knobs for the bounded evidence-gathering cycle; default max_hops=1 keeps the feature dark so it lands without changing observable behavior.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (2/8): extended PipelineState with the loop envelope — hop:int, frontier and visited as set-union-reduced collections of (join_value, source) / (entity_id, source), and an assessment field for the last verdict. Added union_sets reducer alongside merge_dicts; extended test_state.py to prove per-hop deltas accumulate and dedupe.
why: The assess -> re-plan -> specialists cycle needs a hop counter, a frontier of discovered-but-unexpanded join-keys, and a visited set to prevent re-querying; wrapping them in graph state (not the frozen contracts) keeps the contract-shape tests and SSE to_dict() JSON stable.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (3/8): added utils/orchestration/agents/assess/frontier.py with two pure, deterministic helpers — extract_frontier(results, plan) returns the (join_value, source) join-keys surfaced (scoped to sources in a declared plan.joins bridge) and update_visited(visited, results) returns the delta of newly-retrieved (entity_id, source) records. Added test_frontier.py (5 cases).
why: The assess node and the re-planner both need a precise, backend-agnostic answer to what new join-keys and entities a hop surfaced; isolating it in pure helpers keeps the novelty check honest and the graph nodes thin.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (4/8): added the assess package — contracts.py (frozen Assessment: sufficient/gaps/missing_entities/hop/hop_capped/mode/reason + to_dict), policy.py (deterministic join-closure + novelty predicate; single-source plans are one-shot sufficient; opt-in injectable LLM critic that degrades cleanly to the deterministic judge with the fallback recorded; hop-cap short-circuit forces sufficiency at hop>=max_hops), and node.py build_assess_node factory that folds the hop evidence delta into frontier/visited and writes the verdict. Added test_policy.py (10 cases).
why: The assess node is the decision point the loop turns on; a deterministic default keeps the LLM-off build reproducible while the hop-cap short-circuit guarantees termination even if the predicate never converges.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (5/8): added the evidence-aware re-plan entry. utils/planner/schema.py gains SubQuestion.hop (omitted from to_dict when 0, so single-pass plan JSON stays byte-identical) plus subquestion_key + merge_plans (dedupe on (source, sorted entities, normalized text); base ids/joins preserved, appended sub-questions get fresh ids and the hop tag). utils/planner/agent.py gains PlanningAgent.replan(request, evidence, frontier, gaps): deterministic join-key chasing that emits a consumer sub-question + join for producer-surfaced, unresolved keys into a not-yet-queried live source (empty when nothing new). Added test_replan_dedup.py (7 cases).
why: Re-planning must consume accumulated evidence, drop already-answered sub-questions, and route only remaining gaps, or the loop repeats work or never shrinks. Relevance-scored neighbour expansion is the documented follow-on; the deterministic chase keeps the LLM-off build reproducible.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (6/8): closed the assess->re-plan->specialists cycle in the super-graph (utils/orchestration/main.py). Added assess + replan nodes; replaced bundle->synthesize with bundle->assess, a route_sufficiency conditional (assess->synthesize when sufficient/hop-capped else assess->replan), and a route_after_replan conditional (replan->announce_querying when new sub-questions were added else ->synthesize, which also handles the nothing-new terminal case). replan_node bumps hop and merge_plans-grafts the expansion; cursor is untouched so each hop runs only the appended sub-questions. iter_pipeline init seeds hop=1/frontier/visited and the event-order docstring documents the loop. Added test_iterative_loop.py (4 cases: single-pass leaves the join open; the loop chases the consumer and closes it; termination within the cap; hop-tagging).
why: This physically closes the cycle at the specialists->bundle->assess->plan boundary. max_hops=1 collapses assess to force sufficiency on pass one, reproducing the historical single-pass path exactly; recursion_limit=200 remains the backstop.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (7/8): surfaced hop events and enabled the loop by default (ORCH_MAX_HOPS 1->5). The assess node streams an assess event (verdict+hop+max_hops, emitted only when the loop is enabled so max_hops=1 stays byte-identical) rendered by api/services/query.py; the re-plan status frame carries hop/added. Refined the sufficiency predicate to chaseable-frontier semantics (loop re-plans iff an unresolved join-key can still be carried into an un-queried source), eliminating wasted cycles and making assess+replan agree. Web: typed Assessment + assess event, folded onto the run accumulator (assessment/hop) with a vitest case. Confirmed the e2e evaluation is byte-identical at max_hops 1 vs 5 (deterministic sections), so the committed baselines stand; updated event-order goldens (orchestration/specialists/api) for the new assess event.
why: The loop must be inspectable and evaluated before becoming the default; empirical byte-identical e2e output (well-formed federated plans already close joins single-pass) proves the flip is safe for the committed reproducibility baselines.

summary: Iterative Retrieval Loop (8/8): documentation + final regression. Added docs/iterative-retrieval-loop.md (the cycle, chaseable-frontier sufficiency policy, hop cap, join-key chasing, LLM critic fallback, config, reproducibility, key files); updated docs/structure.md (super-graph now bundle->assess->{synthesize|re-plan->specialists}, assess event, ORCH_MAX_HOPS/ORCH_ASSESS_MODE, loop state envelope), docs/planner_agent.md (replan + merge_plans dedupe + SubQuestion.hop), docs/specialist_agents.md (multi-hop re-entry runs only appended sub-questions). Termination proven by tests (policy hop-cap, chaseable-dry stop, loop integration terminates within cap). Full regression green: 1325 passed / 1 skipped (utils+api), 170 passed (web). Confirmed the loop leaves the committed component/e2e eval baselines unchanged (byte-identical at max_hops 1 vs 5; the pre-existing 43-vs-47 component drift reproduces on base main, so it is unrelated to this feature and left untouched).
why: The dominant risk of an iterative retriever is non-termination/overspend; explicit hop-cap, novelty-stop, and dedup tests are the safety net, and the docs keep the four-component migration story coherent.

summary: Intent Classification (1/8): added utils/planner/intent.py — the closed Intent taxonomy (definitional/lookup/enumeration/correlation/remediation/traversal/unsupported), IntentClassification (label/confidence/rationale/cues/source + to_dict/from_dict), the IntentClassifier Protocol, and DeterministicIntentClassifier (priority cue rules, reuses is_definitional_intent, card-aware lookup-vs-unsupported fallback). Added test_intent.py (16 cases) and docs/plans/intent-classification-plan.md.
why: The proposal charges the planner with classifying analyst intent as a distinct step; today it is only an implicit keyword-routing side effect. A deterministic closed taxonomy where every label changes routing makes the step real and testable, mirroring the drafter deterministic-default pattern while the gate stays the sole authority.

summary: Intent Classification (2/8): Plan now carries the classified intent. utils/planner/schema.py adds Plan.intent (IntentClassification|None; omitted from to_dict when None so pre-intent plan JSON stays byte-identical; from_dict tolerant; preserved through merge_plans). The planner subgraph gains a classify node before draft (utils/orchestration/agents/planner/nodes.py+graph.py): it names the intent, and finalize/degrade copy it onto the emitted plan. PlanningState.intent added; PlanningAgent takes an optional classifier (deterministic default) and classifies in the defensive no-draft path too. Added 3 agent-loop tests (converged/degraded plans carry intent; None omitted from to_dict).
why: Intent must live on the plan to be consumed by the drafter, scored by the eval, and shown in the UI. Attaching it at finalize/degrade guarantees every emitted plan reports its intent regardless of path, while the conditional serialisation protects the committed reproducibility baselines.

summary: Intent Classification (3/8): added the hybrid LLM classifier path. utils/planner/intent_llm.py provides LLMIntentClassifier (OpenAI-compatible endpoint reusing the drafter LLM config; validates the label against the taxonomy, clamps confidence, raises ClassifierUnavailable on any transport/HTTP/parse/out-of-taxonomy failure), HybridIntentClassifier (falls back to deterministic, tagging source=fallback via dataclasses.replace), and select_intent_classifier(config) mirroring drafter_factory. PlannerConfig gains intent_llm_enabled (PLANNER_INTENT_LLM_ENABLED, default off); PlanningAgent now defaults its classifier via the factory. Added test_intent_llm.py (10 cases, HTTP mocked).
why: The proposal calls for LLM-assisted planning; the classifier must be able to use the model when available but never depend on it. Mirroring the drafter deterministic-default+clean-fallback pattern keeps the LLM-off build reproducible and guarantees a valid label even when the endpoint is down or misbehaves.

summary: Intent Classification (4/8): the drafters now consume the classified intent so it changes routing, not just decoration. PlanDrafter/HybridDrafter/LLM drafter gain an optional intent param (threaded from the classify node). DeterministicDrafter: a correlation intent pulls in a live, card-valid join partner and declares the canonical join when keyword routing found only one side; the name/id-lookup rescue now fires for a definitional question OR any in-scope intent naming a concrete entity id (mentions_entity_id), so bare lookups (Look up CAPEC-555) and id traversals (up from CAPEC-16) route instead of dropping. The LLM drafter prompt is given the classified intent as a hint. Fixed a classifier false positive (the word attack in the CAPEC term attack pattern no longer flags cross-source). Added drafter/intent tests and updated drafter stubs; regenerated the generated corpus (37->43 cases: bare/id lookups are now routable).
why: Intent is only meaningful if it alters the plan. Correlation-driven partner pull-in and id-aware rescue make the label load-bearing while the gate still validates every added sub-question, so nothing unsafe ships. The corpus is snapshot-derived from agent behaviour, so improved routability legitimately grows it; over-routing is surfaced as reduced precision, not hidden. Precise per-source id-routing (route a CAPEC id only to capec) is a clean follow-up.

summary: Intent Classification (5/8): the planner is now scored on intent. ExpectedCase gains expected_intent; scorer.py adds actual/expected_intent + intent_correct per case and intent_accuracy_rate (over intent-scored cases) to aggregate; build_corpus derives each generated cases expected_intent from an independent TEMPLATE_INTENT map (specialist template taxonomy, never the classifier itself); 4 curated anchors get hand-set intents. Refined the classifier so it agrees with that taxonomy: an id-bearing what-is is a lookup (checked before definitional), scan reads as enumeration, and membership (belong to) is no longer structural traversal. Corpus-wide intent accuracy is 0.979 (47 scored; the lone miss is a tactic literally named Defense Impairment tripping the remediation cue). component_report surfaces it via aggregate.
why: The proposal scores the planner on intent quality; without a measured number, classify-intent is unverifiable. Grounding expected_intent in the template taxonomy (not the classifier) makes the metric a real check rather than a tautology, and the honest sub-1.0 score documents a proper-noun edge case the LLM classifier is positioned to fix.

why: The front end must show, step by step, what the planner is doing; a distinct classifying phase makes step one animate as its own stage while the plan event delivers the label + confidence + cues the UI explains. A dedicated Intent step plus a what/why/how card turns the classifier from an invisible internal choice into an inspectable trust surface, and also elevates the plan rationale/cues that were already computed but never shown.

summary: Fix live SSE progress freezing on the first phase. The Next dev/prod server gzip-compresses proxied responses when the browser sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, and gzip buffers the event-stream — so the workbench showed only the first phase (Probing) for the whole run, then dumped the answer. Added no-transform to the Cache-Control on all four API SSE endpoints (query, conversation-query, admin, eval-run) in api/main.py, which tells the proxy compressor to leave the stream uncompressed. Verified through the proxy with browser-style gzip: Content-Encoding is gone and status(planning/answering) now arrive at ~0.04s, before the multi-second LLM waits, instead of being buffered to the end. Also gave LiveAnswerStatus + the ticker labels for the classifying/orchestrating phases (previously rendered as generic Working).
why: curl did not request gzip so the buffering never showed in API-level tests; only a real browser (Accept-Encoding: gzip) triggered it. no-transform is the HTTP-correct, portable fix — it also prevents SSE buffering behind production reverse proxies (nginx/cloudflare), not just the Next dev proxy.

summary: Smooth answer reveal in the workbench. Once the run reaches the answering phase (synthesis composing the answer), the pipeline menu (mini-stepper + intent card) now collapses smoothly (animated height/opacity) and the answer area shows a Composing the answer loader where the answer will land, then reveals the answer in place with a fade. Previously the pipeline stayed expanded and the Final Answer appeared abruptly. AnswerCard gains latestPhase() + a composing/collapseMenu derivation and a ComposingLoader; the collapse is disabled in the docked grounded card so the full pipeline stays visible there.
why: Analysts found the abrupt Final Answer transition confusing; collapsing the menu and showing an explicit composing loader makes the wait legible and shifts focus to the answer. Sets up the next step: streaming the answer tokens live into that same slot.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (1/6): added the Conflict contract and a standalone deterministic reconciler. utils/synthesis/contracts.py gains a frozen Conflict dataclass (join_value/kind/sources/values/authoritative_source/detail + to_dict/from_dict); ClaimVerdict gains a contested tuple (omitted from to_dict when empty) and VerificationReport gains conflicts + conflict_count/contested_count (also omitted when empty for byte-identity). New utils/synthesis/reconcile.py detects two well-founded cross-source contradiction classes over the federation evidence — name disagreement (normalized) and deprecated-yet-referenced — with a source-authority table; mapping contradictions are deliberately out of scope because the CAPEC->ATT&CK bridge is single-sourced. 6 reconciler unit tests incl. a no-false-positive corroboration case.
why: Closes the consistency axis the audit flagged PARTIAL: groundedness proved each claim traces to a real record, but nothing compared two retrieved records against each other. Building the reconciler as a pure function first makes the crux (what counts as incompatible) independently testable before it touches the verifier.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (2/6): the verifier now reconciles. verify_answer (utils/synthesis/verifier.py) runs detect_conflicts over the evidence after per-claim verdicts, attaches the conflicts to the VerificationReport, and marks (never cuts) the supported claims that assert a contested join value via ClaimVerdict.contested. Contested claims stay in rendered_claims — flag-not-cut, since both underlying records are real. Added verifier tests: a name-conflict claim stays supported+rendered+contested, and a conflict-free answer reports zero with a byte-identical report payload. 80 non-live synthesis tests pass; the 29 red are pre-existing live-DB goldens (empty backend, upstream of synthesis).
why: The verifier is the one mandatory deterministic gate every answer crosses, so it is the correct and only place to guarantee reconciliation runs. Flag-not-cut keeps genuinely-retrieved evidence visible while making the disagreement honest.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (3/6): confirmed the API/event seam carries conflicts. api/services/query.py already emits answer.synthesis as SynthesizedAnswer.to_dict(), so conflicts + contested verdicts propagate on the answer SSE event for free; added a seam assertion in test_verifier proving payload.verification.conflicts and claims[].verdict.contested serialize. Verified 62 api tests + all non-live synthesis tests stay green with empty-case payloads byte-identical (omit-when-empty), so no event/golden drift when there are no conflicts.
why: The golden/event-parity suites pin exact payload shapes; this step proves the empty case is unchanged and adds a populated assertion so a regression that drops conflicts on the wire fails loudly. No new endpoint is introduced.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (4/6): front-end view model projects conflicts. web/lib/types.ts gains ServerConflict + optional conflicts/conflict_count on SynthesisVerification, optional contested on SynthesisVerdict/SynthesisClaim, a UI-ready ConflictView, and conflicts[]/verification.conflictCount/claim.contested on the view. web/lib/adapt.ts buildSynthesis maps conflicts to ConflictView (per-source values sorted, authoritative flag) and stamps contested onto rendered claims. Also extended SynthesizedAnswer.to_dict (backend) to carry contested onto rendered_claims entries (omit-when-empty) so the UI badges the claim it renders. Updated fixtures + synthesisGraph helper for the new required fields; added adapter tests (conflict projection + contested claim + agreeing-payload has none). 175 web tests, production build, tsc clean; 80 non-live synthesis tests green.
why: The workbench renders only from the adapter's view model, so conflicts must be projected before any component shows them. Making the new fields optional/back-compatible keeps older captured payloads rendering unchanged, matching how edges and intent were introduced.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (5/6): the workbench surfaces conflicts. New web/components/center/ConflictPanel.tsx renders a 'Conflicting sources' panel (per-source values with the authoritative one marked) plus a compact ContestedBadge. AnswerCard's Verified Answers body now badges contested claims and renders the panel; the verification pill counts source conflict(s) and goes amber when any exist. ClaimTable rows carry the same contested badge. ticker.ts appends a 'reconcile: N source conflict(s)' line (amber) to the answer event so reconciliation reads as a visible step. tsc + production build clean, 175 web tests pass; the running app loads with no console errors. The conflict rendering itself is exercised by the adapter unit tests (seeded fixtures are test-only; live conflicts are data-dependent since curated ATT&CK/CAPEC rarely disagree).
why: The maintainer's standing goal is that every backend decision be legible step-by-step in the UI. A badge keeps a real-but-contested claim honest at the point of reading, the panel gives the full what/why (which sources, which values, who is authoritative), and the ticker line makes the reconcile step happen visibly — mirroring the intent what/why/how surface.

summary: Conflicting-Evidence Detection (6/6): eval metric + docs + full regression. JudgeVerdict gains a deterministic conflict_count (from the verifier, LLM judge never sets it); JudgeReport rolls up total_conflicts + answers_with_conflicts and e2e_report prints a cross-source-conflicts line. New docs/conflict-detection.md documents the taxonomy (name/status), the single-sourced-bridge scoping, flag-not-cut, authority, on-the-wire/UI, and evaluation; structure.md updated for reconcile.py + the front-end Conflicting-sources panel/badge. Full regression green: 1153 utils+api pass / 215 live-deselected (ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5), 175 web vitest, production build + tsc clean.

summary: One-shot setup wizard: python3 setup.py takes a fresh clone to a running workbench. Stage 1 (root setup.py, pure stdlib — NOT a setuptools file; the build backend is hatchling) finds uv (offering the official installer), runs uv sync, and re-execs stage 2 via uv run python -m utils.setup_wizard. Stage 2 (new utils/setup_wizard/: orchestrator, steps, ui) drives four steps through a describe → detect (idempotency probe) → run → retry/skip/abort contract: prerequisites (npm/node/docker CLI+compose+daemon), .env (copy .env.example; optional customization of ports — with derived NEO4J_URI/GREMLIN_URI kept consistent — Neo4j login via create_neo4j_login, and LLM endpoints across all five *_LLM_* groups), the data pipeline (delegated wholesale to YoloRunner), and web deps (app.ensure_web_dependencies). Finishes by exec-ing app.py --skip-install (new --open flag opens the browser once the stack is ready) or printing the command under --no-launch. Flags: --yes/--fresh/--skip-{sync,env,data,web}/--no-launch/--no-browser/--prod. 28 hermetic tests. Cleanups it forced: stale read-skills console script removed from pyproject (utils/skills was deleted long ago) and its README/skill-doc mentions replaced; yolo _read_runtime_manifest fixed to read load-manifest.json (hyphen — it never matched, so per-load node counts were silently dropped); README Setup section is now the one-liner with the manual steps in a details block.
why: Packaging goal: onboarding was ~10 commands across two toolchains; now one interactive command that shows each step, skips finished work on re-runs, and hands off to the launcher that proves the stack. Verified: 28 wizard tests green; --yes run on the live repo goes all-green and a re-run skips everything; the wizard load_env fix was caught live when a skipped .env step let YoloRunner run with default Neo4j credentials.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (plan on record): added docs/plans/universal-node-extraction-plan.md. The plan replaces the 24-template query registry (15 Cypher + 9 Gremlin) with two schema-agnostic primitives, describe (full node properties + a bounded facet block) and expand (one facet, identity-only, paged with explicit truncation), plus a canonical-derived schema registry, a deterministic anchor resolver, evidence-contract carry-through, and wiring into the existing assess/replan loop. Seven implementation steps, each validated and committed.
why: Committing the plan before implementation makes the step sequence, file blast-radius, and validation gates explicit and reviewable, matching the repo's plan-on-record convention.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (1/7): canonical-derived schema registry + Neo4j property unpacking. New utils/specialists/schema/ (registry.py: DatasetSchema/SchemaRegistry/PlausibleFacet; build.py: walks canonical nodes.jsonl for label->property keys and relationships.jsonl for distinct (source_label, rel_type, target_label) triples, resolving endpoint ids to labels, with a process-cached get_registry(); degree_stats.py: reproduces the plan's degree/facet appendix). label_facets() emits plausible facets in BOTH directions per label (the inbound-visibility the Gremlin dossier lost) and facet_exists() is the structural check the Step-7 validators will use. utils/graph_loader/stores/neo4j.py gains a module-level unpack_properties() that JSON-parses the flattened properties_json blob on read so describe can return every property without a graph reload. SourceCardView gains label_facets()/label_property_keys()/schema_registry() accessors (lazy import, no planner<->specialists cycle).
why: Both universal primitives depend on this foundation: describe cannot enumerate 'all properties' against a JSON string blob, and a facet block cannot show honest zeros without knowing which facets are plausible for a label. Deriving from canonical artifacts (not live DB introspection) keeps it available offline, in hermetic tests, and without Neo4j. degree_stats reproduces the plan's appendix exactly (attack max_degree 858 / 450 nodes over the cap of 25 / max 7 facet rows), guarding against a neighbour cap creeping back in.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (2/7): deterministic anchor resolver. Converted utils/specialists/resolve.py into a package (resolve/__init__.py, unchanged behavior; fixed the now-parent-relative concepts/contracts imports) and added resolve/resolver.py: resolve_anchor() walks a ladder (planner seed id -> exact id in text -> known name/alias -> fuzzy name), returning a ResolvedAnchor for a single candidate or an AmbiguousAnchor carrying every candidate when a tier yields more than one, so ambiguity propagates instead of being silently collapsed to the first match. infer_label() derives a node label from an id's shape; the alias tier takes an optional injected index (the alias source is a flagged open question, so no canonical alias index is built in the hot path). 12 resolver tests (exact id, seed-id precedence, fuzzy/alias title, two-id and two-name ambiguity, id-beats-title, miss, CAPEC native priority). Updated two doc path cites (resolve.py -> resolve/).
why: Today the difference between getting a description and getting nothing is whether the user's phrasing matched a regex — the most arbitrary failure mode in the system. The ladder replaces it with a deterministic path that always lands on a node or honestly reports it landed on several. SCOPE NOTE: the plan slotted the is_dossier_intent/is_definitional_intent deletion here, but those regexes exist only to gate the dossier/name-dossier templates (and the planner's definitional classification) that describe replaces in Step 3 — deleting them now would turn every bare-id task into a dossier and break template tests the plan only rewrites in Step 7. So the resolver lands additively here and the regex removal + planner/composer repoint moves to Step 3, where describe subsumes those templates.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (3/7): the describe primitive. New utils/specialists/primitives/describe.py (DescribeRequest/DescribeResult/Facet + fold_facets/facets_from_count_rows/merge_zero_facets/merge_with_card). Both builders gain a _describe() compiler: Cypher aggregates the 1-hop neighbourhood server-side into a facet block (type(r), startNode(r)=n, head(labels(m)), count(*)) returning n.properties_json; Gremlin projects out/inE reduced to (rel,neighbour label) and folds client-side (CAPEC max degree 59). describe subsumes node_lookup/node_dossier(_by_name) and capec_lookup/capec_dossier(_by_name) — a seeded single-anchor task routes to describe unconditionally (no describe-verb gate); a seedless definitional-by-name question routes to describe_by_name; broad scans stay on label_scan/capec_scan. Both normalizers gained _normalize_describe returning EVERY property (deleted the _DOSSIER_ATTRS allow-lists) plus the facet block with honest zeros from the registry (Gremlin converts plausible rel types through gremlin_edge_label so CAN_FOLLOW matches CanFollow); deleted _DOSSIER_NEIGHBOR_CAP. EvidenceRecord gains a facets field (populated here, carried to synthesis in Step 5). Deleted is_dossier_intent/is_definitional_intent/_DOSSIER_INTENT_RE/_WHATIS_INTENT_RE from resolve; definitional intent detection moved to planner.intent.is_definitional_request (used by intent.py, drafter.py, the builders' by-name gate, and composer's abstention fallback — gated so a non-definitional dead end keeps the generic wording); definitional_name_terms is now unconditional. Regenerated the derived evalset banks + planner corpus (node_lookup/capec_lookup -> describe; TEMPLATE_INTENT/_POOL_BY_TEMPLATE gain describe). Validated live end-to-end: T1059 returns 7 facets incl. HAS_SUBTECHNIQUE out 13 / MITIGATES in 9; CAPEC-98 Phishing shows the previously-unroutable bidirectional CAN_FOLLOW in 2 / CAN_PRECEDE out 6.
why: This is the centre of the plan: the facet block gives the planner a complete, honest, bounded (<=13 rows, ~0.04KB) picture of a node's neighbourhood so it can decide what to fetch next with full information, instead of 25 arbitrary neighbours with 833 silently dropped. Removing the allow-lists and the cap ends the two forms of pre-deciding-what-matters. Full regression green: 544 specialists (incl. live golden/federated/score against the running Neo4j+Gremlin stack), 188 synthesis+conversation, 254 planner+graph_loader, api hermetic, all at ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (4/7): the expand primitive. New utils/specialists/primitives/expand.py (ExpandRequest, ExpandResult, paginate()) and expand() compilers on both builders. Cypher slices server-side (members[$skip..$end]) and reports the true size(members) AS total; Gremlin fetches the (bounded, <=59) member identities and the normalizer paginates. Both normalizers gain normalize_expand() returning an ExpandResult with members (id/name/label only), the real total, and an explicit truncated flag. Facet coordinates (rel_type/direction/target_label) come from a facet block the model saw, so expand is a typed, gate-validated traversal; the facet-sourced idents are regex-guarded before inlining. New SPECIALIST_EXPAND_PAGE_SIZE config knob (default 50). Fixed a CAPEC identity bug: expand member ids fullmatch the clean CAPEC/CWE id shapes so a composite child id (capec:attack-pattern:66:mitigation:0) keeps its own id instead of prefix-collapsing to the parent CAPEC-66. 19 primitive tests (8 describe + 11 expand); validated live end-to-end (T1059 HAS_SUBTECHNIQUE pages 5-of-13 truncated then the last 3 untruncated; CAPEC-98 CAN_PRECEDE 3-of-6).
why: expand returns identity only so a 519-neighbour fan-out is ~8KB not ~500KB; if the planner wants a member's full record it calls describe on it (the same primitive recursing). The paging signal is the point: total:858, truncated:true is an honest answer the planner can act on, where the old cap of 25 was a lie by omission. Page size is a config knob pending the paging-policy product decision (plan Section 2). Full specialists regression green at 555 (incl. live).

summary: Universal Node Extraction (5/7): carry node properties, edge semantics, and facets through to synthesis. utils/synthesis/llm_composer.py _record_line now emits the record's properties (bounded: description survives whole, long strings marked-truncated, bulky external_references dropped with an _omitted_properties marker), the facet block (rel/direction/neighbour-label/count incl. honest zeros), and keeps type/direction/label on related entries — it previously dropped properties entirely and stripped edge type/direction, so the claims composer and (via the shared build_evidence_context) the prose narrator wrote with zero access to what a node is or how it connects. utils/conversation/agents/answer.py evidence_brief gains a per-record Neighbourhood line summarising the live (count>0) facets (with a signalled +N-more cut), since a describe record carries facet counts rather than individual neighbours; _MAX_BRIEF_CHARS re-tuned 3000->4000 for the extra line. New carry-through regression guards: build_evidence_context contains the description, the facet block, and edge direction (the _record_line regression the plan calls out); the brief surfaces the facet neighbourhood.
why: This is an independent bug worth fixing on its own: the normalizers compute edge direction/type and (now) facets correctly, and _record_line filtered them out one layer later, so only the final answer agent ever saw a description. Steps 3-4 made more evidence available; this ensures it survives the trip to the model that writes the answer. 191 synthesis+conversation tests green.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (6/7): wire describe/expand facets into the assess loop. utils/orchestration/agents/assess/frontier.py gains extract_facet_frontier(): every unexpanded, non-zero facet becomes an (anchor_id, rel, direction, neighbour_label, source) expand-worthy frontier entry (a count-0 facet is an honest absence, not a frontier). policy.py exposes expandable_facets(evidence) over it — the pool a facet-driven re-plan or an LLM critic turns into ExpandRequests. This is precisely the frontier the templates never produced, which is why the retrieval loop (bundle->assess->replan->specialists, ORCH_MAX_HOPS default 5) was live but inert. Drive-by: corrected main.py's stale docstring that claimed ORCH_MAX_HOPS=1 is 'the default' (config.py sets 5). Kept the facet frontier deliberately OUT of the reproducible deterministic join-closure verdict so the byte-reproducible LLM-off termination guarantee is unchanged. 6 new tests; full orchestration suite green (53).
why: The plan's insight is that the loop was never defective — the templates simply never returned a frontier worth chasing; a facet block with MITIGATES x 6 is exactly such a frontier. SCOPE NOTE: the plan also slots the llm_drafter entities->anchors schema switch and the card_enrichment gloss deletion here, but those are coupled to the templates that still consume `entities` and are only removed in Step 7 — deleting the glosses or switching the (opt-in, off-by-default) LLM prompt to anchors now would degrade planning while the entities-based templates are still the routing path. They move to Step 7, co-located with template removal, so the planner refactor lands against a system where entities-based routing is actually gone. The deterministic planner (the tested authority) already routes single-anchor questions to describe via seed_ids/name_terms, so nothing is lost by the reorder.

summary: Universal Node Extraction (7/7): registry-backed structural validation of the primitive requests. New utils/specialists/schema/validate.py: expand_request_reasons() checks an ExpandRequest's (anchor_label, rel, direction, target_label) against the registry's real triples (facet_exists), and describe_request_reasons() checks an anchor's inferred label — validating a STRUCTURED request against the canonical schema instead of matching a query STRING with regexes. This is strictly stronger than the legacy _REL_TYPE_RE/_TRAVERSAL_STEP_RE checks and, in particular, catches the bidirectional facets (CanFollow in/out, -[r]- untyped, .outE()/.inE()) that the query-string validators' documented hole let slip through. 7 tests. SCOPE: the dossier/lookup templates (node_lookup, node_dossier(_by_name), capec_lookup, capec_dossier(_by_name)) were already deleted in Step 3 when describe subsumed them. The remaining COMPOUND templates (technique_mitigations, group_techniques, capec_neighbors, ...) and the wholesale replacement of the regex validators are NOT deleted here: their describe+expand replacement for multi-entity questions depends on the autonomous facet-expansion re-plan loop, which Step 6 intentionally deferred (it is substantial new machinery that would risk the tuned join-closure loop and regress the golden suite, whose assertions pin the compound templates' exact related-id sets). The registry-backed validator lands ready for that loop; the compound-template removal + validator swap + planner anchor-switch + card_enrichment gloss deletion are the documented remaining work.
why: Validating a structured primitive request against the registry fails at plan time instead of returning a silently-empty result, and is the natural check once the model emits anchors + facet selections. Deleting the compound templates without the facet-expansion loop would turn a request like 'mitigations for T1055' into a bare facet COUNT (describe) with no way to list the members, breaking the golden must_include_related assertions — so the safe, additive validator ships now and the coupled deletions wait for the loop. Schema suite green (18).

summary: Deterministic Conversation Anchoring (1/4): added conversation_anchor() and referential_followup() pure helpers to utils/conversation/persistence.py. conversation_anchor(turns) returns the thread's focus entities (id, name) most-relevant-first — the most recent dossier-holding turn's ids first, then entity ids found in recent turn text as a no-dossier fallback — reusing the existing dossiers_from_turns/_recent_dossier_ids/entity_ids_in machinery. referential_followup(question) is a conservative cue detector (back-referring pronouns/determiners, facet follow-up verbs, sentence-initial connectives) marking a message as a thread continuation. 5 new tests; test_persistence green (16).
why: Root-cause fix groundwork: a follow-up like 'explore the execution steps involved' lost the just-discussed attack pattern because conversation context reached the planner only through a best-effort LLM rewrite that silently fell back to the raw question when the LLM was unavailable. These LLM-free helpers compute the anchor deterministically so a later step can fold it into the resolved question regardless of LLM health.

summary: Deterministic Conversation Anchoring (2/4): threaded the anchor through the conversation graph. utils/conversation/state.py ConversationState gains an anchor: list[(id,name)] input; iter_conversation (main.py) accepts anchor= and seeds it into the initial state. utils/conversation/agents/orchestration.py adds anchor_question(): after reference resolution, when the resolved question names no entity AND the original message reads as a continuation AND an anchor is held, it deterministically appends '(Regarding <id> - <name>.)' and marks the emitted context event anchored/anchor_id. 2 new graph tests (LLM-off anchoring; standalone question left untouched); full conversation suite green (111).
why: The orchestration node is the single seam every turn passes through and already owns resolved_question, so folding the deterministic anchor here fixes both the graph and quick routes with no change to iter_pipeline or PlanningAgent signatures. It fires precisely in the failure mode that lost context — the reference-resolution LLM unavailable so resolved is the raw follow-up — giving the planner a concrete entity to route on regardless of LLM health.

summary: Deterministic Conversation Anchoring (3/4): api/services/conversations.py stream_conversation_events now derives anchor = conversation_anchor(turns) from the stored thread (alongside the existing history/memory rebuild) and passes anchor= into iter_conversation. The anchored resolved_question already flows through acc['resolved_question'] via the context event, so the anchored form is what gets persisted as the assistant turn's question and carried into the next turn. New api test: an entity-free follow-up ('Please explore the mitigations involved.') after an M1049 turn reaches the extraction runner with 'M1049' embedded and context.anchored true, with the reference-resolution LLM OFF (default). api conversation suite green (12).
why: The API service is the only layer holding the raw turns, so it is where the deterministic anchor must be derived and injected — a one-line addition reusing the existing turns fetch with no extra store round-trip. This test is the end-to-end proof of the reported failure being fixed under the exact LLM-unavailable condition of the transcript.

summary: Deterministic Conversation Anchoring (4/4): added the transcript-faithful regression. api/tests/test_conversations.py test_followup_anchors_via_answer_text_when_no_dossier reproduces the exact reported shape — turn 1 answers about CAPEC-459 with NO stored dossier (the id appears only in the prose), then turn 2 'Please explore the execution steps involved.' with the reference-resolution LLM OFF must still reach the planner with 'CAPEC-459' embedded via the text-level anchor fallback. Full conversation + api conversation suites green (124).
why: Locks in the precise failure the user reported (entity-free follow-up losing the just-discussed CAPEC-459 and returning all 794 ExecutionStep nodes) under the exact LLM-unavailable condition, exercising the id-in-text fallback path distinct from the dossier path Step 3 covered, so a future refactor of the rewrite seam cannot silently reintroduce statelessness.

summary: Deterministic Conversation Anchoring (5/5, hardening): grounded the anchor in retrieved evidence instead of answer prose. Live verification exposed a defect — conversation_anchor scanned assistant final_answer text for ids, so a turn-1 'couldn't find it' reply that printed EXAMPLE ids ('try an id like T1566, M1017, or CAPEC-98') wrongly anchored a follow-up to CAPEC-98. utils/conversation/persistence.py: conversation_anchor now draws only from authoritative sources — dossiers, the focused primary ids the turn actually retrieved (new retrieved_anchor_ids(evidence), capped at 4 distinct entities so a broad list is not an anchor), and ids the USER typed in prior questions — never assistant answer text. api/services/conversations.py persists retrieved_ids on the assistant turn. Tests updated: retrieved-id + user-typed-id anchor paths, a regression guard that answer-prose example ids do NOT anchor, and an api guard that a turn-1 miss does not anchor a follow-up. 40 conversation+api-conversation tests green; live re-verification confirmed T1566 follow-up anchors to T1566 with a correctly SCOPED mitigations traversal (the prior unscoped LIMIT-1000 dump was a downstream effect of the wrong CAPEC-98 anchor).
why: Pulling entity ids from free-text answers cannot distinguish a real retrieved entity from an example/hallucinated id the model prints, which produced a confidently wrong anchor live. Grounding in what the graph actually returned makes anchoring trustworthy and, as a bonus, lets the drafter emit an entity-scoped traversal instead of a list dump.

summary: Describe label bug fix: an id-anchored describe now uses the seed id's own shape as the label instead of a wrong text/planner-attached label. utils/specialists/cypher/builder.py _describe_label previously preferred resolved.primary_label() over the seed-id prefix inference, so 'What is T1566?' (where the deterministic planner falls back to entities=['Analytic']) compiled to MATCH (n:Analytic) WHERE n.attack_id IN ['T1566'] and returned zero rows. It now checks the seed-id prefix map first (T1566 -> Technique, verified live: :Technique matches, :Analytic does not), falling back to the resolved label then Technique only when no seed id is present. New regression test; describe suite green; no new failures across the specialists+planner suites (73 pre-existing live/env failures unchanged).
why: Discovered during live verification of conversation anchoring: even a correctly anchored follow-up returned nothing because the describe primitive mislabeled the well-formed id. An identifier's shape is authoritative (T1566 IS a Technique), so it must win over a label guessed from question text or a planner probe fallback. Directly strengthens the LLM-down deterministic path.

summary: Conversation LLM budget fix: the router/validation/orchestration/naming agents now use config.llm.max_tokens instead of tiny hard-coded budgets (200/300/200/16). Root cause: the configured model 'skynet' is a reasoning model that spends ~2000 completion tokens thinking before emitting any content, so at max_tokens=300 it hit finish_reason=length with empty content and complete() raised LLMUnavailable every turn — surfacing as 'validation LLM unavailable' and forcing deterministic fallbacks for reference resolution, quick/graph routing, validation, and auto-titling (only the answer node, which already used config.llm.max_tokens=2048, and the planner at PLANNER_LLM_MAX_TOKENS=2048 worked). Verified live: at 2048 skynet returns finish_reason=stop with proper JSON; after the fix router/validation emit real verdicts, the orchestration LLM rewrite fires ('this Exploit' -> 'the mitigations and weaknesses of Creating a Rogue Certification Authority Certificate (CAPEC-459) exploit'), and validation correctly flags a facet-count-only answer as insufficient. Regression test asserts the budget is inherited; 115 conversation tests green.
why: The whole conversation intelligence layer was silently disabled by a token budget tuned for a non-reasoning model. One operator knob (config.llm.max_tokens, already honored by the answer node) should size every conversation call so reasoning models get enough headroom to reach their answer.

summary: Native facet expansion for CAPEC anchors (describe/expand over the entity's own edges). utils/specialists/gremlin/builder.py: when a question is anchored to a CAPEC pattern and names its native facet relationships (HAS_MITIGATION, EXPLOITS_WEAKNESS, HAS_EXECUTION_STEP, ...), the builder now traverses those edges directly — a single-facet request routes to capec_neighbors and a multi-facet request ('the mitigations AND weaknesses of X') to a new capec_facets union query returning every requested facet's members. New _resolve_neighbor_rels() reads both resolved relationships and requested neighbour labels (Mitigation->HAS_MITIGATION); the diversion is gated to CAPEC-seeded tasks with no cross-source mapping intent (_has_mapping_intent: MAPS_TO/TaxonomyEntry/Technique/SubTechnique) so genuine CAPEC->ATT&CK bridge questions still route to capec_maps_to and CWE-/ATT&CK-seeded tasks keep their chains. Removed the now-unused singular _resolve_neighbor_rel. 5 new tests (multi-facet beats spurious join, mapping-intent keeps maps_to, label-only maps to native edge, validator accepts the union); zero new failures across the specialists suite (only the pre-existing ORCH_MAX_HOPS event-order failure remains). Verified live: 'Explain the mitigations and weaknesses of CAPEC-459' now answers with CWE-290/295/327 + the native mitigation instead of 'couldn't find'.
why: The drafter mislabelled 'mitigations and weaknesses of CAPEC-459' as a cross-source join to ATT&CK, but CAPEC-459 has no MAPS_TO edge, so the join returned nothing while the answer sat one hop away on the entity's own HAS_MITIGATION/EXPLOITS_WEAKNESS edges. Grounding an anchored facet question on the entity's native neighbourhood is general (no per-phrasing rules) and robust to the exact open-ended wording the user hit.

summary: Make the api conversation contract tests hermetic. api/tests/test_conversations.py temp_store fixture now forces CONVERSATION_LLM_ENABLED=false. These tests inject deterministic runners/stub naming clients and assert the deterministic anchor/route/validation path, but the developer .env sets CONVERSATION_LLM_ENABLED=true, so they were silently hitting the live skynet endpoint every turn — previously masked because the tiny token budgets truncated it to 'unavailable'; once the budget fix let the LLM actually respond, the live orchestration rewrite pulled example ids ('T1566, CAPEC-98') out of a turn-1 'couldn't find it' answer into the resolved question and two deterministic-anchor regression guards failed (and the suite took 100s). With the LLM pinned off the suite is deterministic and runs in 0.35s (14 passed).
why: The suite's own docstring promises no live backend; a latent env dependency broke that once the conversation LLM started working. Pinning it off restores hermeticity and keeps the deterministic-anchor guards meaningful. Note surfaced for follow-up: with the LLM on, the orchestration rewrite can reintroduce the hallucinated-id anchor the deterministic path was built to avoid — the evidence-grounded anchor still stands, but the LLM rewrite has no such discipline.

summary: Carry a related neighbour's description into synthesis. utils/synthesis/llm_composer.py _record_line rendered each related entry with an id/name/type/direction/label whitelist that DROPPED the neighbour's description, so the composer wrote answers blind to a neighbour whose text is its only content.
