A CAPEC Mitigation node has no name — its description ('Certification Authorities need to stop using deprecated... use SHA-256 or SHA-512') is the whole answer — so 'investigate that mitigation' reported 'no description available' even though HAS_MITIGATION expansion retrieved the node. New _related_entry() keeps the identity/edge-semantics AND a bounded (400-char, truncation-marked) description. 3 new tests; synthesis suite green (169); verified live end-to-end: turns 2 and 3 now state the SHA-256/512 mitigation text.
why: Universal Node Extraction step 5 carried the PRIMARY record's properties to the composer but left related neighbours identity-only, which is invisible for an unnamed node like a CAPEC mitigation/consequence whose description carries the substance. The facet-expansion work retrieves those neighbours; this ensures their text survives the last hop to the model that writes the answer.

summary: Structural invariant: a targeted neighbour always carries its description. Two changes make 'return the entity's substance' a guarantee instead of a per-template accident. (1) Live gap — the cypher compound templates (technique_mitigations, technique_detection, ...) return a neighbour's id+name but leave its description in the unretrieved properties_json; a new CypherNormalizer.enrich_descriptions(records, connector), called once at the shared specialist chokepoint (utils/specialists/base.py after normalize, best-effort), batch-hydrates every related neighbour's bounded description from properties_json in one lookup — so ATT&CK facet answers now state each mitigation's substance regardless of which listing template ran. (2) Hardened the expand primitive (both backends) to carry a BOUNDED (400-char) description per member: gremlin projects values('description'); cypher collects node refs, slices to the page, THEN materializes properties_json only for that page (so a 519-neighbour fan-out stays a page of summaries, not full records) and the normalizer extracts a bounded description. Updated the expand docstrings (no longer identity-only). 6 new/updated tests; specialists+synthesis green (737 passed, only the pre-existing ORCH_MAX_HOPS event-order failure). Verified live: 'what mitigations apply to T1566 and what does each involve' now answers with each mitigation's description (Audit=recording/reviewing activity, User Training=educate employees, ...).
why: Descriptions were carried ad-hoc per template — describe/capec_neighbors via full properties, but expand and the ATT&CK compound templates identity-only — so whether an answer had substance depended on which template the planner happened to pick. Enforcing the description at one chokepoint (hydration) plus in the expand contract makes it a property of retrieval, not of the LLM remembering to ask, which is the reliable way for the agent to 'know its task'.

summary: Run the LLM judge calls concurrently in the e2e evaluation. judge_run (utils/evaluation/llm_judge/factory.py) was fully sequential: for a run that LLM-judges N answers it made N blocking requests.post calls back-to-back, so the judge phase dominated wall-clock (~62s for 10 skynet calls) while the live pipeline phase itself finished in ~3s. The LLM judge calls are independent and stateless (each is a fresh requests.post with no shared client), so they now run in a ThreadPoolExecutor with EVAL_LLM_JUDGE_WORKERS (default 8) workers; verdicts are written back by index so the emitted report is byte-identical to the sequential path — deterministic-proxy answers (index >= sample_size) still computed inline, order and llm_covered counting unchanged. New config knob EvalConfig.judge_workers (utils/evaluation/llm_judge/config.py). Verified: 12 judge unit tests green; live --e2e-eval --judge judge phase dropped ~62s -> ~22s (~3x, throughput-bound on the single local model as predicted), and a before/after diff of the 10 verdicts shows identical qids/order/scores and unchanged mean_evidence_sufficiency=0.975.
why: The judge is ~95% of the e2e run's wall-clock and the calls are embarrassingly parallel, so a thread pool is the highest-leverage speedup; placing verdicts back by index keeps the report reproducible so nothing downstream changes. The win scales with EVAL_LLM_SAMPLE_SIZE — judging all 120 answers benefits far more than the default 10. Related: the max_tokens=64000 > model 48000-token window bug that was silently forcing the deterministic-proxy fallback (fixed in the gitignored .env alongside this).

summary: Quiet the gremlin-python client-lifecycle log flood. main.py _setup_logging now raises the 'gremlinpython' logger to WARNING. The library logs 'Creating Client'/'Closing Client' at INFO on every connect/close, and SpecialistBase.run (utils/specialists/base.py) opens a fresh client per task and closes it in its finally, so a batch job like --e2e-eval emitted one INFO pair per entry (~120) and buried the real output. WARNING keeps genuine driver failures visible while dropping the per-task churn. Cosmetic only — no change to connection behaviour; verified --e2e-eval --judge now prints 0 Creating/Closing Client lines and the job start/status/completion lines are intact.
why: The connect-per-task lifecycle in the specialist is deliberate (each run is self-contained), so the noise is inherent to batch runs; silencing it at the third-party logger is the low-risk fix and does not touch the connection model. Root cause noted for any future move to a pooled/reused connector: base.py connect/close bracket every query.

summary: Judge the full LLM pipeline answer in --e2e-eval --judge, not just deterministic claims. Two coupled changes so the LLM judge grades the prose an analyst actually sees. (1) score_e2e.py: when the LLM judge is enabled, synthesize with SynthesisConfig.from_env() (LLM narrator ON) instead of the bare SynthesisConfig() (llm_enabled=False); non-judge runs stay deterministic so the four E2E metrics + report remain byte-reproducible (claims are composed deterministically either way, so only the narrative — which only the LLM judge reads — changes). (2) llm_judge.build_messages now includes the answer's prose narrative as 'ANSWER (prose shown to the analyst)' and the system prompt tells the judge to grade that prose against the claims+evidence as ground truth. Previously the judge scored only rendered_claims() (= the specialist summarize() id-line), so a rich, correct narrative like the CAPEC-66 execution steps was produced and then hidden from the judge, capping evidence_sufficiency. Root cause chain documented in memory ariadne-e2e-sufficiency-ceiling. Tests: evaluation + synthesis suites green (265). Also raised SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS 2048->8192 in the gitignored .env: at 2048 the skynet reasoning model intermittently returned empty (~1 in 4) and fell back to the thin deterministic narrative; 8192 gave 6/6 reliable narrations.
why: The e2e judge was grading the deterministic composer's existence-summary, not the full pipeline's answer, so evidence_sufficiency measured the wrong artifact and understated the system. Gating the LLM synthesis on the judge preserves the reproducible deterministic report while making the judged answer faithful to production. NOTE for follow-up: narration now runs once per answer inside the SEQUENTIAL pipeline loop in score_e2e, so a full 120-answer judged run is much slower (~sum of 120 narrator calls) than the deterministic path; parallelizing that loop is the next lever if full runs become painful. Also, full-LLM judging surfaces narrator hallucination the deterministic path hid (e.g. C-LKP-01 invented an abstraction level/status not in evidence) — expect faithfulness/groundedness to drop below the deterministic 1.0 ceiling, which is the honest signal.

summary: Cap synthesis reasoning tokens (thinking_token_budget) so the narrator stops returning empty. skynet is a reasoning model; uncapped it can spend the entire max_tokens budget on reasoning and return empty content, which surfaced as 'LLM narrator unavailable (model returned no content (raise max_tokens?))' and a silent fallback to the thin deterministic narrative — even at max_tokens=8192. Added SynthesisConfig.llm_thinking_budget (env SYNTHESIS_LLM_THINKING_BUDGET; 0 = half of llm_max_tokens) and a thinking_budget() helper, and both synthesis LLM payloads (narrator.compose_narrative, llm_composer._post) now send thinking_token_budget. Verified against the live skynet endpoint: the server accepts the param (no HTTP 400) and it fixes the failure mode — at a tight max_tokens=2048 uncapped thinking fell back ~1 in 4, with thinking capped to 1024 it was 0 fallbacks in 8; at 8192/4096 it was 8/8 rich. .env set SYNTHESIS_LLM_THINKING_BUDGET=4096. synthesis suite green (169).
why: Raising max_tokens alone did not make narration reliable because a reasoning model scales its thinking to fill whatever budget it is given; the fix is to bound reasoning explicitly and reserve output headroom. This is what actually makes the full-LLM judged run (commit ae8da43) engage the narrator on every answer instead of intermittently. Same knob could be added to the planner/specialist/judge callers if they show the same empty-return symptom — see memory ariadne-skynet-reasoning-budget.

summary: Add a decoupled, parallel generate-only phase for the e2e evaluation. New utils/evaluation/generate_e2e.py runs the assembled pipeline over the whole golden catalogue and persists every answer + the logic/evidence needed to judge it, WITHOUT scoring — so the answer set can be graded by an independent model rather than self-judged. Parallelism is exactly --workers threads (default 4); each worker owns its own SpecialistRouter set via thread-local storage because the Gremlin connector opens/closes a client per task and is not thread-safe to share. Synthesis runs with the LLM narrator on (SynthesisConfig.from_env). Writes one docs/evaluation/answers/<id>.json per case (question, gold assertions, answer narrative+claims+abstentions, logic_flow = plan/sub-questions + per-specialist query+traces, evidence records WITH related-neighbour descriptions, deterministic metric scores) plus manifest.json. Wired main.py --e2e-generate [--e2e-workers N]. Validated live: 120/120 generated, 0 narrator fallbacks; the 19 zero-record cases are all adversarial negatives/boundary/partial where empty is the correct answer.
why: The e2e report never persisted the actual answers (only scores), and the LLM judge was the same skynet model that wrote them — self-judgment the user (rightly) distrusts. Separating generation (save answers) from judging (independent graders) makes the answer set inspectable and lets a different model score correctness against the gold assertions. 4 workers cut wall-clock ~4x with no shared-connector races. The judging step itself is an out-of-band panel of Sonnet-5 agents (one per case) orchestrated separately, not a CLI job.

summary: Add robust front-end handling for stalled answer streams so a hung backend no longer spins 'Composing the answer' indefinitely. New web/lib/streamConfig.ts holds client resilience thresholds (SSE_STALL_MS default 90s, SSE_SLOW_MS default 25s, both NEXT_PUBLIC_-overridable). web/lib/api.ts postSseStream now races each reader.read() against an inactivity timer that resets on every chunk; on silence past the budget it cancels the reader and throws a new SseStallError. Because the watchdog throws (rather than aborting the user AbortSignal), the existing runMachine catch surfaces it via setError + status:'partial', so the AnswerError card renders. ComposingLoader (AnswerCard.tsx) now ticks its own elapsed time and, past SSE_SLOW_MS, escalates to an amber 'taking longer than usual' note. Added web/lib/__tests__/streamStall.test.ts (3 cases: stall fires, timer resets per chunk, normal run completes). web suite 191 green, npm run build + changed-file lint clean.
why: A silently stalled SSE stream (e.g. the synthesis narrator hanging with no terminal event) left the client's reader.read() blocked forever with no timeout, heartbeat, or watchdog — the loader spun for 2+ hours with no way to know an issue had arisen. The client now converts inactivity into a visible error within ~90s and gives progressive status before then, so failures are observable instead of indistinguishable from slow work. Frontend-only per the request; a backend SSE heartbeat remains a possible follow-up to let the watchdog distinguish 'alive but working' from 'dead' and tighten the threshold.

summary: Fix the e2e judging serializer (generate_e2e._record_dict) so it shows the judge the same evidence the narrator saw. It previously kept only a record's description and dropped every other property plus the facets adjacency counts, and capped records at 40 (below the narrator's 50). Now it emits a bounded properties block (Abstraction/Status/... via a _bounded_properties helper mirroring llm_composer), the facets list, related-neighbour role/type/direction, and a 50-record cap. Added utils/evaluation/tests/test_generate_e2e.py (6 cases). Evaluation suite green (43).
why: The independent Sonnet panel flagged faithful, grounded answers as hallucinations (C-LKP abstraction/status, A-CMP counts, A-SCN ids beyond 40) purely because the judging artifact hid the evidence that grounded them — a harness bug, not a pipeline fault. Correcting the serializer is the prerequisite for an un-penalized faithfulness/groundedness re-read of the 120-answer panel.

summary: Add an answer-coverage deterministic metric to the e2e scorer (score_e2e.score_answer_coverage + E2ECase.coverage + an 'answer_completeness' aggregate block). It scores the fraction of gold must_include_ids/must_include_related that the ANSWER actually surfaces (rendered-claim entity_ids + citations + ids named in the narrative), distinct from mapping_recall which measures retrieval into the pool. Added 5 hermetic tests. Evaluation suite green (48).
why: Under-enumeration was invisible to the deterministic scorers: the pipeline retrieves every id (mapping_recall ~1.0) yet the answer surfaces only a sample, so the skynet self-judge looked flawless while the independent panel found missing mitigations. This metric makes the gap deterministically measurable and becomes the cheap yardstick for validating the under-enumeration fix without re-running the 120-agent panel.

summary: Fix under-enumeration: the deterministic composer now emits a structured 'enumeration' claim that names the FULL related/primary id set for which/what questions, instead of the fact claim's 3-id sample. Two shapes: an anchor record with a large related set (techniques of a software, mitigations of a technique, consequences of a pattern), and a multi-record result whose primary ids are the answer set (the techniques a group uses). Added utils.planner.intent.is_enumerative_request (which/list + 'what <plural relationship-noun>', excluding bare entity-type ids). Softened the narrator prompt to defer the full list to the structured claim. Raised the judge serializer's related cap to 100 so it can see the whole set. Live-verified: A-SW-03 coverage 10/55->56/56, A-GRP-03 0/5->5/5, C-CSQ-01 0/4->5/5, A-MIT-05 4/9->10/10, A-SW-01 4/17->18/18. Suites green (synthesis+evaluation+planner 372).
why: Retrieval was already perfect but the composer surfaced only a sample of ids in prose, so 'which techniques / what mitigations / what consequences' answers were faithful yet grossly incomplete — the dominant defect the independent Sonnet panel found. A structured enumeration claim puts the complete, cited id set on the trust surface while keeping the prose short, which is the shape the user chose; the new answer-coverage metric (step 2) confirms full coverage.

summary: Fix C-ABS abstraction-hierarchy role labeling. The gremlin normalizer's _normalize_hierarchy flattened parent (standard) and grandparent (meta) ancestors into bare {id} related entries, so the narrator could not say which was which and once falsely claimed the ancestors were absent. It now tags each ancestor {id, role, name, abstraction} (role from the ancestor's own Abstraction property, else positional). 'ancestors/descendants' added to is_enumerative_request (gap widened to 6 words) so a structured enumeration claim surfaces and labels both ids; the enumeration claim annotates each id with its role ('CAPEC-66 (standard)'); llm_composer and the judge serializer now pass role/abstraction to the narrator/judge; the narrator prompt forbids claiming evidence lacks ids present in a related set. Live-verified C-ABS-01/02/03: coverage 0->3/3 and the narrative now names the standard vs meta ancestor correctly. Suites green (423).
why: The abstraction-walk questions were the only genuinely wrong answers (2 INCORRECT), including the run's one true hallucination (C-ABS-01 asserting absent evidence that was present). Preserving the parent/grandparent role through normalization restores the standard-vs-meta distinction the question demands and, via the deterministic enumeration claim, guarantees both ids are surfaced and labeled regardless of narrator variance.

summary: Brand the app + README with the new Ariadne logo art (images/logos/). Frontend: HeaderBar now renders the logo-only mark (web/public/ariadne-logo.svg) beside the wordmark instead of the inline ThreadGlyph; the browser-tab favicon is the same mark via the Next.js App Router web/app/icon.svg convention (and the stale generic web/public/favicon.svg is replaced with the logo). README: the plain '# Ariadne' heading becomes a centered logo banner using a <picture> element — WhiteText (name included) in dark mode, BlackText in light mode so the wordmark stays legible on GitHub's light theme — plus a centered tagline and tech-stack badges.
why: The workbench and GitHub landing page shipped with a placeholder thread glyph and a generic purple favicon that were not the project's actual logo. Swapping in the delivered logo art gives the app and repo a consistent, recognizable identity; the <picture> theme fallback honors the request to lead with WhiteText while keeping the name readable in both GitHub themes.

summary: Un-truncated retrieval experiment, step 1/3: make every retrieval/synthesis/artifact bound env-overridable and add the two-arm experiment runner (utils/evaluation/experiment_untruncated.py). Bounds now read through the env at CALL time with the committed defaults preserved, so normal runs are byte-identical: SPECIALIST_RELATED_DESC_CHARS / SPECIALIST_EXPAND_DESC_CHARS (normalizer neighbour + expand-member description caps, both 400); SYNTHESIS_MAX_{RECORDS_PER_RESULT,RELATED_PER_RECORD,FACETS_PER_RECORD,PROP_CHARS,RELATED_DESC_CHARS,PROP_LIST_ITEMS} (llm_composer evidence context, 50/30/20/600/400/10); SYNTHESIS_MAX_{ENUMERATION_IDS,ENUMERATION_CLAIMS} (deterministic composer, 200/25); EVAL_ARTIFACT_MAX_{RECORDS,RELATED,FACETS,DESC_CHARS,PROP_LIST_ITEMS} (the judge artifact serializer, 50/100/20/600/10). The runner drives the same 120 golden questions in the same order through two arms — A deterministic (gold-replay plan, no LLM anywhere, deterministic composer) and B llm (raw question through iter_pipeline(use_llm=True), LLM planning + LLM synthesis, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5) — under one common un-truncation profile, and lifts each bank task's authored max_result_rows (300) in memory so the committed banks/gold set/question order stay byte-identical.
why: The independent Sonnet panel's dominant real fault was under-enumeration and evidence the judge never saw: retrieval was fine but caps at three separate layers (per-task row limit, the composer's evidence context, the artifact serializer) sampled it away. To measure what un-truncating actually buys, the caps must be liftable as a profile rather than edited away — the committed defaults stay put so the change is reversible and the normal pipeline is unaffected, and the two arms isolate LLM planning/synthesis from the un-truncation itself.

summary: Un-truncated retrieval experiment, step 2/3: ARM A (deterministic) run + independently judged. All 120 golden questions replayed with no LLM anywhere (gold-replay plan, deterministic drafters, deterministic composer) under the un-truncation profile; 120 artifacts (answer + full retrieved evidence + executed queries) saved to docs/evaluation/experiments/untruncated/deterministic/answers/. A panel of 120 independent Sonnet 5 agents graded each case against its gold assertions AND the full evidence: correctness 0.9500, completeness 0.9534, faithfulness 0.9979, groundedness 0.9992; 112 CORRECT / 1 PARTIAL / 7 INCORRECT; ZERO hallucinations flagged across all 120. The 7 INCORRECT are two clean groups: (a) A-SCN-01/C-SCN-01 — un-truncation itself broke them, the gold asserts a bounded scan (max_records 300, which encoded the old per-task row cap) and lifting the cap returned 821 / 558 records; (b) C-LKP-01..05 — the deterministic composer never projects properties.Abstraction/Status into a claim even though the evidence carries them, so an attribute lookup answers 'Found 1 CAPEC record(s): CAPEC-555.' That is the still-open composer-projection ceiling, not a retrieval problem. Also adds utils/evaluation/summarize_untruncated.py (rolls both arms' judgments into summary.md/summary.json with deltas vs each other and vs the committed truncated baseline), and reloads the live CAPEC/Gremlin fixture, which was found empty (0 nodes) on entry — now 4,769 nodes / 6,972 edges.
why: Arm A is the reproducible control: it isolates what un-truncated retrieval alone does, with no LLM variance anywhere. Its result already answers two of the experiment's questions — un-truncation drives faithfulness/groundedness to ~1.0 with zero hallucinations because there is no narrator to invent anything, and it does NOT fix the attribute-lookup failures, which are a claim-projection gap rather than a retrieval gap. It also surfaces the cost: two bounded-scan gold assertions encode the very cap that was lifted.

summary: Un-truncated retrieval experiment, step 3/3: ARM B (LLM-planned) run + judged, and the two-arm summary. All 120 questions driven from raw text through iter_pipeline(use_llm=True) on skynet (LLM planning + LLM drafting + LLM synthesis, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5) under the same un-truncation profile; 120/120 in 973.6s. A second panel of 120 independent Sonnet 5 agents graded it: correctness 0.7660, completeness 0.7770, faithfulness 0.9479, groundedness 0.9517; 84 CORRECT / 11 PARTIAL / 25 INCORRECT; 18 hallucinations across 12 answers. Headline result: un-truncated DETERMINISTIC (Arm A) beats both the LLM arm and the committed truncated baseline on all four metrics (0.9500/0.9534/0.9979/0.9992 vs baseline 0.8946/0.8952/0.9558/0.9575) with ZERO hallucinations and mean answer coverage 1.0000 across all 66 scorable questions — every baseline weak category (C-ABS 0.17, C-CSQ 0.35, A-SW 0.45, F-CWE 0.59, A-GRP 0.76, A-CMP 0.86) goes to 1.00. Arm B is worse on 33 questions and better on 5; the 33 are planner failures (the federated two-hop join loses its seed: F-CTM 0.99->0.43, F-CWE 1.00->0.20, F-FAN 0.98->0.28, F-PART 1.00->0.35; wrong primitive on A-DET 0.98->0.20) plus 9 pipeline-deadline timeouts, not narration failures. The 5 wins are all C-LKP attribute lookups, where the narrator projects properties.Abstraction/Status that the deterministic composer never puts in a claim. Two costs of un-truncation recorded honestly: A-SCN-01/C-SCN-01 are INCORRECT in both arms because their gold asserts max_records 300 (the very cap lifted), and C-SCN-01/F-CWE-05 overflowed skynet's 64k context in Arm B and fell back to the deterministic narrative. Adds docs/evaluation/experiments/untruncated/{summary.md,summary.json,verdict.md} and a --verdict/cross-arm-disagreement section in the summarizer. NOTE: skynet was down (relay 502) at session start; an initial Arm B on the relay's 'local' model was stopped at 54/120 and discarded, so every Arm B number is from a clean skynet run on the same model as the baseline.
why: The experiment's question was what un-truncating retrieval actually buys, and whether the LLM path is safe to demo. The answer is that un-truncation plus the deterministic composer's structured enumeration claim fixes the entire under-enumeration class the independent panel flagged, while the LLM path regresses: it retrieves MORE evidence (3,401 records vs 1,840) and surfaces LESS of the gold (coverage 0.7989 vs 1.0000), because prose samples where a structured claim enumerates. Recommendation recorded for October: demo Arm A.

summary: Root-cause the eval regression and fix it: three real defects found, deterministic arm now 120/120 CORRECT. FIRST, a methodology correction: the committed baseline (generate_e2e.py) replays each entry's PRE-AUTHORED gold plan (seed_from: q1 hard-wires the federated join) with LLM synthesis, truncated — so neither Arm A nor Arm B differed from it in one variable, and the earlier claim that B-baseline isolated un-truncation was WRONG. Added ARM C (gold_llm) = the baseline's exact config with only the bounds lifted; it retrieved byte-identically to Arm A (1840 records/839 related), making the decomposition valid. Arm C scored 0.9620/0.9618/0.9779/0.9896 (109 CORRECT/9 PARTIAL/2 INCORRECT), i.e. C-baseline = +0.067 correctness, +0.067 completeness, +0.022 faithfulness, +0.032 groundedness — un-truncation was STRICTLY POSITIVE on all four and was never the regression. B-C = -0.196 correctness isolates the LLM planner as the entire cause. SECOND, added utils/evaluation/failure_terminus.py, which locates mechanically (from artifacts, not judge prose) the last stage at which the gold answer was recoverable: gold_cap_collision / pipeline_timeout / retrieval_empty / seed_lost / wrong_query / incomplete_retrieval / property_gap / projection_gap / unfaithful. It showed only 2 of Arm B's 36 failures are faithfulness; 26 of 36 are planning/retrieval. THIRD, three defects fixed: (1) llm_composer.build_evidence_context DROPPED every failed/dependency-skipped sub-question (no else branch) and never read evidence.skipped/unsupported/sequencing/partial, which the federation already populates — so the narrator saw an unanswered request with no reason and invented one ('None of the live graph sources cover this request' for a TIMEOUT). It now emits an execution record, and both system prompts forbid invented absence-explanations, unread counts, and unsupported tactic groupings. (2) The deterministic composer never projected a record's own properties into a claim, so all 5 C-LKP lookups answered 'Found 1 CAPEC record(s): CAPEC-555' while the evidence held Abstraction/Status — added _attribute_claims. (3) gremlin _normalize_neighbors canonicalised the ANCHOR's id but left the NEIGHBOUR's raw, so a CHILD_OF parent surfaced as 'capec:attack-pattern:560' and matched no gold; two tests had codified the bug (one's own message read "expected CWE-89" while asserting 'cwe:89'). (4) Un-truncation now skips PURELY QUANTITATIVE golds ({min_records:250,max_records:300} with no id/name/property assertion): there the row cap IS the answer's specification, not a sampling cap. Verified surgical — exactly 2 artifacts changed (821->300, 558->300), the other 118 materially identical. RESULT: the fixed deterministic arm scores correctness 0.9972, completeness 1.0000, faithfulness 0.9993, groundedness 1.0000, 120/120 CORRECT, 0 hallucinations — vs the committed baseline's 0.8946/0.8952/0.9558/0.9575, 91 CORRECT and 11 answers carrying hallucinations.
why: The user asked why the numbers looked worse than the committed baseline. They were not: the comparison was invalid because the baseline's federated join is hand-authored and Arm B had to discover it. Isolating that with Arm C showed un-truncation helps on every metric, and the failure-terminus pass turned 'the judge says it's wrong' into 'this exact stage lost the information', which is what made the three defects findable. Each fix is causally tied to a class the independent panel flagged, and the deterministic path is now clean enough to demo without caveats.

summary: Fix the planner defect behind 19 of Arm B's 36 failures: a declared join never reached its sub-questions. The LLM planner emits the plan-level join correctly (joins:[{key:'attack-technique-id',sources:['capec','attack']}]) but leaves each participating sub-question's own join_key NULL. The gremlin builder's template router keys on the SUB-QUESTION's field (has_join = resolved.has_join or resolved.join_key=='attack-technique-id'), so a null there silently downgrades the bridge hop from capec_maps_to (.out('MAPS_TO') -> produces join_values) to describe (.project('node','out','in') -> facet COUNTS only). With no join values the dependent hop then runs UNSEEDED and answers a broader question than the analyst asked. Verified on the failing cases: every Arm B q1 ran describe with 0 join values where the gold plan ran capec_maps_to with 6/3/2/10. Fix: Plan.reconcile_join_keys() pushes each declared join's key onto the sub-questions whose source participates (never overwriting an explicit value), applied at the end of PlanningAgent.plan, so routing depends on what the plan DECLARED rather than on which field the model happened to fill in. Verified end-to-end: 7 of 8 previously seed-lost cases now carry join_key='attack-technique-id' and produce join values matching the gold counts exactly; federated cases carrying join values 21/36 -> 29/37; total evidence records DROPPED 3401 -> 2814 because the bridge hop now runs the targeted traversal instead of an unseeded broad query. (C-MAP-02 still None — it is single-source CAPEC, so no plan-level join is declared; different cause.) Also adds docs/evaluation/experiments/untruncated/root-cause.md: the full decomposition (C-baseline isolates un-truncation at +0.067 correctness; B-C isolates LLM planning at -0.196), all four defects with the evidence for each, the arm table, what is still open, and four method traps (provenance timestamps make every artifact appear changed; module caching decides which code a background run used; judge agents drop 2-3 of 120 file writes; skynet reports healthy in /v1/models while 502-ing on completions).
why: This was the last unexplained cause and the largest single one — 19 of 36 Arm B failures traced to two representations of the same fact disagreeing, not to the LLM misunderstanding anything. Reconciling them makes cross-source routing robust to model formatting variance, which is the difference between a planner that can be demoed and one that cannot.

summary: Validate the planner fix end-to-end and close the root-cause analysis. Re-ran ARM B (LLM planning + LLM synthesis) with all five fixes and re-judged all 120 with the independent Sonnet panel: correctness 0.7660 -> 0.8505 (+0.085), completeness 0.7770 -> 0.8692 (+0.092), faithfulness 0.9479 -> 0.9683, groundedness 0.9517 -> 0.9750, verdicts 84/11/25 -> 92/14/14, hallucinations 18 -> 12. The failure-terminus pass confirms the fix removed exactly the class it targeted and only that class: seed_lost 8 -> 0 and retrieval_empty 2 -> 0, both eliminated. Mechanically verified: 7 of 8 previously seed-lost cases now carry join_key='attack-technique-id' and produce join values matching the gold counts exactly (6/5/3/2/1/10/7); federated cases carrying join values 21/36 -> 29/37. Counter-intuitively total evidence records FELL 3401 -> 2814 while answers improved, because the bridge hop now runs the targeted MAPS_TO traversal instead of an unseeded broad query — less evidence, better answers, the opposite of the premise the experiment started from. Final standings across six runs (corr/compl/faith/ground): committed baseline 0.8946/0.8952/0.9558/0.9575 (91/27/2, 11 hallucinations); A+fixes 0.9972/1.0000/0.9993/1.0000 (120/0/0, ZERO hallucinations); C+fixes 0.9690/0.9672/0.9921/0.9983 (110/8/2, 3); B+fixes 0.8505/0.8692/0.9683/0.9750 (92/14/14, 12). Deterministic synthesis is now strictly better than LLM synthesis on every metric — before the property-projection fix the narrator was the only thing that could answer an attribute question, and now it is not. root-cause.md records the remaining work, headed by the same defect in a second guise: the router still downgrades SINGLE-source questions to describe (11 of B2's 28 failures — A-SUB/C-ABS/C-HIE/C-MAP/F-CWE) because there is no join declaration to reconcile against; the fix is to route on the sub-question's declared `entities` (which name the relationship, e.g. ChildOf) rather than on surface phrasing.
why: Claiming a fix works without validating it end-to-end would have been the same mistake as the original invalid comparison. The terminus pass makes the claim falsifiable — the fix had to remove seed_lost specifically, not just move the aggregate — and it did, while leaving a clearly-named successor defect for the next pass.

summary: Make the LLM arm run the workbench's DESIGNED loop (plan -> retrieve -> assess -> re-plan until confident) and measure it. First finding: Arm B never looped. api/services/query.py::stream_query_events calls the same iter_pipeline() the eval calls, so the code path matched the app — but a traced run at ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5 emitted exactly one plan/evidence/assess and went straight to answer. Two causes: (a) the user's .env pins ORCH_MAX_HOPS=1, so the front end is single-pass by configuration; (b) even at 5, deterministic_assessment decided sufficiency purely by cross-source join closure and short-circuited `if not plan.joins: sufficient=True`, so ANY single-source question was complete by construction after one hop, and a describe returning only facet COUNTS looked complete. expandable_facets() — which knows 'MITIGATES x 6 members were counted, never fetched' — was defined and never called. Added ORCH_CHASE_FACETS (default OFF, preserving the byte-reproducible LLM-off verdict) + utils/orchestration/agents/assess/facets.py: relevance-ranks the facet frontier against the request and the plan's declared entities (capped ORCH_MAX_FACET_EXPANSIONS=4/hop) and emits ordinary sub-questions so expansions run the same draft->gate->execute->normalise path. New arm `llm_loop`. THREE bugs found while validating, each of which would have made the loop look functional while doing nothing: (1) the facet reports the GRAPH edge label (CHILD_OF) but the CAPEC card declares a MIXED vocabulary (ChildOf/ParentOf/PeerOf alongside HAS_MITIGATION/MAPS_TO), so the raw label named a relationship the card lacks, the boundary check rejected it, and the expansion hop ran an EMPTY query returning zero records — now resolved through card.relationship_types; (2) the specialists subgraph shares PipelineState, so it inherits the accumulated results and returns them, and the parent's operator.add appended them AGAIN — evidence DOUBLED every hop (one question: 90 results from 14 distinct sub-questions, 16x/8x/4x/2x). Latent bug that only manifests once the loop actually iterates; fixed with an identity-keyed append_new reducer (a first attempt that wrapped the subgraph broke event streaming and was reverted). (3) MY OWN un-truncation profile broke the enumeration claim: it raised SYNTHESIS_MAX_CITATIONS to 200, and _enumeration_claims fires on `enumerative OR len(ids) > cap`, so a small expansion set (1 > 200 = false) with non-enumerative phrasing triggered NEITHER — the loop fetched CAPEC-151 (the gold answer for C-HIE-01) and the claims never said it. Fixed by phrasing expansions as 'list all X reached from Y via Z' + de-duplicating identical claim text (the same anchor was re-described every hop, producing 4 copies). RESULT (corr/compl/faith/ground): loop OFF 0.8505/0.8692/0.9683/0.9750 (92 CORRECT/14 PARTIAL/14 INCORRECT, 12 halluc); loop ON before the synthesis fixes 0.8150/0.8498/0.9608/0.9650 (92/7/21, 8) — WORSE, because incomplete_retrieval fell 11->3 while projection_gap DOUBLED 7->14: the loop fixed retrieval and moved the bottleneck to synthesis; loop ON after them 0.8560/0.8877/0.9575/0.9729 (97/7/16, 15). Net: +5 CORRECT and +0.019 completeness for -0.011 faithfulness and 3 more hallucinations. The loop is a modest win for the LLM-planned path and does not close the gap to the gold-plan arms (A2 0.9972 / D 0.9917).
why: The user asked whether Arm B ran the app's documented iterative workflow. It did not — and proving that required tracing the event stream rather than trusting the config. Wiring the loop properly turned an inert subsystem into a working one and, in doing so, surfaced three latent defects that only appear when the loop iterates. The measured verdict is deliberately unflattering: the loop helps the weakest arm a little, costs faithfulness, and does not rescue LLM planning.

summary: ARM F — deterministic extractor at maximum accuracy + LLM agent-loop synthesizer. New arm `gold_loop_llm`: the catalogue's AUTHORED plan is injected into iter_pipeline via a _GoldPlanAgent wrapper (plan() returns the gold plan; replan()/cards/probe delegate to the real PlanningAgent), so retrieval gets correct seeding with no planner variance AND the facet-chasing loop runs on top — a combination no previous arm had, because the gold_llm arm calls the router directly through score_e2e and therefore has no orchestration loop at all. Synthesis is the claim-grounded narrator. RESULT: correctness 0.9957, completeness 0.9990, faithfulness 0.9960, groundedness 0.9992 — 119 CORRECT / 1 PARTIAL / ZERO INCORRECT, 3 hallucinations, mean answer coverage 1.0000 across all 66 scorable. It also runs LEANEST (1,080 evidence records vs Arm E3's 3,449 and Arm B2's 2,814) and fastest of any LLM arm (533s), because an accurate plan fetches what the question needs instead of casting wide. This answers the question directly: with extraction pinned accurate, the LLM CAN write accurate output — 0.9957 vs the deterministic ceiling's 0.9972, i.e. essentially tied, while producing readable analyst prose instead of a claim table. Also fixed a directional bug the judge caught: _REL_NOUNS labelled CAN_PRECEDE/CAN_FOLLOW backwards. The neighbours template walks OUT from the anchor, so `A -CAN_PRECEDE-> B` makes B the SUCCESSOR (not predecessor) and `A -CAN_FOLLOW-> B` makes B the PREDECESSOR. Naming them inverted states the relationship backwards — a grounded id carrying an ungrounded claim — and accounted for 2 of Arm F's 3 hallucinations (C-LKP-02, C-LKP-05). Verified fixed: 'CAPEC-116 (Excavation) has 1 CanPrecede successor: CAPEC-163'. The measured 0.9957 predates that fix, so the true figure is slightly better. Remaining: the single PARTIAL is F-CTM-01, where the narrative said 'maps to five ATT&CK techniques' and listed 5 of the 6 in evidence.
why: Every prior arm forced a choice between accuracy (deterministic composer, unreadable claim table) and readability (LLM narrator, worse scores). Arm F shows the trade is not real once the narrator is bound to verified claims AND extraction is accurate: 119/120 CORRECT with zero INCORRECT and full gold coverage. It also isolates the last variable cleanly — the LLM-planned arms sit at 0.85 with the SAME extraction and synthesis, so planning, not writing, is what costs accuracy.

summary: Write the standing evaluation record: docs/evaluation/2026-07-26/{README.md,portability.md}. README covers all seven arms with cost/volume, the three findings that matter (un-truncation was positive on all four metrics and never the regression; LLM planning is the entire -0.196 regression; the accuracy-vs-readability trade is not real once the narrator is bound to verified claims), per-category movement against the baseline's weak categories, all eight defects with the three most instructive written out, the retrieval-loop story (it never ran: .env pins ORCH_MAX_HOPS=1, sufficiency short-circuited on `if not plan.joins`, and expandable_facets() was never called), the demo recommendation (Arm F for humans, Arm A as the reproducible fallback and CI gate), reproduction commands, and a limitations section — all 120 questions are anchored so nothing measures open-ended use; the gold set is 120 hand-authored questions with 1-10 per category; the judge is itself a model; Arm A's 120/120 splices two judge runs; one model on one day; two questions overflow the 64k context. Plus the four method traps (provenance timestamps make every artifact differ; module caching decides which code a background run used; judge agents drop 2-3 of 120 file writes; raising a cap is not free). portability.md answers the grant-dataset question from an audit rather than a guess: three layers — Layer 1 harness/orchestration/eval apparatus is fully portable (nothing knows what MITRE is); Layer 2 card-driven describe/expand + the facet loop is the schema-agnostic answer path and resolves relationships through card.relationship_types; Layer 3 is 19 of 24 named query templates, ~6 id regexes, 1 canonical join key, ~16 _REL_NOUNS entries and the 120-question catalogue, all of which must be re-authored. Three scenarios (same shape / new domain similar shape / alien schema), with the real failure point named as ENTITY RESOLUTION rather than templates, and the honest risk stated: when the router missed a template and fell back to describe, A-DET scored 0.20, and the facet loop that fixes it has only ever been measured ON TOP of MITRE templates, never as the sole retrieval path. Recommends running that no-templates experiment on the existing graphs BEFORE the new data arrives.
why: The user asked for a durable reference and, separately, whether the work survives a real grant dataset. Both deserved evidence rather than recollection: the portability claim is backed by counting the MITRE-specific assets in the answer path (24 templates, 5 generic) rather than asserting the architecture is 'schema-agnostic', and the limitations section exists so the 0.99 numbers are not read as a promise about data the system has never seen.

summary: Merge untruncated-eval-experiment into main. Lands the un-truncated retrieval profile (env-gated), the planner join fix that stopped a declared join from reaching its sub-questions, the deterministic-vs-LLM two-arm experiment runner, the Arm E retrieval-loop wiring, the Arm F gold-plan + LLM agent-loop synthesizer, and the standing evaluation record under docs/evaluation/2026-07-26/ plus 2,658 answer/verdict artifacts under docs/evaluation/experiments/untruncated-claimnarr/. Merged as a --no-ff commit so the ten-commit arc stays legible; no conflicts (main had not moved off the merge base). Pre-merge gate: 1305 passed / 2 failed on the non-integration suite at ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5, and both failures are the known environment-dependent ones (setup_wizard inference-step and conversation event-order, which assert LLM-off behaviour while the local .env has the inference server enabled) — neither is touched by this diff.
why: The experiment branch had accumulated the whole un-truncation investigation and its evidence, and leaving it unmerged meant main did not carry the planner fix or the record that justifies the current retrieval defaults. Merging with --no-ff rather than fast-forwarding keeps the arc attributable to one merge point, matching how independent-eval-fixes landed.

summary: Recorded a repository-wide documentation audit and a seven-step remediation plan in docs/plans/documentation-accuracy-purge-plan.md. The audit names 7 stale README claims (agentic framing vs 17 Cypher/11 Gremlin deterministic templates, dead SPECIALIST_LLM_* config, hardcoded deterministic composer, superseded headline metrics, Status/roadmap contradiction), 7 defects under docs/ (inverted Cypher/Gremlin roles in purpose.md, dead notebooks/ citations, the -0.196 vs -0.1185 arm delta), and 7 skill defects (web/src paths that no longer exist, a utils/logger.py that never did, a push rule the project does not follow, and a full instruction file inside a pointer-only Cursor folder).
why: Documentation written alongside the system drifted as the system changed, and several load-bearing claims now misdescribe what the code does. Settling the defect list first makes every later edit traceable to a verified finding rather than to taste.

summary: Emptied the repository root of documentation except README.md. commands_basic.md (a 20-line partial cheatsheet) was replaced by docs/commands.md, a complete command reference verified line-by-line against setup.py, app.py, and main.py's argument parser — including the --graph fixture-qa action and the --golden-eval harness stages that the old file omitted. The untracked 213KB research audit moved to docs/research/audit-2026-08-03.md with an archived-snapshot preamble.
why: Three unrelated markdown files at the root with no stated relationship is the compactness problem in miniature, and the old cheatsheet had drifted far enough from main.py that following it would miss half the CLI. The audit is the most useful record of which claims went stale, so it is relocated rather than discarded.

summary: Rewrote README.md against what the code actually does. Adds a 'What actually runs' table naming, per stage, the deterministic default and the opt-in LLM seam beside it: query construction is always deterministic (16 Cypher + 11 Gremlin card-validated templates, no LLM), synthesis claims are always deterministic and verifier-gated with the LLM confined to narrative prose, and the planner's LLM drafter is off by default and always backstopped. Replaces the superseded 18/18-correlations headline with the 2026-07-26 arm table (A 0.9972 / 120 CORRECT / 0 hallucinations; LLM planning -0.119 against its own control), adds a 'What these numbers do and don't show' section, and resolves the Status-vs-roadmap contradiction over Wk 14-15.
why: The README described an agentic federated system; the source tree is a deterministic template router with opt-in LLM seams, and the project's own seven-arm evaluation says the deterministic path scores higher. Selling the LLM framing both misdescribed the code and undersold the actual finding.

summary: Indexed docs/evaluation/. New README.md separates the current reports (2026-07-26 standing record, portability audit, component + e2e reports, saved answers) from the superseded ones, and moves independent-eval.{md,json} and independent-eval-analysis.md under archive/ with a note that they are the 'Committed baseline' row of the standing table, not current numbers. New experiments/README.md maps each of the seven arm directories to its --arm code and configuration, flags the pre-defect-fix untruncated/ run as non-reproducing of the final table, and marks the two directories that hold answers but no judgments as artifact-comparison-only.
why: Five reports with no stated relationship meant a reader could not tell which numbers were current, and eight untruncated-* directories carried no arm mapping at all. Indexing costs nothing; deleting the artifacts would remove the only evidence behind the headline result.

summary: Corrected the core docs. purpose.md had the two specialists' roles inverted in the flagship example flow (the CAPEC query attributed to Cypher, the ATT&CK mitigation query to Gremlin) and now states the real routing plus an 'as implemented' note that components 2-4 run deterministically by default. structure.md's synthesis row claimed a hybrid LLM composer with fallback; claims are always composed deterministically and the LLM only rewrites narrative prose, so the row now says so and names the unreferenced seams. Dropped the dead notebooks/planning-schematic-agents.ipynb citation from goals.md and structure.md, marked Wk 14-15 in progress with the delivered documentation set named, added commands.md/evaluation/research to the docs index, and annotated the SPECIALIST_LLM_* (reserved, zero read sites) and SYNTHESIS_LLM_* (narrator only) blocks in .env.example. main.py's --graph metavar omitted the fixture-qa action it accepts; fixed.
why: These are the statements most likely to be read by a reviewer and acted on by an agent. The inverted specialist roles in the grant-facing document are the single most misleading sentence in the repository, and a config block documented as a live LLM seam that no code reads sends anyone tuning it down a dead end.

summary: Corrected and re-synced the skills. woven-dusk-design pointed at web/src/styles/tokens.css and web/src/index.css, neither of which exists (the app is Next.js App Router; tokens live in web/app/globals.css). repository-structure used invented utils/logger.py and utils/auth_handler/ examples and called web/ a React/Vite webfront; both now use real packages from this repo. global-project-rules mandated git push at every step (the operator's standing directive is commit-only), still listed synthesis/fixtures/evaluation as 'Future: TBD' after all three shipped, and omitted portfolio-readme from the skills table. .cursor/rules/portfolio-readme/RULE.md held a full instruction file inside a pointer-only folder, referencing a portfolio-readme/references/ tree absent from this repo; it is now canonical at docs/skills/portfolio-readme/SKILL.md with pointers in all three agent folders. All 27 pointers (9 skills x 3 folders) regenerated from one template.
why: Skills are the first thing every agent reads, so a skill naming a file that does not exist misleads at the point of maximum leverage. The repository states its own rule that agent folders are pointers only, and one folder broke it.

summary: Widened test_docs_contracts.py from the four Wk 14-15 contract docs to the whole maintained documentation set: README, structure, purpose, goals, commands, the evaluation indexes, and every canonical skill file. Adds three checks beside the existing cited-path one — every relative markdown link must resolve, every skill must have exactly one pointer in each of .claude/skills, .agents/skills and .cursor/rules, and no file in those folders may exceed a pointer (must name docs/skills/ and stay under 20 lines). docs/plans/ and docs/research/ are deliberately excluded as dated historical records. Verified by injecting a bad link, a bad path, an orphan pointer and a non-pointer file: all four assertions fail, then pass once reverted.
why: Every defect this purge fixed was one a test could have caught. Without the guard the same drift returns the next time a file moves, and the pointers-only rule the repository states about itself had nothing enforcing it.

summary: Scaffolded docs/research/ as the single research record: the section-2 directory tree (experiments, figures/sources, tables, datasets/cards, paper/checklists, templates), the experiment template (manifest.yaml with the full 25-key schema, PROTOCOL.md, RESULTS.md, ISSUES.md, data/POINTERS.md, env/hardware.md), the DECISION and negative_result templates, a directory README, and AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md installed verbatim from the source instruction set with an Ariadne preamble.
why: The repository had a rich results corpus but no machine-readable structure and no ID-based traceability, so no number in it could be traced to a run. The preamble resolves three ambiguities the source text leaves open for this repo: raw artifacts stay under docs/evaluation/ referenced by hash (no DVC), the append-only rule binds completed experiments rather than the living ledgers, and the agent instruction file is the global-project-rules skill rather than a root CLAUDE.md.

summary: Added utils/research_record/ (manifest.py Pydantic schema, validate.py, index.py, scaffold.py, hashing.py, paths.py), CLI wrappers scripts/{new_experiment,validate_research,generate_index,make_figures}.py, and a Makefile with new-experiment/validate-research/index/figures/test-research targets. 26 unit tests over a valid fixture broken one way per check, all passing. Verified by hand that a deliberately broken folder trips required-files, empty-metrics, figure-missing, figure-no-generator and unknown-claim, and that generate_index.py --check reports a stale INDEX.
why: Section 7 of the research-record contract states that convention without enforcement decays, and this repository had no scaffolder, validator, Makefile or CI of any kind. Building the tooling before the back-fill means all eleven back-filled experiments are validated as they are written rather than audited afterwards. The schema is strict about absent fields and permissive about 'unknown' so back-filled provenance can be admitted rather than invented.

summary: Back-filled the 2026-07-26 seven-arm study as EXP-2026-07-001 through -007, one experiment folder per arm A-G, each with manifest.yaml, a reconstruction-flagged PROTOCOL.md, RESULTS.md, ISSUES.md, data/metrics.json and data/POINTERS.md. Every metric is read from docs/plans/robustness/_overnight/numbers.json (itself recomputed from the committed judgment files), never from prose; all 28 metric cells were cross-checked against the standing table and match. The 62 MB of run artifacts stay under docs/evaluation/experiments/ and are referenced by relative path plus a SHA-256 directory hash.
why: The seven-arm study is the repository's publishable asset but had no machine-readable form and no per-arm identity, so no figure in it could be traced to a run. One ID per arm lets any single arm be superseded or re-run independently. Unrecoverable provenance (per-arm commit, seeds, lockfile) is recorded as unknown in ISSUES.md rather than invented, and each arm's ISSUES.md carries the corrections the repository had already found - the pre-fix cost rows, the -0.196 vs -0.1185 delta, and the G-F sign convention.

summary: Back-filled the remaining evaluations as EXP-2026-07-008 (component evaluation), -009 (end-to-end, four goals.md metrics), -010 (the superseded first independent cross-model pass, status: superseded, superseded_by EXP-2026-07-001) and -011 (portability audit, recorded with primary: null because it is a code reading rather than a measured run). Every metric cross-checked against component-evaluation.json and e2e-evaluation.json.
why: The superseded independent-eval pass is the 'Committed baseline' row of the standing table; deleting it would orphan that row, and the record's rules require failed and superseded work to be kept. Recording the portability audit with a null primary metric keeps an audit from being misread as an experiment, and each folder's ISSUES.md carries the caveats that matter most to a reviewer - the planner corpus filtered on its own success, the e2e judge being the model under test, and the 25-not-28 template count.

summary: Seeded the four cross-cutting ledgers and generated the first INDEX.md. CLAIMS.md carries 20 claim IDs: 10 supported or partial with experiment evidence, 7 unsupported (the experiment backlog), and 3 refuted/cut kept deliberately. DECISIONS.md holds 10 dated ADR entries. OPEN_QUESTIONS.md orders 13 questions by what they block, with Q1 (is 0.9972 a capability or a coverage artifact) gating the rest. RELATED_WORK.md curates the audit's bibliography around the claims and leads with the AgCyRAG scoop watch. Validator now passes on all 11 experiments.
why: The claims ledger is where the repository stops flattering itself: the paper's intended headline (template routing beats free-form LLM query generation, C-012) has no supporting experiment, because Arm G is a generic-primitives control and no LLM writes Cypher or Gremlin in any arm. Writing that as an unsupported row makes the backlog visible instead of letting the seven-arm study read as though it already proved the thesis. The -0.196 delta is recorded as cut-not-refuted so the figure stops circulating without re-litigating the finding.

summary: Populated datasets/ and paper/. DATASETS.md indexes the three datasets with the versions.json checksums; cards for ATT&CK 19.0, CAPEC 3.9 and the 120-question catalogue record provenance, licence, and the limitations that bear on results. paper/ holds OUTLINE.md (the Path 1 framing with per-section claim mapping), venue-targets.md (EACL 2027 demo 22 Sept as the recommended first move, plus tier 2/3 deadlines and the three artifact badges), ARTIFACT_APPENDIX.md, and a live EACL demo checklist. All 134 relative links in docs/research/ now resolve.
why: Every field a venue reproducibility checklist asks for is already a manifest field, so committing the checklists early makes submission transcription rather than archaeology. Two release blockers are now recorded where they will be seen: there is no LICENSE for Ariadne's own code (NOTICE covers third-party data only and says so), and GitHub alone does not satisfy the artifact-Available badge without an archival DOI. The catalogue card states the no-holdout and co-authored-with-templates limitations up front, because that is the caveat most likely to be dropped when a number is quoted.

summary: Added the figure and table pipeline. fig-arm-comparison.{svg,pdf} is generated from all seven arms' data/metrics.json by figures/sources/make_arm_comparison.py; tab-component.{md,tex} from EXP-2026-07-008 by tables/sources/make_component_table.py; fig01-architecture is promoted from the hand-authored docs/assets/architecture.svg by a scripted promotion step. SVG is written by hand rather than via a plotting library so output is byte-deterministic (matplotlib embeds ids and dates that would break the CI check); PDF via rsvg-convert, verified byte-identical across three runs. make figures --check verified to fail both on a hand-edited figure and on a changed source metric.
why: Section 4 of the contract calls figures pasted from a notebook the single most common way research repositories rot, so the check has to be real: it compares regenerated output byte-for-byte, not merely that a script exists. Writing SVG by hand avoids adding matplotlib as a dependency and keeps the generator diffable. The architecture diagram is the one documented exception - it is a system diagram, not a plot - but its promotion is still scripted so the promoted copy cannot drift from the authored source.

summary: Amended the three documents the research-record contract requires, with minimal diffs: README gains a 'Research record' section near the top plus three rows in the documentation index and a corrected docs/ tree line; a new CONTRIBUTING.md documents the experiment workflow, the enforced rules, and the test commands; global-project-rules gains a mandatory 'Research record' section and a docs/research/ row in the layer table. Rule 4 was narrowed from a blanket ban on editing docs/research/ to binding completed experiment folders and the dated audit, explicitly exempting the living ledgers and generated files. 33 insertions, 2 deletions across the two tracked files; no existing prose rewritten.
why: Rule 4 as written deadlocked the design it was meant to protect - INDEX.md regenerates on every commit and the four ledgers are living documents, so a blanket in-place-edit ban made the record unmaintainable by the repository's own rules. The agent block went into global-project-rules rather than a new root CLAUDE.md because this repository states that .claude/, .agents/ and .cursor/ are pointers only and must never carry instructions of their own.

summary: Deleted the 53 shipped top-level plans under docs/plans/ (968K to 152K), keeping robustness/ and _overnight/ which are live work and the provenance behind every arm's recomputed metrics. Their cited substance was migrated first: DECISIONS.md gains D-011 (sequential specialist execution, not Send fan-out, because sequential is what makes the committed artifacts byte-reproducible) and D-012 (documentation accuracy is enforced by test_docs_contracts.py). docs/evaluation/README.md and the portfolio-readme skill were repointed; the append-only audit was given an AMENDMENTS section rather than edited. test_docs_contracts.py now link-checks docs/research/ and CONTRIBUTING.md, excluding the dated audit, templates, and the verbatim AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS contract.
why: Deleting a plan that is cited as evidence for a published number would break the provenance chain, so the ordering mattered: migrate, repoint, then delete. Also pinned SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in a shared _svg2pdf helper - rsvg-convert embeds a live timestamp in the PDF Info dictionary, so two conversions of the same SVG differ by ~560 bytes and make figures --check would have failed in CI on the clock rather than on the figures.

summary: Turned on enforcement. .github/workflows/research-record.yml (the repository's first CI) runs the validator, fails on a stale INDEX.md, fails if any promoted figure no longer reproduces from its generator, rejects anything over 10 MB under docs/research/, runs both test suites, and fails if regeneration dirtied the tree. scripts/install_hooks.sh installs a plain pre-commit hook that regenerates and stages INDEX.md then validates only the touched experiment folders; verified it blocks an unknown claim ID and allows a valid change. Added .gitattributes. All ten section-10 acceptance criteria verified.
why: A plain git hook rather than the pre-commit framework because adopting a new tool is an explicit non-goal of this retrofit, and CI is the real gate - the hook only needs to make CI failures rare. The hook stages a regenerated INDEX.md rather than failing on it, since failing a commit for a file the hook can fix itself would just train people to use --no-verify.

summary: Added docs/plans/arm-h-generic-primitives.md, the plan for closing the generic-primitive capability gap found by re-analysing Arm G's committed judgment files. Localised all 42.87 lost correctness points to six termini and reduced them to three missing schema-driven capabilities (join projection, composition, anchor/direction resolution) plus two routing defects. Reloaded the CAPEC Gremlin fixture, which was empty and had been failing 73 specialist tests on its own.
why: Arm G was being read as evidence that hand-written MITRE templates are irreplaceable; the failure localisation shows the generic layer is instead missing three capabilities that a source card already declares. Establishing a true test baseline first was necessary because the empty graph made every live golden test fail for a reason unrelated to any change.

summary: Added docs/plans/robustness/05-holdout-execution-plan.md, the executable plan for the blind holdout described by plans 02 and 04. Verified the preconditions it depends on: both pinned snapshot SHA256s match data/versions.json byte-for-byte, freeze/holdout-v1 resolves to 974e85a, the diff from that tag over utils/specialists, planner, synthesis and orchestration is a single test file, and both graphs answer a real query rather than merely reporting reachable.
why: Plan 02 makes the snapshot hashes and the freeze a hard precondition because a version skew or a behavioural drift produces a low number with a plausible excuse that nobody checks. Confirming the freeze diff is test-only is what makes it defensible to run the arms at all.

summary: Added utils/specialists/evalset/holdout_protocol.py, the committed sampler for the blind holdout: a fixed seed (20260805, deliberately not the 1729 stats.py already uses), populations read from gold_bank.json rather than the loaded graph, and a 12/8/10 stratified uniform draw whose federated stratum is over-drawn and partitioned into answerable and abstention-expected rather than filtered. It also builds the Author prompt. 18 tests cover determinism, population integrity, the partition rule, and that the prompt leaks no repository path, file name, or template identifier.
why: A human-authored holdout cannot be re-run; committing the sampler means a reviewer can regenerate the draw and confirm the anchors were sampled uniformly rather than picked for richness, which is the single most likely way this experiment dies silently. One test asserts the minimum neighbour count across the drawn anchors is exactly 1, because a sampler that had started weighting by degree would show up as a floor well above that.

summary: Committed docs/evaluation/holdout-v1/anchors.json — the 30 drawn holdout anchors with the seed, the three population sizes and their SHA256s, the full draw order, the 10 over-draws, and the federated partition into 6 answerable and 4 abstention-expected. No question text exists yet.
why: Plan 02 section 9 step 3 requires the draw to be committed before any question is written, so the git timestamp proves the anchors were fixed before authoring rather than chosen to suit questions that already existed. The drawn anchors are long-tail (T1543.005, CAPEC-671, CWE-1243) rather than the T1003/T1055 a model reaches for unprompted, which is the check plan 02 section 0 asks for.

summary: Authored the 30 blind holdout questions. One fresh Claude Fable 5 subagent at high reasoning effort per anchor, no shared context between spawns, no repository access, prompt carrying only the anchor id, entity type, catalogue name, category description and the reference-discipline rule. Committed docs/evaluation/holdout-v1/author-prompt.md (the template plus all 30 filled prompts verbatim) and authored.json, with every question checked verbatim against the workflow journal. Validation: every question names its anchor and its catalogue name, none names a second MITRE id, none leaks a template identifier.
why: The write-lock is the experiment, and enforcing it by prompt construction rather than by instructing an agent to avert its eyes is what plan 02 section 3 requires. One defect surfaced and is recorded rather than fixed: H-SW-01 asks what techniques a SubTechnique implements, because the section 5 software category is phrased for a Software anchor while the population is techniques. The question stands as written and the write-up will report n=30 and n=29 sensitivity.

summary: Compiled the holdout bank: utils/specialists/tests/golden/holdout_questions.json, 30 entries with split holdout, H- ids, and expected_template_is_derived true. Gold comes only from gold_bank.py's parse of the raw STIX and CAPEC XML — must_include_related, must_correlate and ex_gold are recomputations, never authored. Zero anchors discarded. 13 tests check shape, that the question text is byte-identical to the authored returns, and that every gold field matches a fresh recomputation; 239 tests pass across evalset, the holdout bank, and utils/evaluation.
why: The tests deliberately do NOT assert that entries route to their expected_template. That field is derived by the compiler from the anchor type and category because the Author never saw the template inventory, so asserting on it would turn a derived value into ground truth — which is the exact mistake expected_template_is_derived exists to prevent, and why template-routing accuracy may not be reported from this holdout.

summary: Added a --bank option to utils/evaluation/experiment_untruncated.py so any single bank file can be run through the identical arm code, and threaded it through load_work, run_arm and the manifest. Verified the holdout bank loads as 12 attack / 8 capec / 10 federated and that the default path still loads the committed 120.
why: The holdout has to run through the same runner as every arm figure it will be compared against; a parallel runner would have to be trusted separately. The change is confined to utils/evaluation, which the freeze covers neither — the freeze binds utils/specialists and the planner, and the arms are still executed from a detached checkout of the tag.

summary: Ran Arm A over the 30 blind holdout questions from a detached checkout of freeze/holdout-v1 and graded it with 30 independent Sonnet 5 agents. Blind correctness is 0.6273 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.477–0.767) against the 0.9972 development figure recomputed from the same arm's committed judgment files — a drop of 0.3699. Added utils/evaluation/holdout_report.py, which rolls the per-case judgments into results.json with Wilson intervals and keeps the two federated strata apart, and scratchpad/judge_holdout.mjs, the abstention-aware judge.
why: The drop is concentrated rather than uniform, which is the distinction plan 02 section 10 asks the per-category breakdown to make: mitigations, tactics, detection, execution, weakness, pattern-to-mitigation and reverse-mapping all score at or near 1.0, while groups (0.0), software (0.06) and mapping (0.075) collapse. All four abstention-expected cases abstained, all four carried the executed query, and none fabricated a mapping. One judgment file was not written by its agent though the agent returned the verdict; it was recovered verbatim from the workflow return rather than re-graded.

summary: Added docs/plans/arm-h-generic-primitives.md, the plan for closing the generic-primitive capability gap found by re-analysing Arm G's committed judgment files. Localised all 42.87 lost correctness points to six termini and reduced them to three missing schema-driven capabilities (join projection, composition, anchor/direction resolution) plus two routing defects. Reloaded the CAPEC Gremlin fixture, which was empty and had been failing 73 specialist tests on its own.
why: Arm G was being read as evidence that hand-written MITRE templates are irreplaceable; the failure localisation shows the generic layer is instead missing three capabilities that a source card already declares. Establishing a true test baseline first was necessary because the empty graph made every live golden test fail for a reason unrelated to any change.

summary: Added _generic_bridge to the Gremlin builder's SPECIALIST_GENERIC_ONLY branch: it walks the declared cross-source join edge and projects the key property, in either direction depending on whether the task is seeded on the anchor or on the key's own values. The edge, endpoint label and key property all come from the resolved JoinKeyEndpoint, so no MITRE literal decides the traversal. Smoke-verified live: F-CTM-01 went from 12 gold ids never retrieved to 0, and its dependent ATT&CK hop now executes instead of being skipped.
why: This single gap cost Arm G 40% of its lost correctness. Without a bridge primitive a federated question routes to describe, which returns facet counts rather than neighbour ids, so the consumer sub-question is skipped for want of seed identifiers and half the question goes unanswered.

summary: Gave the SPECIALIST_GENERIC_ONLY branch the three capabilities the Arm G analysis showed it was missing. Composition: a Cypher chain that BFSs the derived schema registry to every requested label, emitting one independently-aggregated OPTIONAL MATCH per branch, and an intersection primitive returning nodes adjacent to every seed when the seeds are of different kinds. Anchor/direction resolution: a Gremlin union walk that reads the anchor label off the resolved task and the direction off the declared facet, plus a bridge that prefixes the path from a non-anchor seed to the label owning the join edge. Bounded scans now require a definitional cue before routing to a name lookup. Added utils/specialists/schema/paths.py so both branches share one path search.
why: The three gaps were worth 90% of Arm G's lost correctness and none of them needed MITRE knowledge - the source card and the derived registry already declare the edges, directions and join endpoints. Path prefixes are deduplicated on the (rel, direction) sequence rather than the terminal label because a question names a label loosely: USES out of Software reaches both Technique and SubTechnique, and filtering to the named label dropped thirteen of Mimikatz's seventeen gold ids.

summary: Added test_generic_only_isolation.py, which replays ten task shapes covering every branch of the default cascade and asserts the emitted template, query string and params are byte-identical to freeze/holdout-v1. The expected values were captured by checking the tag out with git archive and running its builders, and are committed as fixtures/frozen_default_queries.json. A companion test asserts the flag actually changes routing, so the suite cannot pass by the flag becoming a no-op.
why: freeze/holdout-v1 forbids behavioural change under utils/specialists/ until the blind holdout reports, and the Arm H primitives live under that path. Scoping them to the generic-only branch keeps the freeze intact, but that is a claim about behaviour and had to be tested rather than asserted in a comment.

summary: Added transitive self-referential walking to the generic Gremlin branch: an edge the task named that lands back on the anchor's own label is repeated per depth up to the hop cap, so an abstraction question returns the parent and the grandparent rather than stopping at the parent. Both declared directions of the self-loop are emitted. Verified live: CAPEC-7 now reaches CAPEC-66 and CAPEC-248, which is exactly C-ABS-01's gold.
why: Breadth-first search cannot express a hierarchy - it stops at the anchor label because it has already been visited - so C-ABS was still losing one gold id per question. Both directions are emitted because nothing in the schema says which way is 'up': ancestor-versus-descendant is the domain nuance a hand-written template encodes and a generic primitive must not guess.

summary: Added utils/evaluation/retrieval_coverage.py, a judge-free scorer that measures whether the gold answer reached the retrieved evidence, plus a paired comparison against a reference arm that reports per-question regressions rather than averaging them away. Six unit tests cover the vacuous-entry rule, the skipped-consumer signal and the gain/regression split. Arm G's baseline reads gold_in_evidence 0.7191 with 73/120 fully covered and 56 skipped consumers.
why: failure_terminus needs a judgment file per question because it localises a graded failure, which makes it the wrong instrument for a retrieval change - judging 120 questions costs an agent panel and 'did the gold reach the evidence' is a set membership test. The metric is deliberately not called answer_coverage: score_e2e.py already owns that name for the fraction of gold the answer enumerates over a different population, and quoting 0.7191 against that metric's 0.8979 would be a false comparison.

summary: Ran Arm F over the holdout (30/30, 554 s) and graded both arms with 30 independent Sonnet 5 agents each. Blind correctness: Arm A 0.689 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.550–0.817) against a 0.9972 development figure; Arm F 0.7083 (0.565–0.838) against 0.9957. Deltas −0.3082 and −0.2874. One deviation, logged: the compiler had omitted the join_key on the CAPEC mapping category, so H-MAP-01 and H-MAP-02 routed to describe and returned facet counts instead of the mapped techniques; the three committed C-MAP entries all carry it, so the holdout was being compared against a different plan than the development set gets for the same category. Fixed, both cases re-run and re-judged on both arms, question text untouched.
why: Fixing that was the same class of action as fixing a crash, which plan 02 section 9 permits and requires logging: it is a defect in the harness, not a wrong answer from the system, and leaving it would have broken the like-for-like comparison the experiment rests on. Both cases went from INCORRECT (0.1 / 0.05) to CORRECT (1.0) on both arms, which is why the deviation is recorded prominently rather than folded in silently.

summary: Corrected the timestamps on the six Arm H changelog entries, which had been written by hand in local time and labelled Z. They now carry the UTC instant of the commit that shipped each entry. Also recorded EXP-2026-08-001's known limitations in ISSUES.md before its results exist: the protocol is not a clean pre-registration, no judged correctness is run, two primitives deliberately over-return rather than being tuned to the gold, and the freeze is held by an isolation test rather than by an empty diff.
why: A record whose timestamps are plausible but wrong is worse than one that admits a gap, and the research contract turns on write-time capture. Writing the limitations before the numbers exist is the same principle: they are properties of the design, not of whatever the result turns out to be, and recording them afterwards invites quietly softening them.

summary: Fixed anchor-label resolution in both generic branches. primary_label() returns labels[0] - the order the plan listed entities in - which says nothing about what the seed actually is, so a sub-question seeded with T1110.001 and resolving ['Tactic','Technique'] was anchored as a Tactic and walked HAS_TECHNIQUE outbound, losing the tactic it was asked for. Paths are now derived from every resolved label and each branch is guarded by the label it came from, or fires when the anchor carries none of the candidates. The Gremlin walk anchors by identifier alone, since the canonical vertex id is already unique across labels.
why: Trying every anchor without a guard would have reintroduced the inbound/outbound conflation that caused all six of Arm G's hallucinations - 'which techniques does Mimikatz use' would take the inbound USES branch and return the 51 groups that use Mimikatz. The guard's second disjunct is what keeps it from being too strict: the planner's labels are approximate and a seed's real label is often a subtype it never named, as SubTechnique is here. Verified live on both cases: T1110.001 now reaches TA0006, and S0002 still returns only its 18 outbound techniques.

summary: Wrote up the blind holdout: docs/evaluation/holdout-v1/README.md with Wilson and bootstrap intervals, the per-category breakdown, the two federated strata reported separately, the discard log, both deviations, and the section 10 limitation verbatim. Completed EXP-2026-08-001 (manifest, RESULTS, ISSUES) and updated the ledgers — C-013 refuted, C-001 downgraded to hold only for the relation directions the templates serve, C-014 partial, Q1 marked answered, D-013 and D-014 added. Applied the Branch A section 6 gate, recovered verbatim from git history: Arm A 0.689 is below 0.70, so that branch applies and Steps 6 and 7 do not proceed as written.
why: The drop is concentrated rather than uniform, which is the distinction the per-category breakdown exists to make and the reason this is a usable result rather than only a negative one: seven of sixteen categories score 1.00 on both arms, while groups scores 0.00 and software 0.06 because the templates bind the seed to the Group/Software side and the blind author asked the reverse direction. On the four abstention-expected anchors both arms abstained, carried the executed query, and fabricated nothing — the strongest result in the run.

summary: Merged main into the holdout branch and renumbered the experiment from EXP-2026-08-001 to EXP-2026-08-002, because main's concurrent Arm H work had already claimed 001. Resolved the changelog conflict by merging both sides and re-sorting by timestamp, with every line re-parsed as JSON. make validate-research passes over 13 experiments.
why: Main's Arm H commits touch the cypher and gremlin builders, which are the system under test, but only behind SPECIALIST_GENERIC_ONLY and with a frozen_default_queries fixture proving the default path is unchanged. The holdout is unaffected regardless: both arms ran from a detached checkout at freeze/holdout-v1, made before those commits existed in this tree.

summary: Fixed the transitive hierarchy walk, which the shared Gremlin validator was rejecting outright. It counts every out/in step in the whole query against max_traversal_depth, so unrolling ChildOf into one branch per depth in both directions read as depth 12 and every draft was refused before reaching the database - eight CAPEC hierarchy and precedence questions retrieved nothing at all, including their own anchor. The walk now emits one bounded repeat(...).times(n).emit() per direction, and fits its branches to the step budget cheapest-first, naming anything dropped in meta.
why: The validator is shared code that arms A-F depend on, so under the freeze the query had to change rather than the limit.
