Dropped branches are recorded rather than silently omitted because a truncated walk otherwise reads as a complete answer; the same reason the run reports regressions per question instead of averaging them into the mean.

summary: Recorded EXP-2026-08-001. The generic branch now reaches gold_in_evidence 1.0000 over all 120 questions against Arm G's 0.7191: 120/120 fully covered where 73 were, 424 gold ids recovered, 0 questions regressed, and dependent hops skipped for want of seeds down from 56 to 7 (all of which are negatives where abstaining is correct). No correctness number exists for this arm and RESULTS.md forbids quoting one - no judge ran. Metrics and the per-category table are generated from the artifacts; the manifest, pointers and hashes are complete and make validate-research passes.
why: The retrieval half of C-003 does not survive as written: every one of Arm G's retrieval failures was closable from declarations the repository already held - the join-key registry, the schema registry's facet list, and the seed's own label. What stays template-shaped is precision, since two primitives answer correctly but too broadly and neither can be narrowed from the schema. That is a sharper account of what a template buys than 'accuracy': it encodes which of several schema-valid readings the analyst meant.

summary: Amended EXP-2026-08-001 after a concurrent session merged the blind holdout (EXP-2026-08-002) into main mid-run. Two amendments, appended rather than edited in: the freeze justification is now historical since the holdout has reported, and the holdout's largest diagnosed failure mode - the reverse relation direction being unserved, scoring groups 0.00 - is the same defect class Arm H fixed in the generic branch. Verified against the live graph on one anchor: seeded with T1003 and asked which groups use it, the template group_techniques returns 0 rows while generic_chain returns 21 (13 Groups).
why: The two sessions found the same defect from opposite directions on the same day, which makes it a class rather than a coincidence, and it changes what the study can claim: templates encode the direction the development bank happened to ask. Recorded as a query-construction result on one anchor and explicitly not as a holdout score, because the generic arm has never been run against the holdout bank - that run is now the highest-value experiment available.

summary: Removed the GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/research-record.yml, which ran the research-record validator, the INDEX.md and figure regeneration checks, the size guard and the two test suites on every push to main and every pull request. The .github/ tree is now empty of workflows and no automated checks run on push. CONTRIBUTING.md's 'the rules that get enforced' section no longer claims CI enforcement; the same rules are still enforced locally by the pre-commit hook and by 'make validate-research'.
why: Requested directly by the user. The enforcement is not lost, only relocated to the local pre-commit path - but the safety net for anything committed with --no-verify, or changed through a route that skips the hook, is gone, so docs/research/ drift is now caught only when someone runs the validator by hand.

summary: Ran Arm H's schema-driven primitives against the 30-question blind holdout for the first time and recorded it as EXP-2026-08-003. Retrieval rises from the template cascade's 0.7688 to 0.8952, 26/30 fully covered against 22/30, four questions improved and none regressed. The gain is exactly the two categories EXP-2026-08-002 diagnosed as structurally unserved - H-GRP 0.000 to 1.000 and H-SW 0.103 to 1.000, where Arm F judged 0.000 and 0.050 - and all fourteen other categories are unchanged. Arm A and Arm F retrieve identically, so the facet-chasing loop adds records but no reach on blind questions.
why: Arm H reached full coverage on the development catalogue, but that catalogue was co-authored with the templates, so saturating it was weak evidence; a blind set is where a schema-driven layer either transfers or does not. The decomposition matters more than the headline: splitting Arm F's judged loss by whether retrieval had already succeeded puts 55% on incomplete retrieval and 45% on questions that retrieved perfectly and still scored badly, which bounds what any query-construction work can be worth.

summary: Made the forward generic bridge an outer join. It now projects one row per anchor with its mappings folded into a possibly-empty list, instead of traversing .out(edge) and dropping any anchor with no mapping. A new normalizer branch handles the folded shape and is selected only when tax is a list, so the inner-join paths route exactly where they always did. Verified live: CAPEC-603 (zero MAPS_TO edges) now yields a record with empty join_values, so the dependent hop still correctly stands down while the abstention is grounded in a retrieved record.
why: The inner join was both a recall bug and a grounding bug. CAPEC-116 exploits CWE-1243 and maps to no technique, so it vanished from the evidence entirely; and 'this pattern has no ATT&CK mapping' is a real analyst answer that needs the record it was read from. An inner join cannot express a negative result.

summary: Made the CWE-anchored prefixed bridge an outer join on its second hop only. The first hop stays inner because only patterns that genuinely exploit the weakness belong in the answer; the second folds the mappings so a pattern that exploits the CWE but maps to no technique is still returned. Verified live on CWE-1243, which is exploited by CAPEC-116 (zero mappings) and CAPEC-545 (two) - both now come back. The three remaining blind-set residuals H-CHN-01, H-CHN-02 and H-CTM-02 all reach full gold coverage.
why: Asymmetric joins are the point here: inner on the first hop preserves the question's constraint, outer on the second preserves the honest empty result. Making both outer would have returned patterns unrelated to the weakness, and making both inner is what was deleting CAPEC-116.

summary: Re-ran the 30 blind holdout questions with the outer-join bridge. Gold-in-evidence reaches 1.0000 with 30/30 fully covered and zero gold ids missing, up from 0.8952 and 26/30 before the fix, and against the template cascade's 0.7688 with 22/30. Four questions improved, none regressed, and the five residual ids identified in EXP-2026-08-003 are all recovered. Skipped consumers hold at 3, which are the correct abstentions.
why: This is the run the outer-join claim rests on, and it closes the retrieval half of the blind-set gap completely. It remains a retrieval measurement: Arm H is still unjudged on this bank, so 1.0000 may not be set beside Arm A's 0.689 or Arm F's 0.708.

summary: Added utils/evaluation/answer_gap.py, which classifies the judged loss that survives complete retrieval - the 45% of the blind-set deficit no query work can reach. Classes are chosen by the magnitude of each observable deficit rather than a fixed precedence, because a ladder scatters one defect across several classes: H-PRE-01 states 1 of 4 gold ids and carries a 0.1 faithfulness deduction, and precedence would file a 0.75 failure under a 0.1 symptom. On Arm F the 0.1300 complete-retrieval loss resolves to under_enumeration on 3 questions worth 0.0883 and judge_nuance spread thinly over 19 worth 0.0417.
why: '45% is answer shaping' is not actionable. The decomposition is: one named, fixable composition defect concentrated in three questions, where the answer names the anchor and drops the neighbours the query already retrieved, plus small deductions elsewhere that are presentation rather than defect. That says what to fix and roughly what it is worth.

summary: Re-ran the 120-question development catalogue with the outer-join bridge as a regression check. Gold-in-evidence holds at 1.0000 with 120/120 fully covered and zero regressions; evidence records rise from 950 to 966, which is the unmapped anchors now being returned rather than dropped. Skipped consumers hold at 7. The full specialist and evaluation suites pass at 472 tests, including the byte-identical freeze isolation check.
why: The development catalogue was already saturated at 1.0000, so this run could only detect harm - which is exactly why it had to run. An outer join returns strictly more rows than an inner one, and the risk was that the extra empty-mapping records would displace real ones under the row cap or confuse the normalizer's shape detection.

summary: Recorded EXP-2026-08-004 with metrics, results, issues, pointers and a generated table, amended EXP-2026-08-003 with the two findings that supersede its residuals, and updated C-014. The claim now carries the finding that the directional half of the measured cliff is a property of these templates rather than of routing: a schema-driven layer reading direction from the declared facet reaches 1.0000 gold-in-evidence on the same blind set against the cascade's 0.7688. It stays partial - retrieval only, and open-ended non-anchored questions remain unmeasured.
why: The append-only rule binds completed experiment folders, so EXP-2026-08-003's numbers stand as recorded and the supersession is an appended amendment rather than an edit; those numbers are the measurement that found the defect. C-014 is a living ledger entry and is meant to be updated when evidence arrives.

summary: Added docs/plans/binding-and-direction-portability.md, a seven-step plan for the blind holdout's reverse-direction defect. It treats the defect as a portable one - routing picks an anchor label from an entity mention while binding takes ids from elsewhere, and nothing owns the question of whether they agree - and fixes it by learning per-label id schemes into the schema registry, adding a three-valued binding check, and resolving direction from the declared triples.
why: The narrow repair re-authors MITRE knowledge a different dataset will not share, so the same defect would arrive again with the first non-MITRE source. Steps 1-5 are additive and provable against the frozen fixture; the outer-join port that costs arm comparability is isolated in Step 6 behind an operator decision.

summary: Added utils/specialists/schema/idscheme.py, which learns per-label identifier shapes from the canonical snapshot, and exposed id_schemes/value_verdict/labels_for_id on DatasetSchema and SchemaRegistry. A scheme is a value case-folded with each digit run collapsed to '#', so T1550.002 learns as 't#.#' and G0082 as 'g#'. Verdicts are three-valued and a property with more than 24 distinct shapes is marked open and judges nothing. On the real snapshot Group.attack_id now returns mismatch for T1550.002 and consistent for G0082.
why: The only knowledge of which identifier belongs to which label lived in hand-written MITRE regexes in resolve/resolver.py, while build.py already computed an id-to-label map and discarded it. Deriving it from data is what lets the same machinery serve a source nobody has seen, and the open/undetermined branch is what stops it manufacturing a false mismatch on UUID-keyed telemetry.

summary: Added utils/specialists/audit/binding_audit.py, a read-only audit that drives both builders across bank-derived and schema-derived task shapes, extracts every (label, property, bound values) triple from the emitted query, and asks the registry whether those values could inhabit that property. On 615 cases it reports 283 mismatches across six ATT&CK templates and two CAPEC ones, 22 of them with the seed's own label in scope. Nothing is executed and no database is needed.
why: The blind holdout surfaced this defect in group_techniques and software_techniques because those are the two directions its author happened to ask. Fixing the two the blind set found is the same co-authoring error the holdout exists to expose, so the fix needed an inventory first: the same shape sits under campaign_attribution, campaign_techniques, subtechnique_parent, tactic_techniques and technique_tactics as well.

summary: Added utils/specialists/binding.py and wired binding_reasons into BaseValidator.validate, so a query that filters a property against values it can never hold now fails the pre-run gate with a named reason instead of executing and returning a silent empty result. The check groups bindings by parameter, which is what keeps subtechnique_parent's 'WHERE t.attack_id IN $ids OR st.attack_id IN $ids' passing: judged one binding at a time that disjunction looks broken, judged one parameter at a time it is correct. Extraction moved here from the audit, which now imports it.
why: An empty result from an impossible query was indistinguishable from an honest 'there are none', and the abstention machinery this project rests on cannot work if the two look alike. The check is deliberately timid - only a positive mismatch on every value of a parameter fails - so on an unlearnable identifier it is silent rather than wrong. Grouping was found by the suite: the first version rejected subtechnique_parent, which is a false positive and would have dropped real answers.

summary: Added utils/specialists/direction.py and used it in group_techniques, campaign_techniques, campaign_attribution, tactic_techniques and software_techniques, so a template reads which end of its edge the caller seeded from the learned schemes instead of assuming the direction the development bank happened to ask. software_techniques also stopped requiring an S-seed to route. The Cypher normalizer gained a matching pivot: when the seed appears in the technique column it emits one record per technique carrying the counterpart ids as related, instead of deduping them away. Live, 'which groups use T1003' went from 0 usable records to the technique anchored with 13 groups; the forward direction is byte-identical.
why: Retrieving the rows is only half the repair - the normalizer was discarding the group column, so the reverse ask still produced an answer with nothing in it. Reading direction from the schema rather than re-authoring a second hand-written template is what makes this survive a dataset that is not MITRE: the same code resolves an anchor for any source whose identifiers the registry can learn.

summary: Measured the repaired template cascade against a worktree of the pre-change tree (ec01fe7). The 120-question development catalogue is identical - 0 improved, 0 regressed, gold_in_evidence 1.0000 both sides, 1061 evidence records both sides - which is arm-figure comparability demonstrated rather than assumed. The 30-question blind holdout goes 0.7688 to 0.8952, 22/30 to 26/30 fully covered, 187 gold ids recovered and 0 lost. Reloaded the CAPEC fixture into Gremlin first, which was empty.
why: The additivity claim was that the fix reaches only task shapes that previously emitted an unsatisfiable query, so no arm figure moves. A stale reference root would have conflated this change with everything since, so the baseline is the immediate parent tree run on the same day against the same live fixtures.

summary: Recorded EXP-2026-08-005 with its protocol, metrics, results and issues, regenerated INDEX.md, and reconciled C-001, C-003, C-010 and C-014. Q1 in OPEN_QUESTIONS.md gains the consequence that matters most: holdout v1 diagnosed this defect, so a v1 re-run on the repaired system is co-authored with its own test, which makes holdout v2 a prerequisite for any blind figure quoted after the fix rather than an optional strengthening.
why: A number that exists only in a chat log does not exist, and the additivity proof - development catalogue 0 improved, 0 regressed, 1061 records both sides - is the evidence that every arm figure from 2026-07-26 stays comparable. C-010 moves because identifier schemes left the MITRE-specific re-authoring list and became something learned from the snapshot.

summary: Ported the outer join from the generic bridge to capec_maps_to and cwe_chain under a new tag freeze/arm-baseline-2, with a second frozen-query generation whose two rewritten cases are hand-authored rather than captured from the tree under test. Fixed the honesty regression this exposed: _empty_ok_results treated 'no records' as the only honest empty, so a producer that returned an anchor with an empty mapping list stopped abstaining and the answer never said the pattern maps to nothing. A declared join with no join values is now an honest empty too, and the abstention wording says what was actually retrieved.
why: The five blind identifiers the templates were still missing are all the inner-join defect, and EXP-2026-08-004 had already proven the fix on the other branch. The abstention repair mattered more than the recall: the project's headline claim is honest abstention with proof, and the outer join had quietly converted an explicit 'no mapping, here is the query' into an answer that described the pattern and changed the subject.

summary: Revised the negative-case gold contract per D-015 and the operator's decision: a new expect_no_join assertion replaces expect_empty on the seven cases where the anchor genuinely exists, records are required and join values forbidden, and federated negatives may now carry cited claims provided both abstentions survive. Changes are in the bank generators, not the compiled JSON. An early draft wrongly flipped A-NEG-01 (nonexistent technique T9999) and corrupted its gold from [] to [T9999]; caught by diffing the recompiled bank and reverted.
why: Gold that asserts a retrievable pattern is unretrievable is false in a way no reviewer can check. Editing gold to match code is the co-authoring failure this project distrusts, so the change is scoped to seven assertion flips with no gold value altered, recorded as a decision, and the abstention assertions stay strict.

summary: Recorded EXP-2026-08-006. The default cascade's blind-holdout retrieval reaches 1.0000 with 30/30 fully covered, from 0.8952, recovering exactly the five identifiers EXP-2026-08-005 named in advance; the development catalogue reports 0 improved and 0 regressed. Updated C-001 and C-014, which now records that both halves of the measured directional cliff were defects rather than properties of template routing.
why: The result worth keeping is not the 1.0000 - the metric is saturated on both banks for both arms and can no longer detect anything. It is that a rising retrieval metric concealed a fall in answer honesty, and only the committed adversarial negatives caught it.

summary: Added LICENSE (Apache-2.0, canonical text from apache.org, copyright line 'Copyright 2026 Florida State University'), declared it in pyproject.toml alongside NOTICE, corrected NOTICE which said the project's own licence was not set, and marked the LICENSE blocker resolved in the artifact appendix. The appendix keeps the outstanding half: the copyright holder has not been confirmed and the Innovation Challenge Fund terms have not been checked for a release constraint.
why: Operator chose Apache-2.0; the patent grant is the usual reason to prefer it over MIT for a research artifact with industrial funding. Without a licence nobody outside the project has any legal right to use the code, which blocked ReliaQuest engineers from touching it, any artifact badge, and the archival DOI. Nothing is pushed, so the file is still reversible if the institution names a different holder.

summary: Added utils/evaluation/judge_answers.py, which grades saved experiment_untruncated answers into the committed judgment schema that holdout_report and answer_gap already read. Until now judgments came only from subagents driven case by case, so no arm could be graded without a human present - Arm H has never been judged on either bank. Carries a --calibrate mode that re-grades answers already holding committed Sonnet judgments and reports agreement rather than overwriting them.
why: The rubric lived in subagent instructions rather than in a file, and the local model is not the cross-provider judge the holdout used, so both the prompt and the grader are reconstructions. Calibration is the only evidence about how far that matters, which is why it is built in rather than optional. A 4096-token budget was found to truncate the judge mid-reasoning and return an empty reply that reads as a dead server; the default is now 8192 with a doubling retry.

summary: Added scripts/overnight_sweep.py and scripts/overnight_report.py: an unattended run of the judged-arm chain - calibration, the cascade and Arm H judged blind at equal retrieval, two repeat judge passes for grader variance, answer_gap on both, the same pair on the 120-question catalogue, then Arm F generation 2 - followed by a generated morning report. Phases are ordered by value rather than dependency, each writes results the moment they exist, and a failed phase is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the night.
why: Every figure in the report is computed from judgment files on disk, so a partial night reports as partial instead of reading like a complete one. The composer fix is deliberately excluded: it changes how answers are produced and is not something to do unattended. Recording the results as experiments is left for the morning because which claims move is a judgement call.

summary: Fixed answer_files in utils/evaluation/judge_answers.py: it excluded only names ending '.judgment.json', so a suffixed repeat pass walked straight into the previous pass's output and graded judgments as answers. The third overnight pass reported n=60 on a set of thirty and rolled thirty real scores together with thirty meaningless ones. Any '.judgment' in the name now disqualifies the file, roll_up additionally drops doubly-suffixed names, and utils/evaluation/tests/test_judge_answers.py walks three passes over one answer set to hold the invariant.
why: Nothing raised - the contaminated pass looked exactly like a completed one, and its mean (0.7583) would have entered the report as the judge's run-to-run spread and wrongly shrunk the measured arm delta. Rolled cleanly over the thirty real cases the third pass reads 0.8400 against 0.8367 and 0.8417, a spread of 0.005. The thirty junk files are quarantined under _contaminated_run3 rather than deleted, so the contamination stays inspectable.

summary: scripts/overnight_report.py now renders a '7b. Figures corrected after the run' section from state['corrections'], showing n and correctness before and after alongside the reason. Three of the night's rolls were frozen before their data was complete: E2b judged the previous pass's judgment files, and E3 and E5b each lost one oversized enumeration case to a truncated judge reply that only succeeded at 32768 tokens.
why: A roll-up is frozen when its phase ends, so a figure can be stale by the time the report is written. Recomputing quietly would leave the report disagreeing with the run log with nothing to explain the difference. Every corrected figure is recomputed from the judgment files on disk rather than adjusted by hand, and both readings are printed.

summary: Overnight sweep completed: 14 phases, 129 minutes, one preflight failure (CAPEC's Gremlin store was empty again after a restart, reloaded during the run). Report at docs/evaluation/overnight-2026-08-19/REPORT.md. The report gained a paired before/after section, a rendered answer_gap breakdown, a catalogue abstention table, and a live unpushed-commit count. Headline figures: paired repair delta +0.1167 on the blind holdout (CI +0.0333 to +0.2167, 10 improved / 3 regressed / 17 unchanged); cascade 0.8367 and Arm H 0.8483 blind, indistinguishable; cascade 0.9839 and Arm H 0.9692 on the catalogue; Arm F generation 2 at 0.9157 blind and 0.9852 on the catalogue.
why: Section 4 read the wrong key ('classes' rather than 'by_reason') so the loss breakdown silently rendered as an empty pointer to a file. Section 3 called any arm delta above the grader spread a separation, which at 2.3x is the weakest possible bar and would have read as though Arm H beat the cascade; it now says outright that the two are indistinguishable at n=30 and contrasts the 23x repair delta. The repair delta was absent entirely despite being the question the fix was built to answer, and pairing it case by case removes the grader from the comparison in a way the unpaired means cannot.

summary: Recorded the overnight judged run as EXP-2026-08-007 and reconciled the ledgers. Headline: the repair is real on answers, not only coverage - paired over the same 30 blind questions and the same grader, 0.7200 -> 0.8367, +0.1167, 95% CI +0.0333 to +0.2167. Arms: cascade 0.8367, Arm H 0.8483 (indistinguishable), Arm F gen-2 0.9157 blind and 0.9852 on the catalogue. Grader calibrated at Pearson r 0.9275 against the committed Sonnet judgments with a three-pass spread of 0.0050. CLAIMS: C-001, C-003, C-013 and C-014 updated; C-017 moved from unsupported to partial; C-021 added for the co-authorship gap at 0.1472. OPEN_QUESTIONS: Q2 half answered, Q14/Q15/Q16 opened, and the stale 'no LICENSE file' weakness closed.
why: Project rules hold that a number existing only in a chat log does not exist, and three prior experiments each closed by admitting nothing had been judged. Two findings changed the plan rather than merely filling a table. C-003 - described in the ledger as the strongest result in the study - is contradicted by its plain reading: Arm H disables the templates and judged level with the cascade, so what the templates hold is provable abstention (95% vs 55% query-proof rate, reproduced on both banks), not accuracy. And Arm F's advantage turns out to be purely a coverage effect: +0.079 blind, 0.0013 on the catalogue, while hallucinating in 19 of 120 catalogue answers against 3. A catalogue-only evaluation would have called it a regression and a blind-only one a clear win.

summary: A fresh question bank is now one command: `uv run python -m utils.specialists.evalset.make_bank --seed N`. Three gaps closed in the holdout protocol - draws now accept an exclusion set so successive banks are disjoint, compile_bank has an entry point, and utils/specialists/evalset/author.py runs the Author role that was previously thirty hand-driven subagent conversations. draw() also gained a `scale` multiplier. utils/specialists/evalset/drawn_anchors.json is the committed registry of every anchor ever drawn, seeded with holdout v1's thirty. Also fixed: the `software` category description asked for the opposite direction of its own gold, and the Author's token budget truncated to empty.
why: Plan 02 predicted that a blind holdout dies when a defect it finds gets fixed, and holdout v1 died exactly that way. The trap is not really a discipline problem, it is a cost problem: a test set that is expensive to produce gets reused past the point where it is still valid, every time. Exclusion is not optional - over 59 reseeds against v1, 51% shared at least one anchor, so a fresh seed alone does not give a fresh bank. Blindness is unchanged: the Author still sees four fields of one anchor and nothing else, and its output is now validated rather than trusted (a question naming any identifier other than its own anchor is rejected and re-requested). What is weaker is phrasing diversity, and the generated dataset card says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.

summary: Two composer defects fixed, both found by dissecting the blind holdout's judged cases rather than by reading the loss table. (1) The enumeration claim fired only on `enumerative or len(ids) > cap`, so a small related set was retrieved, grounded and then stated nowhere; all three under_enumeration cases were CAPEC single records with related sets of 1, 2 and 3. Shape A now fires on any non-empty related set. (2) A single-record result now states the record's description, which the composer excluded from attribute claims as prose while the normalizer summaries were id-lines - so 'what is T1036.010, how does this work' was answered with revoked/stix_type/x_mitre_version. Markdown cross-references are stripped to their link text so a description cannot inject an ungrounded identifier.
why: The loss table said `ungrounded` was 58% of the blind loss and under_enumeration 39%, which is what the plan was written around. Reading the actual cases contradicted it: the three lookup questions filed under `ungrounded` scored 0.5 correctness with groundedness 0.9 and faithfulness 1.0, and a 0.1 groundedness dock cannot explain a 0.5 loss. answer_gap classifies by largest computed deficit and has no category for 'answered with the wrong field', so those cases landed in `ungrounded` by default. The real defect was that the description sat unread in the same record the answer cited. Verified end to end on the three failing questions: H-ABS-01 now carries both gold ids (CAPEC-212, CAPEC-620) and the lookups now carry the mechanism the judge said was missing.

summary: Generated the first bank from the new generator: docs/evaluation/banks/bank-2026-08-19/ (seed 20260819, 30 questions, 30 previously-drawn anchors excluded, 2 Author retries, 0 discards, 0 failures). Wall time ~45 min serial on `local`. Carries anchors.json, authored.json, bank.json and a CARD.md stating the machine-authored limitation.
why: First proof the draw->author->compile chain runs end to end and produces a bank disjoint from holdout v1. Serial because `local` is llama.cpp single-stream; author_all now clamps workers to 1 for such models rather than queueing eight requests into the timeout.

summary: Added the free-form LLM query arm (`--arm llm_query`) that C-012 has never had: utils/specialists/llm_builder.py writes Cypher or Gremlin from the source card's schema, wired into both specialist factories behind a NEW SpecialistConfig.llm_query_builder flag and registered at all five sites in experiment_untruncated.py. The arm holds the plan constant (gold replay, deterministic synthesis) so a difference against Arm A is attributable to query generation alone. 21 tests including six asserting the safety gate still refuses destructive, multi-statement, unbounded-path and unknown-label queries the model might emit.
why: The flag had to be new. SPECIALIST_LLM_ENABLED is already set true by Arms B, C, F and H to mean 'LLM drafter/synthesis' and sat unread by any builder - consuming it would have silently swapped the query builder under four committed arms and invalidated the entire arm table. Smoke run found the arm is only a fair baseline if it is told the harness's output-column convention and the Gremlin id-binding idiom, both of which the templated builders have baked in by construction; without them it measures the harness rather than the model. A deeper coupling remains and is NOT yet addressed: the evidence normalizer dispatches on template-shaped column combinations, so a correct free-form query returning group_id+group_name alone still fails to normalise.

summary: Merged-graph counterfactual (C-015) infrastructure: a second Neo4j service `neo4j-merged` behind a `merged` compose profile on ports 5457/5458 with its own volume, documented in .env and .env.example, and ARIADNE_ALLOW_MERGED_GRAPH which relaxes post-load verification from exact-count equality to at-least-this-many. Ten tests cover the relaxation, including that undershoot still fails and that a non-affirmative flag value does not disable the check.
why: Neo4j Community serves exactly one database per instance, and neither SpecialistConfig nor the connector carries a database name, so a merged graph could only have gone into the graph every other arm queries. That would turn `Mitigation` from 44 ATT&CK mitigations into both catalogues' and make every unscoped query return mixed results - silently invalidating figures already recorded against a clean ATT&CK-only graph, with wipe-and-reload the only way back. A separate instance costs a compose profile and no risk. Verification had to be relaxed because it compares graph-wide totals to one dataset's manifest: after the second load a merged store legitimately holds ~9138 nodes where CAPEC's manifest expects 4769. Only overshoot is tolerated; a count below expectation means records did not land and still fails everywhere.

summary: Added scripts/measure_arms.py and scripts/measure_report.py: a four-phase measurement of everything built on 2026-08-19. Phase A re-runs the cascade on the OLD bank and pairs it question-by-question against last night's saved answers, so the composer fixes get a clean before/after with only the code differing. Phase B runs all four arms over the freshly generated bank that no arm has seen. Phase C splits the llm_query arm's failures into query defects versus output the evidence reader could not parse. Phase D writes a plain-language report.
why: Four things were built today and none had a number attached. The pairing in Phase A matters because an unpaired comparison of means cannot separate a code change from grader drift, and the grader's own run-to-run spread (0.0050) is the same order as a small fix. Phase C exists because the llm_query score otherwise conflates two failures that belong to different parties: the model writing a bad query, and our evidence reader being built around the column shapes the templates emit. Reporting them as one number would misrepresent the baseline in whichever direction the reader happens to fall.

summary: EXP-2026-08-008 recorded. C-012 - the paper's intended headline, previously supported by nothing - is now `supported`: on 30 questions no arm had seen, the template cascade scored 0.9467 against 0.5000 for an arm where a language model writes the query itself, plan held constant. Crediting every failure caused by our own evidence reader it reaches 0.5739, so the conclusion does not rest on ambiguous cases. The morning's two composer fixes are worth +0.0983 paired (95% CI +0.025 to +0.180), 10 improved / 2 regressed / 18 unchanged, with the three predicted cases moving 0.50 to 0.95. C-021 is CORRECTED the same day it was written: the co-authorship gap is 0.0483, not 0.1472.
why: C-021's original figure was measured over a pipeline that still had two answer-writing defects in it, and two-thirds of the gap it recorded was those defects rather than the question set - they hit naturally-phrased blind questions harder than catalogue questions phrased in ways that happened to trigger the working path. Re-measured on the same human-authored questions with the composer repaired, the gap collapses to 0.0483. The generalisable lesson is that a bias measurement taken over a defective pipeline measures the defect too. Q18 records the one ambiguity left in C-012, because whether the evidence reader's template coupling is an artifact or a genuine property of templates leads to two different papers and the experiment deliberately reports both figures rather than picking.

summary: A second unattended night: attack the caveats, not the feature list.
detail: Yesterday's arm table rests on one 30-question bank, graded once, by a model sharing a server with the system under test. scripts/night2_sweep.py goes at all three: a second disjoint bank (does the ordering survive a new draw), the query-writing arm at 4x tokens (two of its three gate refusals were empty replies, a harness defect credited to the templates), repeat runs (is the cascade actually reproducible), a cross-model re-grade of the identical saved answers (is the ranking the system's or the grader's), and the merged-store load with a guard that aborts if a load reaches the main graph. Also fixes a provenance defect: _meta() hardcoded v1's author, so every question in bank-2026-08-19 claimed claude-fable-5 while its own card said local.

summary: Second night: the headline replicates, the top three do not separate, and the merged load stopped on a decision.
detail: Bank 2 (seed 20260820, 30 questions, zero anchor overlap) replicates the C-012 result: templates 0.9417 vs LLM-written queries 0.4183, against 0.9467/0.5000 on bank 1. summary: A project briefing across all nineteen experiments, compiled to PDF.

summary: Neo4j relationship names may be CamelCase, as labels already could.
detail: The relationship rule was ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ while the label rule one line above was ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. That asymmetry was never a decision about safety, it was an accident of which names the loader had met: ten of CAPEC's fifteen relationship names are ones this repo invents (the XML expresses those links by nesting, so there is no name to copy) and are screaming-snake by house style, while five -- ChildOf, CanPrecede, CanFollow, PeerOf, CanAlsoBe -- come verbatim from the Nature attribute of the CAPEC XML. CAPEC had only ever been loaded into Gremlin, which has no such rule, so MITRE's spelling first met this validator when the C-015 merged store was attempted, and was refused. Widening it unblocks that load. What the rule actually blocks is unchanged and now pinned: seven unsafe shapes including a literal injection string must still raise. Operator's call, recorded as D-016; the alternative (renaming CAPEC's five) would have made merged-store queries stop porting to the Gremlin store inside the experiment about queries porting between stores.
tests: 131 passed, 1 skipped (utils/graph_loader)

summary: Build the merged-graph counterfactual's dataset: both catalogues, one graph.
detail: utils/kg_builder/merge.py concatenates the two canonical catalogues into a `merged` dataset under data/merged/ -- 9138 nodes, 34641 relationships, 20 labels (Mitigation is the single collision), 25 relationship types -- and generates its source card, schema, manifest and Neo4j constraints. Output lands in its own data directory rather than data/graphs/ and data/source_cards/ on purpose: load_source_cards() globs source_cards/*.json so a merged card in the ordinary place becomes a third source the planner can route to, and discover_datasets() walks graphs/ so a merged dataset there enters the schema registry that binding.py and direction.py build on the DEFAULT path -- both would silently change arms that are already measured. Isolation is by directory because a directory cannot be left switched on by accident. One substantive transformation: CAPEC nodes gain the public id (CAPEC-n, CWE-n) in the same `attack_id` property ATT&CK uses, because every Cypher query anchors on coalesce(n.attack_id, n.id) and a seed of CAPEC-66 would otherwise match nothing. That is the federated system's own translation (_capec_gremlin_id on the way in, the normalizer on the way out) moved from code into data, and the rule is imported from the Gremlin normalizer rather than restated so the two cannot drift -- 894 promotions, exactly the 558 attack patterns plus 336 weaknesses, with composite children and categories keeping raw ids as the federated path reports them. Artifacts are gitignored like data/graphs/; the builder is the record.

summary: Three functions learn the word `merged`; nothing else changes.
detail: SUPPORTED_DATASETS gains `merged` so the loader will resolve it; build_specialist gains a `merged` branch returning the Cypher specialist (unmodified -- it reads labels, relationships and id schemes from the card it is handed, and the merged card declares the union); _native_ids gains a `merged` branch so a question that names its anchor only in prose still resolves. That last one is priority and not union on purpose: a union would make every question naming both a T-id and a CAPEC id resolve as ambiguous, and an ambiguous anchor abstains, so the merged arm would decline exactly the cross-source questions the counterfactual exists to test. Each edit is a new branch that cannot alter an existing one, and test_merged_specialist.py pins the isolation from the other side: load_source_cards('data') still sees exactly {attack, capec} and discover_datasets('data') still does not contain `merged`, so no arm's planner gains a source and no arm's schema registry gains a dataset to walk.

summary: The merged arm: one Cypher specialist over one store holding both catalogues.
detail: Registers `merged` at all five sites in experiment_untruncated.py. _MergedPool builds ONE Cypher specialist from the merged card and injects it under both `attack` and `capec`, so the authored plan replays unchanged -- two sub-questions, the declared join, producer-before-consumer seeding -- and the only thing that differs from Arm H is how many stores are behind it. Isolation is two env vars set nowhere else: ARIADNE_DATA_DIR=data-merged and NEO4J_URI=:5458. Four supporting changes, each gated so it cannot reach a federated arm: the specialist accepts a task whose source its card declares it `subsumes`; resolve() and resolve_anchor() take their anchor rules from the task's declared source when the card subsumes several, so each sub-question resolves exactly as it does federated; the semantic validator unions both rule sets for `merged` (it fell to the ATT&CK arm before, so every CAPEC edge read as illegal); and registry.py stopped keeping its own copy of SUPPORTED_DATASETS, which is why adding a dataset to config.py was not enough. Also two identifier reconciliations in the merged build (D-017) and a separation check script. Loaded and verified: 9138 nodes, 34641 relationships, Mitigation splits 44/1170, main ATT&CK store untouched at 4369.

summary: EXP-2026-08-009 protocol and sweep, fixed before any phase runs.
detail: scripts/merged_sweep.py defines the phases, their order, the grader and its budget; PROTOCOL.md states both hypotheses before the numbers exist. The comparison that matters is `merged` against `generic` -- same schema-driven primitives, same authored plans, same questions, same grader in one session, so the number of stores is the only variable; `deterministic` is graded alongside as a secondary reading because reading the merged arm only against the templated one would confound storage with templating. The federated arms are re-JUDGED rather than re-run: their answers are on disk, and re-running `generic` would add run variance (an LLM is in its loop; the narrator arm measured 0.0283 against itself) while removing only grader variance (0.0050). Judgments go to a .c015 sidecar with force=True, so the committed judgments are untouched and an interrupted attempt cannot leave one cell graded by an earlier pass. Threats to validity are recorded before the run, including the two identifier reconciliations the merged arm receives (D-017) and the neighbour-join advantage that follows from them.

summary: C-015 answered: federating does not beat merging on correctness.
detail: EXP-2026-08-009. With the number of stores as the only variable -- schema-derived primitives and deterministic composition on both sides, no language model in either, so both byte-reproducible -- merging scores -0.0334 against federating on one blind set and +0.0000 on the other (n=30 each, intervals overlapping almost entirely). C-015 as written is refuted; Q5 is answered. What is refuted is the CORRECTNESS claim and only that: 60 anchored questions over two catalogues whose identifier spaces do not collide says nothing about open-ended questions or about colliding sources, and it does not touch the arguments federation is actually made on (provenance, licensing, staleness, not re-running a merge on update) -- none of which is written down as a claim anywhere, and which are now the whole of the surviving case. Secondary, same session: generic (LLM narrator) 0.9833/1.0000, deterministic 0.9667/0.9667. Fabrication counts settle the confound the first pass raised: the two deterministic-composer arms fabricate at the same rate over one store and two (5 vs 4 across 60 questions each), so the composer's habit of calling software 'used techniques' is not a cost of merging. Three cases needed a third grading attempt at 32768 after two empty replies; all are 177k-205k-char answers to one question in every arm, so the size is the question's, not a composer's -- and the largest of the four graded first time while smaller ones did not.

summary: Plan for EXP-2026-08-011: measure schema transfer on ReliaQuest's identity catalog.
detail: docs/plans/2026-08-21-identity-schema-transfer.md sequences nine steps from catalog ingest to judged result. The point is that C-010 is currently `supported` by EXP-2026-07-011, an audit whose own threats section says no non-MITRE dataset was ever loaded -- so the portability verdict is a code reading. ReliaQuest supplied their production graph catalog (72 node types, 21 edge labels, 60 typed triples, 779+118 attributes, no customer records), which is exactly the declared-schema input the architecture claims to need. Two design commitments are fixed here: the identity source stays isolated by directory and store URI as `merged` was, because load_source_cards() globs and discover_datasets() walks, and either would silently add a source to arms already measured; and gold derives from the generator's blueprint rather than from the loaded graph, mirroring gold_bank.py's independence so a dropped edge shows up instead of cancelling out. Steps 1-6 and 8 need no language model at all, so the headline retrieval number is not blocked by skynet contention; steps 7 and 9 are LLM-gated and both checkpoint per item.

summary: EXP-2026-08-011 pre-registered: does the schema-agnostic path work on a schema it has never seen?
detail: PROTOCOL.md fixes four hypotheses before anything is built. H1/H2 are the load-bearing pair: if the generic arm retrieves >=0.90 and the template cascade <0.40, then the arm gap IS the dataset-specific surface measured at run time, which is what C-010 currently asserts on the strength of an AST count in an audit that never loaded a non-MITRE dataset. H3 predicts a specific defect from the data model rather than from pessimism -- a PlausibleFacet is (rel_type, direction, neighbour_label), so when both endpoints carry the same label the neighbour carries no disambiguating signal; ATT&CK has essentially no homogeneous-label edges and this schema has eight, all of them the privilege-escalation edges an analyst would ask about. H4 tests idscheme.py's stated honesty property on data built to break it. Dataset card records the delivery's checksums and its permanent truncation: the export's inner join to customer_attribute_catalog dropped every edge type with no attributes, which is why there is no USER-MEMBER_OF->GROUP triple and why 48 of 60 triples start at GROUP; the operator confirmed no corrected export is coming, so inferred edges are carried in a separate marked block and every result splits declared-vs-inferred. Q19 files the no-shared-key federation idea as a follow-on rather than folding it in, because a hand-built crosswalk would confound transfer with crosswalk quality.
tests: make validate-research OK — 22 experiments

summary: Read a declared schema from a customer catalog instead of deriving one from instances.
detail: utils/kg_builder/catalog/ parses ReliaQuest's two CSVs into one artifact: 72 node types, 21 edge labels, 60 declared triples, 779 node and 118 edge attributes, verified against the dataset card by a test class that skips when the (non-redistributable, uncommitted) delivery is absent. Three things the model insists on carrying rather than flattening. First, declared-vs-observed provenance on every triple -- observed means some node actually has this edge, declared means the catalog permits it, and honest-zero claims rest on the difference. Second, declared value types, which the existing scan path cannot produce at all since it only ever sees a key. Third, the truncation: detect_truncation() runs on every read and returns a verdict either way, calling this delivery incomplete on two structural grounds (MEMBER_OF reaches GCP_GROUP and OKTA_GROUP but never GROUP; 48 of 60 triples start at GROUP) rather than on a hunch, and carrying the corrected query so the artifact holds the fix and not just the complaint. Nothing is normalised on the way in, so the real ENTRA_LICENCE/ENTRA_LICENSE collision survives -- it is a free disambiguation case and cleaning it would mean evaluating against a tidier schema than the customer runs. Three inferred edges are added in a separate module, each with a written justification, tagged so they can never pass as delivered, and refused outright if they collide with a declared triple. One trap caught while generating: GROUP -MEMBER_OF-> GROUP is both inferred and homogeneous, which would have silently enlarged EXP-2026-08-011's H3 population from the delivered 8 to 9 and mixed a finding about ReliaQuest's schema with one about our own reconstruction, so homogeneous_triples() now takes an origin filter and counts break the two out.
tests: 21 passed (utils/kg_builder/catalog); 129 passed (utils/kg_builder)

summary: A DatasetSchema can now be built from a declared catalog, with no instances to scan.
detail: build_declared_schema() sits beside build_dataset_schema() and is deliberately a sibling rather than a branch inside it: the scan path is the evidence behind every measured arm on record, and the safest second path is one that cannot execute a line of the first. DatasetSchema gains two defaulted fields so no existing construction changes meaning -- `provenance` (observed | declared) and `inferred_triples`. The provenance flag is not cosmetic: under `observed` a facet's honest zero means this label can have such an edge and this node has none, while under `declared` the same zero also admits that no node anywhere has one yet, which is a weaker statement, and a caller that cares can now tell them apart. Identifier schemes are left deliberately empty because a catalog has no values to learn from; that makes value_verdict() answer `undetermined` to everything, which is precisely what idscheme.py's docstring prescribes for a source whose values have not been seen, and inventing schemes out of declared value types would manufacture confident verdicts from a type name (STRING says nothing about shape). The consequence -- the binding guard cannot fire on this source -- is EXP-2026-08-011's H4 and is measured rather than worked around. A test pins the mechanism behind H3 as a fact about the data model: GROUP -OWNS-> GROUP yields (OWNS, out, GROUP) and (OWNS, in, GROUP), identical but for the direction field, so the neighbour label cannot disambiguate a question phrased either way. Isolation is pinned from the other side as EXP-2026-08-009 required for `merged`: discover_datasets('data') excludes identity, build_registry('data') does not contain it, load_source_cards('data') is still exactly {attack, capec}, and every schema in the default registry is still `observed`.
tests: 17 passed (test_declared); 778 passed (utils/specialists, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5); 284 passed 2 skipped (utils/planner utils/graph_loader)

summary: EXP-2026-08-010 pre-registered: does Ariadne survive questions it did not co-author?
detail: Every correctness figure this project has published comes from a bank Ariadne co-authored; template banks carry a measured co-authorship bias of 0.147 and the LLM-generated banks are still schema-aware. A web search on 2026-08-21 found no human-authored ATT&CK or CAPEC question set anywhere public, but that search conflated two needs -- human phrasing (Q16, still blocked) and external authorship (Q1, available today). Four hypotheses pre-registered before any code ran.
