summary: An external-benchmark evaluation layer whose primary metric contains no language model.
detail: Four modules under utils/evaluation/external, one property each. fetch pins both dataset revisions and never commits the data -- CTIBench is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and share-alike would follow a redistributed copy into this history, and AttackQA is 7 MB of somebody else's bytes. items turns benchmark rows into bank entries and authors the plan and nothing else; tests assert a derived entry carries neither an assertions block nor an ex_gold block, because this project's own banks carry both and either would hand the answer to the arm under test. oracle reads the canonical JSONL directly, with no plan, specialist or query engine in the way, since anything in the retrieval path would make the ceiling a measurement of the thing it is supposed to bound. score extracts ATT&CK identifiers with one regex and compares sets; macro and micro are both reported because a benchmark whose gold sizes run from 1 to 19 is misread by either alone. The family-mapping test failed twice before passing, both times on anchors rather than the mapping -- T1548 has no campaigns, T1105 has no sub-techniques -- and the reason is recorded in the test, since 'family returns nothing' reads as a broken mapping and was not one.
tests: 28 passed (utils/evaluation/external)

summary: The derived external plan was weaker than the one internal questions get.
detail: This project's own bank entries put the relationship type into `entities` beside the node labels -- H-SUB-01 carries Technique, SubTechnique, HAS_SUBTECHNIQUE. The derivation supplied labels only, on the reasoning that naming a relationship would be doing the planner's job. That reasoning was backwards: withholding it does not purify the control, it hands external questions a weaker plan than the internal comparison gets, which converts a harness deficit into an apparent system failure -- the exact error this experiment exists to avoid making about somebody else's benchmark. Appending it fixes techniques_sub and techniques_parent outright, 0.000 to 1.000; four Software/Group/Campaign families are unmoved by any hint and are a real capability gap. The run was stopped and restarted and the first run's numbers are quoted nowhere. Found the long way round, by checking whether this project's grader had been rewarding answers that omit the requested identifier -- it had not, and reading the bank entry to confirm that is what exposed the third element. An intermediate check was also wrong and is recorded: a substring test for 'T1055' matches inside 'T1055.002'.
tests: 28 passed (utils/evaluation/external)

summary: EXP-2026-08-010 complete: templates cost coverage, and the internal banks were drawn from the shapes they serve.
detail: 182 external questions from CTIBench cti-ate and AttackQA, scored as identifier sets with no judge anywhere. On 60 identical questions the template cascade scores 0.7170 recall and the template-free arm scores 0.9953 -- the graph's own ceiling, exactly. Templates are 0.278 behind on coverage and ahead on precision as a reader sees it, 0.709 against 0.418, because the generic arm returns every neighbour and lets the reader sort them. H1 and H2 both split by arm in a way the pre-registration did not anticipate. Of 14 question types, 8 match the ceiling to three decimals and 4 return nothing at all: every Group-Software and Campaign-Software ask, for which no template exists, so 'what software does this group use' is answered with the group's techniques. Two more lose ~70% to one pinned label -- _group_techniques targets (t:Technique) and three of G0020's four gold answers are sub-techniques; the builder already widens that target but only when the anchor is a sub-technique. Neither showed up internally because all eight group/campaign/software questions across both banks are technique-anchored and Group-Software is never asked at all. That is co-authorship bias located precisely: not a wrong answer, but a question the bank does not contain. H3 held and matters beyond this project -- a direct read of ATT&CK 19.0 scores 0.607 precision against cti-ate's gold, so the benchmark is four releases stale and any cti-ate precision figure read against 1.0 overstates its headroom.
tests: 1642 passed, 2 failed (both pre-existing: setup_wizard, conversation), 214 skipped

summary: A seeded synthetic tenant that obeys the ReliaQuest catalog, plus the blueprint gold will come from.
detail: utils/kg_builder/synthetic/ emits 1,339 nodes across all 72 declared labels and 3,816 edges over 20 edge kinds, byte-identical on re-run from seed 20260821. Conformance is structural rather than reviewed: _Builder.edge() raises on any edge the catalog does not permit, so a non-conforming graph cannot be written in the first place. The blueprint (spec.py) is written upstream of the graph and gold will derive from it, never from the loaded store -- the same independence gold_bank.py gets by parsing raw STIX outside kg_builder, manufactured here because a synthetic dataset has no raw source to fall back on. Without it a dropped edge would cancel out on both sides and be invisible. Two defects found and fixed while building. First, hand-written property dicts silently lost every key whose spelling this project guessed wrong: the catalog keys AD objects as active_directory__user_uid, not objectsid, so the tenant carried no SID-shaped values at all, which would have made H4's `more than half of properties learn as open` prediction easier than it should be; property generation is now driven entirely off declared attributes and types, with identifier shape following the platform prefix in the label (ARNs for AWS, opaque base-62 for Okta, GUIDs for Entra, SIDs for AD). Second, the generator knew a larger topology than any one catalog declares, so it aborted on hand-written test fixtures; every topology block and every planted chain is now guarded by supports(), and chains plant all-or-nothing because a half-planted path would have gold naming a walk the graph cannot make. Also populates the 58 labels that appear in no declared triple -- the same inner-join truncation seen from the node side -- because they are real declared types and they are the honest surface for the abstention measurement.
tests: 25 passed (utils/kg_builder/synthetic); 154 passed (utils/kg_builder); regeneration byte-identical across nodes/relationships/spec

summary: The identity source card, and the tenant loaded into a store of its own.
detail: The card splits the way ATT&CK's and CAPEC's do: the catalog generates labels, properties, relationship types and endpoints, and a committed overlay carries what no catalog can state -- connection, safety, provenance, and glosses for all 72 labels and 21 edges. The glosses are load-bearing rather than decorative: six labels contain the word `group` and one of them (AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP) is a firewall rule set and not a principal at all, so when a question says `group` the descriptions are the deterministic planner's only disambiguation signal. Card and overlay also state plainly what this source is -- schema_provenance `declared`, instance_provenance `synthetic` -- so nothing downstream has to remember which half is real. The semantic validator gets an `identity` branch that, uniquely, derives its legal edge patterns FROM the schema rather than restating them in code, because a rule set restated in code can drift from the catalog it describes. Loaded into its own Neo4j on :5459 behind a compose profile: 1,339 nodes, 3,814 relationships, 72 labels, 20 edge kinds, all matching the blueprint, with the planted DCSync chain walkable in the store. 10/10 separation checks pass. Two defects fixed in the loading. The generator was writing an edge twice when a planted chain wanted one a random pass had already made (USER-MEMBER_OF->GROUP and GROUP-DC_SYNC->DOMAIN both did), which Neo4j MERGEs back to one -- so the blueprint claimed 3,816 against a store holding 3,814, exactly the divergence the blueprint exists to prevent; edge() is now idempotent on (source, edge, target). And the manifest emitted `edges`/`edges_by_label` where the loader reads `relationships`/`relationships_by_type`, so expected counts came through as zero.
tests: 170 passed (utils/kg_builder); 187 passed 1 skipped (utils/graph_loader utils/specialists/schema); 10/10 separation checks; store verified at 1339/3814/72/20

summary: Identity gold, computed from the blueprint and cross-checked against the store.
detail: identity_gold.py derives every expected answer from spec.json and never from Neo4j -- the same independence gold_bank.py gets by parsing raw STIX outside kg_builder, and the reason the suite doubles as an ingestion check. A live test walks the store and asserts agreement on all 22 facet questions plus the node and edge totals; if the blueprint and the store ever diverge, that test is the only thing that can say so. Seven question kinds, each attached to a hypothesis: describe/facet-out/facet-in/multihop for H1, homo-out and homo-in for H3, unanswerable for abstention. identity_bank.py keeps make_bank's three-role separation -- seeded uniform sampler, an author that sees four fields of one anchor and nothing else, a compiler that discards rather than repairs -- but is a sibling rather than a parameterisation, because holdout_protocol's populations and strata are ATT&CK and CAPEC by construction and generalising it would mean editing code four recorded experiments depend on. A test asserts the author's prompt never contains any expected answer, which is the single property that makes the bank blind. One real modelling error caught by its own test: facet gold was walking the edge NAME, but in this schema one name spans many triples -- ALL_EXTENDED_RIGHTS runs from GROUP to six different target labels -- so a question meant to be about the homogeneous GROUP->GROUP triple silently became a question about six triples at once, and H3's population stopped being homogeneous. Gold is now scoped by neighbour label, which is also the retrieval problem actually being posed: filter on label and direction, not on relationship name. 30 questions drawn, zero discards.
tests: 18 passed (test_identity_gold), including the live blueprint-vs-store cross-check over 22 facet questions and 1339/3814 totals

summary: EXP-2026-08-011 bank authored, and a portability defect an AST count could not see.
detail: 27 of 30 questions authored blind against the identity schema; 3 stayed empty even at a 16,384-token budget and were discarded rather than repaired, which is the protocol. The first real query through the source found I-1, recorded in the experiment's ISSUES.md and arguably the headline finding so far: the Cypher builder's label_scan template emitted `RETURN n.attack_id AS id` against a schema with no attack_id anywhere, so every row came back with a null id, the normalizer rejected all of them for a missing record_id, and a valid query over a correctly loaded graph returned nothing. EXP-2026-07-011 counted 19 of 25 templates as MITRE-specific by parsing source for template identifiers and did NOT flag this one -- because its MITRE-specificity is not in its question shape, which is generic, but in the property name it emits. That is a whole class of coupling an AST count structurally cannot see, and it means C-010's bounded surface was undercounted systematically rather than incidentally. Fixed with coalesce(n.attack_id, n.id), the idiom the merged build already uses (D-017), byte-identical on ATT&CK where attack_id is never null on a scannable label. Fixing it now does not burn the bank: the trap make_bank.py documents is fixing something in RESPONSE to a holdout question failing, and this was found by a hand-written smoke query before any arm was scored. From here the line is explicit -- registration gaps get completed, retrieval-quality failures get recorded, because those are the measurement. I-2 is the first of the latter: the planner routes `the Helpdesk group` to AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP, an EC2 firewall rule set, and is left unfixed on purpose.
tests: 794 passed, 2 skipped (utils/specialists, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5) after the label_scan change

summary: EXP-2026-08-011 answered: on the first non-MITRE schema, both arms retrieve nothing.
detail: 27 blind questions against ReliaQuest's customer catalog, no language model in the answer path, gold derived from the generator blueprint. Both arms score 0.0000 on 27 of 27, and the arm gap is 0.0000 -- not because the two are equivalent but because they fail upstream of where they differ. The anchor label is queried on 1 of 27 questions. The mechanism is entity extraction: the deterministic planner matches question words against the card's schema vocabulary, which on ATT&CK is 11 labels of distinctive jargon and here is 72 labels plus 779 attribute names of ordinary IT English. `What can Database Admins generically write?` extracts GCP_SQL_INSTANCE -- because `database` appears in its declared attribute gcp__database_uid -- and scans that instead of GROUP. `Technique` was queried 12 times against a graph that has no such label. H1 is falsified; H2 and H3 are not evaluable because both arms floor; H4 splits, with zero false mismatches (the safety property holds against 72 labels) but an open-rate of 3.7% that is an artifact of the generator's formulaic filler values and must not be quoted as a property of identity data. Judging was not run and is recorded as a scoping decision: with retrieval at zero everywhere, a judge can only confirm that answers containing no gold evidence are not correct. C-010 moves from supported to partial. Its evidence was EXP-2026-07-011, an audit whose own threats section predicted exactly this, and the miss is larger than `some templates need re-authoring`: the audit counted template identifiers and classified them by question shape, so it could not see a generic-shaped template emitting n.attack_id; and it classified the planner as portable when in fact the planner is not schema-scale-independent. Two harness defects of my own were found and fixed before these numbers were taken, both of which had produced plausible wrong results first -- the sweep serialised the evidence bundle with default=str and lost every query, and the card under-declared `name`.
tests: make validate-research OK — 22 experiments; sweep re-run reproduces 0.0000 on both arms

summary: Five structural fixes take the foreign schema from 0.0000 to 0.8519 retrieval.
detail: Working against EXP-2026-08-011's 27 questions as a development set. Every change is schema-driven and none names a label, a group or a question. (1) The name-lookup label guard was a hard-coded list of eight ATT&CK labels, so on any other source the guard read `n:Technique OR n:SubTechnique OR ...` against a graph containing none of them and a name lookup could never match however well the name was extracted; it is now derived from the labels that declare a `name` property. (2) That derivation needed the schema registry to know about `name`, which it did not: build_dataset_schema scanned each node's `properties` dict and `name` is a first-class top-level column, so no dataset -- ATT&CK included -- ever recorded it. (3) The seedless-scan fallback label was the literal "Technique", observed 12 times as a query against a graph with no such label; it now falls back to a declared label. (4) A name-resolved anchor could not be traversed from: walking a relationship was gated on seed_ids, so on any source with no analyst-facing identifier the traversal primitive was unreachable and every relationship question collapsed to describing the anchor and reporting facet counts. (5) The gate onto the name path was `is_definitional_request` -- a 'what is X' phrasing -- so a question that names its subject but asks something else fell to a bare label scan; it now also admits a name carrying structure (space, dot, hyphen or digit), which keeps 'List ATT&CK software entries' on the scan path the gate was put there to protect. Two supporting fixes: the resolver was shredding dotted and hyphenated identifiers (corp.corp.example -> corp + example) so structured tokens are now kept whole, and the Cypher validator's relationship regex could not parse alternation, meaning a query using [r:A|B] had NO relationship type checked against the card at all -- a validator silently declining to validate, fixed independently of the rest. Result on the development set: generic 0.0000 -> 0.8519 with 23 of 27 perfect, reverse-direction questions 0.0 -> 1.0, homogeneous same-label-both-ends triples 0.0 -> 1.0, abstention 0.0 -> 1.0. The template cascade sits at 0.2778, and the arms have separated for the first time on this source.
tests: 1250 passed, 2 skipped (kg_builder specialists graph_loader planner, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5) -- identical to the pre-change baseline, so ATT&CK and CAPEC are unmoved

summary: Ariadne can now answer what software a group or campaign uses. Four external question families went from 0.000 to 1.000.
detail: EXP-2026-08-010 found four of fourteen external question families returning nothing at all, every one of them traversing Group-Software or Campaign-Software. There was no template for those edges, and the dispatcher's unconditional `if has_group` sent the question to group_techniques, which answered with the group's techniques instead -- for a group with none recorded, that is silence. The fix is one builder (_actor_software, either end anchorable, following _software_techniques), two dispatch branches placed ahead of the ones that used to swallow these questions, and one normalizer branch. That last piece was nearly missed: the first version passed its unit test on the query string while the feature did not work at all, because the normalizer had no case for the new columns and every identifier came back as `unknown` -- four records retrieved, none readable. A query-string test cannot see that; the measurement saw it immediately. Two existing tests failed because the gap closed rather than opened, and one of them documented the gap in its own comment: the binding gate was refusing this question because the template could not walk the edge, and there is now no misroute for it to catch. External recall 0.6836 -> 0.7633, exact match 0.4451 -> 0.6593, families at the ceiling 8 -> 12 of 14. The safety check that could have stopped it held completely: the deterministic arm re-run over both committed banks produced 60 of 60 byte-identical answers and did not move a single query string. The proposed second fix -- widening the pinned (t:Technique) target, worth another 0.219 recall -- is NOT taken. evalset/questions.py::_top_level deliberately filters the gold to parent techniques for exactly those templates, so the narrow answer is an intentional roll-up rather than a defect, and the two external benchmarks disagree with each other about it. The patch is kept at the experiment's data/proposed-fix1-widen-target.patch as a decision waiting on an owner.
tests: 804 passed, 2 failed pre-existing in worktree (docs_contracts path check); 60/60 internal answers byte-identical

summary: EXP-2026-08-011 amended: the 0.8519 existed only in a commit message; and a disjoint second bank.
detail: Commit 74d027e raised the identity retrieval from 0.0000 to 0.8519 but touched only code, the changelog and the sweep state -- it never updated the experiment record, so metrics.json and RESULTS.md still reported 0.0000 and the research record contradicted the working tree. AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS is explicit that a number living only in a commit message does not exist, and that a complete experiment is corrected by an appended AMENDMENTS section rather than a silent edit, so that is what this does. Reproduced the figure first: 0.8519 generic against 0.2778 deterministic, unchanged on re-run. A-2 restates the hypotheses honestly -- H1 stays falsified as pre-registered because it predicted >=0.90 with no changes, H2 becomes evaluable for the first time now that the arms have separated by +0.5741, and H3 did not reproduce (homogeneous triples reach 1.0, level with heterogeneous, so the direction defect the PlausibleFacet reasoning predicted did not appear once anchors resolved). A-3 is the one that matters for how the number gets quoted: the 27 questions have now been iterated against and 0.8519 is a development-set figure that must never be reported as blind. So identity_bank.draw() gains an `exclude` parameter and the CLI an --exclude-bank flag, mirroring holdout_protocol's reason for having one -- over 59 reseeds against its v1 draw, 51% still shared an anchor, so a fresh seed alone does not make a bank disjoint. Bank 2 is drawn at seed 20260822 excluding all 24 bank-1 anchors, verified at zero overlap, and is the blind test of whether the five fixes generalised.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; 16 passed 2 skipped (test_identity_gold); bank1/bank2 anchor overlap verified at 0

summary: The identity fixes generalise: 0.7857 blind on a bank they never saw.
detail: Bank 2 -- 28 questions, seed 20260822, all 24 bank-1 anchors excluded and verified at zero overlap, same blind authoring protocol, gold from the blueprint, no code changed between the runs. The schema-derived arm scores 0.7857 against the template cascade's 0.1964. The development-to-blind drop is 0.0662, close to this project's own measured co-authorship bias of 0.0483 and nowhere near what fitting five changes to 27 particular sentences would have cost. The arm gap WIDENED blind, +0.5893 against +0.5741, which is the reading that matters: an advantage produced by tuning against bank 1 would shrink when the questions changed, and it did not. Two banks together also correct a conclusion either would have given alone. The development set showed 1.0 on both homogeneous kinds and on multihop; blind they are 0.6, 0.667 and 0.5, while facet-out went the other way (0.5 -> 0.8333). Five questions per kind cannot tell 1.0 from 0.7, so those 1.0s were partly small-sample luck, and the honest joint reading is that homogeneous and multi-hop sit around 0.6-0.8 and are the remaining weakness. facet-in holds at 1.0 across both banks, so the reverse-direction failure that motivated H3 is genuinely fixed rather than sampled away, and abstention holds at 1.0 across both. C-010 stays partial with the corrected form recorded: the machinery transfers after five defects only a run could find, and the schema-derived path is worth about +0.59 over hand-written templates on a foreign schema.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; bank1/bank2 anchor overlap 0; no code change between the two sweeps

summary: The composer no longer calls a Group or a piece of software a "used technique".
detail: EXP-2026-08-010 caught the deterministic composer writing "S0512 (FatDuke) has 2 used techniques: G0016, C0023", where G0016 is a Group and C0023 a Campaign. ATT&CK's USES joins Group->Software, Campaign->Software and Software->Technique alike, while _REL_NOUNS maps the relationship to a single noun, so the noun asserted a kind the neighbours were not. The identifiers were correct and retrieved; only the label lied, which is the worst shape this can take because nothing in the sentence tells a reader which half to distrust. This was the last known fabrication source in an otherwise deterministic path. A relationship noun that asserts a kind is now used only when the neighbour labels are that kind (_NOUN_EXPECTS); a noun with no entry is unconstrained, so CAPEC's hierarchy roles are untouched, and unlabelled neighbours keep the old wording rather than being demoted on missing evidence. Two further bugs surfaced in the same eight lines: the label fallback was count-blind and wrote "has 1 Skills", and it appended an s to the label verbatim and wrote "1 TaxonomyEntrys" -- a type name with a plural bolted on. Both fixed. The cost is real and was measured rather than assumed: 21 of 60 committed answers change wording, while 60 of 60 keep every identifier they named and every claim entity_id. Recorded as D-024, including the consequence that any judged figure over those 21 was computed on the old prose and only a re-judge can state a post-fix number.
tests: 1152 passed (utils/synthesis, utils/specialists, utils/evaluation); 60/60 answers identical on identifiers, 21/60 changed in prose

summary: Judged the identity blind bank: faithful answers on the schema-derived path, 82% unsupported claims on the templates.
detail: EXP-2026-08-011 originally skipped judging because retrieval was 0.0000 and a grader could only confirm a foregone number; with retrieval now at 0.7857 blind that reasoning lapsed, so identity_sweep.py gains a --stage judge that rebuilds each answer by re-running the deterministic path (no language model in it, byte-reproducible, so the rebuild is exact) and hands the live answer and evidence objects to the existing calibrated judge. Both arms in ONE session on the 28 blind questions. The schema-derived arm: faithfulness 0.9821, groundedness 0.9893, unsupported-claim rate 0.1071, zero conflicts. The template cascade: 0.8893, 0.8500, and an unsupported-claim rate of 0.8214. That last pair is the finding -- retrieval already showed the templates finding almost nothing on a foreign schema, and this shows what the composer does with nothing, which is to keep asserting. Retrieving badly and answering anyway is a worse failure than retrieving badly and abstaining, and only a judged pass separates them. By kind the generic arm's unsupported claims sit entirely in describe (0.50) and homo-in (0.20) with every other kind at 0.000 including the abstention cases, while the template arm is above 0.5 everywhere and at 1.0 on facet-in and on unanswerable -- fabricating most reliably where it should decline. Three caveats recorded rather than smoothed: the generic arm's grader is `mixed` at 25/28 with three answers falling to the deterministic proxy while the template arm got 28/28; judge variance was measured rather than assumed at 0.0035 on faithfulness across two sessions, so the 0.71 arm difference in unsupported rate is two orders of magnitude above grader noise; and a second session that covered the generic arm slightly better was deliberately NOT substituted in, because comparing arms graded in different sessions folds grader variance into the arm difference. Evidence sufficiency of 0.6786 is the known deterministic-composer id-line ceiling, not a retrieval gap on this schema.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; judge stability 0.0035 across two sessions on the same answers

summary: The development-bank judging run failed on server contention; recorded, not reported.
detail: After the blind bank judged cleanly, the same pass over the 27-question development bank was run so correctness could be compared development-vs-blind the way retrieval already had been. The LLM judge reached 12 of 27 generic answers and 0 of 27 deterministic answers, so the deterministic arm was graded entirely by the fallback proxy and the two arms were scored by different instruments -- exactly the confound A-6 refused to introduce when it declined to substitute a better-covered second grading session. Its numbers are not a correctness comparison and are not quoted anywhere; the file is kept and flagged UNUSABLE in its own metadata rather than deleted, per the rule that failed runs are recorded. The cause is environmental and not a defect: a one-line completion that returned in about two seconds earlier in the session did not return within 90 seconds when the relay was checked immediately afterwards, and nothing in the judge stage changed between the successful blind run and this one. Unaffected: the blind judged result stands on its own earlier session at 25/28 and 28/28 coverage, and the development-vs-blind retrieval comparison has no language model in it at all. I-7 records the retry condition -- check that `source` is `llm` for BOTH arms before reporting anything from a re-run.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments

summary: Bank 3 drawn at 117 questions, gold computed; authoring blocked on the relay.
detail: A-5 and A-6 both rest on kinds of two to six questions, and A-5 already records being misled by exactly that -- the development set showed 1.0 on homo-* and multihop where blind showed 0.6 to 0.667, because five questions cannot distinguish 1.0 from 0.7. Bank 3 is the fix: 117 questions at seed 20260823 across 86 distinct anchors, excluding all 49 anchors used by banks 1 and 2 and verified at zero overlap, with facet-in and facet-out at 24 each, both homo kinds at 20, describe at 16 and unanswerable at 12. The sampler CLI now takes comma-separated --exclude-bank and an explicit --shape so the draw is reproducible from the command rather than an ad-hoc script. Gold is computed and committed; only authoring remains and that needs the relay, which is currently returning a one-line completion in over seven minutes against a five-minute judge timeout. One kind cannot be scaled and this is recorded as a limitation rather than worked around: the generator plants exactly five attack chains and banks 1 and 2 consumed four, so multihop stays at n=1. Planting more means regenerating the tenant, which changes node ids and invalidates every gold answer in the earlier banks, so the three would no longer measure the same graph. The multi-hop figure must not be quoted as a rate until a new experiment rebuilds the tenant and re-runs all three banks.
tests: 16 passed 2 skipped (test_identity_gold); bank3 anchor overlap with banks 1+2 verified at 0

summary: Cross-model judging: the local judge overstates faithfulness by 0.43, and the independent judges found a defect it scored past.
detail: C-009 already established that self-judged evaluation materially overstates quality and that the primary evaluation must be cross-model, so the same identity answers A-6 graded on the local skynet relay were graded again by ten independent Claude Sonnet judges. The rubric is the existing one verbatim -- build_messages composes the payloads, so only the model differs and nothing about the prompt does. On the blind bank the local judge reads generic faithfulness 0.9821 where Sonnet reads 0.5500, and deterministic 0.8893 where Sonnet reads 0.3500: overstatements of 0.4321 and 0.5393, four to five times C-009's original 0.1054 gap on the MITRE pipeline. What survives is the conclusion rather than the level -- the arm ordering is preserved under both judges, so schema-derived primitives still beat hand-written templates on a foreign schema (+0.20 faithfulness under Sonnet, +0.09 under skynet), but no claim of near-ceiling faithfulness survives. The Sonnet figures are the quotable ones; A-6 is kept because the disagreement between the two instruments is itself the measurement. Several judges independently flagged the same concrete defect the local judge scored straight past, now recorded as I-9 and located at normalizer.py:885,888: the summary line hardcodes `Found N ATT&CK record(s)` with no card lookup and no dataset branch, so an identity graph reports GROUP, GPO, DOMAIN and AWS_EC2_SECURITY_GROUP objects as ATT&CK records. That is the third member of the same family as I-1 and the Technique-label scan -- MITRE vocabulary baked into code that presents as source-agnostic, invisible to a code reading because there is no schema dependency to spot, only a string. Deliberately not fixed yet: the answers under measurement were produced by the present code, so fixing mid-flight would leave the judged figures describing a system that no longer exists. Two caveats recorded rather than smoothed: six of 108 verdicts could not be attributed to a bank because the agent output schema omitted the bank field and question ids repeat across banks, so they are excluded from the per-bank split; and the two judges are not calibrated against each other, so 0.43 is a raw difference between instruments and not a corrected one.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; 102 of 108 verdicts attributed to a bank, 0 errored

summary: Bank 3 authored by Fable across 8 parallel agents after the relay never produced a single question.
detail: The overnight sequential authoring run against the local relay was checked and had produced 0 of 117 questions before its process died with the session -- the relay never answered one request, consistent with the >7-minute single-line latency measured earlier. Authoring moved to Claude Fable across 8 parallel agents, chosen over Sonnet on the operator's call for stronger cybersecurity phrasing. 117 of 117 authored, zero compile discards, and a leak check confirms no question contains its own expected answer. Four Sonnet-authored slices had already returned before the switch and were discarded rather than merged: mixing two author models inside one bank would leave some questions phrased by one and some by another, which is a confound for anything that reads per-question difficulty. Fable output went to a separate directory so no mixing was possible even by accident. One limitation recorded on the bank itself: banks 1 and 2 were authored by the local relay and bank 3 by Fable, so the author model differs across banks. That confounds comparisons of question phrasing or difficulty between banks, but not grading -- gold is computed from the generator blueprint before any question text exists and is independent of who wrote the question. Note also that the Agent tool exposes the model but not the reasoning-effort dial, so the requested medium effort was conveyed as an instruction to keep reasoning proportionate rather than set as a parameter.
tests: 117/117 authored, 0 discards, 0 questions leaking an expected answer

summary: Bank 3 replicates the transfer figure at n=117 and corrects two per-kind readings in opposite directions.
detail: 117 questions, zero anchor overlap with banks 1 or 2, Fable-authored, retrieval scored with no language model in the answer path. The schema-derived arm scores 0.7877 against bank 2's 0.7857 -- an almost exact replication on four times the sample and a different author model, which makes the transfer figure the most solidly evidenced number in this experiment. The template arm rises from 0.1964 to 0.3177 but remains 0.000 on facet-in, facet-out and unanswerable alike; what it scores comes almost entirely from describe (0.812), the one kind needing no traversal. The per-kind corrections are the reason the bank was drawn and they cut both ways, exactly as A-5 warned they might: the homogeneous kinds were BETTER than five questions suggested (homo-in 0.600 -> 0.975 at n=20, homo-out 0.667 -> 0.833 at n=20) while the facet kinds are WORSE (facet-in 1.000 -> 0.583 at n=24, facet-out 0.833 -> 0.667 at n=24). Neither correction was predictable from the small banks and either bank alone would have pointed at the wrong weakness. So H3's predicted direction defect is now firmly not reproduced -- same-label-both-ends triples are the STRONGEST relationship kind at n=20 apiece -- and the real remaining weakness is the ordinary facet kinds. Abstention holds at 1.000 across 12 questions. multihop stays n=1 and is still not a rate.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; 234 answers run, 0 errors

summary: The evidence summary names its source from the card instead of calling everything an ATT&CK record.
detail: I-9 resolved. summarize() had FOUR hard-coded ATT&CK references, not the two first spotted, and no card lookup on any of them -- so every answer from every source described its records as ATT&CK records. It now reads provenance.source, which emit_record already fills from the source card. Two corrections travelled with it: the source name is rendered after `in` rather than welded into a noun phrase, because a card may legitimately call itself `the ReliaQuest identity graph` and `Found 5 the ReliaQuest identity graph record(s)` is not a sentence; and a record with no primary_id rendered as `Found record : Database Admins`, a dangling colon that reads as a missing citation and was scored that way by the judges. This is not cosmetic and is deliberately not filed as such: composer.py:181 uses the specialist summary as CLAIM text, so the false statement was being promoted into an asserted claim, which is why independent judges marked it unfaithful. The consequence to weigh is that ATT&CK's claim text changes too -- `Found ATT&CK record T1055: Process Injection` becomes `Found 1 record in MITRE ATT&CK: Process Injection (T1055)` -- so recorded MITRE answers will not match byte-for-byte on a re-run. The MITRE golden banks were NOT re-run to quantify that; it touches other experiments' committed artifacts and is the operator's call. Identity retrieval is unmoved at 0.7877/0.3177 before and after, confirming the change altered prose and not what was retrieved. The identity card's source_name was shortened to `the ReliaQuest identity graph` since it is now rendered inline; the full real-schema/synthetic-instances caveat stays in its own unrendered field. Still latent and recorded: the Gremlin normalizer carries the same hard-coding for CAPEC, harmless only because CAPEC is its only source.
tests: 999 passed, 2 skipped (utils/specialists utils/synthesis, ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5); identity retrieval byte-identical across the change

summary: Judged bank 3 after the fix: faithfulness up 0.15/0.36, and the arm gap on faithfulness disappears.
detail: 233 answers over 117 questions, twelve independent Sonnet judges, rubric verbatim, zero errored verdicts and zero duplicate (arm,question_id) -- the bank-attribution defect of A-7 does not recur because the agents were asked for the bank field this time. The I-9 summariser fix is worth +0.1509 faithfulness to the schema-derived arm and +0.3594 to the template arm; both rise because the false `ATT&CK record` statement was asserted as a claim on every answer from both. The consequence that matters: the faithfulness arm gap collapses from A-7's +0.2000 to -0.0085. That earlier gap was substantially an artifact of the defect hitting the two arms unequally, so A-7's faithfulness ARM COMPARISON should not be quoted; what A-7 got right, and what survives, is that the local judge overstates the absolute level badly. What still separates the arms is retrieval (0.7877 vs 0.3177) and evidence sufficiency (0.3691 vs 0.2248), not faithfulness -- the honest statement being that the template arm finds very little and what it says about that little is no less faithful, it simply says less. A new defect, I-11, was found by the judges and then located and verified: _extract_name_terms returns `App Access` for the anchor `App Access 070` because the Title-Case run truncates at the digit, and the CONTAINS match on that returns 54 nodes instead of 1 against the live store. It is a defect in this project's own anchor fix (74d027e), not a pre-existing one -- the structured-token pass added in I-8 matches internal dots and hyphens, which this anchor has neither of. It also exposes a limitation of the primary metric rather than only a bug: gold-in-evidence asks whether expected records are PRESENT, and they are, buried among 53 siblings, so the homogeneous kinds read 0.975 and 0.833 on retrieval while judging at 0.458 and 0.547 faithfulness. The metric cannot see a precision failure and A-8's homogeneous retrieval figures must be read with that caveat. The durable fix is exact-match-before-CONTAINS, a resolver behaviour change belonging in its own experiment rather than an amendment.
tests: make validate-research OK — 23 experiments; 233/233 verdicts, 0 errors, 0 duplicate (arm,qid)

summary: Name anchors keep their trailing number, and an exact name beats a substring.
detail: I-11 resolved in two parts, because the extractor half alone would have fixed one case and left the class. First, _TITLECASE_RUN_RE now admits a trailing numeric token, so `App Access 070` extracts whole instead of truncating to `App Access` at the digit -- instance names ending in a number are the norm in infrastructure data, not the exception, since hosts, OUs, groups and app registrations are all routinely numbered. Second and more durably, both name-matching queries now rank exact over substring: collect the CONTAINS candidates, keep those whose lowercased name equals a search term, and UNWIND that set when it is non-empty and the full candidate set otherwise. A bare CONTAINS is an unanchored substring match over a name space this project does not control, so any source whose names prefix one another defeats it regardless of how good the extractor gets. Expressed as collect/UNWIND rather than a subquery so the safety gate still validates one flat read-only statement. Verified against the live store: the query behind `What objects can the App Access 070 group modify?` now returns 1 record where it returned 54. 999 tests pass, so no MITRE path moved.

summary: Final identity reading: faithfulness 0.5500 -> 0.8175 across two fixes, and why faithfulness alone is the wrong headline.
detail: 234 answers, six independent Sonnet judges, zero errors, measured after both the I-9 summariser fix and the I-11 resolver fix. The schema-derived arm's faithfulness progresses 0.5500 (pre-fix) -> 0.7009 (after I-9) -> 0.8175 (after I-11), sufficiency 0.3691 -> 0.4731, and its per-kind faithfulness flattens: the homogeneous kinds were 0.458 and 0.547 after I-9 and are 0.802 and 0.818 now, level with every other relationship kind, which is the clearest confirmation that the 54-node dump the judges diagnosed was real. The interpretive point that matters more than any single number: the TEMPLATE arm now scores HIGHER on faithfulness (0.9282 vs 0.8175) and this is not an advantage. It retrieves almost nothing -- recall 0.1140 against 0.6923 -- and its answers are bare `Found 1 record: X` confirmations that never address the question, so it cannot be unfaithful. Faithfulness rewards silence; it is a necessary property and a useless headline alone, which is why this experiment reports it beside recall and sufficiency. The I-11 precision/recall trade is measured on the same 105 answerable questions: generic recall 0.7635 -> 0.6571 while precision rose 0.0783 -> 0.1357 and records per answer fell 135.1 -> 22.7, with judged faithfulness up 0.117 over the same change -- so the recall fall is the correct direction, the earlier figure having been inflated by dumps that contained gold by accident. The template arm lost recall with no precision gain at all (0.0561 -> 0.0572), confirming its earlier 0.3177 was scoring by dumping rather than retrieving. A-8's homogeneous retrieval figures are superseded. Still open: multihop judges 0.400 at n=1 and cannot be scaled; several answers return a bare record confirmation instead of an explicit no-such-relationship abstention, the largest remaining sufficiency cost on both arms; and a DEVICE-anchor failure where dc234/lap191/dc212 never appear in their own evidence, distinct from I-11 and not yet diagnosed.

summary: The device-anchor bug: an ATT&CK id pattern was eating host names, and one Title-Case word could suppress the anchor entirely.
detail: The last change's open thread -- dc234/lap191/dc212 never appearing in their own evidence -- is three defects in name-anchor extraction, all in the same function. (1) `_acceptable_name` rejected any candidate matching `_ANY_ID_RE`, which is right on ATT&CK, where `T1055` is an id and not a name, and wrong everywhere else: `dc212` matches the DataComponent shape `DC[0-9]{3,}` case-insensitively, so the single most common host-naming convention in identity data was deleted before it could anchor anything. The rejection is now gated on the anchoring catalogue, mirroring `anchor_dataset`, which had already decided whose id rules apply -- the name path simply was not asking. (2) The bare-word fallback is gated behind `if not terms`, so any single acceptable Title-Case word suppressed it: 'Who can modify the DACL on the device wks225?' yielded ('DACL',) and never saw wks225. A new instance-token pass (`[A-Za-z]{2,}[0-9]+`) runs unconditionally beside the structured-token pass, on the same argument the structured pass already makes. (3) That also removes the fallback's collateral damage without touching it: with an anchor found, the fallback no longer fires and no longer spends the four-term budget on 'identity', 'operating' and 'system' before reaching the host name -- terms that were not merely wasted slots, since each went into the CONTAINS predicate and pulled in unrelated records. An instance token that is a substring of an already-accepted name is skipped, so `srv063.corp.example` does not also anchor on `srv063`; with that guard, ATT&CK name extraction is byte-identical across ten shapes. Two consequential defects surfaced underneath, both hidden until the anchor started binding: `_FACET_AGGREGATION` still selected a bare `n.attack_id`, so describe returned null ids on any source keyed otherwise (now `coalesce`, the idiom `_label_scan` already used); and `_normalize_flat` labelled every scanned row `"Technique"` regardless of source, asserting a DEVICE named srv000 to the judge as an ATT&CK technique -- the same species as the hardcoded 'ATT&CK record(s)' wording, found the same way. Measured on bank 3, both arms, 117 questions: zero per-question regressions, 15 improvements. Generic retrieval 0.6923 -> 0.7094 (facet-out 0.6667 -> 0.7500); template arm 0.1140 -> 0.2194, entirely because all 12 unanswerable questions went 0.0 -> 1.0 -- it had been leaking on every one of them by returning a 240-row label scan that contained everything. The larger gain is invisible to a recall metric: evidence volume fell from 20.60 to 8.24 ids per question on the generic arm (max 480 -> 54) and 14.34 -> 1.95 on the template arm, with precision 0.2565 -> 0.3054 and 0.0589 -> 0.1373.

summary: Two sources on one backend were probing the same store; graph endpoints are now addressable per source.
detail: Loading attack, capec and identity together for the first time exposed a structural limit nobody had hit: `endpoint_for(backend)` resolves a URI by BACKEND, so every Neo4j-backed source in a process shares one address. The planner duly reported `[DOWN] identity (neo4j) -- backend up with 4369 nodes but none of the expected labels present` -- 4369 being ATT&CK's node count, because identity had probed ATT&CK's store. This stayed invisible for the whole life of the project because the demonstration stack held exactly one Neo4j source and one Gremlin source, so NEO4J_URI and GREMLIN_URI could never collide, and the merged-graph counterfactual sidestepped it by putting both catalogues in a single store. It is the same species as every other defect this experiment has surfaced: an assumption that is true of the demonstration data and false the moment a customer has two of anything. The fix is an explicit per-source override, `ARIADNE_ENDPOINT_<DATASET>`, consulted before the backend-wide variable and unset for every dataset today, so every existing runner resolves exactly as before. The cards' own `connection.uri` is deliberately NOT made authoritative: attack declares `:7687` and capec `:8182`, the container-internal ports the build saw from inside the compose network, so the field is not host-reachable and the documented convention of ignoring it is load-bearing -- recorded as I-14 rather than fixed here, since correcting it is a build-side change. With the override set, all three sources probe correctly in one process: attack 4369 (neo4j), capec 4769 (gremlin), identity 1339 (neo4j). An end-to-end question then drew on the customer graph and the threat catalogue in a single answer -- `dc212` resolved in identity with its RUNS_AS user alongside ATT&CK technique records -- which is the first time this system has answered from a customer graph and a catalogue at once. What it did NOT do is correlate them: `joins: []`, because no join key bridges identity and ATT&CK, so the two halves are adjacent rather than connected and ATT&CK's contribution is keyword noise (WRITE_DACL matched `Overwrite Process Arguments`). That is the next piece of work, not a defect in this one.

summary: Three sources at once costs nothing on questions that have an answer, and destroys abstention on questions that do not.
detail: EXP-2026-08-013 phase 1, the routing floor: bank 3's 117 questions and their gold, unchanged, run against a card directory holding ATT&CK, CAPEC and the identity graph at once instead of the identity graph alone. No knowledge is supplied -- no mapping, no join, no authored correspondence -- so the reading is a floor rather than a demonstration. Two defects had to be fixed before the question could be asked. A URI was resolved by BACKEND, so the two Neo4j sources shared an address and `identity` probed ATT&CK's store, reporting its 4369 nodes and 'none of the expected labels present'; fixed with a per-source override. And the first composition held the three cards and nothing else, which left the schema registry EMPTY -- it is built from graphs/<dataset>/canonical/ -- so every schema-driven primitive silently reverted to a hardcoded MITRE fallback and a question routed correctly to `identity` was answered with a query over `n:Technique OR n:SubTechnique OR ...`. That first run showed describe collapsing 0.812 -> 0.438 and read exactly like a routing defect. It was a missing artifact. ITS NUMBERS ARE DISCARDED; the composer now copies the canonical tree and --check refuses a composition without one. The corrected result is unusually clean. Every kind that has an answer is IDENTICAL between one source and three -- describe 0.8125, facet-in 0.5833, facet-out 0.7500, homo-in 0.7000, homo-out 0.5500, multihop 1.000/0.667 -- on both arms, across 105 questions. Not close: identical. Every question that moved was an abstention: 10 of 12 on the generic arm and 11 of 12 on the template arm, none the other way, so unanswerable falls 1.000 -> 0.167 and 1.000 -> 0.083 and the two overall figures (0.7094 -> 0.6239, 0.2194 -> 0.1254) are entirely that one kind. The mechanism is routing, not retrieval: 80 of 117 identity questions routed beyond identity, and evidence volume rose from 8.24 to 180.36 ids per question on the generic arm (max 54 -> 2234) and 1.95 -> 391.47 on the template arm (max 2 -> 2608) -- a 22x and 200x increase buying zero additional correct retrieval, with one abstention question returning 558 CAPEC records beside the single identity record that was the whole honest answer. The capability is real and the discipline is not: the system can hold three databases across two query languages and retrieve exactly what it retrieved with one, but cannot stay quiet about the two that are irrelevant. Phase 2 (cross-source correlation) is deliberately blocked on this, because a correct correlation would be indistinguishable from the noise already arriving.

summary: Source routing is comparative now: three live sources retrieve identically to one.
detail: The rule was `id_hits > 0` per card, independently -- an absolute threshold with no comparison between sources. Adequate while the stack held one Neo4j source and one Gremlin source, whose vocabularies barely overlap; add a customer graph with 72 labels and 779 property names of ordinary IT English and a single shared generic word drags in a whole catalogue. 80 of 117 identity questions routed to ATT&CK, almost always on the word 'group' matching ATT&CK's Group label. The replacement is comparative: the leader is whichever source matched the most request tokens, and any other source is selected only if it matched a token the leader did not -- a source whose entire case is a word the leader also matches has said nothing to distinguish itself. One refinement was needed and it is worth recording because it is the same species as everything else this experiment has turned up. A source's own name is the strongest routing signal a request carries, and it was going to the wrong source: 'What mitigations does ATT&CK list for T1047?' contributes the token `att`, the ampersand having split it, and no label in either catalogue contains that word -- so ATT&CK scored 1 against CAPEC's 2 and a purely ATT&CK question pulled in CAPEC. Source-name tokens now count for their own source EXCEPT where another live card uses the word in an identifier, since `attack` is also the first word of CAPEC's AttackPattern and therefore names neither; 'attack patterns and their weaknesses' stays CAPEC vocabulary. Both conditions were re-run at the same commit so the fix cannot confound the comparison. Three sources now retrieve IDENTICALLY to one: generic 0.7094 both ways, template 0.2194 both ways, every kind equal, ZERO questions differing in either direction on either arm. Unanswerable recovers 0.167 -> 1.000 and 0.083 -> 1.000, routing beyond identity falls 80/117 -> 0/117, and evidence volume falls 180.36 -> 8.24 ids per question (max 2234 -> 54) and 391.47 -> 1.95 (max 2608 -> 2). The single-source baseline is unmoved, which is the check that the rule is inert when there is nothing to choose between. It is also strictly better on the two-catalogue configuration it was not written for: across the 120 golden entries, those whose OWNING source is not routed fall from 14 to 2, and the two that remain are the A-AST boundary cases that ask for an entity type ATT&CK does not have and are supposed to refuse.

summary: Declared the identity-to-ATT&CK bridge: 13 edge types carry a technique, 8 explicitly do not.
detail: EXP-2026-08-013 phase 2, step 1. Every other bridge in this project is a VALUE join -- a property on one side holds the same string as a property on the other, and the planner discovers it by comparing values it read out of two graphs. The identity graph admits no such bridge: it contains no ATT&CK identifier anywhere, not in a property, not in a label, not in an edge attribute, so there is nothing to join on. What exists is a correspondence in MEANING -- a DC_SYNC edge IS the technique ATT&CK calls T1003.006 -- which is a claim about the world, supplied by us, derivable from neither graph. So it is declared in one reviewed place exactly as CANONICAL_JOIN_KEYS requires: never inferred, never produced by a model, never widened at query time. Each mapping cites the customer's own description of the edge from the catalog they supplied, which is the only thing that makes it reviewable BY them -- ADD_KEY_CREDENTIAL_LINK maps to T1649 because their text says 'allowing a certificate to be attached and the target impersonated', not because we assumed it. The partial/whole distinction is theirs too: GET_CHANGES, GET_CHANGES_ALL and GET_CHANGES_IN_FILTERED_SET are marked partial because the catalog says 'One half of the DCSync right pair. Alone it is insufficient', and reporting a half-right as the technique outright would assert something their own catalog denies. NOT_A_TECHNIQUE is as much a part of the declaration as the mapping: MEMBER_OF, RUNS_AS, TRUSTED_BY, GP_LINK, APP_ASSIGNMENT, BOUND_BY, SAME_FOREST_TRUST and APPLIES_FROM each record a state of the environment rather than something an adversary does, and mapping them would report Account Manipulation for every user in the tenant. 13 + 8 = 21, the complete edge set, and a test fails if the schema ever grows an edge nobody classified -- absence from both tables is indistinguishable at the call site from 'carries no technique', which is a claim nobody made. The tests cannot check the mapping against a ground truth, because if one existed the mapping would not need authoring; they check completeness, unambiguity, well-formedness, that the partial distinction survives, and that every technique named actually exists in the live ATT&CK store so a typo is a failure rather than a query that quietly returns nothing. Any experiment whose gold derives from this table measures whether the system USES the declared bridge correctly, not whether the bridge is right.

summary: The bridge works: an identity edge type now seeds ATT&CK, and it is inert on every question that does not invoke it.
detail: EXP-2026-08-013 phase 2, wired end to end. 'Which ATT&CK technique corresponds to what the Domain Admins group can do with DC_SYNC, and what mitigates it?' now declares the identity-edge-technique join, hoists identity ahead of attack, emits T1003.006 as a join value from the edge TYPE the identity record walked, and seeds ATT&CK with it -- 1 exact record where it previously returned 7, the right one among them reached by string coincidence ('sync' matching SyncAppvPublishingServer and Asynchronous Procedure Call). A second question seeds ['T1098','T1222.001','T1484.001'] from the edges its anchor actually holds. Three defects surfaced on the way and one of them is the gate working: the gate REFUSED the bridge, because its producer/consumer check keyed on via_edge alone, saw producers=[], and declined to ship a join it could not validate; it and dependency_map now ask the endpoint whether it `produces`, covering both ways of deriving a key. Second, a leading article was being absorbed into every extracted name: the Title-Case run for 'The App Access 070 group can ...' begins at 'The', and the lookup is an unanchored CONTAINS against a stored name of 'App Access 070', so it matched NOTHING -- the anchor resolved, looked reasonable in a trace, and retrieved zero records. Latent until a question began with its subject, since every question in banks 1-3 phrases it mid-sentence where the article is lowercase. Trimming leading articles also corrected 'Describe Phishing for Information' to 'Phishing for Information' and returned 'List ATT&CK software entries' to the label-scan path the builder's own docstring says that gate exists to protect. Third, the correlation pull-in overrode the router: with a bridge declared, any identity question the intent classifier read as correlational pulled in ATT&CK to close the join, so 'Which containers is the group policy object GPO-13-baseline linked to?' routed to both. The pull-in now declines to re-add a source the selector deliberately SHED -- shedding is a judgement that the source's evidence was subsumed, while the pull-in exists for a partner with no keyword evidence at all. No-regression on the 117 identity-only questions with three sources live and the bridge declared: generic 0.7094 and template 0.2194 both identical to the single-source figures, ZERO questions differing, 0/117 routed beyond identity, evidence volume unchanged at 8.24 and 1.95 ids per question. The bridge is inert for questions that do not invoke it and fires for those that do, which is the property that matters -- a declared correspondence that leaked into unrelated questions would be worse than no bridge. NOT MEASURED: two demonstrated questions are not a result, there is no blind tri-source bank, and nothing here should be quoted as a score.

summary: The bridge measured: 0.8333 on technique questions, and zero false claims on the negatives.
detail: 64 blind questions authored by Fable from a five-field view of one anchor -- name, kind, the relationship it holds, the direction, and whether to ask for a technique, a mitigation, or nothing of the sort -- and never the expected answer, the declared correspondence, the schema, or another question. Gold from the blueprint and the declared map, ATT&CK side read from the canonical export rather than the live store. Audited before any run: 0 of 64 contain a gold identifier, 64 of 64 name their anchor, 0 use SCREAMING_CASE, 0 identity-control questions mention ATT&CK. HALF THE BANK IS NEGATIVE ON PURPOSE, because a run that scored well on positives while failing negatives would have learned to attach ATT&CK to everything, which a recall-only metric cannot see. Schema-derived arm: bridge-technique 0.8333 (n=24), bridge-mitigation 0.3398 (n=16), bridge-refusal 1.0000 (n=12), identity-control 1.0000 (n=12, 0 of 12 reaching ATT&CK at all), overall 0.7724. Template arm: 0.0000 on technique, 0.4167 on refusal, overall 0.3176 -- it scores zero on the questions the bridge exists for AND falsely names a technique on 7 of 12 anchors that no mapped edge touches, the familiar shape of a cascade that answers with whatever a keyword reached rather than abstaining. The mitigation hop is the weak kind and it is not the bridge's fault: the technique arrives on 11 of 16 and the mitigations on 4, because whether ATT&CK then walks MITIGATES depends on the planner resolving 'Mitigation' from the wording -- a pre-existing second-hop limitation now visible because the first hop started working. THREE DEFECTS, and two of them were in the gold. (1) dependency_map returned dict[str,str] and assigned by last-write-wins, so with three sources ATT&CK -- the consuming end of BOTH declared joins -- was assigned to CAPEC, which yielded nothing, and ran unseeded: identity produced T1649 correctly and the wiring discarded it. A consumer is now seeded from the union of its producers, worth 0.3333 -> 0.8333 on bridge-technique alone. (2) The negative anchors were dirty: the sampler indexed OUTGOING edges only while the runtime walk is direction-agnostic, so dc202 was picked as a refusal control on its lone outgoing RUNS_AS and then correctly produced T1098 from a WRITE_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTIONS edge held OVER it. The declaration was right, the system was right, the gold was wrong; bridge-refusal 0.8333 -> 1.0000 and the difference was entirely the gold. (3) The partial-right control is NOT DRAWABLE from this tenant and has been removed rather than reported: every anchor holding GET_CHANGES is also touched by another mapped right, usually ALL_EXTENDED_RIGHTS, which the declaration maps to T1003.006 in its own right on the customer's wording that it includes 'on a domain, the replication rights', so a T1003.006 cannot be attributed to the half-right rather than the whole one. Its first draw scored 0.8889 and that number is discarded. The standing limit: the mapping is ours, so this measures whether the system USES the declared bridge correctly, not whether the bridge is right.

detail: With two catalogues and a tenant identity graph live, 14 probes each naming the one source they are about were run under both source-selection rules. The shipped comparative rule leaks on 1 probe and 5 records. This is the first measurement of the property and the first evidence the routing fix bought anything. The protocol pre-registered that a routing regression would be invisible to a leak metric, and one appeared: 'which group uses T1059.001' now routes to identity alone and answers nothing, scoring clean because the only source consulted returned nothing foreign. Recorded as Q21 with a proposed fix rather than patched. A safety gate cannot see any of this -- in a leak every individual query is legal for the source it was sent to.

summary: Record Hardening step 8 / EXP-2026-08-017: merging rewrote 1,083 catalogue nodes, federation rewrote none. C-022 replaces refuted C-015.
detail: C-015 was refuted on correctness and that result is kept rather than worked around -- the neutrality it measured is exactly what the new claim rests on. What is measurable without confounding is structural: the merged store carries attack_id on 1,083 nodes whose upstream record does not ship it (894 given a derived public id, 189 taxonomy entries given a T prefix), 22.7% of CAPEC, against 0 in the federated condition. Merging does not eliminate the reconciliation, it relocates it from code into stored records, and the edit is due again on every catalogue release. The strongest form is the third source: a customer identity graph loaded unmodified beside both catalogues, three live sources retrieving identically to one. What merging buys is reported beside it -- skipped consumer sub-questions fall 7 of 30 to 3 of 30. Merge cost and onboarding cost are ruled out as unmeasurable here rather than deferred, since ATT&CK and CAPEC merge cheaply because they already share edge semantics.

summary: Record Hardening step 6 / EXP-2026-08-015: the templates-vs-generic gap gets its first confidence interval, and resampling finds a template defect six experiments missed.
detail: Q2's premise was wrong: re-running an LLM-free arm ten times gives ten identical numbers, so pipeline variance there is zero by construction. The variance that exists is in which anchors were drawn. Ten anchor-disjoint banks per population, measured disjoint (0 overlapping pairs of 45, both populations), retrieval only, paired bootstrap seed 1729. Catalogue: templates 0.9900 sd 0.0225 against generic 1.0000 sd 0.0000, difference -0.0100 CI [-0.0233, +0.0000] -- the upper bound is exactly zero, so templates never won a single bank across 300 unseen anchors. Foreign schema: 0.2392 against 0.8514, difference -0.6121 CI [-0.6720, -0.5530], independently replicating EXP-2026-08-011's +0.5893 on a fresh draw. The catalogue metric is saturated for the generic arm and cannot price that gap; a judged metric is needed. The template arm's entire catalogue spread is three questions in two banks, all capec_hierarchy_chain: it emits a fixed two-hop select and returns nothing when an anchor's parent is already Meta-level, the same outer-join class fixed in EXP-2026-08-004/006 in a template those fixes did not reach. holdout-v1's anchors happened to sit low enough to hide it. Filed as Q22, not fixed here.

summary: Q22 fixed: the hierarchy-chain template no longer requires a grandparent, and the catalogue arm gap closes to exactly zero.
detail: capec_hierarchy_chain required a parent AND a grandparent in one select, an inner join over three positions. For a Standard anchor whose parent is already Meta there is no grandparent, so the query returned not even the parent the question asked for. Both hops are now optional(), the same outer-join correction EXP-2026-08-004/006 applied elsewhere, and the normalizer skips an ancestor equal to the anchor since optional() re-labels the anchor into the parent slot when it has none. Regression over all ten variance banks: 15 of 300 answers changed and every one is H-ABS-*, three going from empty to correct and twelve returning identical ancestors. Template arm 0.9900 -> 1.0000, sd 0.0225 -> 0.0000, so both arms are now saturated on the catalogue and the -0.0100 gap was entirely this defect.

summary: Q21 fixed: an identifier's shape now counts as routing evidence, so an ATT&CK question stops routing to the customer graph.
detail: The diagnosis in the open question was half wrong: not a weighting problem but an alphabetical tiebreak. 'Which group uses T1059.001?' scored one matched token to ATT&CK and one to the tenant graph, both on the word group, and max() broke the tie on dataset name -- so identity won on the letter i and the question returned nothing. The identifier t1059 counted for nobody, because the concept index is built from label and relationship names and never from instance identifiers. A request token whose shape matches a learned identifier scheme of a source now counts as an id-hit for it, with shapes learned from each dataset's canonical snapshot by idscheme.py, so no MITRE string enters the router and a source with no learned schemes scores nothing extra. The question now routes to attack and returns a record; leak totals are unchanged at 1/14 and 5 records; and the recorded-answer regression over all ten catalogue banks shows 0 of 300 answers changed.

summary: EXP-2026-08-018 / Q20: with an LLM proposing claims the verifier cuts 32-36 per run against zero deterministic. Kept as an instrument, never a default.
detail: The claims composer was unreachable, which is why EXP-2026-08-014 could only report that four gates cut zero claims from 888: a gate cannot cut what cannot be constructed. Reconnected behind its own flag and run through five pre-registered tests over the 120-question catalogue, three repeats. The gates fire -- 32 to 36 cuts per run -- and the work is lopsided: correlated 92, grounded 19, resolvable 1, cited 0, so the model rarely emits an uncited claim but does invent relationships between things it correctly cited. It is never a default: gold-in-claims 0.6817 against 0.8184, 23% fewer claims, and 67x slower. Engagement is 96-104 of 120 and the shortfall is almost entirely 120-second read timeouts rather than composer defects, so engagement and cost cannot be improved together. C-017's first half now splits cleanly into a ceiling by construction on the deterministic path and a measured filter on an LLM-composed one.

summary: EXP-2026-08-019 / Q2: seeding does not reduce LLM variance, and 32-way concurrency inflates measured quality by failing more often.
detail: Three conditions over 120 questions, three repeats each. H1 refuted: gold sd is 0.0212 seeded against 0.0207 unseeded, because temperature was already 0 at every graded call site and the variance comes from timeout and fallback, upstream of any sampling parameter. The seed stays but must never be called a variance reduction. H3 refuted, and the real finding is sharper: raising workers 16 to 32 buys 19% wall clock, costs 61% higher per-request latency, and doubles timeouts from 14 to 28 of 120. Because a timeout falls back to the deterministic composer at 0.8184 against the LLM's 0.68, failing more makes the arm score better -- r(fallbacks, gold) = +0.62 over nine runs. At 32 workers about a fifth of the LLM arm is not the LLM arm. That generalises: any harness with a fallback to a stronger path reports improvement when the primary path degrades. Practical answer: 32 is fine for ungraded bulk work, 16 for graded arms, and the binding constraint is the 120s read timeout rather than the concurrency ceiling.

summary: Plan for a variant-robustness harness: Sonnet-authored tiered paraphrases of all 120 golden questions, scored against what the original gold question extracts.
detail: Probing on 2026-08-28 showed the router matches schema words exactly with only a trailing-s rule, so defend against, countermeasures, remediate and a one-letter typo all match nothing, the literal name Software Extensions resolves to nothing, and one paraphrase returns four techniques none of which is correct. The plan builds the instrument first and treats it as the deliverable: a stable gold-side reference, a tiered variant bank gated for tier honesty, and a baseline before any code changes. Fixes are staged by cost and by risk to existing claims -- deterministic stemming/edit-distance/gloss promotion, then exact-name resolution which also closes Q27, then a dependency-free keyword index over the 9,138 canonical name+description records, and a gated language-model interpreter only if a measured gap survives.

summary: Variant robustness step 1: gold-side reference capture, proven byte-identical across two runs. Reloading a silently-empty Gremlin store first changed 13 of 120 results.
detail: scripts/variant_harness.py captures what each of the 120 golden questions extracts -- entity ids (primary metric), emitted queries, claims, abstentions -- with NOTHING time-varying recorded at all, so the 2026-08-23 wall_s/timing_ms diff trap cannot recur by construction. The first capture showed 22 questions extracting nothing; --graph verify found the Gremlin store at 0 nodes against an expected 4769, because the container had restarted and the in-memory TinkerGraph went with it while the health check kept reporting reachable. After reloading CAPEC and ATT&CK the empties fall to 9, and all 9 are by-design negative or excluded-at-load cases. Two consecutive captures are byte-identical.

summary: Variant robustness step 2a: a conservative stemmer, bounded edit distance and gloss forms for card-grounded routing. Module only -- not yet wired.
detail: utils/planner/lexicon.py adds the three word-handling mechanisms the router lacks, as pure functions with no I/O so the deterministic path stays byte-reproducible. The stemmer is deliberately timid: one suffix rule then a silent-e pass, no loop. Two passes rather than one because English hides a stem boundary behind a final e -- technique/techniques and mitigate/mitigating each split differently under suffix stripping alone and land on different keys. There is no ation rule; ion already carries it, collapsing mitigation, mitigations, mitigating, mitigate and mitigates onto one key, whereas ation would strand the noun on mitig away from the verb. Edit distance is guarded at five characters because below that one edit spans too much English, and an ambiguous typo returns None rather than routing on dict ordering. Wiring is deferred until after the baseline is measured so it cannot contaminate it.
tests: pytest utils/planner/tests/test_lexicon.py -- 30 passed. Negative cases pinned: use/user, group/groupware, analytic/analysis, campaign/camp, software/soft, access/accessory all stay distinct.

summary: EXP-2026-08-020 scaffolded with its protocol written before the run. Diagnosis: name lookup already works -- the defect is source selection.
detail: Protocol pre-registers three hypotheses, six tiers, and six metrics defined rather than named. The metric that matters most is wrong_entity: the variant returned identifiers and none is one the gold question found, which nothing downstream catches because every claim is genuinely grounded in a genuinely retrieved record. Diagnosis while the authors ran corrected an assumption from the plan: exact-name lookup is NOT missing. What is Software Extensions? resolves to T1176 today. What are the mitigations for Software Extensions? fails because the router sends it to CAPEC -- the name contains the schema word software, so the name extractor reads Software Extensions as a name while the router simultaneously counts software as evidence for the Software label. Two subsystems reading one word differently. Step 5 is therefore a routing fix, not a name-resolution build.
tests: make validate-research -- 31 experiments OK.

summary: Variant robustness step 2: 579 Sonnet-authored tiered variants of the 120 golden questions, mechanically gated for tier honesty.
detail: Twelve Sonnet subagents, one per batch of ten, authored 581 variants across six tiers from a written contract; 579 survive the gate. Tiers run from T1 (identifier kept, schema word swapped) to T5 (entity described using neither its id, its name, nor any word from its schema) plus T6 negative controls about entities that do not exist. The gate is the point: an authors self-declared tier is a claim, not evidence, so a T3+ carrying an identifier or a T4/T5 carrying a schema word is rejected mechanically. Two gate bugs of our own were found and fixed by the first run -- CWE ids were missing from the identifier regex, so ten honest F-CWE variants were rejected for not keeping an identifier they were keeping; and bounded-scan questions have no identifier for T1/T2 to keep, so demanding one rejected the only variants they can have. The two surviving rejections are correct: campaign C0027s name is literally the string C0027, so T3 is unsatisfiable, and the agent flagged it rather than faking it.
tests: gate: 579 kept / 2 rejected; all 120 gold questions covered; 101 have the full T1-T5. Per tier: T1 120, T2 120, T3 101, T4 104, T5 104, T6 30.

summary: EXP-2026-08-020 Arm 0: the deterministic router loses more than half its answers to a synonym, and at T4/T5 all apparent recall is catalogue dumping rather than retrieval.
detail: 699 runs, 120 control + 579 variants, against a byte-stable reference. The T0 control scores 1.0000 on every metric so the instrument is sound. Record identity falls 0.4667, 0.4250, 0.0990, 0.0000, 0.0000 across T1 to T5; queries_exact is 0.0000 for every tier that drops the identifier. The unhypothesised finding is a new metric: catalogue_dump fires on 13.6% of runs and 52.5% of T3, and splitting recall by it shows T4 recall of 0.0719 is really 0.0013 among non-dumping runs and T5 0.0284 is really 0.0000. When the system does not return the whole label it retrieves nothing. Same defect class as I-11 in C-023 on a different axis. H3 refuted: 4 of 30 negative controls answered, one asserting All 158 results for this question about a threat group that does not exist, another returning 558 records -- essentially all of CAPEC -- for an invented attack pattern. The verifier cannot catch this and it is not a verifier bug: every record is genuinely retrieved and every claim genuinely grounded. What is false is the framing, and a claim-level verifier has no claim to reject.
tests: T0 control 1.0000 on records_exact, recall, queries_exact and claims_exact. make validate-research -- 31 experiments OK.

summary: EXP-2026-08-020 Arms 1-2: the lexicon alone converts abstentions into catalogue dumps; paired with an unanchored-abstention fix it beats baseline on every safety metric.
detail: Arm 1 wires stemming, gloss stems and bounded edit distance into the router behind ARIADNE_LEXICON, default off, with the flag-off reference verified byte-identical twice. On the catalogue it is a clean gain: gold recall 0.8698 to 0.9161 over 66 scorable questions, 14 answers changed, 6 better 0 worse 2 same, with three detection questions going from 0.13-0.33 to 1.0000 and three mitigation-coverage questions reaching 1.0000 while returning FEWER records. On the variants it is harmful: wrong_entity +0.0865 at T4 and +0.1154 at T5, catalogue dumps +0.125 and +0.135, abstention down by the same. A better matcher means more questions find a schema word, so more of them route, and with no anchor resolved they fall through to a label scan that returns everything. Arm 2 fixes the fall-through: an unanchored question now runs a real bounded query against an empty id set, returns zero rows legitimately, and the existing enforced-abstention machinery carries that executed query as its proof. Arm 2 is below Arm 0 on wrong_entity at T3/T4/T5, below on dumps at every tier, and takes negative-control abstention to 0.9333 -- 28 of 30 correctly silent against 26. It does not retrieve more; it stops pretending, and records_exact stays 0.0000 at T4/T5.

summary: EXP-2026-08-020 Arm 3 and write-up: the name index resolves 7/9 probes but as a router gains 3 questions and buys 11 wrong answers. Kept off; thresholds need a held-out split.
detail: namesearch.py is BM25 over the 9138 canonical name+description records with an exact-name boost and label filtering, no new dependency, built from the same checksummed snapshot the identifier schemes learn from. The exact-name boost is load-bearing: BM25 alone ranks Blind SQL Injection above SQL Injection and puts Phishing, Mobile Phishing and Voice Phishing in a numerical tie the margin rule then rejects. As a component it resolves 7 of 9 probes and both misses are honest. As a router it is net negative: T3 records_exact 0.0990 to 0.1287 (3 questions) against wrong_entity rising by 5 at T4, 4 at T5 and 1 at T6. Kept OFF. The obvious fix -- raise MIN_SCORE and MIN_MARGIN -- is declined on purpose: both were set before any variant was scored, and fitting them against this bank would convert it into a training set and every figure in the experiment into a training figure, which is the co-authorship failure C-021 exists to measure. Filed as Q28 with the split-first protocol. Ledger: C-001 bounded to questions phrased in the schemas vocabulary, C-010 gains a schema-agnostic surface plus the caution that a catalogue-measured improvement can be an off-catalogue regression, C-021 now demonstrated as three live defects rather than only as points.

summary: Corrected plan for understanding analyst questions, after an external review found three real problems with the first proposal and I verified all three.
