It was right that my design sat downstream of the defect we actually measured, which is a source-selection tie broken alphabetically. And it was right that deriving correctness from recorded system behaviour would define the incumbent as ground truth, a worse version of the threshold-fitting I declined in Arm 3. Two things I could settle from saved data rather than re-running: zero of 238 variants at levels 4-6 contain an exact name, so ten of the twelve new wrong answers are fuzzy-matching failures and not exact-name failures; and one golden question regressed under Arm 3 -- List ATT&CK software entries returned one Matrix node instead of 821 entries, because the name matcher hijacked a bulk request. The reviews objection to always-accept exact names also stands: names are not unique, Phishing sits inside Mobile Phishing.

summary: Steps 1-2: bulk-scan hijack fixed, Q27 fixed at the right layer, and source selection no longer decided alphabetically.
detail: Three fixes. Name search no longer fires on a bulk request -- List ATT&CK software entries had been matching a node called enterprise-attack and returning 1 record where the gold is 821. Q27 is fixed in the normalizer rather than the drafter: the routing placeholder label is legitimate FOR ROUTING, since the plan gate requires every sub-question to name an entity, and the defect was the record inheriting it as its type. _label_for now prefers the identifier shape over the task label, so T1176 reports as Technique rather than Analytic while a device named srv000 still takes Device from the task. And _select_sources now breaks ties on id_hits before falling back to the dataset name: mitigations for Software Extensions gave attack 2 real label matches against capec 1 label plus 1 prose match, both counted 2 tokens, and capec won on the letter C, sending the question to a store without the entity. It now reaches attack and resolves T1176. Also added a preflight guard to the harness: the Gremlin store emptied itself twice tonight while --graph health reported reachable, and an unattended run cannot afford numbers taken against a hollow graph.

summary: Arm 5: exact-name resolution alone delivers the whole +3 gain for +1 wrong answer, where ranked matching cost +11. Shipped behind its own flag.
detail: An external review said the +3/-11 of Arm 3 had never been decomposed and the recommendation to ship exact-name alone was unverified. Both correct, and the decomposition turned out to be recoverable from saved results with no re-run: all 3 gains are at T3, and zero of 238 variants at T4/T5/T6 contain an exact name, so ten of the twelve wrong answers are ranked-matching failures by construction. The reviews second objection changed the design: exact is not unique -- Phishing is a complete CAPEC name that also sits inside Mobile Phishing -- so exact_name_matches returns a list and more than one survivor is an ambiguity to surface, not a tie to break. A subsumption filter stops multi-word names becoming false ambiguities, since Software Extensions contains the complete name Software. Measured: exact-name only is +3 right and +1 wrong against ranked matchings +3 and +11, with negative-control abstention back to 0.9333 and T3/T5/T6 wrong-entity all back to Arm 2 levels.

summary: Steps 4-5: frozen split drawn before any tuning, and understanding-gold derived from data rather than from system behaviour.
detail: The split is by gold question not by variant, so a question and all its paraphrases stay together and the frozen half cannot contain near-duplicates of what was tuned on. The rule is sha256(case_id) parity -- stable across machines with no seed to ship. 63 tune / 57 report, balanced across banks and tiers. Slot gold takes each slot from one of three non-behavioural sources: the anchor from authored seed_ids or ids in the authored question text, its label from the checksummed canonical snapshot, target labels from the snapshot labels of the computed gold answers, and the relation from the authored template NAME read against the cards declared relationship list -- the templates code is never consulted. Coverage is 118/120 anchors, 109/120 anchor labels, 66/120 target labels (exactly the scorable set) and 39/120 relations. The 41 questions with no derived relation are relation-free by design -- describe, capec_neighbors, the scans -- and are classified as such rather than counted as failures. Nine genuine gaps remain and all nine are the deliberately nonexistent or excluded-at-load entities, which correctly have no snapshot label.
tests: split verified disjoint and stratified; slot gold coverage reported per slot with underived cases classified rather than dropped.

summary: Ambiguity now has a consumer: when a question names several entities the answer asks which one, instead of picking.
detail: AmbiguousAnchor existed in resolve/resolver.py with no consumer anywhere in the tree -- a data structure describing a decision nothing acted on. The builders now emit an ambiguous-name draft when exact_name_matches returns more than one survivor: a real bounded query against an empty id set, so the result is legitimately empty, with the candidates riding in meta. base.py turns that into an anchor trace, and composer.abstention_for renders it as "The question names more than one entity, so it was not answered rather than guessed. Did you mean CAPEC-98 (Phishing), CAPEC-116 (Excavation)?". The trace step vocabulary is contract-tested against docs/agent-interfaces.md, so the new anchor step is documented there rather than added silently. Honest limit: the surface is wired but rarely reached on this bank, because a question naming two entities usually also matches a schema word and never reaches the unanchored path.
tests: 914 passed, 2 skipped. Exact-name resolution verified end to end: mitigations for Software Extensions now resolves T1176.

summary: Step 6 / Q28 answered negatively: the fitted threshold gave 12 right 0 wrong on the tuning half and 17 right 8 wrong on the frozen half. Ranked matching stays off.
detail: Q28s protocol executed as written -- split by gold question via sha256 parity, drawn before any fitting, harness filters the frozen half so a sweep cannot reach it. A first grid over score 4/8/12 moved nothing because typical winning scores are 11-17, so every threshold tested sat below what it was meant to filter. Measuring the distributions directly showed the real lever: scores overlap heavily (medians 27.1 correct vs 14.8 wrong) while margins barely do (1.72 vs 1.08), so the discriminating signal is how far ahead the leader is, not how strong it is, and the shipped default of 1.25 sat inside the wrong-answer distribution. Margin 1.4 with no score floor gave 12 right 0 wrong on the tuning half. On the frozen half it gave 17 right 8 wrong -- 68% precision against 67% for the unfitted default, with the margin medians collapsing from 1.72/1.08 to 1.39/1.12. The wider result is the useful one: fitting against the whole bank would have reported 12 right and 0 wrong, and it would have been an artifact.

summary: Third model behind the skynet alias detected by probe (qwen38-27B-v2); D-028 makes recording the served model mandatory, and the record is triaged rather than re-run wholesale.
detail: scripts/model_identity.py identifies the weights behind each relay alias by issuing a completion and reading the model field off the response envelope. GET /v1/models is insufficient -- the relay answers skynet with upstream_model 'auto' because it hot-swaps, which is how the previous two swaps went unnoticed. skynet now serves qwen38-27B-v2; local serves gemma-4-26B-it. D-028 binds four rules: record the served model and date rather than the alias, probe rather than ask, have the harness record it in run_meta, and fail a judged run on a mismatch. Pinning is unavailable because qwen38-27B-v2 is not separately addressable, so detection is the only defence. The migration plan triages the record by which of three roles the model played: roughly four fifths of the primary metrics take no model and are untouched, the Sonnet panels are provider-hosted and untouched, and the exposed set is C-012, C-021 and C-022, which were graded in a window where the served model is not determinable. The cheapest repair is re-grading the saved answers, which changes one variable and needs no pipeline run.

summary: Word handling and exact-name matching are now on by default, and names resolve before the template ladder: +18 right and -8 wrong against the shipped baseline.
detail: Two changes measured in one regression run. ARIADNE_LEXICON and ARIADNE_EXACTNAME now default on, with 0/false still restoring the prior path so earlier arms reproduce; ARIADNE_NAMESEARCH stays off because Step 6s holdout killed it. Name resolution moved from step 7, the no-anchor fall-through, to the top of build -- it used to run only for questions matching no template at all, so Which techniques did the Frankenstein campaign use took the campaign branch with no seed and never reached the resolver. T3 exact identity more than doubles, 0.0990 to 0.2376, its byte-identical query rate goes 0.0000 to 0.1584, and its catalogue dump rate falls by two thirds. Catalogue regression unchanged at 6 better 0 worse. Two design corrections came from tests rather than reasoning: several exact names is a conjunction not an ambiguity, since What exactly is User Training and Software Configuration respectively wants both and describe_by_name already serves several names; and an exactly-resolving name should not take the substring path, because What is Phishing returns four records that way and one this way. A first-token prefilter takes exact matching from a 9138-entity scan to 0.067 ms per call.
tests: 1218 passed, 4 skipped. Catalogue: 6 better, 0 worse, gold recall +0.0463. Variants: +18 right, -8 wrong vs baseline.

summary: Q24 answered: our failure distribution does not contradict Leung et al. The comparison was invalid and our own headline figure did not reproduce.
detail: Two corrections and two survivors, drafted as paper section 9. First, re-running failure_terminus over EXP-2026-07-002s committed artifacts gives 28 non-CORRECT of 120 and 4 unfaithful, not 26-of-36 and 2 -- the 28 matches that experiments own verdict counts and the 36 is most likely an earlier judge run, same species as C-018. Second and more important, our unfaithful class was being compared against Leung et al.s entire Generation stage, which is our narrowest category against their broadest: their Generation covers both stating what you did not retrieve and failing to state what you did, and we split those into unfaithful and projection_gap. Mapped like-for-like, Arm Bs generation share is 42.3%, between their DragonBall-EN 32.7% and CLAPnq 76.4%. So the claim that failures are predominantly planning rather than hallucination is false at the stage level. What survives is better: within generation, under-statement outnumbers fabrication 7 to 4 and the two have opposite fixes, a distinction their taxonomy cannot draw; and the planning result holds as a within-study finding needing no appeal to their pipeline, since Arm A has 0 failures, Arm F 10 and Arm B 28, with 15 of the 18 added failures retrieval-side, a class empty under an authored plan.
tests: failure_terminus recomputed across all three arms of untruncated-fixed; every figure read from that run, none from prose.

summary: EXP-2026-08-021: five grading passes over one frozen answer set. Zero ordering reversals in 60 cells; C-012 survives a grader change at 14-26x the grader's spread.
detail: The alias moved to qwen38-27B-v2, so the saved answers of EXP-2026-08-007/-008/-009 were re-graded to see whether a judged comparison depends on which grader ran it. Gate first: the candidate calibrates BETTER against the committed Sonnet judgments than the instrument it replaces (r 0.9275 -> 0.9612, mean delta +0.031 -> +0.021). Then five complete sessions, 1794 judgments. H8 held completely -- zero ordering reversals across 5 sessions x 12 cells, zero sign flips on either contrast. C-012's margin is +0.4260 +/- 0.0164 and +0.5303 +/- 0.0303. H5 split: 8 of 12 between-model offsets survive at 2x the within-model sd, and every surviving base-cell offset is positive while every surviving .c015 offset is negative, so I-4's directional reading STANDS rather than being withdrawn as the decision rule allowed for. H6 refuted as stated -- spread tracks distance from the ceiling, not weakness. H7 held 4/4, which is the measured justification for grading a whole comparison in one session. Drift was tested and refuted: 0 of 12 cells monotone at k=5, after a -0.060 monotone slide on llm_query bank20 at n=4 broke in r5. The largest finding is incidental: 6 failures in 1794 gradings, ALL in the top 5% by answer size, so judged evaluation fails systematically on the longest answers and a judged mean silently excludes them. None of that was visible at n=1, which graded 360 of 360.

summary: Three follow-ups from EXP-2026-08-021: the extraction path stops discarding judgments, every judged mean now carries its denominator, and Step 4's confound is measured rather than assumed.
detail: (1) _parse replaced a greedy brace match with raw_decode scanning, and now chooses the first object that actually looks like a judgment rather than the first that parses. That fixes two of the three failure modes EXP-2026-08-021 recorded -- the 'Extra data' case, where a greedy span covered a draft and a verdict and discarded a judgment the model had produced, and the 'missing 5 fields' case, where a lead object carrying only verdict won on position. Truncation still raises, correctly, because there is no judgment in a reply that stopped mid-object; that mode is handled instead by a third budget rung at EXP-2026-08-009's 32768, and the budget actually used is recorded on each judgment so a spread measurement can exclude escalated cases rather than absorb them. Five tests, one per recorded failure shape. (2) utils/evaluation/coverage.py reports answers present, judgments written and cases that failed, wired into overnight_sweep.roll_up -- shared by five scripts -- and into holdout_report. A judged mean was being quoted with an n and never with the number it was out of, so n=29 read as a complete set of 29 rather than 30 answers with one ungraded; verified live on bank20260820/gold_loop_llm, which now says so. (3) The Step 4 confound was measured instead of estimated. The deterministic arm has no model in it, so re-running it at HEAD over both fresh banks isolates the builder exactly: of 60 answers, 29 byte-identical, 30 changed in answer text with retrieval identical, 1 changed retrieval and that one is an improvement. So 9f02dc6 is a rendering change with one retrieval fix; retrieval-scored work can go straight to HEAD and only judged arms need the worktree. It also surfaced that 9f02dc6's regression check covered the 120-question catalogue but not the two fresh banks, which are the banks carrying C-012, C-021 and C-022, and half their answers moved.

summary: EXP-2026-08-022: the shipped builder change is invisible to the judge on both fresh banks -- and grading order turns out to bias a paired comparison by about 0.01.
detail: 9f02dc6 changed 31 of 60 deterministic answers on the two fresh banks, almost all in text with retrieval identical, and its own regression evidence covered the catalogue and variant bank rather than the banks carrying C-012, C-021 and C-022. Judged over four sessions with the 29 byte-identical answers as an internal null control, the difference-in-differences is +0.0019 +/- 0.0172 and -0.0167 +/- 0.0170, sign-unstable on both banks; the changed answers also regressed LESS often than the byte-identical ones (11.8% vs 17.2%). The larger finding is about the instrument. The null control showed a consistent -0.0088 signed difference on identical bytes across three forward sessions, in all of which the old condition was graded first. A fourth session with the order reversed flipped the control's sign on both banks, +0.0071 and +0.0167: the condition graded SECOND scores lower whichever it is, by about 0.01 -- the same size as the effect being looked for. So EXP-2026-08-009's rule to grade a whole comparison in one session is necessary and not sufficient, since it cancels between-session drift and creates within-session position bias. H1 failed and the pre-registered rule said stop; rather than adopt a difference-in-differences after seeing the numbers, the reversal was run as a prediction and confirmed the mechanism first. Also recorded: 29 of the 31 changed answers were already at 1.0, so an early '0 improved, 5 regressed' reading was 0 improved out of 2 that could, and this design can say the change is not a regression but cannot say it is an improvement.

summary: Grading-order bias fixed in the sweeps and corrected in the record: C-022's reported -0.0334/+0.0000 is one pass by an unidentified model, order-corrected to -0.0587/-0.0520.
detail: EXP-2026-08-022 measured that the condition graded second in a session scores about 0.01 lower whichever it is. Tracing the sweeps found merged_sweep.py grading (MERGED_ARM, *FEDERATED_ARMS), so merged was always first and generic_composed -- the federated control, the other half of C-022's comparison -- always second, on every bank in every pass. The bias loaded entirely onto federation, in the direction that made the experiment's conclusion easier to reach. Prevention: utils/evaluation/grading_order.py counterbalances the order per block, wired into merged_sweep so merged grades first on one bank and last on the other; every judgment now records its position, which is what makes a comparison correctable when counterbalancing is unavailable, as in measure_arms which runs over a single bank and therefore has no second block -- documented rather than papered over. Correction: eight passes, six forward and two reversed. The order effect on this contrast is only +0.0043 and +0.0059, immaterial. The larger defect is the grader: the reported -0.0334/+0.0000 comes from the .c015 pass, one pass by a model that cannot be identified, and it is the least federation-favouring of all eight. Order-corrected under the calibrated grader the contrast is -0.0587 and -0.0520, federation ahead on both banks rather than one-and-a-tie. The conclusion is unchanged because +/-0.06 question-sampling at n=30 swallows it, but 'merging is not worse in any way this study can measure' rested on an exact zero that was an artifact and must not be quoted.

Preflight verifies both stores, probes the grader alias and hashes the bank; two more arms answer the dev half; all three are judged twice with grading order counterbalanced so the ~0.01 position effect is subtractable; a paired forward/reverse contrast resolves the tension between A-4's same-shape comparison and A-5's confounded aggregate; property, containment and abstention failures are classified by cause without a model; everything is recorded as EXP-2026-09-002; and the report is rendered to PDF from artifacts on disk with a mandatory section listing what did not run. summary: Overnight orchestrator, paired direction contrast, anomaly triage, and a jargon-free PDF morning report — the four pieces the overnight plan needs.
detail: expansion_overnight.py runs 16 phases ordered by value rather than dependency, records each in overnight-state.json and skips completed ones on restart, so a crash costs one phase. The three model-free analyses run BEFORE grading, because they answer the questions the night is really for and grading is the long pole. direction_contrast.py pairs on shape rather than on anchor: pairing on (shape, anchor) yields only 2 pairs because the draw never asks one entity both ways, whereas pairing on shape gives 20 and still removes the confound A-5 actually has. All three views are reported — confounded aggregate, shape-paired, anchor-paired — so the difference between them is visible. anomaly_triage.py classifies failures from the artifacts with no model, and found property reads and containment failing identically: the query is built and returns zero rows, 63 and 68 cases. morning_report.py renders to PDF via reportlab with the Markdown written first as a fallback, and treats a missing phase as 'did not run' rather than omitting the section.

summary: The llm_query arm's 153 empty queries measure a reasoning budget, not the model's ability to write a query — probed, recorded, and carried into the morning report as a caveat.
detail: The C-012 baseline arm returned records for 67 of 284 questions, and its dominant recorded failure was the gate refusing an empty query on 153. That is only a baseline if the model wrote bad queries; it is not one if the model never emitted anything. The served model is a reasoning model behind an OpenAI-shaped relay: chain of thought lands in a separate 'reasoning' field and 'content' stays empty until it stops thinking, so a budget spent entirely on reasoning returns finish_reason='length' with content='' — downstream indistinguishable from a model with nothing to say. builder_budget_probe.py replays the exact builder prompt for real failing cases at several budgets. At the budget the arm actually ran under, 2 of 2 replies were blank after burning the whole allowance on reasoning; at 8x, the one reply that returned contained a query (8,269 completion tokens against the arm's 4,096) and the other hit a relay 502 ReadTimeout, recorded as plumbing rather than counted as a failure. Two provenance traps were caught while establishing this and are documented in the script: D0 questions are excluded from the sample because an empty query is the CORRECT behaviour on a negative control, and the effective budget is read from DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS rather than the environment because experiment_untruncated never calls load_env() — the arm ran on code defaults (localhost:9090/default-model, 4,096) while .env declares 2,048 for a different endpoint entirely. Neither value was large enough, so the silently-ignored setting changed nothing tonight, but the report says so. morning_report.py now renders the caveat beside the arm table with every number read from the probe artifact, prints nothing at all if the probe did not run, and states explicitly that whether the recovered query is CORRECT is a question the probe does not ask. Nothing about the system itself was changed.

summary: Overnight sweep finished 16/16. Schema-assembled queries beat the template library on the broad bank: generic 0.6576, deterministic 0.4934, llm_query 0.3712 (the last confounded by a reasoning budget).

The EXP-2026-09-002 experiment record is deliberately NOT written: the plan reserved it for a waking decision.

summary: Repair plan for the four defects behind EXP-2026-09-002's weak tiers. The reported single defect is actually three, and the fourth is in the measuring instrument rather than the system.
detail: EXP-2026-09-002 reported '63 of 63 cases the query is built and returns zero rows'. Inspection of the run's own 572 answer artifacts falsifies both halves: 455 of 572 results carry records, and anomaly_triage.py:53 reads row_count off the result object while the field only exists in traces[].detail, so the sum is always 0 and classify() has one reachable branch. Re-derived, the 131 failures are: 53 property reads the system answered correctly and the scorer cannot credit (recall is exactly 1/(gold_width+1) in all 53 because the anchor is the only creditable item and sits in the denominator; score_answer_coverage already documents returning None for property-only entries, and the expansion bank re-enabled it by putting a prose value into must_include_related); 62 from gremlin/builder.py:425 hardcoding hasLabel('AttackPattern') for View and Category anchors, which is the View property reads and 60 of the 68 containment failures as one bug; 8 from the cypher ladder's unconditional Group and Tactic branches capturing property reads before describe; and ~8 unexplained. Nine steps in three concurrent workstreams (scorer / retrieval / llm_query budget) converging on a single 16-way re-run as EXP-2026-09-003. The bank is fixed, not regenerated, so prior arms stay comparable; the 288-question holdout stays sealed.

summary: The anomaly classifier read row_count off the result object, where the field never exists, so 'query built and returned no rows' was its only reachable verdict. EXP-2026-09-002's 63/63 and 68/68 were that artifact, not a finding.
detail: The specialists record row_count inside traces[].detail (utils/specialists/base.py:94); anomaly_triage.py:53 read result['row_count'], which is absent from all 632 results in the run's 572 artifacts. The sum was therefore always 0, classify() returned query_built_returned_no_rows for every case that built a query, and its three remaining branches were dead code. The claim is contradicted by the same artifacts it was computed from: 455 of 572 results carry records, and one supposedly-empty Group case returned 22. row_count() now reads the trace detail, preferring the execute step (the raw driver count) over the downstream assess/normalize re-records, and falls back to the materialised records list when no trace recorded a count. Re-run to a NEW path so EXP-2026-09-002's hash-pinned anomalies.json stays intact: property reads split 53 partial_recall / 8 evidence_extracted_but_wrong_entities / 2 query_built_returned_no_rows, and containment 45 / 17 / 6. The single shared cause was an instrument defect; there are three real ones underneath it.

summary: Property reads were scored against a rule no arm could satisfy: the gold is a value (a description, an alias, a platform name) resolved through a set that holds identifiers only. All 63 D1 questions scored at most their anchor.
detail: score_answer_coverage resolves gold via _surfaced_ids, which collects claim entity_ids, citation primary_ids, and narrative matches of _ANSWER_ID_RE (T####/TA####/[MSG]####/DS####/CAPEC-#/CWE-#). The expansion bank's D1 tier puts a property's literal value in must_include_related, a coverage key -- so gold for 'What does T1037 describe?' is the whole prose description and gold for 'What else is G0092 called?' is CHIMBORAZO/Hive0065/Spandex Tempest. None is an identifier, so none could ever be credited: 53 of 63 landed on exactly 1/(gold_width+1), the anchor alone over a denominator that includes it. The function's own docstring already said it returns None for 'property-only' entries; the bank re-enabled the path by accident. Both gold kinds are affected, not only the 22 text ones -- 'Linux', 'True' and an ISO date are no more identifiers than a paragraph is. property_gold.py adds a deliberately threshold-free rule, pre-registered in its docstring and committed before any figure was computed: normalise both sides identically (strip (Citation: ...), casefold, split on non-alphanumerics), credit a value when its token sequence appears contiguously in the answer text, and score the fraction of values surfaced. Contiguity buys word boundaries, so gold 'True' is not credited by 'truest'. No partial credit within a value: a truncated description scores 0, because that is a real finding about the composer rather than something to smooth over. is_property_read() keys on structure (steps == [] and Label.prop shapes), so the golden catalogue -- which carries no spec -- can never enter the path. The change can only raise scores and raises them for every arm equally, so it is not evidence any arm improved; the record must carry the pre-repair figure beside it.
tests: 15 new tests pass; utils/evaluation/tests 104 passed. 30 pre-existing failures (29 test_golden_synthesis capec + test_score_e2e_live_subset) verified identical with the change stashed -- the ariadne-gremlin container is up but unhealthy and its store is empty, so every CAPEC query returns cleanly with no records.

summary: Re-scored the 572 saved answers under the pre-registered property rule. D1 rises 0.3958 -> 0.5624 and pooled 0.4522 -> 0.4727, but the reweighted headline does not move at all: 0.5060 before and after. Only 21 of 63 property reads were a scoring artifact; the rest are three real defects, one of them new.
detail: score_bank.py gains --rescore-property-gold (default off; the unflagged path reproduces EXP-2026-09-002 exactly at 0.4522/0.5060/0.4350/0.4683, which is the harness's own regression check). The identifier half of each verdict is read back out of the artifact's recorded missing list rather than recomputed, so the two figures differ in exactly one thing. Reweighted recall is unchanged because property shapes carry no census instance count -- 0 of 28 have a weight -- so the tier contributes nothing to the comparable figure. That is the important reading: the defect never touched the number the project designates as quotable, and the repair cannot be accused of inflating it. One implementation correction was needed after the first re-score: normalize_tokens did not resolve markdown links, so a gold value beginning '[Operation Spalax](https://...)' had the url's words sitting inside its token run and failed contiguity against the composer's rendered label. Fixing it is what rule 1 already promised and introduced no threshold; it moved 6 of 68 unmatched values (15 questions before, 21 after) and both figures are recorded. The remaining 42 unchanged questions are NOT a scoring artifact, which corrects the earlier attribution. 62 gold values are genuinely absent from the answer, and the cause is upstream of both the scorer and the composer: across all 23,879 records retrieved in the run, x_mitre_contributors, aliases, first_seen, last_seen and is_family appear on ZERO, and x_mitre_platforms on 39. Gold is computed from the raw STIX snapshot, so the bank is asking for properties the knowledge-graph build never loaded. That is a sixth cause the repair plan does not cover and is now the largest single one -- roughly 46 of the 62 absent values.
tests: 17 property-gold tests pass; unflagged score_bank reproduces the published EXP-2026-09-002 figures byte-for-byte

summary: Rule 4: a boolean gold value is credited only when the answer names its property. A bare 'False' was being satisfied by the composer's trailer, which prints several unrelated booleans per record. D1 settles at 0.5466, down from the 0.5624 first reported.
detail: Found by inspection of the questions the first re-score moved. 'Can T1072 be applied remotely?' has gold 'False'; the answer never mentions x_mitre_remote_support, but every record's deterministic trailer carries 'revoked: False; x_mitre_deprecated: False; x_mitre_is_subtechnique: False', and the bare token matched one of those. Four of the 21 questions that moved were spurious this way. A boolean is uninformative here by construction -- the composer emits several per record -- so true/false gold now requires '<property> <value>' as a contiguous run. Scope is deliberately boolean-only: the first attempt required qualification of EVERY one-token value and wrongly rejected CHIMBORAZO as an alias of G0092, a distinctive proper noun the composer never prints as another property's value. Known residual risk recorded in the docstring rather than papered over: a short closed-vocabulary enum (High, Detailed, Implicit) could match incidentally the same way; none was observed doing so, and widening the rule to catch a hypothetical costs real matches. Final figures: D1 0.3958 -> 0.5466 (19 questions move, all to 1.0), pooled 0.4522 -> 0.4708, dev 0.4350 -> 0.4492, holdout 0.4683 -> 0.4911, reweighted 0.5060 unchanged. The correction LOWERS the figure from the 0.5624 first computed, which is the opposite direction from fitting a rule to a result.
tests: 22 property-gold tests pass

summary: The ATT&CK build kept a hand-maintained allowlist of ten properties and silently discarded the rest, making 24 of the expansion bank's 63 property questions unanswerable. Policy inverted: keep every scalar-valued property, name what is excluded and why.
detail: Worked example: 'Who contributed C0057?' The raw snapshot carries x_mitre_contributors on the campaign; the built node did not, so the system retrieved exactly the right record and could not answer. Across all 23,879 records the overnight run retrieved, x_mitre_contributors, aliases, first_seen, last_seen and is_family appeared on ZERO. The gap was invisible for as long as the question sets were themselves written from the graph -- nothing could ask for a property the graph lacked. The census-derived bank reads the raw STIX instead and found it immediately. _node_properties now keeps any scalar or flat list of scalars, minus a named EXCLUDED_PROPERTY_KEYS: STIX envelope refs, fields the graph expresses as edges (kill_chain_phases, x_mitre_analytic_refs, x_mitre_log_source_references), and nested detail up to 36 KB per object (x_mitre_log_sources, x_mitre_mutable_elements). external_references is kept despite being nested because id extraction and the citation surface both read it. LEGACY_NODE_PROPERTY_KEYS is retained purely so a test asserts the inversion is a superset. Post-rebuild the export carries contributors on 746 nodes, aliases 230, first_seen/last_seen 56 each, is_family 726. CAPEC needed no change -- it never had an allowlist, which is why View.Type was already present and its failures belong to the Gremlin label bug instead.

summary: Two Gremlin loader defects the widened build exposed: a hard 14-property ceiling from one binding per property, and a payload 'id' that silently redefined a vertex -- which had been costing the live CAPEC graph one edge for the whole project.
detail: Loading the widened nodes died with '499: The [eval] message contains 17 bindings which is more than is allowed by the server 16 configuration'. TinkerPop's stock maxParameters is 16 and the loader bound one parameter per property, so a node was silently capped at fourteen. Fixed by batching rather than by mounting a custom gremlin-server.yaml: a reviewer must be able to load this graph against the unmodified tinkerpop/gremlin-server image. vertex_upsert_batches splits the write so no submission exceeds MAX_BINDINGS, later batches matching the vertex the first created; vertex_upsert_traversal now raises rather than truncating. Binding names are indexed (p0, p1) instead of derived from the key, because two keys can sanitize to the same identifier and a collision would drop a property. Deliberate semantic change, recorded not smuggled: properties used to sit inside the coalesce's addV branch and were written only on CREATE, so a reload after a build change kept the old values and the upsert only ever inserted; they now apply to the created or matched vertex alike. The second defect surfaced when a reload produced 6375 nodes instead of 6374: exactly one export node, capec:external-reference:REF-97, carries properties.id == 'REF-97', which was written after the identity property and renamed the vertex. The HAS_REFERENCE edge pointing at the real id then matched no vertex and was dropped with no error -- the live graph has been carrying 8581 of 8582 edges -- and a reload could not find the vertex and duplicated it. Identity is no longer overwritable by payload. After the fix CAPEC loads clean at 6374/8582 for the first time.

summary: The template ladder picked a query by which labels a question mentioned, not by what it asked. Group and Tactic property reads were answered with the anchor's techniques; CAPEC containment questions fell through to describe.
detail: Steps 1-4 of docs/plans/2026-09-03-template-routing-repair.md. Cypher: 'if has_group:' and 'if has_tactic:' fired on a label's presence, so 'What does APT38 describe?' (entities ['Group'], no edge, no target) returned APT38's 22 techniques -- a valid query, the right group, a different question. Both are now gated on technique intent; the frozen group_techniques case carries ['Group','Technique'] and routes exactly where it did. Gremlin: _resolve_neighbor_rels knew only the seven edges leaving an AttackPattern, so a Category's own membership edge was invisible. Three things had to be right at once. (1) The bank asks in the source's vocabulary -- Category -[HAS_MEMBER]-> AttackPattern, container to member -- while the build stores AttackPattern -[MEMBER_OF]-> Category and AttackPattern -[IN_VIEW]-> View, member to container; HAS_MEMBER exists nowhere in the graph, so the first implementation would have traversed an edge that does not exist. The container's kind picks the edge, the anchor's role picks the direction. (2) _REL_TARGET_LABEL maps MEMBER_OF to Category, which read from the container's side filtered the members -- AttackPatterns -- down to Categories and returned nothing; containment now carries no target label, since a View's members are both kinds anyway. (3) Containment routes only when it is the ONLY relation named: a compound question carries ('PeerOf','MEMBER_OF') and routing on its second hop answers the wrong one, measured at 0.3333 through describe against 0.0000 through containment. Live: CAPEC-156 returns its 6 members, CAPEC-1000 its 9 categories, CAPEC-580 the view it sits in. The frozen behaviour lock held -- no generation 5 needed.

Of the 9 predicted movers that did not: 7 are compound two-shape questions the new containment guard deliberately refuses, 2 retrieve correctly and score zero, and 0 are retrieval failures. Four answers in the run scored this way, one at 0.1667 (ISSUES I-2). Larger: the scorer recognises the source's id vocabulary and not the graph's. Mean recall is 0.4059 as scored and 0.5913 counting the URN form -- the defect is worth 0.185 on this set (ISSUES I-3). That is the third defect of this family in three days: the bank asks in the source's vocabulary and the system answers in the build's, and every mismatch reads as a system failure. summary: The llm_query arm's token budget was read at import time, which made a written-down setting silently ignorable. It now resolves at call time, and the arm's builder model is identified rather than inferred.
detail: Step 6 of the repair plan, and the diagnosis in EXP-2026-09-002 ISSUES I-3 was not quite right: experiment_untruncated DOES call load_env(), and its --llm-max-tokens default is 16384, not 4096. summary: Repeat grading sessions and a paired bootstrap, so tonight's cross-family number can be interpreted. First output: the 0.1623 gap now has a 95% CI of [0.1258, 0.2001], which EXP-2026-09-005 I-1 recorded as missing.

It waits for the main cross-family pass, then keeps the gemma endpoint busy with repeat sessions at a FIXED grading position until 30 minutes before the endpoint disappears, discarding any session cut short rather than averaging a partial pass in. The reason is the question scripts/grader_repeats.py was written to settle: whether a between-model offset measured at n=1 survives the within-model spread. qwen's spread is on record at 0.0050 over five sessions (EXP-2026-08-021); gemma's is unmeasured, so a qwen-versus-gemma difference tonight would be indistinguishable from one grader being noisy. Contrasts are computed WITHIN a session so a session-level offset cancels instead of inflating the spread. The analysis also runs a paired percentile bootstrap over questions on the pass-averaged per-case scores (2000 resamples, seed 1729, the project's own method), which is the cheapest thing that gives the arm gap an interval; D-010 and EXP-2026-09-005 I-1 both record its absence. summary: Split the llm_query re-run across two dedicated GPUs at 16 concurrency each, with a readiness gate, a clock-vs-budget probe, and a plain-language report generator that reads every figure from disk.
detail: Operator directive: 16 concurrency on default-model-2 and default-model-3, each its own GPU on :9090, both serving qwen38-27B-v2. The bank is split 144/140 STRATIFIED BY d_tier, because D4-D6 are where the previous run collapsed and an unstratified split would hand one GPU the easy half. wait_then_split_run.py exists because a port being open is not readiness: the first probe fired 0.6 s after launch and got ten responses with no choices key at all while vLLM was still loading weights; readiness now means a real completion with non-empty content from each alias twice in a row. The probe then settles a question two days of runs could not: 9 of 10 hard D4 questions emitted content at 32768 tokens and 16-way concurrency, completing in 258-388 s, so the remaining failures are not the equipment. That also refutes the throughput model I argued from -- I predicted 16-way would starve each request to 5.2 tok/s and it did not; dedicated GPUs do not behave like the shared relay the estimate was extrapolated from. finish_split_and_report.py waits on the run PIDs rather than a name match (a name match killed a launcher on 09-04 and then reported it as running), merges the halves, refuses to judge fewer than 284 answers or a built-query count no better than the previous 140, serialises against the :4000 grader, and renders the report. plain_report.py writes the whole 3-5 September arc for a reader who does not know the codebase, reading every figure from artifacts, naming the six system faults and three measurement faults separately, and carrying a section of my own errors because each cost hours.
tests: probe verdict recorded from 10 real calls; report renders to PDF from artifacts on disk

summary: The fair llm_query re-run finished: 235 of 284 built a query and it scores 0.3781 -- almost exactly the 0.3712 that was dismissed as a budget artifact. Two days of instrument repair confirmed the original number rather than overturning it.
detail: Split across two dedicated GPUs at 16 concurrency, budget 32768, cutoff 4096 s: 284 answers in ~2.4 h per half, 235 built a query (83%) against 140 on 09-04 and 2 before the timeout fix. Only 12 empties remain and 37 are gate rejections of genuinely malformed queries, so for the first time the arm's failures are the model's rather than ours. Judged on :4000 by qwen38-27B-v2, two counterbalanced passes, 562 judgments: 0.3781 overall and 0.3703 conditional on a query actually being built. THE POINT: EXP-2026-09-002's 0.3712 was correctly flagged as confounded and correctly withheld from citation, and the fair measurement lands within 0.007 of it. C-012 is now supported at n=284 with a baseline that cannot be called starved -- the model receives the schema, the seeds, the gate's constraints and a repair loop, and still writes a worse query than a template library. Three arms, same instrument, same protocol: schema-assembled 0.6569, templates 0.4946, model-written 0.3781. Also wired, at operator direction and NOT yet verified against a live endpoint because both GPUs went down after the run: a 512-token thinking cap via LLM_THINKING_BUDGET, sent through both chat_template_kwargs and extra_body since which applies depends on the served model's chat template.
tests: 562 judgments over 284 cases; thinking cap emits into the payload but is UNVERIFIED against a live server

summary: The web workbench's Settings button was drawn as a sun, not a gear. GearIcon was a hub circle with eight radiating rays -- the standard brightness/light-bulb glyph -- so the entry point to LLM configuration did not read as settings. Replaced with a real 8-tooth cog outline.
detail: Step 1 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md. The old path was `M12 2.5v3M12 18.5v3...` -- eight spokes around a central circle, which is what every icon set uses for brightness. The new outer path is a genuine gear outline generated as 32 alternating tip/root vertices (8 teeth, outer radius 10, root radius 7.6, about a 12,12 centre) with strokeLinejoin=round, keeping the existing r=3.2 hub and strokeWidth 1.5 so it matches the rest of the inline icon set. Verified side by side at 16px and 96px: the old glyph is unambiguously a sun and the new one is unambiguously a cog. Operator-reported: 'the button should be a gear icon not a light bulb'.

summary: Added utils/llm/config.py: one ARIADNE_LLM_* group every stage inherits from, with per-stage overrides kept as the escape hatch, and unset_env_values() so 'inherit' can actually clear a key instead of freezing a value into .env.
detail: Step 2 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md; purely additive, no consumer touched yet. Lookup is <STAGE>_LLM_<FIELD> -> ARIADNE_LLM_<FIELD> -> built-in default, and the load-bearing test asserts that with nothing set every stage resolves to exactly the pre-refactor values -- the ~20 scripts under scripts/ and every arm in docs/research/experiments/ pin those numbers. LLMSettings.inherited names which fields came from the primary, which is what lets the UI render a stage as inherit-vs-custom. Two invariants land here: max_tokens and thinking_budget are COUPLED (overriding either carries both, so a stage can never run a budget sized against another scope's token cap), and a positive thinking_budget must be strictly less than max_tokens -- validate() reports it as a field error for the API to 422 on, clamped() is the last resort for a hand-edited .env and logs when it fires. 0 still means 'send no cap', which is what every run predating the cap did. unset_env_values comments the assignment out in place rather than deleting it, so a cleared override stays legible and its documentation comment survives.
tests: 49 pass (29 new resolver tests + 20 config tests incl. 4 new unset round-trips)

summary: Added the utils/llm provider layer: OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and Gemini adapters, model discovery that never raises into a UI, and a probe that proves a real completion rather than an open port. Until now no Ariadne call site sent an API key at all, so only a local server could ever be used.
detail: Step 3 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md; still additive, no existing client rewired yet. Adapters are PURE -- they build a request and parse a response and never open a socket -- so every backend's real wire shape is testable with no network, keys or GPU, and all HTTP policy lives once in client.py. The differences absorbed are the ones that fail silently: Anthropic hoists system out of messages and 400s otherwise, uses x-api-key with a pinned anthropic-version, returns typed content blocks, and spells truncation stop_reason=max_tokens; Gemini renames the container to contents and the assistant role to model, puts maxOutputTokens under generationConfig, prefixes listed ids with models/, and returns 200 with an EMPTY CANDIDATE LIST for a blocked prompt -- now surfaced as 'blocked: SAFETY' instead of an unexplained silence. seed and the vLLM thinking channels are dropped for both rather than sent, since Gemini ignores unknown keys rather than rejecting them, which looks like success. discover_models returns a DiscoveryResult with three distinct empty states (unreachable / reachable-but-empty / no-listing-endpoint) because they need three different fixes. probe() sends a real tiny completion and requires non-empty content back: the 2026-09-05 record has ten replies with no choices key while vLLM was loading weights, which both a TCP check and a /models call would have passed. Connect and read timeouts are separate numbers, pinned by test.
tests: 66 pass offline (21 adapter shape checks, 16 discovery/probe contract checks, 29 resolver)

summary: Every agent's LLM config and transport now resolves through utils/llm, so one ARIADNE_LLM_* group configures all five stages and carries an API key for the first time. Three thinking-budget sources collapse into one. Recorded answers are byte-identical on both banks.
detail: Step 4 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md. Each from_env() fills its existing llm_* fields THROUGH the resolver, so per-stage vars still win when set (the ~20 experiment scripts keep reproducing) but fall back to the primary group; each config gains llm_settings() giving transports the provider and credentials the legacy shape had no room for. Ten hand-rolled requests.post(.../chat/completions) call sites now go through utils.llm.chat, with prompts and parsing untouched -- for an unauthenticated OpenAI-compatible endpoint the request on the wire is unchanged. The conversation layer's hand-written CONVERSATION->SYNTHESIS chain is gone; SYNTHESIS_LLM_* survives as its default so an existing .env resolves identically, but the primary group now wins over another stage's override, because following a sibling stage was the hack that made the chat pane configurable only through a field labelled 'synthesis'. THE THINKING BUDGET had three sources -- a global LLM_THINKING_BUDGET, SYNTHESIS_LLM_THINKING_BUDGET, and an implicit max_tokens // 2 inside SynthesisConfig.thinking_budget(). Now one: sampling_params takes the resolved value, the derivation is DELETED, and LLM_THINKING_BUDGET is honoured as a legacy alias so the five recorded runs that set it are unaffected. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a deployment that set SYNTHESIS_LLM_MAX_TOKENS and left the budget unset previously got half of it implicitly and now gets no cap. judge_answers.py keeps its own transport on purpose -- stdlib-only, its own retry loop and budget escalation, and it reads back the served model id to attribute a judgment to real weights rather than a relay alias.
tests: 1786 pass (1 pre-existing docs-contract failure, verified on HEAD). Recorded-answer regression vs an unmodified-HEAD run of the same banks: 30/30 identifiers AND 30/30 full answer bytes on both bank-2026-08-19 and bank-2026-08-20.

summary: /api/config now exposes ONE provider-aware LLM group plus per-stage deltas instead of four sibling groups, with a write-only API key. Adds POST /api/llm/models (discovery) and POST /api/llm/test (a real completion), both accepting unsaved values so Refresh and Test work before Save.
detail: Step 5 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md. The old shape exposed planner/specialist/synthesis/eval and NOT conversation -- which is the group the chat pane actually ran on -- so the modal could not be connected to the answer an analyst got. Now: llm.default plus llm.stages keyed by stage, each carrying `inherited` so the UI renders inherit-vs-custom from a server fact rather than a guess. LLMGroupUpdate gains an explicit `inherit` list: an omitted field means 'leave it alone' and a named one means 'clear it', because collapsing both into null makes them indistinguishable on the wire. Clearing routes to unset_env_values, never to rewriting the default's current values, which would pin a stage to a snapshot. thinking_budget < max_tokens is enforced as a model validator AND in validate_update, which re-resolves the would-be environment to catch the partial case (lowering max_tokens under an already-stored budget) that the request alone cannot see -- a 422 with a named field rather than a silent clamp. Discovery and test are POST because the body may carry a key, and both always return 200: an unreachable GPU box is a normal state, not a server error. llm_health reads the unified group instead of SynthesisConfig. Also fixed a test-isolation bug I introduced: a PUT test without an ENV_FILE redirect appended two ARIADNE_LLM_* lines to the operator's real .env, which then leaked into a later run as two phantom conversation-config failures; the preserve_env fixture is now autouse and redirects for every test in the module.
tests: 86 pass (was 65); includes an override->inherit round-trip asserting the .env key is cleared, and that a real .env is never written

summary: Settings is now ONE language-model menu -- provider select, Refresh-backed model picker, Test button, and a collapsed per-stage overrides list -- replacing the four sibling agent forms. Verified against the live app: Refresh listed 10 real models, a dead port renders as an empty state, and an over-budget value disables Save.
detail: Step 6 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md. The four LLMSection forms (planner/specialist/synthesis/eval) are gone; there is one Language Model fieldset plus a Per-stage endpoints disclosure covering all five stages, each defaulting to `inherit` and showing what it inherits. EndpointFields is deliberately shared by the primary group and every override, so there is exactly one implementation of 'ask this URL what it serves' and Refresh/Test cannot drift between them. Discovery is sequence-numbered and abortable: a slow reply for a half-typed URL can otherwise land after a fast one and repopulate the dropdown with the wrong server's models. It runs once on open rather than per keystroke -- a fetch per character is what makes a modal feel frozen -- and Refresh is the manual lever. The model field stays an input backed by a datalist, never a bare select, because discovery legitimately returns nothing for a gateway with no /models and a picker that then offers no way to type is worse than the plain box it replaced; the three empty states render with the server's own reason. Max tokens and thinking budget sit together with live validation and a 'use half of max' shortcut that writes a REAL number rather than reintroducing a derivation. Switching a stage back to inherit sends the field names to clear, never the default's current values. Also corrected llm_health to report the CONVERSATION stage rather than the primary group: an .env predating the unified group has every stage overridden and the primary unset, and the header pill was showing an idle :9090 default while every real call went to :4000.
tests: npm test 204 pass (15 new), npm run build clean, npm run lint unchanged at the 2 pre-existing errors; api 86 pass. Live check against the running app: Refresh listed 10 models from the real :4000 endpoint, an unreachable port rendered as 'Could not reach ... is it running?', PUT with budget==max_tokens returned 422 naming the field, and .env was byte-identical afterward.

summary: Rewrote .env.example section 8 around one ARIADNE_LLM_* group with the per-stage names demoted to a documented override appendix, collapsed the setup wizard to write one group instead of fanning three values across five prefixes, and fixed a real bug: CONVERSATION_LLM_ENABLED never fell back to the group.
detail: Step 7 of docs/plans/2026-09-07-single-llm-config.md. The complexity the operator hit was as much documentation as code -- the old section 8 spent four blocks explaining which of five endpoints wins. It is now one group of four settings plus an 8b appendix covering the per-stage overrides, why they still exist (every arm under docs/research/experiments/ pins them), that MAX_TOKENS and THINKING_BUDGET are coupled, and that switching a stage back to inherit CLEARS rather than copies. The thinking-budget block spells out the >= max_tokens failure mode and names the behaviour change from deleting the max_tokens // 2 derivation. SYNTHESIS_LLM_CLAIMS, SPECIALIST_LLM_QUERY_BUILDER and EVAL_LLM_SAMPLE_SIZE stay per-stage on purpose: they select a code path or a sample size, not a model. The wizard now writes ARIADNE_LLM_* once and CLEARS stale per-stage overrides from an earlier run -- without that they would silently outrank the endpoint just chosen and the operator would watch their new server be ignored. Its _enabled() reads the group rather than PLANNER_LLM_ENABLED, which was never the same question. BUG FIXED: ConversationLLMConfig.from_env read env_bool('CONVERSATION_LLM_ENABLED') directly, so the chat layer ignored ARIADNE_LLM_ENABLED entirely -- an operator could turn the LLM on in one place and have the chat pane stay deterministic with nothing on screen explaining why. Caught by a before/after comparison of the operator's own .env migration, not by a test. Also added an autouse env-clearing fixture to the conversation config tests: api/main.py calls load_env() at import, so collecting api/ in the same run drops the real .env into os.environ and those assertions silently start measuring that file.
tests: wizard 39 pass, api+conversation+llm+config 125 pass, web 204 pass, npm run build clean. Live: the Settings Test button returned 'OK - gemma-4-26B-it answered in 4453 ms' against a real endpoint, naming the served model rather than the 'local' relay alias it was asked for.

summary: Added an SSE keep-alive wrapper so a stream can prove it is alive while a stage is silent. Measured cause: 5 of 12 concurrent llm-drafter runs went quiet past the browser's 90s stall budget (longest 429s) and were cancelled client-side even though every one of them finished server-side.
why: The pipeline is a blocking iterator, so nothing reaches the socket while a planner/specialist/synthesis LLM call runs. web/lib/api.ts cancels any stream idle past SSE_STALL_MS, which is why the ticker stops on 'planning and routing the question' about half the time. The keep-alive is an SSE comment, not a new event, so parseSseFrame drops it and the typed event union, run machine and fixtures stay byte-identical.
tests: api/tests/test_heartbeat.py 5 pass

summary: Both the query and conversation SSE streams now emit a keep-alive comment while a stage is silent, so the browser stops cancelling runs that are still working. This is the fix for the ticker stopping on 'planning and routing the question'.
why: Nothing was failing: 12 of 12 concurrent llm-drafter questions completed server-side, but 5 of 12 had a silent gap past the client's 90s SSE_STALL_MS and would have been killed in the browser -- 240s after status(planning), 429s after a specialist, 114s after status(answering). The keep-alive is an SSE comment so parseSseFrame drops it and the typed event union is untouched; the period is SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S (default 10s), read per call so it can be shortened in a test. _collect in the api tests now skips comment frames the way a browser does.
tests: api 95 pass (the one failure is pre-existing: .env's ORCH_MAX_HOPS=1 leaks into the suite via load_env(); 95 pass under the default). web 206 pass (2 new), npm run build clean.

summary: The API imports both specialist backends at startup so no request thread ever takes a module import lock. Fixes a live wedge where one stalled request held the import lock for utils.specialists.cypher.specialist and every later query -- and eventually /api/health -- blocked forever.
why: build_specialist imports its backend lazily, which is right for the CLI but a hazard in the service: the import runs on a LangGraph worker, so a request that stalls partway through it poisons the whole process until restart. Captured with py-spy on 2026-09-07: one thread inside exec_module for cypher.specialist, another blocked in _lock_unlock_module inside build_specialist. build_specialist itself is unchanged -- the warm-up only means its lazy imports are always already resolved. Test lands in api/tests/test_warmup.py rather than the test_main.py the plan named.
tests: api 97 pass, utils/specialists 550 pass. One pre-existing docs-contract failure (test_every_cited_repo_path_exists, two EXP folders citing docs/evaluation/composition/authored/ingested.json) is unrelated and present on HEAD.

summary: PIPELINE_TIMEOUT_S now binds at synthesis, not only inside the specialist loop. A run that has already spent its budget composes deterministically and says so on the wire instead of adding another full LLM timeout.
why: The value is documented as the total-pipeline deadline but was read only at agents/specialists/nodes.py:84, so a slow planner could spend the whole 120s allowance and synthesis would still start a fresh 240s call. Measured: 114s and 93s silent tails after status(answering) in a 12-way concurrent run. The plan node deliberately gets NO check -- it runs ~0.2s in, so the deadline cannot have passed and the branch would be unreachable. test_event_parity's timeout sequence gains one status frame, which is the notice itself.
tests: api + orchestration + pipeline 164 pass. The new guard was verified to FAIL against an unmodified utils/orchestration/main.py.

summary: app.py now hands the API child the environment as it was BEFORE .env was loaded, so a fresh worker reads the current file instead of a launch-time snapshot. Without this, a model endpoint changed in the Settings modal silently reverted on the next --reload restart.
why: The launcher loads .env into its own process for preflight, the API child inherited that, and load_env does not override real environment variables -- by design, so a shell or CI value wins. The side effect was that .env could never win in the API, even though the workbench's own Settings modal is what writes it. Observed while investigating the SSE stalls: /api/config reported :9090/default-model, a reload was triggered, and every stage came back as :4000/local with nothing on screen saying so. A genuinely exported shell variable still wins because it is already in the snapshot.
tests: utils/launcher 28 pass. Verified live: an API started with the ARIADNE_LLM_* keys unset resolves all six groups to :9090/default-model from the current .env, where the inheriting worker resolved :4000/local.

summary: Recorded EXP-2026-09-013 with the before/after for the SSE stall, and kept the instrument as utils/tests/sse_gap_probe.py. Before: 12/12 runs succeeded server-side and 5/12 (42%) still exceeded the browser's 90s stall budget, worst silence 429s. After: 0/12, worst silence 10.0s -- the heartbeat interval, hit exactly.
why: The failure is invisible to the test suite because the server reports success on every run that the browser then cancels, so the measured quantity has to be socket SILENCE rather than latency and the instrument has to be kept. supports_claims is deliberately empty: this measures the web layer and says nothing about retrieval quality. ISSUES.md records what was not established -- one before run only, an unexplained 434s outlier at ~24-way concurrency, and the import-lock trigger, which the fix does not depend on knowing.
tests: make validate-research OK (46 experiments).

summary: Plan for a hybrid rewrite stage in front of the deterministic engine: a fixed intent form filled deterministically where stems, exact names and the resolver ladder can bind it, then by a language model choosing only from candidate lists the name index and the card produce, gated so anything off-list or off-card abstains, cached by question hash, and rendered to the tier-0 sentence the engine already answers at 1.0. Measured on the frozen 579-variant bank per tier and the 572-question expansion bank, with default-model and default-model-2 on :9090 at three seeded runs each against a byte-identical model-off arm.
why: EXP-2026-08-020 showed the engine's correctness is a property of phrasing (T4/T5 record identity 0.0000 across every arm) and that the name index's accept decision cannot be made by a threshold (68% precision on the frozen half). The operator asked for a hybrid that keeps the deterministic engine for query construction and uses the model only where it is needed; the model-comparison arms are the operator's directive. Step 7 of the 2026-08-29 plan described this seam and was never built.

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 0 of 8: preconditions. Both graphs verify clean (ATT&CK 4369 nodes / 27669 edges in Neo4j, CAPEC 6374 / 8582 in Gremlin) after retiring a runtime manifest that had ATT&CK checked against a Gremlin store CAPEC has since replaced. Probed :9090 twice -- default-model and default-model-2 both serve qwen38-27B-v2 under the same vllm fingerprint, -3 and -4 return 502, and -2 flapped between the probes. Re-captured the 120-question reference and scaffolded EXP-2026-09-014.
why: Every later number is read against this reference, so it has to be re-derived on graphs that are actually loaded and model strings that name weights rather than aliases. The re-capture is NOT byte-identical to the shipped reference_arm6.json -- 0 of 120 cases differ on entity_ids, but 60 differ on queries, 15 on claims and 11 on abstention wording -- so R0 is scored against the fresh capture and the drift is recorded rather than reconciled. The four default-model-* aliases are replicas of one deployment, so step 7's second-model arm would be a repeatability block rather than a model comparison; that is the operator's call.
tests: uv run main.py --graph verify --dataset attack|capec both pass; scripts/model_identity.py --json; variant_harness.py capture (120/120).

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 1 of 8: utils/planner/canonical.py adds the IntentForm (anchors, labels, relation, direction, mode, datasets, unbound), a card-driven renderer, and form_from_slot_gold; scripts/rewrite_roundtrip.py renders all 120 gold forms and diffs what they retrieve against the Step-0 reference. Round-trip 89/118 overall -- 74/78 single-source, 15/40 federated. 33 unit tests; the flag-off 120-question capture is byte-identical to Step 0.
why: The whole hybrid rests on one property: a correctly filled form must render to a question the engine answers as it answers the gold. Proving it before a model is involved is what makes every later number a comparison rather than a hope. The step's load-bearing finding is that the renderer's FUNCTION words cost more than its nouns -- 'related to' is a correlation cue and pulled the join partner in, 'list' is a bulk-scan cue and returned the whole label, and appending the card's relation gloss imported labels the question was not about; classifying each candidate sentence with the router's own cue rules and keeping the least-misread one took 61 to 89. The remaining misses are gold-side and are recorded in ISSUES.md rather than reconciled: 25 federated cases have no slots to render (and a one-relation form cannot express a chain), 2 cases where the incumbent under-enumerates and the rendered form is right, 2 null relations, and 2 records with no slots at all.
tests: uv run python -m pytest utils/planner/tests -q: 220 passed, 2 skipped. variant_harness capture byte-identical to reference_2026-09-08.json.

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 2 of 8: deterministic_fill() binds every slot the shipped machinery can -- the drafter's own source selection, the resolver's per-dataset id ladder, exact complete-name matches, the intent classifier for mode, the schema registry for direction -- and reports the rest as unbound with a reason. Flags ARIADNE_REWRITE / ARIADNE_REWRITE_MODEL / ARIADNE_REWRITE_CACHE_DIR added to PlannerConfig and .env.example, all default off. Bind rate: T0 0.3583, T1 0.5917, T2 0.5250, T3 0.2574, T4 0.0288, T5 0.0288, T6 0.2667.
why: This is the skip-the-model path: everything it binds is free and byte-reproducible, and it must never guess -- the ranked name index is deliberately not consulted, since its accept decision was measured at 68% precision on a frozen half. Three findings came out of building it. Source-naming words were leaking into the target labels ('att' reaches ATT&CK's Matrix gloss), so entity matching now runs with those words removed. A complete-name match that is also a schema word ('Software') was anchoring a bounded scan on an arbitrary tool. And an anchorless form that is not actually a scan is now reported unbound rather than rendered as 'list the mitigations', which is a catalogue dump wearing a question's clothes. ISSUES.md records why the T0 bind rate is only 0.3583: 'uses' is a router stopword, so the USES edge is unreachable from the word 'use', and where two edges both fit the fill reports the ambiguity instead of picking one.
tests: uv run python -m pytest utils/planner/tests -q: 232 passed, 2 skipped. variant_harness capture byte-identical to reference_2026-09-08.json with the flags off. Gold-form round-trip 88/118.

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 3 of 8: candidate_lists()/candidate_lists_all() build the closed choice set -- top-5 entities from the shipped BM25 index scoped by the anchor label, plus every relationship type and node label from the card with their glosses -- and scripts/rewrite_candidates.py measures recall@k of the gold anchor per tier on the TUNE half only. Anchor ceiling: T0/T1/T2 1.0000, T3 0.6275, T4 0.4528, T5 0.5660, T6 0.0000. namesearch gains description_of() so a candidate carries the sentence that tells it apart.
why: The index works as a component and fails as a router, so it is used here purely as a list producer: no accept decision, no threshold, nothing that can be over-fitted. Recall@k is the ceiling on what any chooser can reach, and knowing it before the model runs is what lets step 7 say whether the model was the problem. Two bugs found by measuring rather than by reading: the ranked search was scoped by the TARGET labels, which at T3 guaranteed the gold anchor could not appear, and when routing left the source unbound -- over half the bank at T4 -- the lists came back empty, so the questions with the least footing were handed nothing to choose from. Fixing both moved T4 recall@5 from 0.0417 to 0.5106 and T5 from 0.0962 to 0.5882. A third fix, binding the anchor from whichever source owns the identifier rather than the leading one, took the T1/T2 anchor ceiling to 1.0000.
tests: uv run python -m pytest utils/planner/tests -q: 233 passed, 2 skipped. variant_harness capture byte-identical with the flags off. Gold-form round-trip 88/118.

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 4 of 8: utils/planner/rewrite_llm.py (prompt, transport, JSON parse, RewriteUnavailable, apply_choice, fill), utils/planner/rewrite_cache.py (content-addressed by prompt version + SERVED model + question) and canonical.gate_form(). The model's entire output is indices into numbered lists; anything that is not an int in range is discarded, and the finished form is re-checked against the same closed world. 29 fake-client tests. Live smoke: a T5 paraphrase reached a bound form, the cache replayed it in 0.03s against 24.4s, and a fully bound form never reached the model at all.
why: This is the one new seam, and it differs from the LLM drafter (-0.1185) and the free-form query arm (0.50) in kind rather than degree: it cannot name a source, choose a hop, write a query, or emit an identifier that is not on the list it was handed. Three independent things enforce that -- the prompt asks for indices, _pick refuses anything that is not an int in range, and gate_form re-checks the result -- because any one of them alone is an assertion rather than a property. Direction is never the model's to choose; it is read from the declared endpoints, and a relation whose direction cannot be resolved is refused. The cache keys on the weights that ANSWERED rather than the alias, so one model's choices can never be served as another's, and it is what makes running an LLM arm twice cheap -- which Q2 has been open on since August.
tests: uv run python -m pytest utils/planner/tests -q: 269 passed, 2 skipped. variant_harness capture byte-identical with the flags off.

summary: Hybrid Rewrite Stage step 5 of 8: a canonicalize node between classify and draft in the planner subgraph, so the drafter receives the rendered canonical sentence when the form binds and the analyst's own words otherwise. PlanningState gains original_request / canonical_question / intent_form / rewrite_trace; Plan gains an optional rewrite block that names the rung (off | deterministic | model | abstain), the served model, cache hit, the filled form and any unbound slots. Live end-to-end with the stage on: a T5 paraphrase with zero deterministic footing produced a bound form, the sentence 'In ATT&CK, give the mitigations that mitigates sub technique T1059.003' and real records.

summary: Token meter on the LLM transport, so an arm's cost is read rather than estimated (Q38)
detail: utils/llm/client.py accumulates prompt and completion tokens for every successful chat() and exposes token_meter()/reset_token_meter().
