summary: The full judged development half, three arms and both grading positions: the LLM arm reaches 0.9211 and the model-free arm 0.9210, from 0.7845 and 0.7537 at Step 6. Fabricated cross-catalogue mappings, the kill gate's metric, go to zero on both.
detail: 1,704 judgments over 284 questions. Every tier of the LLM arm rose; the two the repairs targeted rose most, two-step 0.5405 to 0.8603 and cross-catalogue 0.4556 to 0.8767, and the adversarial tier gained 0.15 from the identifier work alone. The two grading positions agree to 0.005. The template control is a wash at 95 up and 97 down, which rules out the grader having a good day. The two real arms have CONVERGED: the language model was worth 0.064 at the reference and 0.031 at Step 6 and is now worth 0.0001, because every fault repaired was in routing, retrieval and identifiers, which both arms share. Two caveats. The comparison is ONE-SIDED — the reference columns were graded in an earlier sitting — and a true paired control re-runs the pre-repair code today. And the hallucination count rose 254 to 291, which classifying every flag shows is NOT invention: our own id-example help text fell 176 to 54, real identifiers the rolled-up gold omits rose 62 to 106 (an answer being more complete scoring worse), while two genuine defects rose and are recorded open as I-15 (node text read as an identifier, 114 flags, faithfulness only) and I-16 (a false absence claim naming the question's edge rather than the store's — a View's members hang off IN_VIEW not MEMBER_OF — 15 flags, costing correctness).

summary: Plan for closing out the correctness repair: fix I-16 (false absence claim naming the question's edge) and I-15 (node text read as an identifier), run the paired control as the protocol pre-registered, mint and seal a fresh evaluation set with seed 10140325, and write up. Each step verifies on a named small slice before anything larger runs; Steps 3-4 chain unattended with a resumable state file.
why: The development half reads 0.9211 but the comparison is one-sided, two grader-exposed defects are recorded rather than fixed, and the only figure that can replace 0.6546 on a slide is one from a set nothing here has touched. Two facts found while grounding the plan: the scorer that produced control-metrics.json was never committed, and the question-author defaults point at :4000, so both must be supplied.

summary: Close-out step 1 of 5 (I-16): an absence claim is now judged against the edge the store resolved, not the name the question used. Containment relation names fold across one public list shared with the Gremlin builder, and an absence is refused when the enumeration beside it calls those neighbours by the noun the absence would deny. Adds a contradiction property to scripts/mechanism_check.py and a reproducible before/after artifact.
why: The composer was writing 'CAPEC-703 has no MEMBER_OF relationships' directly beneath the fifteen members it had just enumerated — a false statement carrying full provenance, and the only open defect that cost correctness rather than faithfulness. Self-contradictions go 7/6/5/6 to zero across both banks and both model-free arms with no gold-text-recall regression.

summary: Close-out step 2 of 5 (I-15): answers no longer carry example identifiers, text-valued neighbours are quoted and labelled rather than listed as identifiers, and the judging view of a related neighbour now carries its content instead of an allow-list of keys. Adds a reproducible flag classifier and files I-17.
why: The 12-case judged slice the plan pre-registered showed quoting alone removed none of the 'node text read as an identifier' flags. Reading the grader's own words found the real cause: generate_e2e built the judge's view of a neighbour from nine identity keys plus 'description', so a CAPEC consequence's scopes and impacts never reached it and a correctly-rendered claim had no warrant in the evidence it was graded against. The two target flag classes go 39 to 0 on the slice, which now carries no flags of any class.

summary: Adds scripts/paired_control_score.py, whose acceptance test is re-deriving the committed Step 6 pair (0.7188 -> 0.7845) from the judgment files, and hardens scripts/repair_control_run.py: the reference commit runs in a git worktree rather than a checkout over the working tree, every arm asserts ok == count from its manifest, cells resume, and a new --stage dry runs eight questions through both sides first.
why: control-metrics.json was committed without the code that produced it, so the experiment's headline pair could be quoted and not re-derived. The runner's checkout left the repository unusable mid-run and lost everything if it died between checkouts, and a reference worktree that cannot see data/ fails 255 of 288 cases while still exiting zero — which would read as a catastrophic pre-repair score.

summary: Mints the fresh question set at seed 10140325: 282 questions authored by Claude Opus subagents from blind briefs, validated, style-checked for homogeneity, and SEALED before any arm runs. Adds scripts/closeout_run.py to chain the remaining stages, --name/--no-split to build_bank.py, and --exclude-answered to select_bank.py.
why: The development half selected the configuration and the holdout has been graded twice, so neither is unseen. The seal earned itself immediately: it caught three drawn questions that an earlier render probe had already answered, which the bank-based exclusion could not see, and the selector now reads the runs tree so a future draw cannot repeat it.

summary: Cut the README from 492 to 418 lines by removing what a person trying to run the repository does not need. The research figures, the July study, and the week-by-week plan are all one click away in the record, and the README now points at them instead of restating them.
detail: Five cuts. The week-by-week roadmap tables and their three milestone check-ins go to docs/goals.md, leaving two sentences. The July seven-arm table goes to docs/evaluation/2026-07-26/, leaving the two findings that still drove the defaults. The Results section keeps the three-comparison table and compresses the costs table, the external-benchmark line and the five caveat bullets into two paragraphs that name the same limits and point at CURRENT.md. The documentation table drops from 17 rows to 8, cutting the internal record-navigation rows that docs/research/ indexes itself. The configuration table drops from 19 rows to 9, keeping ports, credentials, dataset versions, the LLM switch and endpoint, the hop cap and the timeout, and pointing at .env.example for the other 28 keys. Nothing was deleted outright: every cut item is reachable by a link in the section it left. Contents line, anchors, relative paths and check-docs all re-verified.
tests: make check-docs

summary: I-18: a CAPEC pattern's mapping to OWASP or WASC is no longer stated as an ATT&CK mapping. The MAPS_TO noun is now taken from each entry's taxonomy_name rather than hard-coded, and asserts ATT&CK only when every entry says so.
why: The paired control's kill gate failed at fabricated_mapping 1 -> 3. Two of the three were one template-arm case counted twice and one was a real retrieved mapping the gold omits, but the fourth flagged item was genuine: 'CAPEC-126 has 2 ATT&CK mappings: OWASP Attacks:Path Traversal; WASC:33', where neither is ATT&CK. _NOUN_EXPECTS could not catch it because all three taxonomies arrive with the label TaxonomyEntry. Nine answers per arm, 9 -> 0.

summary: Restores the full close-out chain (both grading positions, every stage through the holdout regression), makes paired_control_score.py able to score a run in progress with --partial, and adds scripts/closeout_status.py.
why: The operator wants the whole cycle run overnight to validate the workflow end to end, and wants to see it working rather than find out at the end. Twice today the honest answer to 'is it running?' was no, and nothing said so.

summary: Plans EXP-2026-09-019: whether the Generic tier needs a 27B model or can run on MiniCPM5-2B at localhost:4000, and — separately and more cheaply — whether it needs a planner at all. Five steps, concurrency measured before anything else, each widening only after a single-digit slice clears.
why: Every headline arm replays an authored plan, so 0.92 is the ceiling for retrieval and composition given a correct decomposition rather than an end-to-end figure. That gap is model-free to close and reframes the small-model question, so it runs first.

summary: Added scripts/local_endpoint_probe.py and its tests: an identity gate that reads the served model off the response envelope, a max_tokens ceiling bisect that keeps the server's refusal verbatim, and a concurrency ladder with hard stops on errors, p95 blowout and load. Ran it against :4000 and recorded endpoint.json under EXP-2026-09-019.
why: Step 1 of the small-model/planner-necessity plan. Every later step's worker count, timeout and token budget is a function of these three numbers, and guessing them on llama.cpp makes a workstation unusable. The gate caught that the alias 'local' still serves gemma-4-26B-it rather than the intended MiniCPM5-2B.

summary: Re-probed the endpoint: MiniCPM5-2B is served by the llama.cpp router on :7070, not by the :4000 relay whose 'local' alias still resolves to gemma-4-26B-it. endpoint.json now holds the gate-passing MiniCPM run (knee at concurrency 4, 210 tok/s aggregate); the earlier Gemma measurement is kept as endpoint-gemma-4-26B-it.json.
why: The identity gate refused :4000 twice. Keeping both measurements makes the 2B/26B comparison free and stops a figure being attributed to the wrong weights.

summary: Split experiment_untruncated's real-pipeline runner by explicit LLM posture: _run_real_pipeline(use_llm=...), with run_planned (False) for the new generic_planned arm and run_rewrite (True) left byte-identical for EXP-2026-09-014's arms. run_meta now records the posture instead of hardcoding 'deterministic'. Added the generic_planned arm plus tests asserting each arm's seams and the use_llm argument.
why: iter_pipeline applies use_llm as dataclasses.replace(config, llm_enabled=use_llm), overwriting PLANNER_LLM_ENABLED/SPECIALIST_LLM_ENABLED/SYNTHESIS_LLM_ENABLED. A socket trace caught generic_planned's planner opening a connection to the configured endpoint while its own env said model-free. The posture now lives at the call site where it is visible and testable.

summary: Step 2 result: ran generic_planned against generic_composed over all 284 development questions and scored them paired with the new scripts/planner_cost_score.py. Gold coverage falls 0.8611 -> 0.4797, a paired difference of -0.3814 (se 0.0262), with the planner retrieving nothing on 77 questions where the authored plan retrieved records. Recorded in EXP-2026-09-019 with PROTOCOL, RESULTS, manifest and ISSUES.
why: Every headline figure in this programme replays an authored plan, so 0.92 was only ever a ceiling given a correct decomposition. This is the first measurement of what producing that plan costs, and it is large enough to change how every later number is read.

summary: Added the generic_local_narrator arm (MiniCPM5-2B on the synthesis seam only, specialist and planner off, generic primitives on) plus scripts/narrator_seam_health.py and tests for both. The endpoint, model, token cap and thinking budget are read at call time so the arm can be repointed without editing code. Fixed the LLM preflight to probe the model the arm will actually use rather than the --llm-model default.
why: Step 3 of the small-model plan. The narrator is the seam where a weak model is least dangerous, because claims are composed deterministically and the verifier runs unconditionally, so the question is whether it degrades prose or facts. The preflight fix matters because an arm pinning its own endpoint was being checked against a model it never calls.

summary: Added the generic_local_full arm: the narrator arm plus a model drafting the queries. It sets SPECIALIST_LLM_QUERY_BUILDER rather than the SPECIALIST_LLM_ENABLED the plan names, and its pool is constructed with llm_query_builder=True the way llm_query's is. Tests assert both, and that the arm is the narrator arm plus exactly the specialist keys.
why: No query builder reads SPECIALIST_LLM_ENABLED - four other arms set it to mean LLM drafter/synthesis. An arm built to the plan's literal wording would have run with no model writing any query and reported that as a healthy specialist seam.

summary: Added generic_narrator_off, the control Steps 3 and 4 actually need. _run_gold_replay builds a bare SynthesisConfig() for deterministic synthesis and SynthesisConfig.from_env() for LLM synthesis, so generic_composed composes at max_citations=8 while any narrator arm composes at the un-truncated 200. Two of forty enumeration claims differed on that alone; against the new control it is 40 of 40 identical.
why: Reading the narrator against generic_composed attributed a composer cap to the model. The claim-identity gate caught it at n=40, before the full pass was scored.

summary: I-20: an Analytic that DETECTS a SubTechnique was rendered 'has 1 sub-technique', asserting a hierarchy the edge does not support, and contradicting the absence claim beside it. DETECTS now names its own noun, and noun comparison normalises spelling so the I-16 guard and scanner can actually see hyphenation variants.
why: The I-16 scanner compared 'sub-technique' against 'subtechniques' literally and reported 0, so two real self-contradictions sat inside a capture recorded as clean. With the scanner made noun-aware the control's answers read 2 and the fixed tree reads 0.

summary: Added generic_planned_local, the 2x2's fourth cell (real planner + 2B narrator), which required separating the synthesis seam from iter_pipeline's use_llm flag - that flag sets planner, specialist and synthesis together, so the cell could not be expressed by it. _run_real_pipeline now takes an optional llm_synthesis and passes an explicit synthesis_config. Added the specialist token budget as a call-time override so the 2B's query-drafting failure can be tested against a larger budget rather than assumed.
why: Step 5 needs the cell nobody has run, and it must differ from its neighbours in exactly one variable each. The budget override exists so the Step 4 negative result is a measurement rather than an excuse.

summary: Step 4 result: the 2B specialist seam produced 0 working queries out of 17 drafts. 11 were rejected empty and all 6 that cleared the gate failed at the database. Re-tested at 4x the token budget: 0 of 16, with the failure mode shifting from truncation to malformed queries. Added scripts/specialist_seam_health.py and tests; its denominator is drafts reaching the gate, not questions - the first version divided by questions and reported a rejection rate of 1.22.
why: The plan's rule is that above 25% rejection this seam is not viable at 2B and the step records that rather than widening to 284. The observed figure is total retrieval failure at both budgets, so the full pass was not run.

summary: Step 5 complete: ran the 2x2 over {authored plan, real planner} x {no model, 2B narrator} on all 284 dev questions, plus single-user latency at one worker per cell. The plan effect is -0.3814 without a model and -0.3787 with one; the model effect is +0.0000 and +0.0026; the interaction is +0.0027. Added scripts/twobytwo_score.py and tests, folded every seam result into metrics.json, and filled PROTOCOL, RESULTS, ISSUES, POINTERS and the manifest. EXP-2026-09-019 marked complete and validating clean.
why: The two variables could have interacted - a weaker plan and a weaker narrator failing on the same questions - which would have made the corners misleading. They do not. Step 2's headline also re-derives unchanged against the corrected control.

summary: Corrected I-8. The 11 differing claim texts in Step 3 were not a latent composer defect under load: a concurrent session committed 1f507002 (adds DETECTS to _REL_NOUNS) at 17:30:38, and the two arms straddled it - the narrator arm's process started 16:56 and held the pre-fix module, its control started 18:47 and loaded the fixed one. All 11 cases are DETECTS-family edges. Re-running both arms over those 11 on one code version gives 11/11 byte-identical.
why: The first explanation was wrong and would have left a phantom defect on the record. It also strengthens Step 3: the narrator changed nothing at all, and the claim-identity figure would have been 284/284 from a single tree.

summary: Regenerated the 2x2's authored-plan/2B cell into the twobytwo root on the current tree, so all four cells come from one code version before the judged pass. Claim identity goes 273/284 to 284/284, closing I-8 over the whole bank rather than an 11-case slice. Every 2x2 figure reproduced exactly; only wall clock moved (93.527s to 80.988s), which is contention.
why: Judging cells generated on two code versions would have inherited the I-8 straddle silently - the same mistake, one stage later and much more expensive to find.

summary: Records the fresh-set result: 282 questions at seed 10140325, sealed before use and graded once. generic 0.9043, generic_composed 0.9037, deterministic 0.5508, with zero fabricated mappings on all three arms.
why: The development half selected the configuration and the holdout has been graded twice, so neither could carry a headline. This set had never been asked or graded, and it holds within two standard errors of the tuned figure.

summary: Added scripts/twobytwo_judged_score.py and tests: the 2x2 on the judged correctness scale, paired per question, averaging both grading positions and reporting how many cases actually got two. Armed an unattended overnight judging chain that waits for the operator's 05:00 window, holds through the 04:00-04:20 internet outage, restores the :9090 SSH tunnel if the outage kills it, retries each cell, and scores the result itself.
why: The operator is asleep and asked that problems be resolved directly. :9090 is an SSH tunnel to skynet, so the outage is likely to break it; a chain that stops to ask would lose the night.

summary: Records the two Step 6 deliverables that were never produced: single-user latency at both synthesis budgets, and the T6 entity-fidelity rates under rewording. Raising the budget 120s to 600s costs 1.13s per answer and removes all three fallbacks; wrong_entity is 0.0950, the lowest of seven arm captures.
why: Q37 asked for the latency figure at the shipped budget, and the kill-gate protocol asked for T6 rates not above the reference. Both were outstanding from Step 6.

summary: Closes the holdout regression at 288/288 on all three arms: deterministic 0.5443, generic_composed 0.8987, generic 0.9014. The sealed fresh set and the spent holdout land within 0.003 of each other on both repaired arms.
why: The value is the agreement, not the level. Disjoint banks graded on different nights agreeing to three decimal places says the repair generalises rather than fitting the set it was measured on. Recorded as regression evidence only -- the holdout was spent at 1,152 judgments per arm and can never be a capability figure.

summary: Withdraws the narrator's latency ratio of 'roughly 90x' and replaces it with ~1,340x, re-measured rather than re-derived. Also measures what the template engine was buying in speed: 0.04s per answer against the model-free composer's 0.05s.
why: The 90x divided generic's per-answer 66.82s by generic_composed's total for 20 questions -- a unit mismatch understating the cost fifteen-fold. And the case for retiring the template arm rested on coverage alone, which left open whether it was worth keeping as a fast path. A hundredth of a second says it is not.

summary: Marks EXP-2026-09-018 complete and builds data/metrics.json from the judgment sidecars via build_metrics.py, putting fresh_generic_composed_correctness 0.9005 (n=282) into CURRENT.md. Publishes a three-page reader's briefing, docs/research/reports/2026-09-14-retiring-the-template-engine.pdf.
why: The manifest still said 'planned' with empty metrics while all nine steps had run, so nothing in the repository was allowed to quote the result. metrics.json is built by reading the sidecars rather than typed, because typing manifest numbers by hand is the failure EXP-2026-09-016 A-8 was made of.

summary: Updates the README's primary comparison from the pre-repair 0.6569 vs 0.4946 to 0.9005 vs 0.5525 on the sealed set, adds rows for the narrator and planner comparisons, and rewrites the honest-limits paragraph around the planner. Files Q57 and Q58. Corrects ARCHITECTURE.md to name all five generic primitives with their measured usage, and a stale experiment count of 20 where the record holds 38.
why: Every headline figure replays an authored retrieval plan, and the planner costs -0.3814. That changes how every other number on the page should be read, so it belongs in the README rather than only in an experiment's RESULTS. ARCHITECTURE described describe and expand as the generic path, which is where the directory is but not what the record measures.

summary: Re-hashes the two data pointers this week's work invalidated: EXP-2026-09-007's judge (21793 to 29003 bytes over five transport-reliability commits) and EXP-2026-09-001's brief writer. Both notes now carry the superseded hash and the git show that recovers it.
why: Both were pointed at 'as at HEAD', and HEAD moved. Neither experiment's numbers change -- the grader prompt and sidecar schema are untouched -- but a re-run today is not the same binary and must not be reported as a repeat.

summary: EXP-2026-09-020 crosses query engine against plan source and answers the app.py question. Given an authored plan, primitives lead templates by +0.2184 (separable); at the real planner the workbench runs, +0.0261 and NOT separable, with 85 empty answers against 55. Interaction -0.1923, and the effect changes sign by tier. Renames the 2026-09-14 briefing from 'Retiring the template engine' to 'Templates, primitives, and the planner' and rewrites its recommendation from replacement to routing.
why: The swap being considered is one env flag, SPECIALIST_GENERIC_ONLY. Every figure supporting it was measured with the planner replaced by an authored plan, which app.py cannot do -- api/services/query.py calls iter_pipeline. No arm on record was production's configuration because every deterministic-family arm replays the plan. The briefing had already gone out recommending retirement, so correcting it is part of the result rather than housekeeping.

summary: The judged pass completed: 2272 judgments, 4 cells x 2 counterbalanced positions, no failures. Plan effect -0.3294 on the grader's correctness scale, converging with the -0.3814 from deterministic gold coverage. The 2B narrator RAISES correctness (+0.0171, +0.0471, both separable) but lowers faithfulness and groundedness and roughly doubles flagged hallucinations. Extended the judged scorer to report every grader dimension, not just correctness, and recorded the unverified-narrative finding as I-10.
why: Correctness alone would have reported a model that helps and omitted that it invents. The narrator runs after the verifier, so its prose is the one output nothing checks - which both the grader's flags and a direct measurement on the prose independently found.

summary: Adds docs/plans/2026-09-14-frontend-prototype-configuration.md, a seven-step plan for what the public workbench should ship. Its spine is separating retrieval breadth from presentation breadth: rank and bound the composer's enumeration first, then gate each measured coverage win on a T6 re-run.
why: Three unions each raise coverage at production's plan source (engine merge +0.0548, facet chasing +0.0358, planner union +0.1799) and the merged configuration then FAILS T6 -- catalogue_dump 0.0915 to 0.1157. Both are the same change: unions add records and the composer enumerates whatever it is handed. Shipping order has to fix the composer before turning any union on.

summary: Provenance note: several EXP-2026-09-019 commits used `git add -A` while concurrent sessions wrote to the same checkout, so ~2,500 judgment sidecars from fresh-2026-09-12, paired-control-2026-09-12 and plan-source-2026-09-14 were committed under small-model-generic messages. Nothing was lost or altered; .gitignore tracks *.judgment.* deliberately (D-033). History was NOT rewritten.
why: Anyone reading git log to find when a given experiment's judgments landed would be misled by the commit message they sit under. Recording that here is cheaper and far safer than rewriting shared history. Future commits in this experiment scope their `git add` to their own paths.

summary: Step 2 of the frontend prototype plan: the enumeration claim now ranks a related set against what the plan asked for before listing it, and states how many entries it withheld instead of truncating silently at MAX_ENUMERATION_IDS.
why: EXP-2026-09-020 A-5 found the merged configuration failing T6 -- catalogue_dump 0.0915 to 0.1157 -- because every retrieval widening hands the composer more rows and the composer listed them in arrival order. Ranking changes which of an over-wide set is shown, not what was retrieved or claimed.

summary: Steps 3-5 of the frontend plan, gated on T6 over 579 paraphrase variants. The ranked composer is a no-op on fidelity (correct, with no merge on). Facet chasing ships: +0.0358 coverage at zero T6 cost. The engine merge is refused at 0.1088/0.1140 against a 0.0950/0.0915 reference, and ranking does not rescue it.
why: A-5 reasoned the merge's cost was over-long enumerations and that bounding them would absorb it. Measured, it does not: the extra rows arrive as additional records, each composing its own claim, and the enumeration bound governs entries within a record rather than the record count.

summary: Step 7 of the frontend plan: separates the narrator from the query builder. The composer defaulted to drafter='llm' so answers read as prose, which also handed query construction to a model; it now defaults to deterministic with 'Plain prose' as its own toggle, wired end to end through /api/query, /api/conversation-query and the conversation graph.
why: drafter='llm' sets the planner, specialist AND synthesis seams together. Wanting readable prose therefore silently selected the query-writing baseline that scores 0.5000 where the template cascade scores 0.9467. The narrator is the one seam measured not to change a fact -- 284/284 claims byte-identical, +0.0000 coverage.

summary: Adds narrative_source to the synthesis contract, so an answer says who wrote the PROSE as well as who wrote the claims. Verified live: narrate=false gives deterministic/deterministic at 12ms, narrate=true gives deterministic/llm at 19.7s, both 3/3 claims supported.
why: composer names who wrote the claims, which is the trust surface. Nothing recorded whether the sentence a reader reads first had been rewritten by a model. For a workbench that cites the record and the query behind every claim, leaving the prose layer's provenance invisible was an omission.

summary: Records A-7: the frontend prototype plan implemented and verified end to end. Ships ORCH_MAX_HOPS=5, ranked bounded enumeration, facet chasing and a per-question narrator toggle; refuses the engine merge (T6) and the LLM planner (needs a live endpoint). Full stack verified against :9090.
why: The frontend work found a defect no arm could have caught: the composer defaulted to drafter='llm', so wanting readable prose handed query construction to the 0.5000 baseline. Every evaluation arm sets its seams explicitly, so none was ever the configuration the UI shipped.

summary: Plans the workbench control surface: replace Plan/Full-answer, Drafter and Plain-prose with Verify, Readable prose and a selectable thinking budget (128 doubling to 16384), defaulting to the ~1s deterministic path.
why: A deterministic turn takes 43s and 42 of them are the chat wrapper, not the pipeline: validation at 29.68s and answer at 40.39s against a graph that answers at 1.09s. No control turned them off because with_llm_enabled() is one-way.

summary: Step 1 of the workbench-controls plan: ConversationConfig.with_llm_enabled is now two-way, so a caller can turn the chat layer off as well as on.
why: enabled resolves from the shared LLM group, so ARIADNE_LLM_ENABLED=true switched the conversation layer on implicitly and the one-way setter could not switch it back. A turn the workbench labelled deterministic still made four model calls: 1.09s of pipeline inside a 43.27s turn.

summary: Amends the workbench-controls plan: verify gates the validation agent alone, not the whole conversation layer, and readable prose selects whether the answer agent writes the reply or uses the pipeline narrative. Records the per-stage costs and identifies the final->done gap as thread auto-titling.
why: The operator corrected the assumption that verify:off should kill the layer -- router and orchestration are wanted. build_conversation_graph already takes a separate validation_client and evaluate_sufficiency short-circuits when it is disabled, so the finer split needs no new branch.

summary: Step 2a: a new thread is titled at the START of its first turn and on a worker, so the ~2.9s naming call leaves the critical path and the sidebar is named while the pipeline still runs. Also guards the fallback, which previously turned a failed title into a failed turn.
why: title_for reads the question and nothing else, so running it last in _persist_turn was pure latency and a worse interface. The guard matters because the fallback calls the same client that just failed, and title_for catches LLMUnavailable but not an arbitrary transport error.

summary: Steps 2-3: verify, narrate and thinking_budget travel on both query surfaces and reach the agents they name. verify gates the validation agent, narrate gates the answer agent, and the budget is applied to the conversation config; router and orchestration stay on in every mode.
why: Each control maps onto behaviour graph.py already documents as the deterministic path -- validation=pass, answer=narrative -- by injecting a disabled client, so no new branch is added. A None budget leaves the environment alone so an untouched deployment is unchanged.

summary: Step 4: the composer now carries Verify, Prose and a Thinking budget (128 doubling to 16384) instead of Plan/Full-answer, Drafter and Plain prose. Both toggles default off, which is the fast path.
why: The old controls named implementation seams rather than choices, and drafter=llm turned on the planner, specialist and narrator together, so reaching for readable prose silently selected the 0.5000 query path. Plan-only is a debugging view the inspector already covers.

summary: Step 5: the four control corners timed end to end. Default 0.25s against 43.27s before, verify-on 28.56s, prose-on 32.20s, both 78.87s. Records A-8 with the two defects the measurement caught.
why: The claim this work makes is a latency claim, so it is only finished when measured through the running stack. The first corner run found verify:on finishing in 0.08s -- the control was not authoritative and would have shipped looking wired.

summary: Replaces the numeric thinking control with named levels (None/Low/Medium/High) behind a custom dropdown. None sends 1 rather than 0, because the sender omits a falsy budget and the model then reasons unbounded -- a literal 0 measured 11.27s against an explicit zero at 1.28s.
why: A control labelled None:0 would have selected the slowest option, an eightfold error in the direction the label promised. Changing the sender guard instead would switch every caller with an unset budget from full reasoning to none.

summary: A-10: the thinking cap now reaches the wire. ConversationLLM.complete never passed a sampling block, so no conversation agent ever sent thinking_token_budget; and None now sends an explicit 0 via thinking_budget_explicit. A verify-on turn is 5.27s at None against 25.25s at Medium.
why: A-9 concluded the model ignores the cap. It does not -- the probe prompt was too easy to reach the ceiling, and the control was dead on the conversation path, so there was no budget effect to observe rather than a weak one.

summary: Corrects A-10: a Medium-thinking verify-on turn is 5.81-5.85s across three runs, not the 25.25s reported from a single contended sample. None is 1.32-1.35s. Medium costs about +4.5s, which is what 512 tokens at ~115 tok/s predicts.
why: The 25.25s figure was taken while the endpoint was serving long hard-prompt probes and a concurrent session, and was reported without repetition. A single-run latency figure on a shared endpoint samples the endpoint load, not the setting.

summary: Fixes a 500 on every /api/query: main.py sent thinking_budget= to stream_query_events, which had no such parameter. The workbench query path now takes the cap and applies it to the synthesis config with llm_thinking_budget_explicit, so a requested None/0 is transmitted as a real zero; the narrator seam sends an explicit zero the same way llm_composer already did. Passing a config takes over from iter_pipeline's llm_enabled=use_llm derivation, so llm_enabled is set here in both directions and a budget-only request stays deterministic even with SYNTHESIS_LLM_ENABLED=true.
why: The A-10 plumbing landed on the conversation path only; the query path got the caller and not the callee, so the startup smoke and every workbench query failed before the pipeline started.

summary: Plans paraphrase robustness at T0-T3: re-baseline the variant bank on the shipped tree, test whether the primitive engine is verb-robust, re-gate the shelved rewrite stage on the tiers in scope, then scope relation ranking only if a gap survives. Every step carries a pre-registered prediction and falsifier.
why: EXP-2026-08-020's tier table ran at 0ae78c19, before the name-resolution reorder and the EXP-2026-09-018 repair, so no figure on record describes the current system's behaviour under rewording. The operator needs T0-T3 to work and the existing 0.0990 at T3 is stale in an unknown direction.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 1 of 6: EXP-2026-09-021 pre-registered with three hypotheses and their falsifiers, and the reference capture proved byte-reproducible over two runs (T0 = 1.0000, a determinism control). Adds scripts/revalidate_load_manifest.py after the loader's staleness check (I-21) blocked the run a second time.
why: Variants are scored against their own gold question's capture, so an irreproducible reference would make every tier figure meaningless. The revalidation script re-stamps only when the canonical manifest differs solely in build_timestamp AND live per-label counts match, so it cannot paper over a real data change the way a hand edit could.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 2 of 6: the shipped tree re-baselined over all 579 variants. T1 0.3917, T2 0.3667, T3 0.1782, T4/T5 0.0000. H1 (T3 >= 0.25) is NOT met. The August tier table is not a like-for-like comparison -- the EXP-2026-09-018 repair moved 51 of 120 gold entity sets and 74 of 120 gold queries -- so the comparison is redone on the 39 stable gold cases, where T2 is unchanged and T1 is -0.0257.
why: Reading the naive August-to-now difference as a regression would have reported a T1/T2 decline that did not happen: records_exact scores a variant against its own gold question on the same tree, and the repair changed what the gold questions extract. The repair's real effect at T3 is fidelity, not accuracy -- catalogue_dump 0.5248 -> 0.1683 with abstention rising to 0.4752.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 3 of 6: H2 falsified with the sign reversed. Schema-derived primitives score T1 0.2167 against templates' 0.3917 and T2 0.2500 against 0.3667. Paired per variant they solve a near-strict subset: across 341 variants at T1-T3 they succeed on exactly ONE the templates miss, so the oracle bound on choosing between engines equals templates alone.
why: The hypothesis was that an engine which never reads a verb cannot be hurt by a changed verb. The opposite holds: removing the template ladder removes the only component that turns 'defend against' into an intent, and the primitives abstain twice as often instead. It also shows the union-equals-oracle shape EXP-2026-09-020 found twice is a property of that bank and plan source, not of the two engines.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 4 of 6: the rewrite stage re-gated on T0-T3 FAILS its ship rule. T3 +0.1386 passes, but T1 -0.1167 and T2 -0.0667 are far outside the -0.02 tolerance. Paired counts show the mechanism: where the identifier survives it breaks 32 and fixes 10; where the identifier is gone it fixes 44 and breaks 7.
why: All three pre-registered hypotheses are now falsified, which is a complete result. The sign split is the actionable part: the stage canonicalises away the identifier the template ladder was reading, so it is not wrong but unconditional. Gating it on 'no identifier resolved' is computable at run time without gold, and is filed as a Step 5 hypothesis rather than claimed, because A-3 reasoned a bound without running it and was 0.27 too high.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 5 of 6: implements the identifier gate (ARIADNE_REWRITE_ONLY_WITHOUT_ID, default off, new RUNG_SKIPPED_ID) and measures it. T1/T2 return to baseline exactly (0.3917/0.3667, outcome-identical on 239 of 240 variants) while T3 reaches 0.3267, above the ungated 0.3168. It passes 8 of 9 pre-registered clauses and FAILS T3 catalogue_dump at 0.1089 against a 0.0915 cap.
why: Step 4 showed the rewrite stage is not wrong but unconditional, and the separating condition is computable at run time from the question alone. The flag ships off: the T3 dump rate is better than the shipped baseline's 0.1683 but above the pre-registered cap, and relaxing a threshold after seeing the value it failed is what pre-registration exists to prevent. Flag-off path re-verified byte-identical across all 579 variants.

summary: Paraphrase Robustness step 6 of 6: ships the identifier-gated rewrite stage (ARIADNE_REWRITE, ARIADNE_REWRITE_MODEL, ARIADNE_REWRITE_ONLY_WITHOUT_ID all on) under D-034, the operator's 'not worse than the shipped baseline' fidelity rule. T3 goes 0.1782 -> 0.3267 while T1/T2 stay at baseline. EXP-2026-09-021 closes complete with all three pre-registered hypotheses falsified.
why: The pre-registered rule capped T3 catalogue_dump at 0.0915 and the gated arm is 0.1089, so the recorded verdict stays FAIL at 8 of 9 clauses; gate_verdict.py now computes both rules and the original is preserved rather than re-scored. Shipping is an operator call on a product question. Two costs are recorded where they cannot be missed: that dump overage, and T4/T5 wrong_entity roughly tripling to 0.3077/0.2981 as abstentions become answers.

summary: EXP-2026-09-021 AMENDMENT A-1 / D-035: gates T4/T5 separately by refusing to let the model choose the anchor (ARIADNE_REWRITE_REQUIRE_RESOLVED_ANCHOR, shipped on). T3 keeps its full 0.3267 while T4/T5 wrong_entity falls 0.3077->0.1442 and 0.2981->0.1346, removing ~81% of the cost D-034 accepted. Files Q59.
why: Reading the Step 5 artifacts showed the mechanism: the model chose the anchor on 82 of 104 T4 and 88 of 104 T5 variants but only 24 of 101 at T3, and wrong_entity tracked it exactly. deterministic_fill already refuses to guess an anchor; the model rung was doing it anyway. Probing the refusals then found Q59 -- an entity name is never looked up unless the router first picks a dataset, so 37 T3 variants reach no exact anchor because a lookup never ran.

summary: Records a portable open-question discovery plan and pre-registers EXP-2026-09-022 before implementation. Separates candidate recall from answer completeness and preserves ambiguity across sources.
why: The operator wants T4/T5 improvements that transfer through source cards and graphs rather than benchmark-specific wording.

summary: Adds an offline source-card-driven discovery prototype and a frozen diagnostic harness. Candidates retain canonical source-qualified identity, field matches, graph context, and ambiguity; unrelated-domain tests exercise the interface.
why: Measure lexical candidate coverage and graph-context tradeoffs before changing anchor acceptance or workbench behavior.

summary: Completes EXP-2026-09-022 with recorded candidate-retrieval ablations, generated tables, and a prioritized design for portable open-question answering. Records negative fusion results and remaining acceptance/completeness gaps; keeps raw predictions hash-pinned outside git and files Q60.
why: Candidate coverage provides measurable guidance for T4/T5 research while keeping answer-accuracy claims and future source portability separate.

summary: Adds docs/plans/2026-09-15-open-question-correctness.md: a ten-step, pre-registered plan merging this session's proposal with EXP-2026-09-022's design. Seals an entity-held-out bank first, then exact-name hygiene, Q59 anchor-first routing, expand-on-unbound-relation, direct form execution, generic-engine parity, a gloss-generated relation lexicon, disclosed T4/T5 acceptance, and a workbench ship step with a no-catalogue-literal portability test.
why: The operator asked for a step-by-step plan to make the workbench answer open-ended questions correctly while staying portable to other graphs on cards and records alone; the review found the shipped name index already beats the new prototype, so the plan builds on it.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (1/10): seals docs/evaluation/variants-holdout-2026-09, an entity-held-out bank of 40 gold questions (20 ATT&CK, 20 CAPEC, drawn from the composition banks with seeds absent from every exposed-bank anchor) and 160 authored T3-T6 variants that pass the gate 160/0. The reference was captured twice at 32 workers and is byte-identical; SEAL.md records every hash and utils/planner/tests/test_holdout_bank.py enforces them. scripts/variant_harness.py capture and scripts/author_variants.py prepare gain a --gold option.
why: Every rule and threshold in the plan's ancestry has read the exposed bank, so a fresh bank held out by entity is needed to confirm rules without choosing them there.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (2/10): scaffolds EXP-2026-09-023-anchor-hygiene-and-q59 with H1 (a corpus-frequency distinctiveness rule for exact names, 1% fixed) and H2 (name lookup before dataset routing with the router as tie-break) pre-registered with falsifiers on both banks. Step 0 enters the 2026-09-15 review probes into the record via data/shipped_vs_prototype.py and data/exact_name_probe.py: the shipped index beats EXP-022's prototype at every budget >= 5 on T4/T5, and every single exact-name bind at T4/T5/T6 is a wrong ordinary-word name (Credentials, Malware, at).
why: Numbers that exist only in a chat log do not exist; the hypotheses must be written before the sealed bank is opened.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (3/10): exact-name hygiene. namesearch.exact_name_matches gains a distinctiveness rule behind ARIADNE_EXACT_NAME_DISTINCT (struct: a one-word name binds only when written as a standalone proper noun; df: the falsified 1% frequency rule kept for reproduction) and exact_name_matches_all runs every source with nesting suppressed across sources. Both query builders gain an unanchored-relation dump guard behind ARIADNE_UNANCHORED_RELATION_ABSTAINS. Tests on a non-cyber fixture and the real snapshot; flags documented off in .env.example.
why: Ordinary words that are also node names (Credentials, Malware, the tool named at) bound 54 wrong anchors on the exposed bank and 43 on the sealed one; removing them exposed seedless relation templates that scan the catalogue.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (4/10): Q59. deterministic_fill looks identifiers and complete names up across every live source before dataset routing (ARIADNE_ANCHOR_BEFORE_ROUTING / PlannerConfig.anchor_before_routing, passed through the canonicalize node); the router's own selection breaks a cross-source name collision and an unbroken collision is reported as an ambiguity. scripts/variant_harness.py gains the hygiene and anchor_first arms with every new variable pinned in every arm; the experiment's arm_table.py and paired.py tabulate arms from scored files.
why: An entity name implies its dataset; routing on the question's other words first left 37 of 101 T3 questions with no anchor on the exposed bank.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (3-4/10) record: EXP-2026-09-023 completed. H1 (1% frequency rule) falsified and replaced by AMENDMENT A-1 (structural proper-noun rule); H2 (Q59) resolves the anchor on 97 of 101 exposed T3 questions (unresolved 37 -> 4) but T3 records_exact reaches 0.3465, not the predicted 0.45, because the rung's rendering is the next defect. Every catalogue dump on both banks is gone and T6 answers nothing wrong. D-036 and the Q59 amendment recorded; scored arms hash-pinned; INDEX and CURRENT regenerated.
why: A number that exists only in a chat log does not exist; the hypotheses' verdicts and the ship-decision inputs for Step 10 must be in the record.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (5/10) code: when the anchor binds and no facet is question-relevant, the loop's first re-plan expands the anchor's smallest non-zero facets (at most ORCH_MAX_FACET_EXPANSIONS, none over ORCH_EXPAND_UNBOUND_MAX_MEMBERS=50, never on a definitional request) instead of answering with one record. Behind ORCH_EXPAND_UNBOUND, default off; facet_counts() reads member counts off the facet block; harness arm expand_unbound; EXP-2026-09-024 pre-registered.
why: 54 of the 172 T1/T2 misses bind the right anchor and no relation because the card lacks the analyst's verb; a bounded neighbourhood is a better answer than the anchor's own description.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (5/10) record: EXP-2026-09-024 complete. The unbound-relation fallback raises exposed T1/T2 recall by about 0.05 with dumps and wrong-entity flat, and is falsified on its exact guard: it widens 26 answers whose gold is the anchor's own single record, and the intent classifier cannot separate those from the 14 it improves. Flag stays off pending Step 10's judged pass; .env.example documents it.
why: Exact-match cannot grade a widened answer; the verdict and the protocol flaw belong in the record before the next step builds on it.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (6/10) code: form_plan.py turns a bound IntentForm into a Plan (anchor id in the text, labels and relation in entities, a second source via the declared join key). Under ARIADNE_FORM_EXECUTE the canonicalize node emits it and draft uses it first, falling back to the rendered sentence if the gate rejects it. A question naming a target label other than the anchor's is now an enumerate even when classified a lookup. Harness arms form_execute and form_execute_ids; EXP-2026-09-025 pre-registered.
why: The render-and-re-parse round trip broke answers whose form was right, and a describe-mode form for a relation question never consulted the model rung; a form is graph-agnostic and executes on any card.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (6/10) record: EXP-2026-09-025 complete. Direct form execution lifts exposed T3 exact 0.3465 -> 0.3762 (4 fixed, 1 broken; predicted +0.05) with T1/T2 byte-identical and guards flat; lifting the D-034 identifier skip on top is falsified (T1 exact 0.39 -> 0.30, 15 broken vs 4 fixed), so the skip stays.
why: The verdicts and the re-affirmation of D-034 belong in the record before Step 7 builds on the arm.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (7/10) code: the generic Gremlin dispatch chooses the cross-source bridge by seed origin, not vocabulary. A joined, seeded sub-question bridges when its seeds belong to no label of this source (the registry's learned id schemes), when it names mapping vocabulary, or when it names no native relation. Tests on the fixture card; harness arm generic; EXP-2026-09-026 pre-registered.
why: Under paraphrase the schema-derived engine bound an ATT&CK id as a CAPEC id or walked the native hierarchy and starved its consumer; the cascade won those categories on vocabulary alone.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (7/10) amendment: the generic reverse bridge lands on the label that owns the join edge (registry) instead of the plan's entity; harness arm generic_form pairs the generic engine with direct form execution because the rendered sentence over-matches entities and blows the chain's traversal budget. Recorded as EXP-2026-09-026 A-1 after the first generic arm falsified parity.
why: The first generic arm lost 17/12/28 exposed answers at T1/T2/T3; two of the causes were dispatch defects, not template knowledge.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (7/10) record: EXP-2026-09-026 complete, parity falsified. The dispatch fixes close the reverse-mapping category (16 template-only cases -> 2) but the generic engine on the executed form still loses 11/6/14 exposed answers at T1/T2/T3 and 18 of 40 sealed T3, as wider neighbourhoods (recall at parity, exact not). Templates stay; SPECIALIST_GENERIC_ONLY remains off.
why: The plan's Step 7 falsifier says the surviving categories are listed and the templates are not retired.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (8/10) code: scripts/generate_relation_lexicon.py generates, once and offline, the words an analyst uses for each declared relationship from the card's gloss and endpoints (one local-model call per relationship, routing tokens and cross-relationship words dropped, ungenerated relationships recorded) into data/source_cards/overlays/<dataset>.relation_lexicon.json and the overlay; the router reads the sidecar behind ARIADNE_RELATION_PARAPHRASES as gloss hints. Harness arm paraphrases; EXP-2026-09-027 pre-registered.
why: The card carries one gloss sentence per relationship; 54 of 172 T1/T2 misses bind the anchor and no relation for want of the analyst's verb.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (9/10) code: utils/specialists/schema/rerank.py re-orders the name index's top 25 by bge-small embedding similarity (in-process fastembed or the evaluation venv over a pipe; off without a backend; stands down on an exact name) behind ARIADNE_RERANK; under ARIADNE_ANCHOR_DISCLOSED a model-chosen anchor stands and the answer's headline names the resolution (utils/synthesis/disclosure.py). Harness arm disclosed; EXP-2026-09-028 pre-registered.
why: T4/T5 answer nothing under D-035; a reranked closed choice that says which entity it picked is a visible, correctable resolution instead of a silent wrong one.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (8-9/10) record: EXP-2026-09-027 and EXP-2026-09-028 complete. The generated relation lexicon lifts exposed T2/T3 exact by 0.03 each and costs T1 0.03 (nouns like 'tool' bind USES too widely) so it is not shipped; disclosed anchor acceptance passes its wrong-entity guard on the sealed bank (0.10/0.15) but reaches only 0.125/0.20 exact and fails the guard on the exposed bank (0.35 at T4), so it becomes a clarification, not an answer.
why: Both verdicts and the ship positions belong in the record before Step 10 decides the .env.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (10/10): ships ARIADNE_EXACT_NAME_DISTINCT, ARIADNE_UNANCHORED_RELATION_ABSTAINS, ARIADNE_ANCHOR_BEFORE_ROUTING and ARIADNE_FORM_EXECUTE in .env and .env.example (D-037); keeps expand-on-unbound, generic-only, the relation lexicon and disclosed acceptance off with reasons (D-038); amends Q60; rewrites the README's question-rewriting row; verifies the shipped path through the workbench and the API stream; adds the no-catalogue-literal test and the judge bridge; pins ORCH_CHASE_FACETS in every harness arm.
why: The frontend is the deliverable: every mechanism that met the not-worse-than-baseline rule on both banks is on, everything else is recorded off.

summary: Open-Question Correctness (10/10) judged pass: EXP-2026-09-029 records the local judge's reading of the shipped arm on the sealed bank — T3 completeness 0.9187, every invented anchor abstained, T4/T5 near zero, two fabricated-mapping verdicts that are composer wording defects. Faithfulness and hallucination columns are marked unusable because the judge bridge carries claims but no evidence records.
why: The plan's last deliverable, with its limitation stated rather than its numbers quoted uncritically.

summary: Synapse Graph Transfer (2/6): the graph loader resolves any dataset that has a source card under <data_dir>/source_cards, not only the four built-in names; semantic validation for such datasets reads labels, types and edge patterns from the schema the export shipped (the identity branch generalised), with no pattern check when none are declared; main.py --dataset drops its choices list. New tests in utils/graph_loader/tests/test_external_dataset.py; attack/capec/merged paths untouched. Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-16-synapse-graph-transfer.md.

ARIADNE_ENDPOINT_<DATASET> now normalises hyphens to underscores on both sides, so a dataset like mnp-cs-03000-r2 is addressable from a shell variable. New tests in utils/specialists/tests/test_external_dataset_specialist.py.
why: The specialist constructor was the last name-keyed dispatch on the query path; the card already carries the backend.

Live suites: 921 passed; the one failure (test_llm_builder generic_local_full) predates this work (arm added 2026-09-14).

summary: Synapse Graph Transfer (4/6): dataset names are pattern-validated strings in the API (GET /api/graph/{dataset}, admin dataset) instead of a two-name Literal; the graph and query services label a source's backend from its card (utils/planner/cards.load_card_backends) with the old literals as fallback; specialist-start SSE events carry the lane's backend; the web client files a lane by that hint and only falls back to the source-name rule for the built-ins.
why: The web client inferred the lane from source === 'capec', which would misfile any third source; carrying the backend in the event is the smallest change that keeps ATT&CK and CAPEC exactly where they were.
detail: Tests: api/tests/test_graph.py (card-backed name reaches the service, malformed name is 422), utils/orchestration/tests/test_event_parity.py key set, web/lib/__tests__/runMachine.test.ts lane-by-hint. api+orchestration 183 passed; vitest 207 passed; npm run build clean. npm run lint reports 3 pre-existing errors in AnswerMitigationMatrix.tsx, ThreadHeader.tsx and Dropdown.tsx, none touched here.

summary: Synapse Graph Transfer (6/6): one Synapse graph (mnp-cs-03000-r2, 1399 nodes / 2132 edges) was exported, copied into data/, loaded into the profile-gated external Neo4j, verified, and answered a question through main.py --query and the API stream (14/14 claims supported); then every artifact was removed. Two engine defects it exposed are fixed: the Neo4j relationship MERGE is keyed on the edge id (it collapsed 93 parallel edges), and deterministic_fill cites an exact-name match's id only when the resolver can read it back.
why: The plan's claim is that a Synapse graph loads and answers without a code change per graph; doing it once is the proof, and the regression diff is what shows ATT&CK and CAPEC did not move.
detail: Regression: deterministic arm over bank-2026-08-19 and bank-2026-08-20 on this tree is byte-identical (30/30 identifiers and content, both banks) to a worktree at pre-plan commit 94648087, and identical with and without the third card present. The committed answers under docs/evaluation/experiments/bank2026081{9,20} predate several main commits (template and composer wording changes) and are no longer a valid gate on their own. Full sweep: pytest utils/ api/ = 2447 passed, 218 skipped, 1 deselected (the pre-existing test_llm_builder generic_local_full failure). Known leftovers: --graph verify passes vacuously when a load failed because no runtime manifest exists; the compose bind mount leaves an empty root-owned docker/neo4j-external/ that no container-side rm could delete on this host (SELinux/btrfs) — remove with sudo.
